text: Sort of pricey. The beer selection was OK. I'm not really sure what distinguishes this restaurant as specializing in either bread or beer.

resp.text:
Dorn,

We're sorry that your experience was sub par. One of the things that distinguishes us as specializing in beer is that we offer a wide selection of beers on tap, in cans and in bottles. We work closely with local brewers from all over the state to ensure that you have the best of Alaskan craft brews and we like to think that we have an extensive beer knowledge . As for bread, most of our menu is bread based, and we also locally source our bread.

Hopefully you can come in again and we can change your rating. Three star reviews really hurt our business, and we hope that we can can change your mind in the near future.

resp.text:
Thanks for the review, we absolutely pride ourselves on our food and service. We have a 4.8/5 rating on Facebook, yelp and google, with over 1000 reviews. If there was an issue with your food not being tasty or delicious, we are the first company to offer you a completely new meal on us. We are a small family owned restaurant and we absolutely pride ourselves on our hospitality and customer service. Our “toaster over” is actually two air impingement ovens. We’d love to give you a full tour sometime. Again, we’re sorry if the food isn’t for you, but we’d love to invite you back to give us another try.

-Alexis

text: This location is frequently "out of" various menu items, their ice cream machine is often broken, and they don't post signs at the drive thru so you know what they are out of, you keep ordering to be told they don't have it. ALWAYS check your order before leaving as they frequently get the order correct when taken (check your receipt) but substitute or just screw up when putting the items in the bag or on the tray. Have them REPEAT your order to you in the drive thru, they are easily confused. They are the slowest drive thru in town, don't have the sense to have people with large or custom orders move to the wait area, they make everyone in line wait. They usually have loser high school kids with low IQ in the drive up, but recently changed crew to include a lot of friendly, more efficient adult Phillipino and other Asians. They really are the WORST McDonald's overall, they can't seem to get it right. If the drive thru improves the counter quality, such as it is, goes down. Why even go here you ask? I am retired and can wait, but even I have limits, and they get until the end of summer 2018 to get it together, and then I start going to the Taco Bell next to them, which, amazingly, can get an order correct the first time, they tell you up front of they are out of anything (rare), and they fill it efficiently and courteously. I bet the owner of this McDonald's eats at the Taco Bell, because otherwise their own service would improve...or maybe not, who cares, not them.

name: Alex Medina
text: Great Mexican food! Have been up here for a few years and missed our easily accessible Mexican food in CA. This place has given me renewed hope of getting good Mexican food.  We ordered a LENGUA and AL PASTOR Burritos.  Both had great flavor.  The lengua was not dried and was tender.  The Pastor was very flavorveble delicious.  We also ordered carnitas tacos and plain quezadillas. Which all tasted great.  Will definitely come back!

name: Gregory Hartley
text: Best Mexican restaurant in Anchorage. (And there are a LOT to choose from, so that's not an empty claim.) Great cultural vibe and excellent decor. Friendly service. Lots of space for social distancing. Truly friendly server, and super accommodating. For families: great kids meal options at very reasonable rates. (That's big deal when dining with kids.)

name: Emily Mehlman
text: Finally, amazing authentic Mexican food in AK! The shrimp diablo was exactly what I had in mind and even exceeded my expectations. The chicken mole enchiladas were very good as well. The sopapillas were the only thing that was not as I had pictured, they were dense dough covered in cinnamon and sugar instead of the hollow ones I'm used to. I did not come for dessert though, so I'm very happy and will be back!

text: This was my first time dining at Moose-AKa's and they definitely made a great first impression. They also won't rush you out so you can relax and enjoy yourself, so you'll need to ask for the check once you are ready.

name: Bea Jackson
text:
My first time eating Serbian & This place made our trip PERFECT! From the knowledgeable, friendly staff; the beautiful decor; and the amazing food. Zac and Ali were all smiles and were so awesome about explaining each item on the menu to us. They were so great even took our pix with our food. The stuffed schnitzel was TO DIE FOR and the cabbage rolls were absolutely melt in ur mouth amazing! The homemade Sangria was so great! They even bottled it up so we can take one to go!!
Definitely a must try when going thru Denali!

text: Only one word describes the experience: Fantastic.  When you walk in you will immediately not the decor.  It was almost all created by the owner.  Then there is the food.  It is even more fantastic.  Quite a variety of Serbian inspired dishes.  I thoroughly enjoyed the beef crepe.  The pictures below are the beef crepe, Mt Denali crepe(chicken) and the French mixed berry crepe.   When you come to Denali you must come here.  If you don't you won't know what you are missing.

name: Nat Luengnaruemitchai

name: Amalesh Murali
text:
I was pleasantly surprised that they served vegetarian and vegan food. There is a significant wait time for the meal but it is really tasty. We liked the place a lot and we dropped by twice on the same day.
Only down side is that some menu items are available only in the afternoon but the staff explained well the reason behind that.
I wish in the future they could offer that the entire day. Desserts are very yummy and light on the stomach.
The entire cooking is done by one chef with no assistance which is incredible and without compromising the quality.
The view from the restaurant is amazing overlooking the mountains.

name: Robin Dern
text: The Park Strip is a favorite spot in downtown Anchorage. It’s a popular summer location for kite flying, festivals and outdoor yoga. In the winter local schools use the long expanse to introduce students to cross country skiing. Year round, it is an excellent place to have fun with your dog. In addition to a myriad of recreational opportunities, the park is home to several memorials and outdoor exhibits. Yesterday we had the chance to visit the one that honors Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. and other notable Alaskans who shared his vision of living in an equal and just world.

name: Ryan Stafford

name: JEFF PETERS
text:
The Seward Windsong Lodge was very comfortable and modern. You will see you in one of my photos that the television is the old cathode-ray style too. That photo was taken in 2000 and 8, so you have to expect that they have upgraded all of their television since then.

It's a modern facility that has a cabin or Lodge style Motif. The surroundings are quiet and you're in a wooded secluded area that gives you the feeling that you are truly part of nature.

Some of the staff come up from the lower 48 states every year. One of our guides that we used to take us to one of the local glaciers and national parks was a retired High School teacher. He and his wife come up every year in their motor home and then spend the summer at the Seward Windsong Lodge as hotel workers and naturalists. So the staff really know what they're doing as far as telling you what is happening within the ecology and how the landscape has changed over the Millennia.

The rooms were absolutely quiet. We had been in there during High season and you could not hear anything that you didn't want to. They have free Wi-Fi and it worked well for us. Transportation into the town of Seward is available. The beds were comfortable and we slept soundly.

If and when I go back to Alaska, I will try to stay at the Seward Windsong Lodge.

name: Anita Kingree
text:
Denali National Park and Preserve is a beautiful place with lands untouched by man. It is important to note that Denali is more of a preserve than a "park." Cars are not allowed beyond the bus station. You must buy a bus ticket to go to Eielson Visitor Center. If you buy a bus ticket, you can get off the bus at any stop and catch another bus later. The only problem with this is, the buses are really full, and it's very hard to find a bus that has room for you. At Eielson there is a ranger that will put you on a waiting list, and they control how many people get back on the buses from there so it is easier to get back on a bus there than at other stops.
I should also add, there is no where to buy food or drinks past the bus station, so make sure you bring all you will need for a full days' adventure! Eielson has picnic tables where you can eat lunch if you brought it. It also has a couple of small trails to beautiful views.

name: Elizabeth J
text: This place is a little pricey but it did not disappoint! Amazing food and excellent service. Highly recommend.

name: Elizabeth Angel
text: I had the seafood risotto and it was delicious. You need a reservation but they do offer seats at the bar for people without reservations. The mojito was not good at all kinda tasted watered down but the other drinks I had were good. I recommend the strawberry martini if you like sweet drinks.

name: Maxim Culacov
text: It's a 5 star review for all the work that has been put into this place and it's authenticity. Food is mediocre but you don't go there for the food. Don't expect fine dining here because it's not supposed to be part of the experience. It's an amazing experience as is :)

name: Kevin Hause
text: We had a wonderful time with a very friendly waitress! Halibut fish and chips, shrimp risotto and the senator new york strip. Everything was done perfectly and not a single complaint, reservations are a must on a weekend and We will 100% be going back soon!

name: Glitter Bunny
text: Nice atmosphere if a little loud. Not a wide selection though. Took a while to get even a salad and soup. But polite staff. Definitely expensive though

name: Brian Williams
text:
Probably the best dinner I've had in Fairbanks, AK.  Absolutely the best.
Had the sea food platter and  it was amazing. Very friendly and knowledgeable wait staff. Will definitely be back for more.

name: thomas Huddleston
text: We made a reservation ahead of time since we knew that the pump house was always busy. We were seated right away even though we showed up 15 minutes early and the waiter definitely took care of us with recommendations. We ended up getting the crab mac and cheese for an appetizer that was absolutely amazing, considering I don't even really like make and cheese.  Definitely great food

name: Phil
text: We had a wide selection of foods: seafood chowder, house salad, Caesars salad, spinach and artichoke dip. The entrees of grilled halibut with vegetables and Red deer tenderloin with a sweet potato hash and broccolini were all excellent. We finished off the dinner with their strawberry crumble with vanilla ice cream. Server was friendly and efficient and met our best expectations.

name: Ehren Schachle
text: Great place year round, fancy or relaxed. Inside or out the Pumphouse has great food and atmosphere.

name: Shanon Hendrix
text: I just started working there and so far I love the place and the staff very friendly and kind

name: Ginger Fontes
text: Fairbanks isn't known for their high quality cuisine but Pump House is our go to, when friends/family from out of town visit. Always amazing service, good food and great desserts. They even have a cheap kids menu, which I appreciate as a parent.

name: Jessi Scott
text: Really enjoyed the experience.  Had the Elk Meatloaf and it was probably the best meatloaf I’ve ever had.  Our waiter was great, kept the beer and wine refills coming. The place has cool rustic decor.  It’s a little pricy but worth it. Everything we ordered was great. (Spinach artichoke dip, elk meatloaf and fish and chips) If you’re in Fairbanks, this place should be on your list to try.

name: Mylissa Kramer
text: Great atmosphere (lots of Alaskan decorations) and great food. Plenty of parking available and overall a nice place to take family. Good for birthdays/going aways/celebrations. Decent menu variety and Alaskan King Crab was amazing! A must go for people visiting Alaska!

name: David Maddison
text: If you just go here for the carrot cake, your life will be complete! Amazing food and super friendly service! An assuming tin shed transforms into a beautiful restaurant filled with nostalgic items when you pass through the front doors. There are so many options on the menu that you’ll struggle with choice when dining but we were not disappointed but the half dozen options we ordered. If you’re in town - just go!

name: Aaron Ludwig
text: Awesome place to go to hang out, they have a full size old school shuffle bored, and two super awesome old school pool tables that are available as well :-) a very important part of Fairbanks history as well

name: Elizabeth Pietryk
text: Food was quite disappointing. I had oversalted seafood risotto and dry meatloaf. The worst part of the meal was the stinky drinking water they poured for us. All of us at the table, even the children, agreed it tasted bad and preferred to stay thirsty.

name: G T
text:
The food was definitely delicious, and the presentation was on point. They have huge portions too.  Our server Christina was amazing today. The food may be pricey but i guarantee you, that you will not be disappointed.
Definitely worth it!!!

name: Michael Catona
text: Been a couple times and the staff is always great along with the food. Price is a little higher but it fits with the theme and is expected. The outdoor seating is great! On my last visit there got to see a plane land then take off on the river and was told it happens often there. Seating on the deck is broken up between dinner guests and walk ups. You can seat yourself on the deck and still get full service as if on the dinner side.

name: Madeline Boyd
text: Everything at The Pump House is delicious, from the starters and specials all the way to their specialty cocktails. I’m so thankful they’ve been able to stay open this year and am anxiously awaiting their weekend brunch once the pandemic is over.

name: Kaelen Chapman
text: First off our server was comedic and professional. Such a likable guy! Second the food was amazing. The lamb chops (medium rare) were super tender and cooked perfectly. The asparagus was tender yet crunchy. The elk meatloaf was moist and flavorful. And the apple pie was to die for. The apples were crisp and not over cooked, the crust had superb flavor and the ice cream was on par! Will defiantly come back.

name: Aaron Majors
text: I ordered nachos,  zucchini sticks, and beer.  The nachos, beer, and service were good.  The zucchini sticks tasted ok but looked pretty rough.  In the past they were served stacked like a log house and the presentation was good. Now they are short pieces that are slightly overcooked.

name: sari r
text: Excellent place. Superb food. Very good service. The place is decorated very special.

name: William Bruno
text: We had a very enjoyable time with drinks then supper with great friends. We have always enjoyed the atmosphere and the great service.

name: Becky DeSmet
text: Fabulous brunch. Awesome atmosphere. Excellent customer service. Full of antiques and history!

name: Clayton spann
text: Was ok. Great atmosphere ambience but food was just ok.  Raw oysters were  medium size also had clam chowder which was very thick and starchy with potatoes on the crunchy side server was very nice but food came out in shifts so wife was almost finished before I got mine

name: Paulness
text: The Pump House is a pretty decent bar/grill in Fairbanks.  The prices are are on par for Alaska (meaning it's a bit pricey), but the experience is worth the cost. It's a cool place to sit outside on the deck under the midnight sun drinking a beer.  They serve a very diverse menu, I recommend the elk meatloaf or chicken denali.  There's a good selection of beer and spirits for any palate.  If you get the chance, sit outside and enjoy the view on the Chena river.  It's awesome.  The location has historic significance related to the gold rush days, and the decor reflects it.  Our server was friendly, informative, attentive, and accommodating.  I would recommend stopping by and trying it.  It's worth the wait and the cost.

name: Pamela Cook
text: Great food, great service, and a wonderful historical site. A little pricier but definitely worth the extra money. You will not be disappointed.

name: Kayne Phillips
text: Seafood chowder was excellent, king crab was good but overcooked.

name: Deep Jariwala
text: Fantastic food and wine. Probably the best place to eat in Fairbanks. Can't rave enough how much quality the food is. The meat quality, spices, degree of cooking all great.

name: Roger Maddox
text: Awesome and abundance of food per serving. Great variety of beer, wine and other alcoholic beverages. Beautiful views and outdoor dining roght beside the river.

name: Bridget Edwards
text: Delicious food every time! The seafood risotto is my absolute favorite!!

name: Jeannie Laitinen
text: Amazing food and service.  My new favorite place to go for special occasions.

name: Fawn Silas
text: Had the seafood pasta and strawberry rhubarb crisp with vanilla ice cream. The sauce for the seafood was delicious the fettuccine noodles were a little undercooked. The strawberry rhubarb was good. The service was great!

name: Vincent D'Antonio
text: Went here for dinner and wasn't disappointed.  Read they had filet, lamb, and reindeer.  The lamb and filet were out of this world and the best dinner so far.  Cooked to perfection med rare lamb and med filet.  We had to have desert, peanut butter pie and chocolate lava cake, with coffee and tea to end the night.  With your check you can read about the dog sled sculpture hanging from the ceiling......no spoilers so you have to go to read the story.

name: Robert Nowicki
text: Wife and i made reservations for our 6 year anniversary and we had an outstanding time. The wait staff were very attentive to our needs and the food was spectacular. We will definitely be going back,

name: Ola Alhammami
text:
Nice fancy restaurant, clean and food tasted great.
I got sea food Risotto and it was so delicious 😋

name: Rhiannon Reed
text: First time, service was amazing, fast. And was even more amazing, and fast lol. It was great for my first time there :)

name: kham1211
text: Food was delicious, waitress was friendly and funny and went out of her way to make sure that we were happy with our experience.

name: Steven Smith
text: Food was good.  Place was extremely crowded, yet the service was attentive.  We were pleased :-)

name: Bonnie Wesselhoff
text: Great unique atmosphere...old time and interesting antiques. First rate service. Good variety in the menu. Service was good, but a little cool.

name: valerie reece
text: We enjoyed having our dinner in the bar. The food was great and the service was very good.

name: Ruth Dinardi
text:
Place looks good.
Service was good and attentive.
Small Sour dough bread fresh and good.
Appetizer- cheese, fresh honey and bread very good. Lack of freshness on fruits.

Dinner
Beef- mean ordered medium well (good cooked) not very tasty. Have tasted better. Brocolli was ok. Additional side with bacon (well no bacon at all seen, not a very surprised) over all points for this dish out of 10 (5pts)

Seafood Pasta Scampi- very good. TASTE ON POINT. Shrimp clean and tasty, scallops very good, Oysters well done and open. Small tomatoes well cooked and tasty. Angel pasta well done (al ˈdɛnte) lemon sauce good. Sparagus in my opinion was an unneccessary additional ingredient. Overall taste of plate out of 10 (9pts).

Desert- Every desert is done "in house". Tey bring you a big platter with the presentation and availability of each. Good strategy but they looked a little bad and old.

We took the chocolate big cupcake, medium warm, did not had much of a taste. Appeared like a big muffin but not done same day. (I can be wrong but that was kind of hart) again fruit where old, better job on this area.

name: Lynn Jackson
text: The cocktails are water down. My husband’s hot pastrami’s sandwich didn’t have enough meet. It’s a good restaurant, but I think it should be better! Dessert was yummy, I didn’t have time to take a picture!

name: Erica Stoner
text: I ordered a 6oz filet mignon medium well, when I cut into it, it was more like medium rare. Very bloody and red. The server took it back for additional cooking and the photo I'm providing with this review is the final result. Still red and somewhat bloody. It's unfortunate that I was not pleased with this meal. Nice environment though.

name: Danny Lee
text: Great dining experience! Reindeer steak was delicious, tender, and cooked just right. The creme brulee was light and delicious. Highly recommend for a special occasion for the price is at the higher, fine dining range. My wife and I will definitely be returning again.

name: Samuel Kyung jin Choi
text: Kind of pricy but good food

name: Lizbet Hernandez
text:
This place is amazing , friends took us here for our anniversary and let me tell you everything was perfect. From the drinks to their steaks, you wont be disappointed.  Friendly staff,  nice atmosphere.  Love our friends even more for bringing us here.

Have to down grade to 3 stars, or maybe 3.5. Ok so steaks are amazing but the burgers are either charred and chicken burger was so bland. My burger was supposed to be with bacon and I ate half of it (I was starving) when I realized there was no bacon. Didn't finish it. Really disappointed,  I was really hoping for a good meal on a good place after all this hectic couple of months.

name: Parobr
text: Amazing atmosphere. Great food and the best steak

name: Cara H.
text: Delicious deer steak and meatballs.  Perfect wine pairing.  I'd make a reservation before coming. We were lucky to get squeezed in.  We came at 4 not knowing they don't serve the dinner menu until 5. Bar menu didn't serve the venison steak.  We had a couple of drinks in their saloon which was manned by one person and a bartender and moved to the restaurant at 5 where we were told all the tables were booked.  If you don't make a reservation, the saloon is where you'll sit and you'll be waiting for your food for a long time.

name: Misti Dople
text: Food was good atmosphere was not. Only allowed outside seating if you were drinking. Patio seating was a nightmare no social distancing at all. Had some kind of party with 20ppl seated in the middle of the room. All the men in it buying shots and getting louder by the minute. Good waitress very sweet. We couldn't even try to talk it was so loud. And since no social distance. Idk how it's so popular

name: Carlos Danger
text: Excellent service &  food was oh so good.

name: John Pile
text: Same quality and delicious food it has always been. Great service. During Covid, all servers wearing masks. Bar and deck open. Wonderful night out.

name: Mike and Nancy Riley
text: The food was too expensive for whst you received. Cost $80 for 3 beers, chicken and broccoli fettuccine, a chicken breast with a portabello mushroom gravy, and 2 cups of soup. You are paying extra to for the building because it is in the National Register of Historic places. The food was good just over priced.

name: Julia Haynie
text: Delicious food, good drinks and a huge variety of generously portioned food! Brunch is great and so is dinner. Favorite appetizer is the fried zucchini!

name: bethany rosendahl
text: Everything was amazing ! One of my favorite places to eat in Fairbanks

name: bleesdo
text: Excellent evening.  Fast friendly service.Good beer,wine, scotch and whiskey menu. Amazing seafood chowder. Seafood pasta, blackened halibut and grilled halibut were top 5. Right on the river with plenty of room.  Great atmosphere and a lot of original antiques from the gold rush days. Plenty of parking.  Nice experience.

name: Clifton Souvenir
text: Great environment with great food.

name: Chris Betts
text: Looks like the place to be in Fairbanks. Great food great atmosphere and fantastic service.

name: Rod P
text: Wonderful dining experience of grilled salmon and wife had New York steak.  Enjoyed the time on the deck overlooking the Chena River.

name: Tena Storgaard
text: Great place to eat in Fairbanks.   Right on the river.  Food was excellent.  The elk meatloaf was excellent and I had the salmon which was also delicious.

name: Carol Ann
text: Pretty good food & nice views. Service was a little slow & could never get a drink refill.

name: melisa kelsey
text: Family celebration was amazing 😃service was fantastic, food outstanding. Thank you for serving our community so well for so long

name: Candy Fortner
text: Amazing birthday dinner with family. Thank you server Sara for an awesome experience.  I will be back.

name: Vasin mohcharoen
text: Awesome!! Good place great service 👍

name: Doug Urwiller
text:
Great food! Great service!
Overall Great place!

name: Keith Kinder
text: One of the two best meals we had in our 2 weeks in Alaska great food, great service, the waiter was very proper. The building very well restored.

name: DAWN CURTIS
text:
Seafood risotto and blackened halibut!.
Yummy

name: Lucinda Brinks
text: Great selection of seafood.  I had a Crab Cobb Salad.  Alex the waiter was awesome.  There is an outdoor patio overlooking the river too.

name: Into DaWild
text: Very nice place to eat and relax. Good service and excellent staff.

name: Matthew Denakis
text:
A local tourism spot. But the tourism and attraction, doesn't affect how good the food is.
Service was admirable. And the food was fast and good.
A decent beer selection, and a nice atmosphere. Highly recommend getting a reservation on the busier days, just to be safe.

name: Kitsana Dounglomchan
text:
My absolute favorite place to eat in Fairbanks. In the summertime they have lovely outdoor seating seating right on the Chena River. I’ve gone her 6-7 times for dinner and once for brunch and I’ve never been disappointed with the food or service. I’d actually recommend making a reservation because this place always seems to be busy and can fill up.

Bottom line: if you were in Fairbanks one night and wanted a place to eat that would give you a high quality experience of Alaskan cuisine I’d tell you go to the Pumphouse.

name: Jose Carrasco
text: The food was delicious. They have a great view to see the river and the ships in it.

name: Sharon Yatlin
text: Good food, thank you.  River did a really good job.

name: Ed Rogerville
text: Nice atmosphere and good food!

name: Eva Hansen
text: Always great food

name: Shane Johnson
text: Food was good. Staff was friendly. My meat was cold in the center and they quickly took it away and brought me a new plate that was perfect.

name: Mathew Generally
text: Great staff Great food

name: Dan C
text: Hands down the best place to eat in Fairbanks that isn't Thai food.

text: The food is always amazing.

text: Great food and service.

name: Andrew McKay
text: Everyone loved there food although it took a while to get

name: Tell Burger
text: Great food and service. Bartender (Laura) makes really great Mocktails!

name: William Rowland
text: Got the duck, it was amazing. Almost everything I've ever gotten here has been amazing. Server was friendly and checked on us often. Great experience.

name: R P
text: Very nice experience. Alex was a great waitress. Food was really good. Bread was fantastic!! Good beer selection.

name: Tell Burger
text: Great food and service. Bartender (Laura) makes really great Mocktails!

name: Christina Ried
text: We really enjoyed a kid free Sunday and decided to indulge and go to Sunday brunch! We were not disappointed! So many delicious options and high end choices. Great hot entrees, nice cold spread of fruit,cheese, shrimp and smoked salmon, great desserts and 2 mimosas included. If it were a little cheaper, we'd probably go more often, but great for a special occasion.

name: William Rowland
text: Got the duck, it was amazing. Almost everything I've ever gotten here has been amazing. Server was friendly and checked on us often. Great experience.

name: Y G
text: It is considered "fancy" in Fairbanks but it's really not fancy. Food is okay. Desserts were good!

name: ChengYang Chen
text: Nice seating, sea plane and pedal steamer cruise

name: native ridge
text: Extremely well prepared meals and if you look at the desserts on offer you will likely not turn them down. 5 states plus, great night had with friends. Highly recommend

name: Catherine Hatcher
text: Good food, energetic service, nice atmosphere.

name: Mickey Knipp
text: Sea food chowder makes the trip worth it

name: Michael Vandeventer
text:
Very good food and service this time. Came with large group and they took care of us fairly quickly.  Have been here a few years ago for a work related Christmas party and it was not as good as this time.
Cater to a young crowd so be prepared. Fantastic old wood decor. When paddlewheel boat goes by, they both blow whistles at each other. Kind of cool!

name: Xiang Cui
text: Certainly a fine place for dining choice in the area. We ordered the cod and the deer meat, both are good choices. The waitress was super warm and enthusiastic. Also loved the decor with a feel of local culture.

name: Sheri Schoenberg
text: The food was tasty.  Atmosphere congenial.  Staff needs a bit more trading to polish their skills

name: Renee Tatusko
text: First time here, even though I've been to Fairbanks on multiple occasions.  I was there for a group dinner, and the food and service was excellent.  I will be back!

name: Dmitry Berezhnoy
text: Well worth the wait. Make a reservation or get on the wait list ahead of time. Wild Alaskan salmon and King crab were great. Choosing a dessert was a fun show.

name: jammie duvall
text:
The buffet was on the expensive side with not a lot of options. Some of the food was hard and seemed like it had been there a while. We spent over $90 for 3 people.

The lunch menu is a different story. We really enjoyed the lasagna and the burgers. Would give it a 5/5.

name: Liz Langley
text: Jenna was our server and she was fantastic.  The food was great as well, we had a variety of items from the menu.  Definitely will go there again, and will ask for same server.

name: Alizza Ramirez
text: It was all great. Great food , comfortable setting , family friendly, food came out really fast my husband and I were surprised, the waitress super kind and was always coming to check if everything was fine and was on top on filling the drinks before they were empty

name: Dmitry Berezhnoy
text: Well worth the wait. Make a reservation or get on the wait list ahead of time. Wild Alaskan salmon and King crab were great. Choosing a dessert was a fun show.

name: Mickey Knipp
text: Sea food chowder makes the trip worth it

name: Bobbie Ann Hunter
text: When I walked in it was so busy and looked clean and I wished I could eat there.

name: Renee Tatusko
text: First time here, even though I've been to Fairbanks on multiple occasions.  I was there for a group dinner, and the food and service was excellent.  I will be back!

name: Alexis Fay
text: This is one of my favorite places to eat in Fairbanks. They have the best brunch in town and also great for dinner. There are many seating options such as spectacular outdoor seating on the water, indoor seating with a water view, the bar area is very fun and they also have regular tables indoors and even private rooms for special gatherings. Good for large groups or more intimate options for couples. I’ve been here with extended family, on date night and with a large group of girls they for brunch. All great experiences. The brunch buffet is sooooo good (I’m typing this at night but my mouth started watering when I was typing about brunch) the dinner entrees are also great. Brunch comes with a bloody Mary’s or mimosas.

name: Elisa Mao
text: Must go, decoration and food are good

name: Brook
text: Sunday brunch. The food was delicious! Great variety: breakfast-- waffles, eggs and potatoes, lunch-- salmon and kippers, crab salad, shrimp. Something for everyone, all super yummy

name: Matthew Muir
text: Double duck meal was very good. The risotto that came with it was excellent. Ribs were also a hit. Service was nice and energetic. We got there early with a little kid, and it was good.

name: Sullivan Sedgley
text: Very good food, but a tad expensive. My waiter was extremely polite and professional.

name: Some Guy
text: Super experience. Delicious gourmet level food. Beautiful, riverside setting. Enclosed patio makes eating outside very enjoyable.

name: Justin shults
text: Had great drinks, amazing food, and great ambiance.  Our original waitress was not that good, however the waitress we had for the end of dinner and dessert was amazing and definitely made up for the experience.

name: Sky Light
text: Very friendly staff and excellent service and hot and fresh great cooked dishes and meals

name: Carlos Anciany
text: the bar does not live up to the restaurant, though the staff is as caring a polite.

name: James Wells
text: This is a hit or miss place.  Sometimes it is delicious other times it is just OK.  The atmosphere is also hit or miss.  Sometimes I get great seating with great service and other times it is uncomfortable.

name: Kyla Phillips
text: We saw this restaurant recommended on a list of where to eat and we quickly discovered why. The food was very high quality and delicious.  Their tartar sauce had a unique flavor that I wish I knew how to replicate. Sooo yummy! The only thing we felt was lacking was the bread.

name: HEY SCRIBBLES
text: Only tried bar menu and Sunday brunch. Both experiences are excellent, exceptional, and well worth the price for both the food and service. The environment is a relaxing "at home" feeling. When you eat here, you are surrounded by Fairbanks' rich mining and river transport history. If you are visiting or even a local, the Pump House is a place you must visit.

name: Elizabeth Pruitt
text: Okay service.Beatifully resting right next to the water. Their fries are super good. We went during dinner time and they brought us a bar menu but maybe because we were sitting outside? When the noticed the kid we had with us they brought her a kids menu and that was nice. Overall food quality is okay. Definitely nice that are against the river.

name: James Wells
text: This is a hit or miss place.  Sometimes it is delicious other times it is just OK.  The atmosphere is also hit or miss.  Sometimes I get great seating with great service and other times it is uncomfortable.

name: Julianne Oates
text:
TLDR: Not sure if it was worth the cost, but the scenes were nice. Staff was nice but maybe understaffed.

This is the first time I have been here in about 10 years. The staff was really great and they were quick to get answers about nuts in different dishes as we have nut allergies in our family. It would be helpful if the signage had allergens listed. We came in at 1pm and it was very busy and there was a few mins where they did not have plates for the buffet and a few items were not refilled. They did get everything back up but it seemed they may have been understaffed for how many people were there. Also, the bathroom was not as clean as I would have expected.  It was fun to see the river and the grounds are very pretty. I'd recommend once. Not sure if we will return.

name: Darwyn Klatt
text: The seafood was risotto was quite good. I wish the proportion of seafood to rice was a bit better for the price, though. Plenty of craft beers available, as well.

name: Darwyn Klatt
text: The seafood was risotto was quite good. I wish the proportion of seafood to rice was a bit better for the price, though. Plenty of craft beers available, as well.

name: Laurie Rockstad
text: Fantastic food, great atmosphere... A favorite of locals!

name: Danny Cartes
text: They wouldn't serve me and my kids dinner

name: Morgan Smith
text: Excellent brunch that includes mimosas. Salad bar, hot bar, and dessert bars. It’s too cold now, but the porch looks like an amazing place for dinner during the summer.

name: Jason Brown
text: Ok, so if you dont mind eating in full snow gear. This is the place for you. December 20th anniversary dinner with my wife. We arrived at 1700 and was seated right away. 1st thing we realized was it was approx 50° in this restaurant and we decided to eat with our coats on. Along with many other guest. Recieved the bread basket, cheap store bought bread with butter packets. Couldn't even splurge on a dish for butter or maybe warm the bread up to above room temp. Food was decent, wouldn't say 5 or even 4 star. Overall it was an  alright experience. Expected a bit more by some of the reviews. It will be a while before this local goes back..... maybe summer.

name: Koby Despard
text: Fantastic atmoshere and service.

name: Maureen MacDonald
text: Best restaurant in town! Amazing food, good cocktails and great views!

name: Leigh Eberhart
text: A great historic restaurant a little upscale for Fairbanks. The service is excellent and the food and drinks are always great. They have lots of Alaskan dishes on the menu and most desserts are made in house. They have a great bar, good drinks and a good bar menu. The view of the River in the summer is always wonderful, bonus points if you can time it so you can watch the river boat cruise past!

name: Y G
text: It is considered "fancy" in Fairbanks but it's really not fancy. Food is okay. Desserts were good!

name: Samantha Warner
text: Amazing. Great food. Great service. Great dessert. Great everything.

name: tiffany sampsel
text: Our food was delicious and the server was excellent on the bar side however,  the hostess wasn't very friendly. We had reserved a table for 8:45 & when we got there the host greeted us with we close the dining room in 15 minutes,  do you want to stay. text: I feel bad to be critical but when it comes to seafood there is a fine line between perfect and overdone. I reluctantly ordered the grilled Halibut but tried asking for the fish to be pan seared because I feel grilling is too hot and would impart a strong flavor in the delicate fish but was told no. It took 50 min for our appetizers to be delivered so they sent an extra coconut shrimp to our table. Let me say the iced tea, seafood chowder and coconut shrimp were excellent but that's where it ends. The Halibut was inedible and splintered when I cut into it with my fork. The only thing I could taste was the grill and becsuse it was so overcooked they ruined a great fish dinner. My plate arrived very sloppily put together and I was unable to eat any of it. My daughter ordered the duck but it was too undertone for my taste. I had high hopes of having great Salmon, King crab and Halibut on my trip after all Alaskans should be the best at preparing an abundantly available product but I was sadly mistaken. I ordered Halibut 5 tines and not 1 time was it prepared correctly. My daughter informed me there are the lower 48 standards and there are Alaska standards, I guess my standards are just too high because not 1 meal was excellent during my entire trip.

name: Rob Pare
text:
We arrived and were told it would be a 2 hr wait. But the 'bar menu' seating was available. We found a place to sit right away. That's about the only thing that went well...
We got some water. It looked brown and tasted like it had dirt in it. I decided to just not drink much. Every drink was worse than the last. We ordered. We waited. And waited. And waited some more. Finally after nearly 45 minutes, we asked where our food was. The server said she'd check. About 8 minutes later she emerged from the back with our meal, along with another party's.
I tried a fry. It was cold. My wife's sandwich was cold. It looked like the plates had been sitting around for 15 minutes waiting to be served. We waved down our server, told her about the food. All she said was 'sorry.' Never offered to remake the meal.
We left without eating or paying. Spoke to the manager who said the same thing as the server. As we were leaving, another patron had similar issues. We will never return.

name: Danny Lee
text:
FOR TIRES INSTALLATION.

TLDR: I recommend American Tire & Co for tires over Costco. If you have a Costco Tire appointment, plan for a wait for at least 2 hours, if not longer.

Made an appointment for winter tires, special order because they weren't in stock in the store. Made an appointment for 5PM, was out of the store by 840 PM. Even if you make an appointment, plan for at least a 2 hour wait if not longer. There was a group of us in similar situations, all waiting for our tires to be put on. On a positive note, met some friendly people while waiting.

Fast forward a day after. Had a flat while going to work, the  valve stem was defective and leaking air, causing the flat. Had to put spare on, no problem. Drove to Costco at 10AM sharp, guy told me 45min ETA. No problem. Hour of shopping later, they told me it will be 15 minutes until they pull in my car and start working on it, because I was a walk in.

If you want tires, Costco is an option, but I recommend going to American Tire & Auto, which I have done before with no problems. I only went to Costco because I was going to move stateside eventually, so I thought why not. I'm giving 3 stars just because of Emmit, good guy, very helpful.

text:
I love this place! When the other membership warehouse closed, I was sad since we had nothing like it closer than 360 miles. Then Costco announced they would take over the old building. Could I hear the sound of Angels' rejoicing? After watching them remodel the store for several months, I was excited to finally shop in the new store. The doors opened, I purchased a membership, and I was off to the races. Literally (not sure what that word means) skipping down the aisles while throwing rose petals, I was in heaven! With all the happy people looking around in wonder, I knew the opening was worth the wait.
I have been shopping here almost a year now, and I still love it. The associates are always so helpful. The store consistently has what I am looking for. Even when the parking lot is full, the store feels open and inviting. Prices, Wow, everything feels like such a great deal, and then they have regular sales, so much value! My goodness, I almost forgot, free samples, need I say more, why yes I do. They always have free samples, and my daughter and l look forward to wandering from booth to  booth sampling the goods. I love this place! When the other membership warehouse closed, I was sad since we had nothing like it closer than 360 miles. Then Costco announced they would take over the old building. Could I hear the sound of Angels' rejoicing? After watching them remodel the store for several months, I was excited to finally shop in the new store. The doors opened, I purchased a membership, and I was off to the races. Literally (not sure what that word means) skipping down the aisles while throwing rose petals, I was in heaven! With all the happy people looking around in wonder, I knew the opening was worth the wait.
I have been shopping here almost a year now, and I still love it. The associates are always so helpful. The store consistently has what I am looking for. Even when the parking lot is full, the store feels open and inviting. Prices, Wow, everything feels like such a great deal, and then they have regular sales, so much value! My goodness, I almost forgot, free samples, need I say more, why yes I do. They always have free samples, and my daughter and l look forward to wandering from booth to  booth sampling the goods. What fun! Compared to the previous membership warehouse, Costco is a shopping dream. I will continue purchasing the yearly membership, as long as Costco keeps their doors open. Was very excited to join when they opened but have been disappointed. Here is why...the products are always changing. I don’t like to go here everyday so I usually go to do a big “haul” and I meal plan appropriately. But when I get there, something I previously purchased is no longer there without a viable substitutes. Also, unlike sams, you can’t check online to see if something is in stock. So a lot of wasted trips. I don’t feel like we save much, of anything shopping here. The only real bargain is the rotisserie chicken and food court items. I also do love the frozen stir fry veggies that I can’t find anywhere else. But the few pros don’t outweigh the cons in my opinion.

Edit to change from two stars to one. This place is always a blood bath no matter what time you go. The people that answer the phone always seem inconvenienced that you are calling them. Save your time and money and do free Walmart grocery pickup.

The only reason I didn't give five stars is that someone urinated on the floor and it smelled bad when I had to go to bathroom. It had that old smell so I suspect it was one of those "it's not my job to clean it up" scenarios. The food was good and hot.

Weird thing that it came out in two servings. The pancakes came out about five minutes after the meat and home fries. Anyway I'd rather get it hot than together.

name: Fishhooks
text:
Ever eat a spoon full of salt - you will here!

Don't believe me or know what I mean?  Go to this place and order the spaghetti and meatballs for $15.99 then sit back and get your $15.99 education.  They'll serve you literally .25 cents worth of spaghetti with a pile of sauce made up of 3 tablespoons of salt, a 6 oz can of tomato paste, and 6 ounces of ketchup.  I'll bet my life the cook is a lifetime Camel unfiltered cigarette chain smoker who hasn't been able to taste anything for the past 30 years.  However, I gave it one star because it's not as bad as the absolute most disgusting food I've ever paid for in my life.  That title goes to the Denny's located at 1 Center Dr, North East MD 21901, at a Flying J truck stop.  ALL of the food literally tasted like you were eating pure salt.  From the fried chicken, to meatloaf, to mashed potatoes, to the banana pudding and they don't serve sweet tea!  This place is so disgusting, I've told people to stop by and see how awful it is.  Here in Fairbanks, I just tell everyone to stay away from Denny's and you're better off eating food from the dumpster behind China King.

text: --1 Star really.   We were seated, sat for 20 minutes with no service,  called for a waiter, when he was done checking on the table across from us. He came over, after be summoned,  and took our order. 35 minutes later no food, no update on how much longer. We saw people come in after we were seated, they  ordered,  got their food and then leave . There were 5 tables thay needed to be bused for dirty dishes,  but it was like the staff didn't know how to operate a small restaurant. Poor, poor, Management,  & training of employees. It was a Friday night, April 19, 2019, after a community event at the Carlson Center,  and we decided to stop in, but left disappointed and hungry. Denny's needs to train the Management better, so they can manage the staff better.....poor business practices.

name: Lee Petersen
text:
*I had to go back and re-rate and edit an old review because of the terrible service I recently received here. I will never shop here again after my latest experience. The bottom line is, terrible customer service (never even received a "thank you" or "sorry for this inconvenience" for my issue), most employees don't know anything about the products they sell, I interacted with 3 employees that were unwilling and unable to help, or even willing to try to understand my problem.

I spent $1200 on a snowblower that had a defective part. It took over 3 hours combined between my wife and I to get the situation resolved. I was dumbfounded at the basic lack of customer service or even basic politeness. The way the situation was handled even furthered our inconvenience, as it was clear no one at Lowes wanted to do any "work" to help resolve the issue.

Here's my original review from about a year ago (3 stars): It was so difficult to get help that I put back the things I already had in hand and went to Home Depot. I understand that customer service in big stores like this are always changing, but I was absolutely ignored by employees that were just chatting with each other. It will probably be a while before I give them a shot again. I only give 3 stars based on other more neutral experiences I've had here in the past.

text: Beautiful atmosphere: cozy, warm and lovely lighting. The service was nice, it was slower when we first arrived and we had 2 servers helping us; as it got busier it was harder to get drinks, etc. When we first arrived we had soup and warm towels brought to us - a nice way to fight off the chilly weather. The sushi was amazing! I got the Kani Crab Nigiri and my wife and I split the Mt. McKinley roll (so good, a little spicy) and a Las Vegas roll. We had food leftover! My only real complaints are that there wasn't a ginger salad on the menu (we ordered one our server said was similar but it wasn't) and that it took awhile for the server to bring some much needed water after that wonderfully spicy Mt McKinley roll 😂 Otherthan thise tiny things it was perfect!

text: It's not bad, considering that they are trying to serve raw fish that are not native to Alaska. Most everything seems to have a recently-defrosted taste and texture and the seaweed salad was far from palatable, BUT the presentation was very nice and the sushi was well made. The staff was very friendly and attentive and the interior decor was pleasant. The miso soup was strangely creamy but decent. But still, they probably should not be serving sushi in the Alaskan interior.. 😂 If you have never had good sushi, you will be blissfully ignorant here.

(Translated by Google) It is the worst Japanese restaurant. I ordered the sashimi platter and stone-roasted bibimbap, but the bibimbap tasted weird with no garnish, and the sashimi was all melted. The water was sloppy, and the taste was worst, and the mackerel marinated in vinegar (89 cents per pack in LA). Besides, the rice was like rice cake, and the miso soup tasted very strange. After paying $ 62 without a tip, it felt like I was being robbed, and I was very uncomfortable for a long time because I ate fresh sashimi. It is a strong light. The 4.5 star rating in this restaurant seems to have been given by people who have no taste of Japanese food. I regretted the visit. It is a strong light.

name: John Pearson
text: Super clean inside, friendly owner, quality work, what more can you want.

name: DAVID PEASE
text: Great experience for all. Very friendly staff who really knows and cares about the animals there. They have very interesting information about all various animals that visit the area from seals to whales and salmon to sea otters.

name: Tyler Reid
text: I can't say enough on how awesome this place is. If you've never been go! Right now during covid they have sanitizer everywhere and require a mask 😷. The staff is super friendly and are knowledgeable about sealife. The exhibits are amazing if you want to see alot of alaskan ocean animals (which is why everyone comes here) check this out. The sealing are massive and you can even pay to feed the animals. Go with the family or a friend...heck go alone and learn something new about sealife! 👍👍👍👌👋

name: Justin Allison
text: Always a great time! I drive the kids down to check it out at least once a year. The sea bird exhibit is my favorite!

name: Vicki Vinzant
text: Love bringing the grandkids here! It is always fun and interesting!! Seeing the kids smile and be excited is pure joy!!

name: Matt Green
text: Very cool place. The tour is self guided.  There are no otters or very large animals but there are seals and sea lions, lots of fish and birds.

name: Cindy Main
text: Amazing place to go and learn all about the Sealife of Alaskan critters.

name: Evelyn Posala
text: We took our kids during spring break and they enjoyed it! Although everyone was required to wear mask, they allowed our son (who is autistic) to go through without one. He just had to wear a sticker to inform the employees of his disability. He doesn’t understand and doesn’t keep it on as he hates anything on his face. Thank you for the memories and understanding our situation with our son!!

name: David Daniel
text: Good sealife center. Was an all around solid experience. I would recommend it to any visitor to Seward.

name: Mari Rueter
text: This was my first visit and I absolutely love it! You can tell they really care about the animals in their care and do a great job educating the public about how to protect wildlife and the ocean. I hope they are able to stay open because we need places like this!

name: Baby baby
text: It was fun but I was expecting more but I was pleased to say the least

name: Stephen Wood
text: Great time for the kids and adults alike. The animals were very active. I would say the only thing missing is a polar bear

name: Danielle and Bill
text: They do such wonderful things here to rescue, rehabilitate & release injured mammals, sea birds, etc. Its a great place to learn so much about the local wildlife and so close up.  My favorite part is the touch tank. With the pandemic they need extra support, if you can donate they be SO appreciative.

name: Michael Jenks
text:
During COVID, they're pretty good. You get a 2 hour window for your "group" and it's fairly easy. Not a lot of crowds, but the sea life is all there. It was a pleasant visit. Even picked up a new jacket on sale :)
They have directional arrows to let you know the flow of traffic. It was probably my 5th time there and would go again. Just fun to see and our son loved it.

name: Gabriel Gross
text: We loved this stop. We went mainly for the puffin but enjoyed every display. The prices are a bit steep, but we expected that and didn't have a problems paying it. Staff were all happy and excited about what they do. Establishment was clean and easy to see every display.

name: Jody Bauer
text: This place reminds me of why I enjoy living in Alaska! Visitors to the area get an opportunity to experience a wonderfully summarized version of what keeps us immersed in our surroundings year round. We've been bringing our kids here several times a year since they were babies, as teenagers they still enjoy every single visit!

name: Amanda Hamell
text: Great visit in the winter. Pretty quiet. Doing good with covid precautions. Kids loved Wrangell the Octopus.

name: Elizabeth Angasan
text: Great place to bring kids!! Our toddlers, kindergartener and teen all enjoyed themselves! Granted, this place isn't as grandiose as other aquariums out of state, however, it's worth adding to your Seward bucket list! They also have a nice gift shop.

name: John Pile
text: Love this place. Well run and great opportunity to see Alaskan sealife.

name: Seen So
text:
Road to Seward from Anchorage wasn’t as bad as we thought. The sea life center has hand sanitizer stations at every exhibit and masks are required for entry. There is also a one-way flow that customers need to follow. Interactive exhibits have been shut down but the tide pool is still up.

IG: @icseen

name: GraysonGoesGlobal
text: A lovely experience, as always! Great place for family’s and couples, and coming alone is just as fun. Staff are friendly and helpful, the building itself is clean and organized. Parking and camp grounds are nearby for RVs, which comes in handy when needed. Many exhibits are interactive which is great for children, and adults :) Over an amazing destination for anyone visiting Seward!

name: Michael Buck
text: The Alaska SeaLife Center is a pretty awesome place to visit. They have a bunch of exhibits that is set up more of an educational place rather than a zoo or park. The facility seemed to be very well taken care of and the animal habitats were all pretty clean. It's enjoyable for all ages. A must-stop when visiting Seward.

name: Kymberly Coffey
text: Even in this pandemic... Was a wonderful... ✌ visit & much needed... Thanks to all of the staff

name: Iris Fletcher
text: Such a wonderful aquarium to visit and learn about all the cool marine life, especially knowing it's supporting the only marine mammal rescue/rehabilitation/release operation in Alaska! I love to bring all my friends and family that visit Alaska, and they're doing a great job of being COVID conscientious!

name: Lee Anne Roquemore
text:
Excellent visit. We went in September and between COVID, the reduced seasonal tourism and the scheduled appointment times, it wasn't crowded. I took my 9 year old daughter and we had a BLAST. We could've watched the seals and sea lions all day.

Super short walk to Zudy's Cafe for a 5 star lunch, and we were able to easily re-enter to continue our visit. Super cool touch tanks, and a lovely gift shop. Highly recommend.

name: George
text: It was a really cool place, highly recommended visiting. Really informative and had some really cool animals there. The gift shop was quite nice and showcased tons of art for sale.

name: Cathy Knappen
text: Great place to take your family!! Great place to learn about sea life! You should definitely go there and support their efforts to educate the public, and care for the marine life. 😊😊

name: Barry Kwan
text:
If it's in Anchorage, I would had bring my kid there every week or every other week.
Awesome place for kids.

name: Lizzie Pinder
text: My boyfriend and I make an annual Alaska SeaLife Center trip and we love it. Just remember, if you want to do an encounter (especially the octopus) schedule it ahead of time because spots fill up fast.

name: Scott Langley
text: Always a great place to take visitors. The wildlife is amazing.

name: K.
text: Kids love it . Save it for a rainy day

name: ReBecca
text:
We really enjoyed our visit. We spent about 2 hours walking around looking at everything. The puffin exhibit is neat because they're so close.
I was a little disappointed that the otter interaction was just watching through a fence and window and a speech about the animal🤷🏻‍♀️ my daughter thought by the photos that promote this that she would be able to feed one. Even just tossing a fish would have been something. While I understand why not, it is just a little misleading.

name: Aaron Menshouse
text: Must see on your visit. This facility does a lot of great conservation work. Fun for all ages.

name: David Buel
text: This place is wonderful. We visited in February and had a blast. They had sea lions (huge), seals, beluga whale, sea otter, several different birds, fish and crab. Really cool touch tank my son (5yr) was glued to.

name: Iris Fletcher
text: Such a wonderful aquarium to visit and learn about all the cool marine life, especially knowing it's supporting the only marine mammal rescue/rehabilitation/release operation in Alaska! I love to bring all my friends and family that visit Alaska, and they're doing a great job of being COVID conscientious!

name: Jack
text: Awesome place to take the kids and learn about ocean life!!

name: Lee Anne Roquemore
text:
Excellent visit. We went in September and between COVID, the reduced seasonal tourism and the scheduled appointment times, it wasn't crowded. I took my 9 year old daughter and we had a BLAST. We could've watched the seals and sea lions all day.

Super short walk to Zudy's Cafe for a 5 star lunch, and we were able to easily re-enter to continue our visit. Super cool touch tanks, and a lovely gift shop. Highly recommend.

name: Bailey Kirkland
text: I absolutely love this place. Great memories from high school trips when we visited for the Tsunami Bowl days, was glad to show my husband this wonderful center.

name: doug richards
text: Very informative you are able to view many aquatic birds and animals you don't normally get close to.

name: Andrew Fry
text: This place was much more educational than I thought it would be. The kids loved it. The baby walrus was so cute. Keep up the good work

name: Chris Betts
text: A must see in Seward. Great place for conservation efforts and education on local wildlife and allows you to get up close and personal with some very friendly puffins.

name: Drew Litwack
text: So much fun. My son and girlfriend loved it also. Please support this amazing place. Lots to learn and be amazed by looking at.

name: patricia wells
text: I admire the work that they do here they saved many marine animals it's fun to go and see all their displays great for kids and adults We joined in their membership program

name: Elizabeth Maxson
text: Lots of fun for little kids and older ones. Lots to see and do and plenty of activities throughout the day. Also local eateries within walking distance and other activities to spend the day in Seward. I didn't give it 5 stars because there wasn't much of a variety compared to other marine centers.

name: Athina Tennant
text: We absolutely LOVE our trips to the SeaLife Center! As a homeschooling Mom, I love that the winter hours include Alaskan residents get free entrance on Wednesday! A beautiful drive from Anchorage or the Valley and some great marine science my kids love being able to interact with the staff.

name: doris hernandez
text: Everything was clean the employees took great care to make sure social distance was observed  but not taking away from the experience.

name: Ethel Reed
text: It's a wonderful place to take Children, Young tweens, tourists,even locals at times would enjoy the sea life information. The various kinds of to do, touch, to see, interact with, indoor as well as outdoor activities is extremely well created and thought out, price wise is a bit steep, should be brought down, if you want to bring more people to the center.

name: Kevin Solloway
text: A must see if you're spending time in Seward. All the animals and displays were amazing.

name: Loren Breshears
text: We had a wonderful time! The staff was top notch! They were engaging and very informative

name: Erik Ottosen
text: A wonderful aquarium and research facility, well worth going out of your way for, and worth the $30 even with some stuff down due to COVID-19.

name: Liz Cullivan
text:
My father was visiting from out of town and we decided to take him to Seward for the day. Even during the slower seasons of Seward the Sea Life center was an enjoyable stop. My favorite attractions was the underwater viewing sections. We got to see puffins swimming under water! It was also amazing to really grasp how big the sea lions are when viewing them practically a glass panels distance from you! It also makes for some cool photos too.

I highly recommended this as a place to visit year round and for all ages. Exhibits were very kid friendly. There is a touch tank too!

name: Intuitive Truth 33
text: Great place to visit with kids and family!

name: Pamela Tapert
text: Learned some great stuff, love the puffin

name: Norman Tweet
text: If you're passing through Seward as a tourist, this is definitely the top attraction in town. The exhibits are instructive and fun to browse through. The admission fee is rather high (especially if you're not an Alaskan resident) but I would still highly recommend a visit if you've got some time to burn.

name: Tanya Aanrud
text: Such an amazing and informative experience.

name: Philippe Jeanty
text: Very interesting museum with clear exhibits and nice aquarium. Well worth the visit

name: Andrew Fry
text: This place was much more educational than I thought it would be. The kids loved it. The baby walrus was so cute. Keep up the good work

name: Benjamin Elizalde
text: Is it worth it? Well, if you have kids or love wild life, maybe yes. Is it still worth going if not? Yes, cuz you are supporting vets, scientist, and animals to have a better life.

name: Jess Pooley
text: Had an amazing time and can't wait to go back this summer.

name: Bruno Couto
text: Great place to spend some time and observe Alaskan sealife. Not too big compared to aquariums, but serves a good purpose and rehabs lots of injured critters, so you know your money is going to a good cause. Great staff that are happy to help answer any questions you may have and are very knowledgeable.

name: doug richards
text: Very informative you are able to view many aquatic birds and animals you don't normally get close to.

name: Keith Black
text: Outstanding what they are doing in research and rehab of sealife.  Exhibits I've never seen before and I'm 55

name: Robert Bredlie
text: Fun place to visit. Informative staff.

name: Noah Johnson
text: Excellent for the kiddos. Everyone really enjoyed the puffin exhibit! It doesn't hurt that it's located in a beautiful part of Alaska!

name: Stephanie Illguth
text: Not really worth the high cost of taking your family.  I felt they needed more exhibits and more interactive stations. Covid has shut down what little they had also.  The employees were all super friendly though.

name: Dave Chiu
text: Great sealife center. They have very friendly staff and lots of education. They do rehab on animals and had a baby sea otter at the time and show how they take of it. Great bird exhibit too that you can walk in with puffins and other swimming birds which you can view below water level as well.

name: LeAnn Wall
text: Honestly, this place is fantastic! Had a hard time leaving lol we wanted to stay outside with the ducks and birds all day lol very well put together and covid friendly! They had a cute path to follow allowing you to see everything on the way! Clean and the bathrooms were immaculate!! Must see if you go to Sewerd!

name: Nicole Nutt
text: We had a really great time at their FREEzing winter Wednesday. Our daughter had a wonderful time getting to see all of the different exhibits. She got to feel starfish in the touch tanks and there was a great play area with a boat that kids can run around in. The sealife center is right next to the ocean with wonderful views of the mountains. We enjoyed seeing the seal and sea lion, and it was a wonderful educational experience. I would recommend this for family's of all ages, and if you are residents you can get in free with ID on Wednesday during the winter.

name: Ryan Stafford
text:
If you're looking for an aquarium then the Alaska SeaLife Center is your next stop in Alaska.

You'll find plenty of parking and food in the area including areas to sit in the sun and relax.

If you look at everything here then you'll need an hour, but if you interact with the exhibits then you'll need up to two hours.  The people here are very friendly to not only visitors, but also residents of Alaska.  If you're a teacher then you can get a discount on your ticket.

The birds are may favorite exhibit because you can nearly touch them and they sound interesting too.

name: Paul Marshalek
text: The Sea Life Center was a great afternoon visit. For such a small town of Seward, the Center has exceptional access to sea life due to it's proximity of some of the most active sea life on this planet.  The staff was very helpful.

name: James Beck
text: A must visit, great opportunity for closeups of puffins, sea lions and many more

name: Racahael Lowe
text: Nice little aquatic center (for its area) a little pricey for what you get. But not much else to do in the area

name: Damon Landreau
text: Nice aquarium.  If you are in Seward, go see it.  The kids loved it.  Very friendly staff.  Excellent display of AK sealife.

name: Jason Hotch
text: Though smaller than many aquarium/sea life centers, it is set up really well, presented great and worth the trip!

name: Sarah Greenwood
text: Such a wonderful place, in a beautiful location. Very well maintained, and all the critters are loved and happy. Will be back for sure!

name: Colin Whalen
text: High quality aquarium for educating and diverting the family for the day. The views of the mountains are also quite nice.

name: Ryan Newton
text: A must when visiting Seward! Nice gift shop as well. The kids love it! 😍

name: Charles Campbell
text: Neat education center. Great for kids and adults. Excellent rainy day activity.

name: Ryan Griffiths
text: Great place. Lots of learning. Go see for yourself.

name: Janice Amos
text: So amazing. My friend and I all 24 year olds and older extremely enjoyed the Alaska Sea life center. The bird viewing area is a must see. The best part about the SeaLife center was that all of the exhibits you could see above water on the 2nd floor and below the water on the first floor. Another great part is that you can come and go all day. Definitely worth going to see.

name: Dawn Maeda
text: Such important work these individuals do here. Glad to come and support their cause. I adore sealife!

name: Chris Terry
text: An amazing place to see Alaska's sealife up close. And they are amazing at taking care of injured animals.

name: Matt Cope
text: Awesome sea life center! Great place to visit.

name: Amanda Smet
text: My kids love this place but I think I love it more! Reasonably priced and the hands on tanks were amazing!

name: Karen Best
text: I first visited did this place 17 years ago. It's still amazing with displays and research facilities. A great Hands-On place to learn about ocean sea. It has great educational opportunities both at the facility and is extension through the University of Alaska. If you've come this far to Alaska you don't want to miss this place

name: Holly Swabb
text: Great place to see sea life and learn about helping out the environment! Great for children!

name: Aaron Howard
text: A bit expensive, but well worth the admission. The otters and other wildlife being cared for here make it well worth the price. Kids are especially welcome as they have alot of exhibits just for kids to play and touch. Bring your wallet tho, at around 30 a head, it's a bit expensive for a large group.

name: Shawn Tu
text: It's an awesome to-do item in Seward, lots of aquatic and feathered critters to look at. Friendly staff!

name: Bryan Wentz
text: Friendly staff, affordability priced for an Alaskan aquarium. Wide variety of Alaskan sealife. Property is well maintained and an excellent view of resurrection bay right outside. If you are in Seward this is a must-see. Can get a bit crowded as it is a tourist spot, so if you can go during nonpeak hours, Try too.

name: Rob Christiansen
text: Super fun place. Do the tours!

name: soisso
text: Lots of different wildlife here to look at and learn about, just a great place in general

name: Bob Chan
text: I really did enjoy this site, however if you compare it to any aquarium or zoo in the lower 48 you’ll be quite disappointed because there isn’t as much to do or see and it’s similarly priced

name: Jack
text: Awesome place to take the kids and learn about ocean life!!

name: Christian Jacobs
text: Great place to take the family and awesome great marine life. You can see larger marine mammals and go to the touch ponds and touch Sea Stars and other small critters.

name: Evan Nunley
text: The Sealife Center itself is incredible and the staff were friendly and constantly sanitizing. HOWEVER - if you dont want to get COVID, might not be the best place to go right now. The staff are trying their best to social distance families, but there are a TON of tourists in town and no one seems to give a dang about trying to social distance themselves or wear masks, or follow the directionsand STAY AWAY if they are sick. My family went today, and we heard at least 4 different groups of people coughing BAD. The reservation times online mean nothing, so many people were pouring in off the street when we arived for our 3:45 prescheduled visit. Huge groups of people touching everything in sight and coughing everywhere really makes it hard to enjoy our time at such an incredible place. Again, no fault to the staff. No wonder its spreading so fast everywhere.

name: Danny Rowland
text: It is a great little place. A nice location and they do a great job of rehabilitating. You get the feeling that the center exists primarily to help the animals which is very refreshing compared to some zoos and aquariums. Not many animals, but the ones they do have are done very well. There is a touch tank as well. There was a baby walrus there which was very cute. There are not many walruses in captivity so it was cool to see one up close, especially a 6 week old baby ciddling with the human who was feeding it.

name: Mark Essert
text: I really enjoyed seeing all the seabirds and marine life exhibits.

name: Eric McPherson

text: I'm an Alaskan resident band this is always my go-to destination while visiting Seward. The view outside the facility is amazing. The employees are very helpful and friendly. I really love the fact that a huge amount of the money you spend during your visit actually goes towards saving and rescuing animals for rehabilitation. The indoor facility is beautiful and well put. You will not regret visiting this place or regret the money you spend here. It is always clean here too!

text: The aquarium has a great mission. We saw some decent exhibits, but I left feeling it wasn’t worth $30+ per person... maybe $15. I’m comforted by the fact that they are really trying to rehabilitate injured animals and reintegrate declining populations into the wild. The aquarium was small, with not many exhibits. The one exhibit that did stand out however, the sea birds exhibit. This is probably a decent size aquarium to take your kids. But considering this is a world class research facility, I would have liked to learn more, even if the animal portion of the exhibit stayed the same. For example, why was there so little information next to each fish tank?! I want to learn more about each animal other than it’s name!

As a bonus, the encounter tours are amazing! I had the opportunity to go on the marine mammals tour this spring. There was a lot of good information that I never knew about our local sea life, and we even got to pet a seal! It was worth every penny.

Because they help animals in need, there is something new to see each time. I have seen them nurse a walrus back to health, and otters. They also helped a baby beluga whale. Also, if you see an Alaska sea animal in distress, call them. They will help if they can.

name: Ethan Link
text:
It's for the cause! This isn't a zoo, and it's not SeaWorld (perish the thought).  This is a well staffed, mission driven refuge and research facility that deserves your contribution.

You will get some great up-close time with colorful and popular water birds, especially puffins. The seal and sea lion habitats are worth 30 minutes of contemplation. The touch tanks are a fun dare for all.  Take your time and read the info posts; you really will learn a lot and it makes the trip valuable.  Otherwise, if you are pressed for time it can be a quick walk through.

Your visit helps do the research needed more than ever as climate change challenges some of our nations rarest animals.

name: Tammy Kosusnik
text: Was not impressed with Sealife center today , not one bit!!!! Went there to do bird encounter, got to front counter, where admissions is the lady says they are sold out for both sessions, no signage nothing letting you know this before you get in line, period. Suggestion, put up sign letting paying customers know when the encounters are full. Second the lady at admissions counter says oh you can should pay for tickets for encounters online it reserves spots, again no signage letting you know this, how is one suppose to know this, unless you have been to their website. Then what really had me upset was, I purposely came down to see the sea lion feeding,  there is to be 2 feeding of sea lions a day or a combination of either they are fed or harbor seals. Ok this morning, they feed seals, I come back at 1:00 P.M. to see the 2:30P.M. showing of the sea lion feeding, I'm standing outside on observation deck, a good hour before time to feed them, there are 2 scuba divers and a women. The scuba divers get into tank, I think ok cleaning tank no problem be done before feeding. Lady above nothing , nothing said from her, I am still standing there,  divers come up, not out of water, lady still top side nothing, divers go back down nothing said. I'm still standing there, then the lady top side  in the sea lion exhibit. Finally says the are doing a diving pre certification test on somebody that the tank is closed, that they won't be feeding the seals today, but will be harbor seals!!!! What ever happened to letting people know, the feedings and exibits were closed for however long, at least but a sign up or do a announcement or put a person there to let people know!!!! There was my worst experience with sea life center and that is putting it mildly, I have half a mind to not visit again!!!!!!

name: David Holmes
text: It was the standard Buffalo wild wings fare with a few caveats. I was excited to see lemon pepper sauce on the menu only to be disappointed. It wasn't the sauce that I remember from 10 years ago. It was more lemony and salty, with less heat, and not a very good consistency. It was not the sauce of the past. The Carolina reaper sauce did not disappoint. The first bite had great flavor, and the second bite set my mouth on fire for a good 5 minutes. They have an orange sauce now that's also new. If you look at the sauce menu you see it's right next to the Asian Zing. To be honest it tasted like the Asian Zing sauce except with a strong orange flavor. Don't get me wrong I liked it, but it was just kind of interesting to see it next to the Asian Zing and have the same consistency and heat. The online menu said that they had Sam Adams Oktoberfest on tap, but unfortunately they did not. I was also disappointed to find out that they no longer had the waffle cut fries that they called Buffalo Chips. The service was good, the food tasted fine, and everything else about it was the normal Buffalo Wild Wings experience you would have expected. On a Tuesday night you get buy one get one wings so it's well worth the money.

What made this visit so much more enjoyable is the attention we got from the bartender. We were sitting in the dining area, outside of the bar area but the bartender went out of her way. She ended up acting as our waitress and even with a lack of staff she continued providing continuous and genuine attention. My favorite was the extra refills on the drinks that dont have refills because of the long wait. Overall a good meal and good atmosphere.

text: I placed an online order on a Tuesday night that was supposed to be ready for pickup at 8:10PM. I arrived right on time and the hostess told me it would be about another 10 minutes. While I was waiting, the hostess was telling walk-in customers that the wait for food would be 60-90 minutes (the dining room wasn't even busy). I finally got my order at 8:40PM and it wasn't right. Since the wait to correct it would be another 30-45 minutes - I took it, but the hostess didn't even offer any compensation for the order mix up since I prepaid online. This BWW is a joke for the cost, I won't go back - there are so many mom and pop joints in town that have better wings and better service.
