text: I love the food here but they do not deal with crowds well.

name: Dokies Yupanik
text: Good service, clean. Fries were amazing but didn't come with a whole lot. Burger was a bit sloppy but good size patty. Fast service. Pricey.

name: Lonnie Tyone
text: First time and first impression: This place is big, a lot of space. Was greeted and welcomed with a smile. The booth where we directed to sit was dark but no problem. The waitress, Renee was cordial, kind, and very informative. Chicken wings were great. All in all I gave Buffalo Wild Wings 5 stars.

name: Mary Childs
text: Good service and great food.

resp.text: Hey Mary.  Thanks for the kind words.  Hope to see you again soon!

name: Lisa Haughton
text: Overpriced! Wings were good though.

resp.text: Hey Lisa. Thanks for letting us know. Feel free to leave us more feedback on the form at the bottom of BuffaloWildWings.com/FAQ where it says 'Orders & Visits'

name: John Henry Littlefield
text: Very courtious waitress. Made me and a friend feel very welcome

name: Matt McCarter
text: Had a great experience here watching the UFC fight. The place was packed, standing room only!  However, we still got served and had did not feel forgotten or lost in the crowd. The food was good and even though it was busy, we didn’t wait forever as I thought we would. Thought we had a great meal and excellent service.

name: Kortney Redick
text:
As you can see from my review history, I almost never write reviews with less than 3 stars...
I went there today for lunch. The place was not packed, I'd say it was about 25% full, as in 75% of the tables were empty.
It took 40 minutes for our food to arrive.
The restaurant was probably about 50 degrees. I keep my house at 65 and I was freezing as were my husband and son.
My sons food was cold, as in the fries were probably cooked about 20 minutes before they came to our table.
My food and my husbands food was slightly warm.
We were obviously disappointed. =(

name: Noah Belt
text: Heavily understaffed on 28june2020 and the staff was visibly and audibly stressed.

resp.text: Hey Noah. Thanks for letting us know about this. Please fill out the form at the bottom of https://www.buffalowildwings.com/faq/ if you don’t mind so we can get some more info.

name: Stephanie Cullers
text: Great wings, sandwhiches, and drinks. I went with friends and had a really good time.

name: Micheal Dorris
text: Hot and getting run down. The place feels dirty. Our serves was great but the supervisor seemed unfriendly.

name: Angie Flasch
text: Awesome food.. great service.. love this place..

name: Justin Knowlton
text: This Buffalo Wild Wings was not as good as others I have had in the lower 48. They still gave good service and the queso we had was good as well. The wings however seemed like they were frozen chicken nuggets that had been reheated. We also enjoyed the quesadilla!

name: Duke of Curb
text: Good food and a fun place to have a meal.

name: Sierra C.
text: I enjoy their  wings ,any of their wings... but was disappointed that they took off, maybe the only vegetable besides salads off the menu... which was the deep fried mushrooms ; (... won't go there as often because of it....

name: TOO KOO
text: Me and some friends went here for dinner. The waiter took forever to get to us. We ordered some burgers. Tell me why it was an hour n still our food didn't come out. We were the only ones in there. It was a ghost town. We left before the food came out. They comp our beers, horrible place. Don't go here

name: Nolan Oliver
text: Good if you have a craving for some wings or bar food. Excellent selection of sauces, though the vary greatly so you'll need to figure out what your preferences are .Prices are high and only seem to go higher. If you go during lunch-time or on days they have deals (Tuesday for bone-in, Thursday for boneless) you can get an okay price, but it's still not amazing. Perfect if you have a craving, however.

name: Lynn Schell
text: Great place, really accommodating, an the drink selection is pretty big an good. Food is really good. Usually just get wings which are always good but tried a few different wraps an they're all really good as well. You have to try their hottest sauce on a couple wings, just for the taste/ experience.

name: Braxton
text: Worst experience of my life! Waiter was extremely slow, food was cold, and the worst part of it was , the waiter knew she was slow and didn't care, she would rather talk with her friends than serve. I was beyond disappointed with this establishment. Will never go back and definitely will not reccomend!

name: Millie Taylor
text: The food is decent, but unless you're sitting at the bar, be prepared for a long wait.

name: ashley johnson
text: It has wings. That's about it. Two visits ago they forgot my food, then brought me the wrong food, and made the worst old fashioned ever. I refused to go again... Until the boyfriend was sick and wanted some comfort food. This most recent time I got a drink that tasted good (yay) and didn't eat. Our waiter for the first time was helpful and pleasant (a lot of new staff), but it drove me crazy to see how inefficient they were. The table next to us sat in various stages of dirty for 30 minutes (really!) before it got wiped off. Lots of staff either milling about, vacuuming the same 10 sqft area, or completely absent. Support a different wing joint, or a local restaurant instead of this place. The bf has agreed we'll go elsewhere next time.

name: Steven Weeg
text: Staff was friendly as all get out and the atmosphere was just awesome. I have never had a better mudslide ANYWHERE

name: Rob Petrie
text: Fortunately several restaurants serve cooked wings that taste great. Unfortunately BWW is not one of them. If you enjoy under cooked or raw chicken this is your place, staff are too busy doing something besides their jobs. I might go back for a burger sometime,  but the wings forget them. Salmolle is not your friend.

resp.text: Hey Rob.  We apologize for the poor experience you had.  Please give us a call at 866-704-0777.

name: Rob W
text: Pretty awesome wings, excellent service!

name: Mark Jensen
text: Four star sports bar. Plenty of big TVs. Clean. Had I known before I would have been there for the big games.

name: Allen Finneseth
text: 20 minutes to get a drink and 20 more minutes to place a order. 20+minutes we finally get food. Asked for napkins and a fork, after 5 minutes one person at my table got up and found silverware as needed to eat. Do not sit in the bar area. I am sure the service is better in the non bar seating area.

name: Andrew Chong
text:
Wings, excellent.
Price, excellent.
service, not really good.
i think you guys need to hire more people, but the servers there were real grumpy from working overtime, that's what im assuming why they were grumpy. because when i was there last week, and the week before, and the week before that, the same server was excellent.
but not lately.

name: Bex Hill
text: Yum,  yum! Clean, great waitress. Fresh salads, and great wings!

name: U.B. Fury
text: This place is going down hill fast. Barely anyone in there and food took forever. Waitress kept disappearing and never brought utensils.

name: Murray Colvin
text: Go eat and meet your taste buds! This buds for you too!

name: Philip Weedin
text: Okay, the Garlic Parmesan wings? Yum, 10/10. But the service, especially around the super bowl? Not great. Even overheard that they have to reheat their wings in the microwave before you get there. Plus I feel like the price is way up there.

name: Benjemin Harris
text: The food is okay, but nothing to write home about. It's also pretty consistently slow, even when there's not that many people. Go for the specials, but probably not much else.

name: Michael Lane
text: An all around fantastic family restaurant and sports bar.  The options to play trivia or poker enhance the overall experience.  Food is usually excellent but they do occasionally over-saunce the tradition wings.  Service can also be slow at time but always friendly.

name: Alice McKechnie
text: The waitress was wonderful, we did not worry about a thing. She exceeded our expectations about the chicken wings by making sure there were no hot sauces involved. I love the honey bar b que, my friend was equally pleased by the teriyaki sauce. So when wings are calling...

name: Theresa Philbrick
text: If you are after beer and wings...then a bazillion stars. And, the appetizer tacos are delicious. Other than that? Meh. Our salads were  drenched in dressing. Chicken breast had consistency of gristle.

name: John Paul
text: Great little restaurant average prices good service good attitude if you have one go ahead and go in there and get a burger or some wings they do it good you'll be happy if price is not an issue

name: Ryan
text: The food is pretty good for a chain place.  Service is hit or miss depending on who you get.  If you like sports of any kind you can watch it on TV though.

name: JAY hansell
text: Great place for beer and sports

name: GUTTA WAYZ TV
text: If you looking to get some great wings, ( and u know how black people are with chicken ) this place is da bomb... Prices are affordable and the customer service is great!!!! No pool table buuuut just come with friends to enjoy each other, large tv screens and great atmosphere shouts out to BUFFALO WILD WINGS. #YLG #DaTruf ( If I wrote it then it's tru )

name: Kyle and Jenn Todd
text: Great place for a group, some drinks, and of course wings. Hot wings, spicy wings, good burgers, whatever it is you are craving they probably have it. I routinely meet up with a group of other Toyota 4x4 owners and BS about off-roading and despite not even knowing a group size they are accommodating to us.

name: Zack Williams
text: Juicy

resp.text: Hey Zack. Glad you liked it! Come back soon?

name: Jim Avery
text: Great food in about 12 minutes. Friendly and fast service, but I would rate it $$.  $15.79 for a small order of wings.  If you want to splurge, the wide range of flavors offers a good option.

name: M Tauf
text: Service was a little slow and the food took longer than expected.  It wasn't crowded.  Caribbean jerk wings were Hella bomb and the onion rings.

name: Elizabeth Meliah
text: Even though we booked as a party of 7 they charged added gratuity for a group of 8 or more. We came early to be sure to get a good view of our game and they tried to change our screen to another game.  Waitress screwed herself out of a good tip by adding her own.

name: Elsy Danedi
text: Ordered for pick up and was told that the food would be ready in 20 minutes, but ended up getting there around the time they said it would be ready only to wait an additional 45 minutes. When we asked the cashier why it might be taking so long,  he seemed irritated that we even asked and snapped "it'll be ready in a minute" at us. But otherwise, great food and fun vibe in the restaurant.

name: Farid Sanouvong
text: Pretty hectic - but it’s usually by the crowding customers. Overall it’s a really good Bdubs. Matter of fact, it’s the only one in town. I really can’t complain about this place but it does have really great service and attractive servers. 😜

name: Desiree Wood
text: Great food but need to hire staff that know what customer service is about. Don't get me wrong they are trying.

name: Andrew Van Ness
text: What can you really say about BWW that hasn't already been said? The one in Anchorage had a huge selection of beer, including the local favorites - Alaskan Brewing Company.  I tried the Summer Ale and White Ale.  Both were good. Split some medium-spicy wings with friends.  Some of the wings were burnt and over-crisp. The bartender was Josh; he was very cool and gave tips for the trip.

name: Greg Naatz
text: Very, very good tonight!  Three great flavors.  Spicy Garlic, hot BBQ, and Caribbean Jerk.  All great!

name: Laurita Cottonham

text: Good food, kind and caring service. Great lunch.

name: Tammy Vig
text: Okay place, made my friend throw up. They have loud music, and a bad atmosphere. The food is medeoker.

name: Florence Bailey
text:
We've been here twice already and have had terrible service. The first time, we had a bubbly waitress. She couldn't remember what our drinks were - to the point where she asked us to taste ours to see what flavors they were. Our drinks were served but she never came back to give us any refills even though she obviously had the time to sit down at the table across from us to take orders from the guys that were sat there. We ordered Spinach Artichoke dip and the pita bread was so overcooked to the point that it was completely inedible. My 2 year old tried to bite it and he couldn't even break the bread. My poor baby handed it back to me. I tried eating it and I couldn't break any part off. We would have asked for them to send us another one but our waitress never came back. I had to walk up to the host's table to ask for refills and to let them know that we were ready for the check and to leave.

The second time, it was so hot in the restaurant. When I asked about it, they told us that they didn't have a/c. The wait times were so long that we were sitting there for a little under 45min with 2 toddlers in the heat. It wasn't our waitress' fault though. She was serving so many people and worked whatever she had.

We won't be returning.

name: Kirk Byron
text: It was ok for Bw's been to many better for less

name: A H
text: Typical and decent tasting bar food. No drink specials. Prices higher in AK than in lower 48.

name: Trevor Ryden-Selk
text: Tons of wing flavors all the ones I tried where amazing service was great the beers were tall and the tv where everywhere great for watching sports

name: Kimberly Gilhousen
text: Always excellent wings!

name: Nick Myers
text:
Must be severely understaffed. Two visits were enough to determine that this location isn't up to par with the other B dubs I've been to.
They should seriously consider adding ranch or blue cheese dressing to take out orders. Most people like those sort of things with their chicken wings. I didn't know I had to specifically  ask for it at this particular location.

name: Ryan Rampton
text: Waitress was nice and food was good. Not an amazing experience, however. I would go back but only if I had a good deal for it.

name: Tristen Ray
text: Yun yum yum! great place for a good beer, tasty wings, and some entertaining staff. they know how to have a good time here.

name: Dennis Lindsay

name: David Stock

name: Ian Walser

name: London Love

name: 5 days 5 DAYS
text: $86 online order gave them a $10 tip paid for my order before i knew i was gonna be waiting there 20 mins for ny order that was supposed to be done by 6:40 and got home to find out the wings were not what we ordered and paid $6 per order of fries that was barely a handfull.  Save your money and eat in or go somewhere else :(

name: Elizabeth Maxson
text: Love the atmosphere and the food!  I was hesitant taking the kids but they had some great kid options too and I didn't feel like I was a bother to anyone :)

name: Dorothy Massey

Tuesday is original wings discount and Thursdays is discounted boneless wings.
For a twist of a dish try the chips and salsa.

name: Joshua Carney

name: Nick Schumacher

name: John M

name: Mark Miller

name: Mario Blandino
text: Mediocre customer service, high prices, and minuscule portions. But really, the wort thing... they don't toss the wings! (They serve it on the side to dip in) How can a place that is supposed to be all about buffalo wings not toss them in the sauce? It blows my mind.

name: John Anderson

name: Michael Rosebeary
text: There was hardly anyone there. It was quick and easy for get a drink and popcorn. Nice, friendly staff and great movie.

name: Ryan Stafford
text:
2018/10/06 - Watched Venom today at 4:10 PM, ticket price $8.25.  Had a great time and enjoyed the movie.

When you want to see a new movie in the valley then you'll visit The Valley Cinema.

Plenty of parking!  Buying a ticket is very quick and easy.  If you're getting food then buy the ticket at the same time. You can buy an alcoholic drink here, but you can't drink inside the theater.

The bathrooms are in the lobby, so hold on to your ticket or you may have trouble reentering the auditorium.

Seats are clean and soft. There might be additional leg space here compared to other theaters.  Sadly there is the customary 30 minutes of previews here too.

name: Rhinesguard
text:
Its open, safe enough, and has all your movie going NEEDS!!!

If you like the movie going experience, then this sufficient to make you happy!!!

name: Naynaylovesmakeup
text:
Updated Again- 2020 (Photos Only)

Updated- 2019
I am a big movie lover and we always sit with the metal bar in front of us to be able to put my feet up. The snacks are yummy all over priced but it’s part of the experience. The seats are big ppl friendly. They slightly recline. Bathrooms are always clean, and fully stocked. I have never experienced waiting they have a-lot of stalls. Staff is patient when it comes to my elderly father placing his order each time which makes the difference to me when he’s treated with respect. I have and will keep coming back. The popcorn always tastes great; its hot, fully popped kernels, yummy butter taste. When you order a large size you get free refills which it great for our group each time. They have a self serve condiment station- ketchup, mustard, butter pump, & napkins. I think the floor does have popcorn kernels and a few M&Ms on the floor and I have had sticky floors once in a while but nothing that serious to complain about.

My Family and I are big movie lovers, it runs deep in our family. Going to a theater has always been a time for togetherness and sharing memories. One year back in 2004 we went to 41 times to the theater. We go to about 16-20 a year these days and we always choose to come here.

2017-
I always have a great time at the movies. I come from a family of movie gurus and going to the theater has always been a place of good memories and this theater has been a part of those memories when it comes to the next generation of our family. My daughter and I have gone with my family many times and will continue to make more.

This place has decent prices, very friendly staff, clean floors, game room for kiddos to play while we get snacks and take our seats, they have a mini resturant lol im not sure what to call it but they have pizza, burgers, etc. Also a side note when u get a large size of popcorn u get refills free and they have a self serve butter station which I always take full advantage of.

For those night when u dont want kids to tag along they have over 21 movie showings for those u like a beer and a movie together.

I AM GOING TO SURPRISE MY DAUGHTER TOMORROW AND TAKE HER TO THE EMOJI MOVIE SO WE CAN HAVE FUN BEFORE SCHOOL STARTS BACK.

text: Actually was quite quick getting thru ticket & concession line (granted we were there at noon on a Thursday).  There was a young man working the counter that just had "trainee" as his name badge and I have to say that he was great.  Very courteous, polite, efficient and did a great job with my request of "lots of extra butter" on my popcorn.  Theater was clean and movie was great, but I really have to commend the young man at the counter since I've heard other bad reviews of the service at the theater.  We had great service today!

Theater we went into was not cleaned at all yet the trash at the door was over flowing. Blame it on the holiday for short staffing but I think it was more lack of caring.

I do love the self service butter dispensers for popcorn. I prefer to hit the 21 and over shows so I don't have to listen to kids and teenagers.

text: The theatre is clean and well maintained. Seating is comfortable, but certainly not comparable to the high end super recliners in deluxe theaters. Decent sound system. Food prices are somewhat high, with a modest but varied selection.

text: It's a decent movie theater. I went to see the new Jurassic park movie and I didn't get the feeling like the movie theater is a dive spot. The only suggestion I would make is that a employee be present to make sure movies get started in each theater showing before leaving the projector room. Our movie didn't start and had to wait almost a half hour before someone restarted the computer so the movie would play. Other than that I would definately come back.

And they keep the theaters clear of noisy patrons

name: Rick Feller
text:
With the availability of online media, I don't venture out to theaters often, but this visit with my granddaughter was enjoyable. No sticky floors or boisterous theater-goers.

Yes, the concessions are more than expensive, but that is how they manage to keep the doors open. Sometimes there are movies that you just want to see on the big screen with a great sound system. And sometimes, you just want to take your granddaughter to a movie. I don't mind occasionally supporting the theater through my patronage so that they are there when such opportunities arise.

Stadium seating, clean and comfortable seats, great sound system - this is a modern, well-maintained theater that's never given me a bad experience.

name: Emma Frisby
text: Have you heard of Movie Pass? It's $10 a month, they send you a credit card, you install an application on your smart phone, and then you can see one movie every day. Definitely worth it, just to go to one movie a month even. Guess what else, The Valley Cinema accepts the movie pass credit card! All you have to do, is select the movie you are going to, in the app, then use the machine to buy a ticket, like you're paying with a regular credit card. Save money with Movie Pass, then you can buy all the snacks you want. This theater is the best one in Wasilla to see all the movies at. :D

name: Beth Hurst
text: 5 stars.  It helps of course that I LOVE dogs but a great Ranger Led talk and display non the less.  Seeing these dogs doing what they love to do is always rewarding.  You can either take the bus from the Visitors Centre up to the kennels (you get some info on the bus from the Ranger so it's good option) however, you can drive up there (limited parking) but the plus side to this is you can go outside of regular 'show' hours and while they are herding everyone back on the bus back to the visitors centre you can stick around and visit with the dogs without the crowds.   This is a FREE program but they do ask for donations which you can deposit at the entrance (all proceeds stay within the dog kennels).

name: Anita Kingree
text: I stopped by Humpy's for a late dinner before a 1am flight out of Anchorage. My husband and I seated ourselves, and waited quite a while for a waitress to come by and take our drink order. We didn't mind or say anything, because it was busy and we had plenty of time to waste before our flight.  I ordered water and my husband ordered diet coke. We also ordered our meals at the same time. When the waitress brought our drinks, she brought us both water. She walked away before we had a chance to let her know my husband's drink was incorrect. Since she was so busy and the bar was open, I just went over there and let them know we needed a diet coke because we had gotten two waters. The bartender was super friendly and nice about it. I was trying to help out the waitress by not flagging her back down because the place was so busy. Once we received our food ( I ordered Halibut and chips, and my husband ordered a burger) and began to eat, the food was good. I have no complaints about it. What happened next is the reason I left only 2 stars. As we received our check to leave, my husband asked if we could by chance get a to-go cup for our drinks. The waitress said "no", which isn't a big deal, but then she got really sassy and said, "By the way! You did NOT order soda anyway." Her tone of voice was very rude. First of all, YES, he did order diet coke. I heard it, the lady sitting beside us (who was equally shocked by the rudeness) heard it, and it's exactly what he said. If you get an order wrong, that's fine. We weren't rude in any way about it....but there is absolutely NO reason to be hateful to a customer because of your own mistake ...especially, when the customer went out of their way to help you on a busy night. Customer service is everything in my opinion. I can excuse mistakes, and even mediocre food...but I cannot excuse rudeness to patrons who are being kind to you. What did she think? We are Diet Coke scammers who go around scamming restaurants out of one diet coke per meal? Ridiculous!  Very disappointing!

Home Made Pies.  If you're visiting Alaska and you want to enjoy a dessert that locals travel hundreds of miles to taste then you need to stop at Eureka Lodge. Stretch your legs and enjoy a quick meal during your travel in Alaska at the Eureka Lodge.  Credit cards accepted, no smoking inside, and make sure you have your shirt and shoes on.  If you get your order To Go then expect a charge ($0.50) for the box.

Shared from a friend.
Shame on you Eureka lodge.
My sons father had a tire blowout around 11pm on Friday night January 3, 2020. He limped to your parking lot and pulled up to a light on your building so he could get out and assess the damage. He didn’t know that he tripped the camera and the owner (who pointed out he owned the place since the sixties) showed up angry for waking him and his family up. When asked if he could have a room for the night the owner wasn’t interested in helping and he was turned down.
It was -30 and he slept in his car all night. State Farm in TN called him every 30-45 to make sure he was still ok.  They tried every tow truck company and he finally had one 11:00am the next day.
What happened to helping people in an emergency situation? Especially when you have the means to help....he would have paid for the room. He was only asking for a warm place to wait.
I will never set foot in that place again!

name: Ryan Stafford
text:
If you want to walk on a glacier then the Matanuska Glacier may be your best opportunity.

You'll need to stop and pay for access at Matanuska Glacier Adventures of Alaska.  Once you've paid then you have a short drive to a very uneven parking lot.  Follow the orange cones and you'll soon find the Matanuska Glacier under your feet.

Bring a medium jacket because the temperature drops as soon as ice is under your feet.  The wind will increase a little too.  If you're scared of slipping then bring cleats, but there is so much silt and small rock that you may not slip at all.

name: Anita Kingree
text: My husband and I stopped by Latitude 62 for dinner while in Alaska on vacation in July 2019. This was by far one of our favorite meals of the whole trip. The place was rustic and cozy. Our waitress gave amazing friendly service and really went out of her way to make sure we had a pleasant experience. The food was delicious. I ordered a king crab meal with a side Caesar salad, which came with a baked potato, steamed veggies, and bread. My husband ordered fresh grilled salmon with a creole soup, which came with a baked potato, steamed veggies, and bread. I would recommend both of those plates! This is a must stop restaurant if you visit Talkeetna!

text: Good food. Breakfast is served 8-11am.  Missed it by a few minutes the first time we came.  Ended up having lunch instead.  I had been having seafood everyday of the trip so opted for something different and had the chicken strip basket.  It was great.  Loved the breading and seasoning.  Huge portion.  Was only able to eat about half of it.  Friend had the fish and chips which were also very good.  Went back to try breakfast the next day.  Great service and friendly waitress. We asked if there was anywhere we could get some fresh bread in town, because most places were already closed for the season.  She came back out with half a load of bread which was very thoughtful and nice of her to do for us. Bacon was very flimsy and undercooked.  Our waitress seemed less than thrilled that we were there, didn’t really want to interact with us much when we tried to engage in some small talk.

text: Over-priced food that seemed more like microwaved store fare. The ambiance is good, the restrooms were a bit iffy, and the parking was fine. The fish of the fish and chips looked and tasted like I had just deep-fried some breaded halibut bricks straight from the box of frozen halibut with the guy in the yellow jacket on the front. The burger was definitely cooked, but was a bit greasy and tasted rather bland. The best part of the meal was the fries. They were pretty good and did not seem store-bought, but not really sure. Add to the lackluster food taste the really high price, and you have a disappointed traveler who wished he had eaten at one of the higher-rated places in town.

We are closed just two days a year, Christmas Day and Thanksgiving Day.  Our food is hearty and home made.  Cook Josh is our amazing soup king.  It smells so good in that kitchen when he's brewing up a new pot of something delicious.  We have prime rib every Saturday night, a favorite of the locals.  At any time a group of local musicians might start a session, never know who you may run into.  We love our customers!  Thank you for stopping in!

name: Vincent Sabio
text:
Terrific experience! We rode the tram up (a bit pricey at $35 per adult; I'll bet it's cheaper when there aren't any cruise ships in town). The views from the top are spectacular! There's actually quite a bit to see and do at the top, including several scenic hiking trails.

We then walked the Mt. Roberts Trail to the bottom. It took us about 75 minutes at a nominal hiking speed -- not fast, not slow -- to reach the Basin Road Trailhead. From that point, it was a pretty short walk into town. The trail to the base is not a technical hike, but it's also not a smooth, level walking trail, either.

The views along the trail are pretty good -- not as breathtaking as the views from the tram or from the summit, but you also don't get the same sense of accomplishment that you get from walking the trail down. And sure, one would have a greater sense of accomplishment from hiking the trail UP -- but, at my age, obeying gravity is an important survival concept.

Enjoy....!

name: Dr. Martha Martinez
text: Let the LOVE BIRDS, Chaak (Eagle) and Yeil (Raven) take you up (or down) to fantastic views of Juneau, Douglas and Admiralty Islands, mountains and wetlands, etc.  Great hiking trails.  Enjoy native flora and fauna (very easy to see mountain goats, birds, and other wildlife here).  Helpful interpretative signs.  Excellent historical movie.  Restaurant has great views and a comprehensive menu with local delights, including several vegan and vegetarian options. First Nations owned and operated.  Tramway operator (Young man with a drum) is funny and engaging, but also true to his heritage.  His touching rendition of a Tlingit lullaby alone is worth 5 stars. Look him up!

name: Jonatan Almanza V.
text: Good place close by the pier downtown, open from 9am but with the ships from 7am. Offer a round trip pass of 35 Canadian dollars, nice view and just 4.5 minutes ride up to the top. In there, you can buy  from basic souvenirs up to the up scale ones. Credit card accepted.

name: Jennie Louwes
text:
Not all lift operators are created equal; and, if only going round-trip, once, it's an expensive ride! Those two things being said, as a local, I love the tram. The views are stellar and it's a wonderful experience to see Juneau from new heights without hiking up a mountain on one's own to do so.

Most of the tramway 🚡 operators are knowledgeable, out-going, and enjoy what they do. I have yet to meet an employee working the tram that I didn't like! Be aware that the tram, as it's being docked at the top, does slow down and rock gently back and forth prior to it lodging firmly into place for your safe exit on the top of Mount Roberts. If you have a fear of heights, the rocking motion may make you uneasy; and, it's important to note, the tram does have you riding above treetops. If afraid of heights, look out and not down! The lift takes about 5 minutes to go up and 5 minutes to go back down and is made available for either direction within reasonably spaced, short intervals. Once off-loaded, at the top of Mount Roberts, take your time to enjoy the Nature Center, the Gift Shop, Grab a Bite to Eat, and find your way to Father Brown's Cross for Amazing, Awe-inspiring Views that seem like movie back-drops but are perfectly real; a place where time stands still.

What goes up, must come down; thankfully, a tram like the one in Juneau is safe, secure, and smooth. It seems to glide as it brings you back down to earth. It's a brilliant contraption that's well maintained and kept clean. If a tourist, the expensive, round-trip ticket is worth the cost for a once in a lifetime experience like none other. If a local, the season pass would be a good thing to nab as it'll save you money and allow you to travel, by tram, as often as you'd like. 😊

name: Christian Cruz
text: One of Juneau’s main attractions. For a little over $30, head out from one of the busiest tourist hubs up to top of Mount Roberts on a cable suspended car. On high cloud cover days or sunny days, get an amazing view overlooking Downtown Juneau and see Douglas all the way across the channel. Once you make the 5-7 minute trip to the top, explore the restaurant, the eagle rescue center, a small movie theater showing the history of Juneau, or take the trails at the top for some of the best high altitude photography of Juneau.

name: John Auerswald
text:
It's great.  I get a season pass every year.

(It's funny that people complain about the price when you can hike up & down the mountain for free.)

text: One of the key sites to see in Juneau is the view from the Mount Roberts Tram. It goes straight up from the dock area into the hills overlooking Juneau. First it is an amazing engineering marvel, but foremost it is a breathtaking view. The cost is a bit steep at $33/person, but still worth it in my opinion. Once you get to the top there are wonderful hiking trails to go around and at each curve and hill is yet another spectacular view. I highly recommend this if you end up in Juneau.

Keep this in mind, especially if you're racing to the top before your cruise ship is scheduled to depart. (Ask employees about the wait up top to get the most reliable information.)

name: JEFF PETERS
text:
It's a fun experience when you're in Juneau Alaska.

The tram goes up the mountain where you get some amazing Vistas. You're overlooked shows the port of Juneau and the surrounding downtown area as well as the wooded hills and mountains which hug you gently. It takes a little time to go up the mountain and then while you're there you can do some hiking and sightseeing. There's a small Raptor rescue area where eagles are taken to mend and sometimes live if they are unable to go back to the wild. Be prepared for cool weather or even snow even into early June. We were there on June 11th 2009 and there was a sign that said last snowfall May 30th. There was still snow on the ground at sea level all around the downtown area. That's just part of the charm and experience of going to Alaska.

name: Paulness
text: So this is an interesting place to get pizza, right on the eastern edge of Denali national park (for those of you that still think or say "Mckinley", you're way behind the times).  Anyeay, the locale is cool, right next to a vicious creek.  Theres a horseshoe pit and cornhole lane in the front.  Plenty of space outside for you to get ravaged by mosquitos, so bring bug spray.  The views of the m li mountains are awesome.  Inside it's a quaint place, where strange but friendly locals hang out.  The pizza itself, for anyone from places where real pizza is made like the upper east coast, is a bit disappointing.  The sauce is really sweet for starters.  The crust is ok for a pie made outside of the tri-state area, and the toppings seem fresh.  But the flavor is just not what I'm used to eating.  Its wasn't bad, but it's nothing that I'd rave about.  I visited during the whole COVID pandemic, and social distancing or mask-wearing was not an issue nor was it enforced or respected.  All in all, I would not go out of my way to eat her again, I may never eat her again period, but at least I can say I tried it.  I'm not  saying dont go, go and give them s try, judge their pizza for yourself.

Duck Confit is my very favorite dish and I've sought it out all over Europe and North America. Kincaid Grill does it pretty well. The skin was just sufficiently crispy, the fat well rendered while the leg and thigh were still moist and fell off the bone. Its difficult to balance that equation. There's still room for improvement though. I'd give it a 92%, the best we've had in Anchorage so far. We will return and order it again for consistency.
The staff is well trained and professional while still friendly and personable.
Good wine list.
We prefer the rear dining room. There's much less traffic at the cul de sac.

text: I stayed in a room with a mountain view. my room was quiet except for in the morning when the dumpsters were being picked up (probably not an issue with the windows closed).  the room was clean and comfortable.  I had minimal interaction with the staff but check in and out was easy.

name: Doug Williams
text: The rooms are nice, and the bed was comfortable.   I stayed at the hotel for a convention.   The hotel staff did an excellent job of providing everything we needed for the conference rooms.  The hotel catered our meals and our banquet.  I  was very impressed with the quality of the food.

name: Angel Gonzales
text: My organization and I have been coming to the, Baranof, for the past 5 years. They are centrally located in downtown, Juneau.  It's a short walk to the Capitol, or to various stores, restaurants, or meeting spots. The hotel and rooms are very nice and they've made some beautiful revisions in the lobby. I also love the coffee shop that is attached to the hotel.

name: Henry Brannon
text: Great view. Rustic gold Rush era feel and look. Downtown. Exhaust fan in restroom worthless (not sure if there even is one). The staff is very professional and nice. Parking area is too small and not guaranteed, nor does it look like a secure area.

name: Tetyana M.
text: I was very pleased with this hotel.Clean rooms, I didn’t have too many issues with it being too loud it being Christmas Day and the hotel was pretty much empty. The coffee shop right outside the lobby had great coffee as well. The only complaint I have was the size of my bath tub - it was almost half the size of a regular tub and was just very strange,but not a deal breaker.Gorgeous back views of the mountains- sure looking forward to my next stay !

name: Natasha Hoover
text: People may have bad reviews but understand this place is worlds better than other hotels in downtown Juneau. They dont have A/c but its Alaska and it's not often needed. They do offer fans, have windows that open and have heat. The staff is super friendly and more helpful than they need to be. We thought we left medication in our hotel room and they searched for it. Asked  the person who had checked in already if they had seen it who let staff look under the bed, searched the linens, kept looking until it was located. I am so very impressed. Rooms are typical hotel rooms. Beds are comfortable. Soaps etc provided. Stay here they are great!

name: Mathew Maxey
text: I stayed for a week while attending a professional training. A nice location downtown and close to the shops. Close to food and some hiking trails, great for what I enjoy. It's definitely got a classic, well used/loved feel. I would stay there again.

text: Really good place to stay, located in downtown's heart, you can do and go wherever you want from this point. Very centrical, even drugstore and natural stores are close by. If you are looking for excursions or activities, a few blocks from the hotel heading to the seaplanes locations, you will be able to find them.

There was an uncovered window in the bathroom that looks to other buildings where people can see straight in to your shower. It had a curtain rail, but no curtain. When I brought this to managements attention, they said they would send maintenance up while we were gone to fix it. Upon our return, there was a towel, literally a bath towel, draped over the curtain rail.

We checked out early and went to the  Goldbelt hotel which was astoundingly better. It felt like returning home compared to the Baranoff. I walked into my new room at the Goldbelt so relieved!

name: Trista Crass
text:
I took my fiance there for his birthday. The restaurant itself is gaudy, with a cheesy,  1980s daytime-TV opulence. There are light-up menus, in the spirit of any mall-chain family dining experience. The service was good, but kind of offbeat. They would drop by and ask us how everything was while we were waiting for our appetizer.

The food is nothing short of terrible. Tasteless, unimaginative, NOT what is actually on the menu, and overpriced.  Entrees do not come with a soup or salad, and the menu is often a flowery description of what you actually get. I ordered the  Macadamia-crusted Halibut, served with Yukon Gold Potatoes and a mango chutney, only to receive a dry piece of deep-fried fish, made soggy by plopping it atop a glop of watery, tasteless mashed potatoes. The 'Mango Chutney' was actually just white vinegar, with grey, indeterminable vegetables. My fiance got a better piece of fish, but the side dishes were awful. The lot wasn't edible, but we had already waited about 45 minutes.

Thinking dessert would get the taste of disappointment out of our mouths, we ordered the pecan pie ala mode. We were given an $8 sliver of old, refrigerator-flavoured pie, with spongy, goopy Costco ice cream.

We laughed it off as the worst dinner ever, but the $120 bill (for two meals, two drinks, an appetizer and dessert) still kind of hurt, knowing it wasn't worth it at all.

text: Food is super over priced BUT that view is absolutely insane and totally worth the inflated prices. Mixed drinks..... not so much. Over all, a really great experience though and would totally encourage others to go as well.

name: Sierra
text:
The best place to eat in the Anchorage area. With views that are unforgettable from every table and service that is the best you could get, this restaurant is a must see. Make sure and get on the team 15 minutes before your reservation. Summer or Winter itll be an amazing meal unlike anywhere else.
An absolute must see!

name: Jason G
text: Very nice restaurant. Definitely a quite little spot. Great views and awesome food and drinks. The smoked salmon was great. So tender and flavorful.  The chocolate cake was smooth and rich. The drinks were smooth and had a nice kick. Definitely well worth the wait. The staff was more than friendly and accommodating. Well worth the trip up the tram to get here.

name: Yeva S-yan
text: Wow, loved it. We just visited, basically winter and snow... Was really beautiful, was little bit cloudy, but overall planning to come back ☃️🎄

text: Excellent service.  Romantic ambience.  Great food.  Try their chef's tasting menu.  Wine pairing was perfect.  Best to make a reservation.

name: Alex Hannan
text: This place is truly amazing. Award winning food, a great selection of drinks and epic views! What more can you ask for?!

name: Lawrence Goodrich
text:
👎🏻My review is based on a bill of $265 for 3 people.  Service: ⭐️the waiter was terrible, was not attentive at all! Like he never worked at a restaurant. Food: ⭐️⭐️Had a good flavor but lacked any presentation (don’t they watch MasterChef?). View:⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️it is on the top of the mountain and you could not have done better. Price: way too much is this meal.

My advice go up and eat at the deli for a lot less.

name: Mandi Ward
text: We sat down right away to a table. The restaurant was not busy at all. They have a decent but not large selection of foods. Everything we ordered was delicious and the staff was very accommodating.

name: bublehed
text: Great views, service and food. Would have given 5 stars but the menu is a bit over priced. We had the  salmon and beef filet.

name: Scott Daletas
text: We ate here on my Graduation dinner and just had a great time! This is an up-scale pricey restaurant, but for us worth it due to the occasion. The food was smaller portions but was not unexpected. It was delicious! I find the best part is the Tram ride up and back down after a Fizz! You must order a Fizz drink, let them know it's your first time ordering one and you will see why!

name: luckylexi
text:
Such an amazing experience!
We took our granddaughters to this restaurant.  It was really very nice they had our food served by 3 wait staff at once so everyone got their food at the same time.  So great presentation.  If you can go there when it is clear the view is to die for.  But we got a blizzard.  Still had a great time though.  My 11 year old granddaughter got the oysters and blew my mind by eating them all.  But it didn't seem like she liked them at all.  Still thought pretty impressive.

name: Alaskan Campbells
text: Great views.  Limited menu.  Difficult for food restrictions.

name: Ryan Larson
text:
Beautiful views, was disappointed by our actual meal. The free Tram Ride up the mountain was amazing. The restaurant is spectacular where it is perched and they have an amazing wine selection. Service was great as well.

Some of our food (Such as the Scallop soup) was some of the best I have ever had. Our cheese selection was lacking and our entrees were sub par. They called my steak American Wagyu but it was touch and chewy. My wife ordered the pork chop and our server warned us that it might come out as *medium* which my wife would have been happy with. The chop came out overcooked and tough. Both of our sides were lackluster as well. Some sort of beans came with the Pork Chop and my steak came with greens and quinoa, I had a tough time remembering what it came with and I was there a week ago.

Definitely worth a trip up the mountain to see this place, just be careful on what you order.

name: Preston Miller
text: Awesome place.  Great food, views, and staff.  If you want fine dining with breathtaking scenery in Alaska, this place is a must visit.  You take the tram up to the restaraunt from the Alyeska resort, the tram ride is great too.

name: Molly Woo
text: Love the hiking, recommend to bundle ticket which gives you up to $20 meal credit which only costs you $9 extra. Great location, great raindeer sausages!

name: Blake Jones
text: Great place. Food is overpriced but it is good.  Not my style of resturaunt but the view is awesome and it's a cool place to go.

name: marcus
text: Did not get the best view because of the snow but a great experience! Dinner is very pricey but the restaurant has two walls of awards! You can taste the quality in the food. Definitely a must at least once in your life!

name: Klaus Bello
text: First restaurant in Alaska which served great quality food, tasty salmon and delicious soup. Just excellent.

name: Stacy Harvill
text: This place was so much fun!  Friends took me up to share the views and the famous fizzy drink.  A great place to bring the visiting family.

name: Brian R
text: Love this place. Was a great family gathering which offered everyone plenty of room to sit with lots of food options.

name: Don Krupski
text: Top of the mountain dining! This is a place for worthwhile memories, the view is phenomenal ,food is delicious and the staff is attentive to your needs.

name: Helen Walicka
text: The flagship restaurant of the Alyeska resort up on the mountain reachable by cable car or tram as it’s called in the US. If you have a reservation the return trip is free. Get there early as there’s a great cocktail bar. The menu and food is underwhelming I’ve never seen cheese on the menu as a starter! Good thing is no one under 21 is permitted. It gets booked up so if you’re planning to go book ahead.

name: Thomas Knotts
text: You can't beat the view. Makes everything taste that much better. Love it every time. Great for all occasions.

name: Fabiana Kirtley
text: Absolutely amazing.. location, food and ambiance! Everything!!

name: Shailesh Soliwal
text: Stunning views and delicious food, Scallop Bisque was out of this world !

name: Stanley Vang
text: Waited 2 hours to get sitted got in and there was an open table everywhere. Food was like yall need some real seasoning. Took my food home and gave it to my dog talk about fine dining. Had to make another stop for food on the way. Service was blah for fine dining and a bunch of empty tables service could of been better.

name: Chief Reviews Everything
text: One of the best experiences while I was in Alaska, truly life changing dining experience. Amazing food ( Halibut was out of this world), great beer, breathtaking scenery! I would definitely recommend!

name: Dan Wilding
text: This place was wonderful.... Nestled at the top of the ridge at ten l the Alyeska resort. The restaurant is a short team ride from the hotel. The view is fabulous! Service was top notch! The food was fabulous. The price was, as expected, a bit higher than usual, but when you consider the view, it was worth every penny. Is recommend this as a high end dining experience too all.

name: Pratyush Jaiswal
text: Amazing setting for a lovely meal. Prices are a bit high but perhaps appropriate for the setting.

name: lisa fender
text: Gorgeous Food Gorgeous View

name: Shawn Van Arsdale
text: Up scale dining with a view. The best food around with an experience to go with it.

name: Leigh Eberhart
text: The view from this place is amazing! It is definitely fine dining, but not too pretentious. The food is very good and prepared with care, and the service is definitely fine dining class. The bar is worth a stop even if you don't eat at the restaurant, good drinks and friendly service. And really, the view!!

name: Danielle Beckmann
text:
The view and the service was phenomenal. The food was sub par. Everything was over cooked in the Alaskan seafood dish, the oysters were poorly shucked (my girlfriend choked on a large piece of shell), the steak was cook to the perfect temp but the steak sauce fell flat.
All in all, great service and view but the food is extremely disappointing.

name: MrJamesIkanov
text: The lunch food is great. Just slightly overpriced because they have to haul it up the mountain. The food isn't bad by any means. In fact, the fries are good, the sandwhiches are great. Just expect to pay $8 for large side of fries, or $3 for a single kid sized bottle of juice. A sandwich meal combo is around $11-18. Not a terrible process for a tired skier or someone on vacation. But definitely not cheap.

name: Amanda Kolstedt
text: Great atmosphere, unique and wonderful food, the friendliness staff, and you can't beat those views.

name: Akhenaten T'inshing
text: food and service were fantastic. Views can't be beat.

name: Tom Reale
text: This is the best restaurant in the state.  Terrific menu of mostly local provenance, excellent beer and wine, presentation beyond compare, attentive service, and the views have to be seen to be believed.  Not cheap, by any means, but well worth the price for your special occasion.

name: Peter McDougall
text: The wine list impressed at a price, but as for the food... A starter of Yak tartare was quite yuk, a tasteless chewy grind. Mains of wagyu steak were over seasoned and careless. In all my years, I've never seen a restaurant offer a cheese course as a starter!!!!  Decorum please!  The views out of the window of the lift machinery weren't what I'd call impressive. Then it appears to have gotten interesting...  The bill was $238. The charge on my card I only now find out was $23,800!  This was apparently immediately reversed and corrected BUT still cost me $160 in fx charges. I didn't even know!  Okay, mistakes happen, my credit card Co will sort the damage, not right though nofor them not to fess up and at least say sorry.

name: Sandra Garrison
text: If you have reservations you do get a free tram ride and the top of Mt Alyeska views are beautiful. We had reservations for our party of 9, it was easy to set up and all the staff was very nice and attentive. But the view was mainly of the tram building and cables. They do have extensive bar and wine list but our food was just OK especially for the price and with 9 people someone should have been impressed with their dish. The nice thing about Alaska restaurants you do not have to be dressy. Some are but some of us were in our nicer hiking pants and boots.

name: Baloo Number 2 Marty
text: Very scenic venue. Food excellent. Very  worthwhile  BUT quite expensive.  If we had to ADD CABLE CAR  dollars  we would not have gone.  However  was  special occasion  so  we enjoyed ourselves. Staff were attentive  but a bit "ALWAYS " around. 4/5. Would we do it again no. Travel  from Australia and same meal there would  be about 50%. But this is Alaska.

name: Jonathan Zack
text: Great food. Pricy, but worth it. We had wonderful service definitely try the soup. It's been around since the restaurant opened

name: Robert Bredlie
text: The service is very good. The servings are very small for the price

name: J Thomas
text: Really special. The kobe fillet was the best steak I've ever eaten.

name: The Legend
text: Food was wonderful! I felt weird walking inside wearing my hiking gear though, thank goodness for no dress code

name: Reverend Richard Stoneking
text:
We had reservations in advance, the wait took a bit. Not sure what that was about, there wasn't a queue. We took a chance and had a multi course, was pretty nervewracking, but glad we went through with it. Tried some new things and overall wasn't a bad experience. I am not sure if all of the staff is new but people seem lost and very confused at times. I personally would not go back due to price, the food was acceptable, and obviously there is a view, but I'm not paying to look out the window at dinner.
I would recommend for special occasions, which is where this place shined! The dessert that we got had "Happy Anniversary" in the desert, which was a very nice personal touch that wasn't requested whatsoever. Delivery was over the top there.

name: Don Dubois
text: The views are amazing. Reservations are suggested. With a reservation you get a tram ticket. If you decide to just pop in, there may be starting in the bar area. Same great views, same great menu, same great service, just no free tram ticket.

name: vernon andrews
text:
“Better than the view”
The cuisine and service are both phenomenal. They might be only thing better than the view. You get to decide. Either way you are the winner. I have dined here numerous times and have never been disappointed. It's like going to culinary heaven, you don't want to return to earth

name: Mike Harrelson
text: Amazing food and views. Everything on the menu is absolutely amazing. Cant wait to come back

name: Perry Albright
text: Great Food and Customer Service

name: Liz Cullivan
text: I love going here for cocktails and appetizers. The view of the hill and surrounding area is amazing. I haven’t checked it out for dinner but bet it’s even more fantastic.

name: Uroš Michael Knežević
text: Great view and good food, awesome skiing

name: Caroline Ramos
text: Phenomenal view and food. Wonderful atmosphere and perfect service. The only complaint is a steak that was ordered medium well came out rare. They took it off the bill which resolved the issue. Great experience.

name: Justin Wright
text: Great food.  Top notch restaurant.  Good selection and portions.  Bar tenders are on point and very attentive.  Got a rookie waiter or just one that wasn't reflective of the rest of the normal crew.  Only reason for 4 stars instead of 5.  Will visit again but will be attentive to wait staff.

name: Wesley Hardman
text: Amazing food and even more amazing views! We make it a point to take our friends and family here when they're visiting from the lower 48. Highly recommend!

name: Melissa Moody
text: Perfect for dates... Or a gin fizz while skiing.

name: joseph Rapoza
text: Had a great time playing triva on Friday night.

name: Brian Slater
text: The tram ride up can be a little chilly depending on the time of year, but the food is great, and the service is terrific.  I recommend going there for lunch if you want to spend a little less.  We had an amazing view from our able, which made for a delightful anniversary date.

name: Linda L
text: Impeccable service. Great hearty Alaskan food artfully prepared. Best restaurant in Alaska.

name: Vishnu Thankachan
text: It was amazing. Food was delicious. Staff was okay. View was just breathtaking. I'd suggest you guys to get a ticket with food included.

name: Debra Weinberg
text: My FAVORITE !!! best to visit early enough (before nightfall) so you can see the views.

name: Ryan Stafford
text:
If you're celebrating your anniversary, wedding dinner, or just a date night then you need to dine at Seven Glaciers Restaurant.  In my opinion the most romantic restaurant in Alaska is the Seven Glaciers Restaurant.  The tram ticket is included with your reservation, so you'll have this amazing view prior to arriving at the Seven Glaciers Restaurant.  Once you're in the restaurant have a seat at the bar and enjoy a drink while waiting for your table.  Hopefully you'll have a view of the valley at your table, but if not you'll have your eyes on your date and delicious food.  My wife and I love the Seven Glaciers Restaurant and I think you will too.

Living in great state of Alaska sometimes becomes monotonous to even to its most ardent residents.  Break your dull routine, but taking you loved one to the Seven Glaciers Restaurant high on the Mountain at Alyeska Hotels in Girdwood.  The spectacular views and the food will only outdone by smiles on your faces!

If you want to go enjoy the view, pay the ride up and go to the bar for a cocktail and hit Chair 5 for dinner.

name: Kathy Hayes
text: Girdwood's best restaurant!!  Delicious food - as a vegetarian I was able to find several options that were delightful.   The salad was unbelievable - not something that is said of salad often!!!!  The Asian bowl was yummy too.  We ate here two nights - would have been three but they were closed one night.  The service was friendly and quick, the meals high quality and the ambiance was crisp and minimalist.  A lovely place to eat after a long day on the slopes.

name: Jake Light
text:
The Individuals at Jack Sprat always do a great job.
I can say they do the best Irish Coffee that I've ever ordered at an establishment. The atmosphere contrast between the rooms is very nice! The prices are very reasonable and I've  never had a disappointing moment there. Hopefully on my next review I'll actually have photos to post.
Thanks guys!

name: Rachel Heath
text: I've only had positive experiences at this restaurant. It's a lovely place to enjoy a meal.

name: Tyler Watson
text: The attention to detail and quality of ingredients is amazing. We got takeout from here recently due to the "hunker down" and it was a great experience. Happy to support our local restaurants during these crazy times!

name: Ken Fitzpatrick
text: A must go for anyone in the area. One of the best restaurants in Alaska. The nachos and cheesecake are fantastic.

name: Aspen Knight
text: Jack Sprat is a great place to have dinner; the menu contains fresh ingredients. I had their giant scallops; this appetizer dish comes with only 3 scallops but I added 5 more. Mmmm, it was perfectly cooked, still tender and soft and well seasoned. I highly recommend it, be sure to call ahead for reservations if your driving from Anchorage. The scenic highway may distract you from reaching the restaurant in time.

name: Jennifer Pittman
text: This is a great restaurant with a cozy ski lodge vibe.  I had the duck breast medium rare and it was perfect!  I love that they have local beers on tap as well as great wine.  I love coming here when I’m in Girdwood as they never disappoint with the quality of food or service.

name: Racahael Lowe
text: Delicious chef inspiration dishes! Try the vegan nachos as a starter you won't be disappointed 😋

name: Xavier Orozco
text: Great place, service and food. The boillabase was excellent. The duck was good. Did not have that crispy skin you see at a traditional french cuisine place. That made it overall gelatinous in texture. A sauce to go with the duck would've also helped. The desserts were amazing. Oysters were good. My wife loved the bacon wrapped dates with blue cheese cream or mash. It was pretty delicious. Didn't have the two beers on the menu I wanted. Still it was an excellent experience with supreme service and overall I really recommend and would visit again.

resp.text: Always open to beer recommendations. Thanks for the review!

name: Kristen Davis
text: Such a wonderful experience. We ordered the vegan nachos, steak and bibimbap and were impressed with all of it. Easy to find something on the menu to accommodate food sensitivities and allergies. Very pleased and quite possibly the best meal I’ve had in my 5+years in Alaska.

name: Ahmed Badri
text: Really 5 star restaurant.  Very delicious food and so friendly staff.  My advice is you have to reserve a table before you go there,  science its so bz.

name: Fabiana Kirtley
text: We were half an hour early for our reservation so we decided to get drinks out in the garden. I got a Kambucha cocktail and my husband ordered a “the radler”. Nice we got inside I ordered the Peanut Pan with tofu, my husband ordered a BiBimBop with pork. Both really good!

name: Robert Schwartz
text: Always Amazing, service, food. Worth the wait.

name: bublehed
text: Jack sprat is a great upscàle Girdwood restaurant. They have small unique menu . We had the smoked salmon past, ribeye, bouillabaisse, and shaved pork rice bowl. The meals were great and our server was awesome.

name: Brian Vana
text: I love meat, but the vegan nachos were wonderful.  The service and the ambiance are wonderful. They are doing a great job dealing with the current times.

name: Amaguq Media
text: Great staff and service and the dishes are amazing!

name: Kenny lowe
text: Oh my God this place is so good!

text:
Amazing blood Mary and food all around.
The service was wonderful and the atmosphere was very relaxing.
Truly enjoyed everything about here.
Will return again.

name: Klaus Bello
text: So far one of the best eateries in Alaska. Finally some delicious food. The boujabese was served with a tomato stock, local spin on it, great delicious fish and service. Lived it.

name: Tim Jones
text: Absolutely delicious! I had the octopus and an Alaskan IPA for a fantastic lunch with a great view if the mountains.

name: Melissa Moody
text: An absolute favorite.  Wonderful service, great local atmosphere, and truly delicious food.  The variety of offerings keep things interesting, so you can go often. But their standards are high, so it's a special place for any special occasion.  The drinks are local and well-selected as well!

name: Stephanie Randrup
text: Amazing place with delish food!!! I LOVE their impossible burger with yam fries 😛

name: Boyd Soule
text: Fantastic fresh food but on the more expensive side. Would love to eat here again.

name: srivathsan varadarajan
text: I was recommended this restaurant to celebrate my wedding anniversary and it lived up to its recommendation - delicious food (even for vegetarians), great service, and cozy ambience. Gem of a restaurant at Girdwood!

name: The Legend
text: Reminds me a lot of the goofball restaurants in Austin but this place is good! Really give it a shot. They had a fire roaring outside too. The Bibimbop, bloody mary, and vegan nachos were wonderful.

name: Salley Kim
text: I love all their vegan and vegetarian options. It was awsome!

name: Vince Prep
text: I'd walk 500 miles for Klondike Scallops. Mother Hubbard's Cupboard next door is really cute as well. Could not find them on Google Maps but worth visiting if you're at the restaurant. Steve Keene art in the bathroom. Very cool people. Even though they were fully booked, they managed to get us a three top inside. Killer food. Attentive staff. Kept my family happy. Love this place. We'll be back for sure!

resp.text: Thank you for dining with us!

name: LOUIS FORTE
text: Excellent food and great service from Kaitlyn our waitress.  Would highly recommend this restaurant.

name: Debra Cyphert
text: Very eclectic restaurant. Food is very gourmet and beautifully plated. Don't ask for any changes. What's on the menu is how it is served. This spice lover was a little disappointed. Our waitress was awesome. I'd go back to have coffee and dessert to just chat with her!

resp.text: We are curious now. What did you want us to spice up? Our chefs are usually very accommodating in that way.  . .

name: Bekki Weaver
text: I heard that it was great, but I was underwhelmed. The hummus plate was good, as were the cucumbers on the octopus appetizer. I ordered a steak and ceasar salad both were just ok. If you're in Girdwood and want fine dining skip this one and go to Seven Glaciers where you won't be disappointed.

text: It was a super cute place! We stopped in for lunch on our way to seward. The staff were super friendly and attentive.  The ambiance was lovely with the open windows that let in the sunlight.  The music was also on point! We had the special salmon toast and the salmon salad caught fresh from the resurrection!

name: M M
text:
Wonderful menu.  I've had very positive and one horrible experience here.  With a reservation, they sat 2 adults and 2 young children in a small room with a tour bus.  The noise level was extreme, like a middle school lunch room.  One of my children is autistic.  We barely saw the server.  Management was kind enough to respond to my complaint, but there was no resolution or suggestions about how to avoid the situation in the future.  The evening was a nightmare.  I would recommend leaving if seated with a tour bus.

Update:
Date of meal: 7/24/2018, 5pm
We have not returned since.  Please suggest a way to avoid this happening in the future.  We were the only small table seated in a mind-crushingly loud room.  Your server could barely shout loud enough to communicate, yet no one suggested moving us to a different table.

resp.text: Could you tell us when you visited?

name: Benjemin Harris
text: Wow. Never had food this good from such an eclectic menu! I highly recommend the ramen bowl. Service was also top notch.

name: Shopping Bag
text: This is the place where Anchorage residents (who love out-of-this-world food) come to eat amazing dishes that please the palate, excite the tastebuds, and expand our culinary horizons. One of my top three restaurants in Anchorage... and this is a 30-minute drive from town! Worth the trip down and always worth the wait.

name: Athena Schreur
text: Sweet place, great food and drink menu options, with a very friendly staff. They are known for their yam fries served with jalapeno aioli, and it was worth the stop.

name: Rick Kelly
text: Absolutely one of my favorite restaurants. This is the place to go if you appreciate a great meal with a good selection of specials. I don't have a "go-to" meal here, because every single thing on the menu is what I  seem to crave that day.

name: Catherine Kenney
text: Wonderful!  From the wine selection to the excellent service to the outrageous olive oil chocolate cake!  The chef came out to visit and the wait staff were a team and helped complete the experience.  This is a must in Girdwood.....Give me a like below if this review was helpful.  Thanks~ Cat

name: John Howell
text: Very cozy, great environment. Everything youd expect from a small restaurant in Girdwood. All their meals are made with high quality organic clean ingredients. Our waiter was very friendly and caring. There is a section where you can sit with a perfect view of the mountain with high windows which is beautiful. No background music, nice and quiet.

name: Chuck Bradley
text: If you like Gourmet "healthy" food, you will like it here a lot. If you're in the mood for a steak or Burger this is not the place. Meal for two with no alcohol plus tip $120. The wait staff was fantastic.

resp.text: Our rib-eye steak is a mainstay on the menu year-round! At lunch we serve a delicious burger. Also, on Wednesday nights during the winter we offer multiple burger specials!

name: Connor Reynolds
text: Well, they have vegan options. Not many, but it's better than none. A little expensive, but it's all about the experience. Beautiful decor and the view is amazing. The vegan meals we ordered both tasted exactly the same, one of them was just in burrito form. The rest of our party seemed to enjoy their crepes and chili. Will definitely be back in the spring to try Jack Sprat again.

name: Quinn Lira
text: Beautiful warm spot to grab a bite. Excellent service, and the 01/01/20 burger was incredible!

name: Sierra Mills
text: Delicious and marvelous atmosphere!

name: Aditi Partani
text: What a beautiful place and wonderful people. We just stopped there for coffee and found out that they have great creative options for food as well. Never had that coffee before in my life in the woods. This is a must go place👍👍

name: rudd plate
text: Tonight dinner was lovely.  Worth the drive to girdwood.  I have eaten here more the a few times,  sometimes it's not so great, but today's dinner was the best I have had there in a long time.  The flank steak was very good, the both kinds of fries were excellent and crisp.  The service was excellent and timely.

name: William Day
text: Easily the best value to quality restaurant in Alaska. Top notch, local, seasonal ingredients, and the atmosphere radiates Girdwood’s ski-town warmth. Do not pass up this dinner.

name: C Lippert
text: Food wonderful, especially the borsh and wrap. Service was quietly attentive.

name: James Mcedwards II
text: Great food, great staff!

name: Ana Kokaurova
text: Love this place. If you like vegetables order the vegetable curry.

name: Brenna Dinkel
text:
Absolutely amazing customer service options for every one local sourced ingredients  great food and good atmosphere my favorite  restaurant in Alaska! It’s always an amazing treat to come here
Thank you so much!

name: Phillip Flippo
text: We ordered several items including their house ramen, everything we ordered looked really nice, everything we tasted was pretty bland and in the case of the ramen, it literally tasted like water. I've been here a few times with different folks over the years and this was the worst it's ever been.

name: Tim Newton
text: Amazing yam fries for appetizers, and incredible olive oil chocolate cake for desert. In between those, the food is "interesting". I don't mean bad, but more like exotic. Just not an exotic I seem to like, and I've tried several dishes now. So, for my tastes, the entrees aren't greatly satisfying. But definitely at the high end on prices.

name: C E
text: We went here for brunch shortly after arriving in AK.  The food was great and for the quality the prices seemed quite fair.  There are great views of the surrounding area.  There are loads of windows and some really cool paintings and stain glass hanging around.  Is a cozy place.  Would not hesitate to go again if in the area.

name: Leah Hercules-Jandres
text: Imaginative, delicious food, wonderful service and great ambience! My husband and I can for our Anniversary and this place did not disappoint!

name: Elizabeth Kiddle
text: I love this place! It always pushes me to try new tastes and flavors. We just went and had the classic yam fries, which are perfect for 4 adults, and they have a chocolate cake right now with mascarpone cheese that is to die for, worth every penny! My husband got a steak that was over done and the waiter was very gracious in having another one fired up for him that was medium rare. Couldn't tout this place enough. It's not cheap, but good food shouldn't be :)

name: Jessica Maves
text:
Food was delicious, as always. The atmosphere is perfect for a romantic evening or a ladies night out. I try to visit everyone I am in town.
PS Bring back the hash for breakfast, please!

I would go back, wonderful experience.

name: Aran Skates
text:
I hate to be negative but my experience here is so different than the reviews.   For 21 dollars tge wife got a lukewarm half full bowl of oily soup that they call curry.   Its cleverly disguised as healthy by adding a few shreds of carrot and some red quinoa.    Lipstick on a pig.    It doesnt even taste like curry and ive been all over southeast Asia.    Truly not healthy and a waste of time and really overpriced.   If this is "new American" cuisine id like an airplane ticket and a time machine.   There are plenty of better places to eat in girdwood.   Among those are the quick stop at the highway.   You can buy a burrito and p uhh t it in the microwave and it will be better than this charade of a meal.   Its the only dini g experience that left me mad and cheated.   Next customer please.   If youre serving this kind of food I really feel like youre just coasting at this point and relying on your glowing reputation.   That wont last forever.
I want to be clear.   I'm posting this to let the management know that there are problems with the way you run your restaurant.    I know its hard to serve food that doesnt rely on fat and salt and sugar for taste but this wouldnt fly in Thailand or Vietnam or Cambodia or for that matter wasilla.   There ive said it.   Ive had better curry in wasilla.   Game over.    I dont want to sou d like a pi$$ ant who likes to badmouth or whatever.   I'm sure youre heart is in the right place and whatnot but this was an infuriating experience.

I didnt drive back to girdwood and demand a refund.   But I felt like it and I should have.    My life would have been better if I had set those 21 dollars on fire and threw them out the window as I drive past girdwood.   This was served 14 july at 6 pm.    It ruined bastille day for me.

resp.text: Everything we make is from scratch in our kitchen. There are many variations of curry throughout the world. If you really dislike a meal, the proper thing to do is notify your server and ask for it to be fixed or replaced, so that we can help you have a good experience.

In fact, it was hands-down the best ramen I've had in Alaska. The broth is really what stood it apart, as it was full of umami and savory flavor. Other Asian restaurants have really let me down with their watery and bland ramen, but I was pleasantly surprised to find a great bowl at a New American restaurant in Girdwood!

The atmosphere was awesome, and I wish we could have stayed to sit down. We'll be back to get the full experience soon!

text: The bacon wrapped dates were terrific and that was it. We were so disappointed in the entrees that we couldn't believe it considering all the good things we had been told. We were on an spontaneous trip to Girdwood and we had been told several times by friends and strangers that this was one of the best restaurants in Alaska . . . I hope not. The location and ambience was nice and we were enjoying ourselves but the service was slow, really slow and the restaurant was not half full. Then we found ourselves fighting off mosquitos while we enjoyed our drinks . . . we were sitting inside. Oh it should be mentioned that the mosquitos problem persisted all night. My girlfriend ordered the bouillabaisse and I ordered the lamb. I wish they tasted half as good as the presentation. The lamb was of the worst I've ever eaten. The texture was fine but the flavor was awful. The best description of the bouillabaisse is that it tasted exactly like we remembered spagettios. It was so gross. At $120 this was one of the most disappointing restaurants we've eaten at in Alaska and if your friend recommends this place then your friend has bad taste.

text: The yam fries, which we started with, were thick cut, crispy, and the aioli to dip it in was excellent.  There were four of us, and each person remarked about the excellent quality of the food here.  It's not cheap, mind you.  This was the best high-end meal I've had in all of Alaska!  I had the duck which was juicy, tender, and wonderfully seasoned.  The other dishes ordered were the halibut, steak, bibimbap, and veggie curry.  Lastly, we all shared the spruce tips creme brulee, which was surprising and alternated between being pronounced and subtle in flavor.  The meal was around $250 for four of us, with one bottle of rosé.

name: Alexia Hines
text:
Beautiful, safe place to take a little stroll with family or even alone. The trails are made of compact rocks and are very well maintained. I went during the fall on a beautiful sunny day. I've never heard of a wheelchair safe trail, but on days like this you could definitely take a wheelchair if your heart desired.
Unfortunately they do not allow dogs on the trail, but maybe you could dress your dog as grandma and cart him around in the wheelchair. I dunno.

I loved the tons of signs telling all sorts of facts about the wildlife and there was never a moment where I feared I was lost or had to wonder how long the trail was.

The only thing that gave me a little bit of a hard time was finding the trail entrance.
When you enter the resort just stick to the main little road and follow the signs to the car museum entrance. You can park here.
There is a little trail between the car museum and the woods that leads you directly to the trail head.

The Wildlife Sanctuary was beautiful and relaxing and something I can see myself visiting very often. Hope you get a chance to enjoy it soon as well!

name: Alison Kelley
text: This is one of the best city parks you'll find in the US, and I've been to many throughout the Lower 48. You can always see moose and on rare occasions beat and the elusive lynx. The park is quite large with plenty of different trails, including single track as well as wide open Trails for those who are less comfortable in the woods. It's possible to go here everyday for a week and not be on the same Trail twice. They're places for biking, running, hiking, fishing, swimming, and even dog trials. There's an archery range and a Bionicle on field. The park is much more crowded in the winter when the junior Nordic skiing is well underway so I tend to go there at night in the winter where I can enjoy the ski trails to myself. The only complaints I have are 1) there aren't enough multi use trails considering 37% of Anchorage households own a dog, and 2) there aren't enough diagonal only ski trails. Most of the ski trails have been widened in the highways to accommodate large groups of States gears, which takes away from the beauty of the forest.
