text: My favorite hotel in Alaska. Great location, feels like a real hotel from a bygone era that has all the modern amenities. Right in the heart of downtown, with views of the sea, and the mountains; always fun if the volcanos are venting.

name: Mishell Harkey
text: Christmas atmosphere, restaurants and shops! Highly recommended.

name: Jessica James
text: The hotel is amazing. I'm a huge pirate fan and the artwork and decor was stunning. The pool was small and it was extremely warm in there, but my kids had a blast. They only have two official entrances to the pool, through a men's or women's locker room, but the concierge brought up someone to take us through the back so I didn't have to send my boys through the locker room alone. The room was extremely clean and beds very comfortable. I had a couple of drinks in the Crows Nest and the bartender even charged my phone for me so I could talk to my husband, who is deployed. Highly recommend getting reservations to breakfast if possible, because the cafe was packed. We ended up going to Snow City, which was only a block away. Parking around the hotel was difficult to find, so I recommend doing valet. You won't need your car, because there's so much within walking distance anyways.

name: Mitchell Selby
text: Great rooms, friendly staff. Hotel restaurants are convenient!

name: Izaak Philip Bruce
text: My room was excellent and I appreciated the hotel’s location in the city. Many of the places I wanted to visit were within walking distance.

name: Dow Jopp
text: Want to mention it is the absolute best place for cocktails and views. That being said, service recently for a business meeting was kinda poor. Unfront was decent, backside to get things boxed was way too long. It took 30 minutes to get a dessert boxed that I had initially asked boxed. Sat awhile before seeing server after dinner as well.

name: Linda Friend
text: Well I had nothing but problems when I first checked in. But I talked to a great guy named Brian and he, fixed all my issues and  upgradedmy room for the inconvenience. So i will definitely be returning here doe sure.

name: Tim Weinberg
text: Nice place to stay, it has everything

name: Christopher Zamora
text: This place is epic! In December they have a gingerbread display for the public! The staff are amazing, and the gift shops have a lot to give, and offer. I highly recommend this place because its is also inexpensive, but high quality.

name: Bridget Coolick
text: The staff was exceptionally friendly, the hotel is large and has many amenities, restaurants and seating areas.

name: Ashley DeHart
text: Employees are always friendly! This hotel is always clean, the food is delicious, and the athletic club is the absolute best! I am never disappointed with my visits here. The architecture is beautiful and has a boat vibe to its' design. Love it.

name: Jeanette Rose
text: Taking from our room window

name: Alicia Westberg
text: Best accommodations in the state of Alaska!

name: Amie Kirby
text: Clean, welcoming, lots of space. Would stay there again.

name: Tom O
text: A really nice hotel in downtown Anchorage.

name: Helen Walicka
text: What a delight to come back to a proper hotel after a few days travelling around Alaska. The front of house staff were extremely professional and surprisingly allowed us to check into a room on the club floor at 11.30. The lounge offered breakfast and evening drinks with a great view. Well worth staying.

name: Dmytro Fitilnikov
text: Clean rooms and nice service

name: Jim Ketcham
text: Great location, large, clean rooms with fridge (but no microwave). Excellent gift shops, 3 restaurants in house (one for breakfast and lunch only). Other restaurants in easy walking distance. We stayed here in connection with Princess cruises and connections to/from airport and cruise dock in Whittier were great.

name: Raquel Liliana
text: Didn't appreciate from desk service not as a guest staying but invited for dinner. However room service workers and kitchen staff extremely polite and friendly helpful. Rooms are beautiful

name: Jon Farmer
text: I was there for a work retreat. The restaurant at the top is amazing. The staff is great. The overall hotel is a great place. Very clean on the inside and friendly staff.

name: Kyle Foster
text: Restaurant at the top has nice views. Very spendy.

name: Roya Rakhshani
text: Great location,  close to restaurants and shopping downtown.

name: Nathan Smith
text: Not worth the money if all the amenities are shut down.

name: Peter McDougall
text:
I hate big corporate hotels, the Capt Cook is everything I shouldn't like, but what stands out is the positive staff, and the confident presentation. Couldn't fault it.

We ate in the posh restaurant on the top floor. Cocktails were good. Waitresses funny and helpful, food was the weak spot. I had buffalo steak which was yuk, we had king crab fritters which were battered deep fried rice balls that were disgusting and missing the key ingredient... CRAB!!!

The hotel is the high spot of Anchorage. Even if you don't stay, grab yourself a cocktail, enjoy the view. Take sandwiches...!

name: Thomas Larabee
text: Top notch classy place, probably one of the very best in Anchorage. Check online for discounts. It's definitely not a budget Hotel by any means.

name: Darko Sijakovic
text: Amazing and comfortable.

name: Karin Woofter
text: Great amenities and great food! Could increase the number of bathrooms though... long trek from meeting rooms, down a hall and then downstairs, then with only 3 stalls there

name: Kristin Mabry
text: Great hotel with thoughtful accommodations. Easy to have productive meetings!

name: Diego A. Vasquez Corzo
text: It was my wedding anniversary and I decided to treat my wife with some good food, a great view, and the restaurant definitely provided that. We got seated in front of a great view of the inlet. Food was excellent and I want to say Aaron, our server, was so helpful and accommodating with my allergy to mushrooms. I recommend this place.

name: Jamie Mahoney
text: Very nice hotel. Zachary at the front desk was very friendly and accommodating. The rooms were clean and comfortable and had great views. The housekeeping staff was on top of everything. Fletcher's restaurant had amazing food and atmosphere. I wouldn't recommend ordering room service from the hotel. I ordered twice and the food left a lot to be desired.

name: M M
text: I recommend visiting this hotel off season.  It's a fun place to stay, but the summer rates are totally outrageous, even by Anchorage standards.  The hotel is old and worn out.  In the summer it is hammered with group tours.  In the summer, look for a newer midtown hotel.  The Capt Cook bar Fletchers is one of the best in AK, but the Whale's Tale wine bar always disappoints.

name: Victor Rodriguez
text: if this place isn't what you would call a great spot with amazing service I don't know how else to explain it. Drago from Serbia is on point. It is his first night serving and absolutely did a phenomenal job. Try it, love it, and let them show you an amazing avocado tomato blue cheese salad

name: brian koliba
text: The service was impressive, everyone from the front desk to the bellman to the servers in the bars and restaurants gave stellar service and seemed happy in their jobs.

name: Arlene Acuna
text: Great vintage hotel with cimmon areas reminiscent of another era. Rooms spacious and updated. Good eateries and shops. Steps away from a nice waterside walk if you have the time.

name: Francis B
text: Beds are comfy and please. Staff is very polite and professional. Rooms have a ceiling fan and regular air conditioning. Some minor flaws, bathroom is subpar. The sink drain didn't keep up with the water flow and I can see it overflowing if you forgot to turn it off. Toilet flush is weak. The shower/tub doesn't have the handle head, but it has great water pressure.

name: Brian Deal
text: I could not have Imagined a better experience. Everyone went above and beyond to ensure we had a great stay. The hotel is beautiful. Since it is historic, the rooms might seem smaller than one might expect but it doesn't take anything away from it. You can't beat the views from some of the higher floors on a clear day.

name: David Sanders
text: I have to say that I love spending the night at the historic Captain Cook Hotel. With its great mountain, and inlet views, fine dining at the Crows Nest, and various other amenities, the "Cook" as it is called locally, offers much more than other hotels. Great place to book special events and meetings.

name: Ann Watts
text: Though this is one of the the best hotels in Anchorage, they know it and they're uppity about it.  My husband and I have stopped staying here because of the "we just don't care" attitude of many of the staff. Their restaurants all suffer from the same disease. Unless you like people looking down their noses at you, I recommend going to another hotel.  There are many great ones in town without all the baggage.

name: Christopher Cole
text:
We had a pleasant experience. Our room was clean and spacious, the towels were softer than normal, which I appreciated.

The only thing I would say is the place as a whole feels a bit out-dated.

The service was top notice, very impressed.

name: Rebecca White Wolf
text: Lots of history here. Beautifully kept. Great views!

name: Lyle Myre
text: The staff treat everyone with respect and do not stereotype based on first impressions.

name: Mike 907
text: The captain cook is by far the best hotel in anchorage they have so many awesome stores in the hotel as far as gift shops clothes, carvings and cool decoration items for your home they have two restaurants and a coffee shop called the cubbie. My first impression is shocking as I walk in two grant doors opened and welcomed by the valet and the floors are shiny and clean along with the entire lobby and decorated to the theme of christmas as I came in december just very beautiful would recommend this to all my friends also the staff at the front desk was very helpful and was detailed assuring us we wouldn't get lost finding our room. All around great experience thanks again!!!

name: Shopping Bag
text: While the hotel is slightly dated (and not quite historic yet) everything bout the rooms and the customer service here is 5-star. We are locals and this is the go-to place for our staycations or special occasions. Conveniently located near the core of downtown Anchorage and within 2 minutes of the spectacular Tony Knowles Coastal Trail.

name: Dana inknmyblood
text: Amazing service!!! Clean and great atmosphere. Food was on point but I could have had a larger portion for the price.

name: kirsten scharber
text: Upscale historic hotel in the heart of downtown Anchorage. So many Alaskan adventures within walking distance! Or if you prefer to stay in, there are 3 restaurants, gift shops, a fitness center with swimming pool, sauna and spa all available daily- some open late. A beautiful hotel!

name: shahab aria
text:
Beautiful place, good location as a HOTEL.
But as a restaurant, DO NOT RECOMMEND IT AT ALL!!!!
Quality of the food is not bad (if you can tolerate chicken that are dryer than mcd's chicken nuggets. But the prices are in the sky if you compare it with the quality of the food that you get and the staff are rude ( server litterally throw my food in front of me!!!).
SO AS A HOTEL LOBBY IS A GOOD PLACE BUT AS A RESTAURANT, DISASTER IS THE WORD THAT COMES TO MY MIND.

name: Janel Betlej
text: They treated me as a queen! Room was clean and quiet. Love this place!

name: Marc Theiler
text: I adore Captain Cook hotel. Our family always stays here. It's rich in history and old school service.

name: Mike Gerbman
text: Great service, exceptional restaurants, wonderful room and staff, walking distance to most downtown areas.

name: Lyndzee Fix
text: Wonderfully beautiful environment, fantastic, friendly staff. All around amazing place.

name: Christine Hohf
text: Rooms especially on concierge  are small and outdated and overpriced. Also no extra service on weekends.

name: Chester Ince
text: Service was outstanding, food was delicious

name: Jeni Brown
text: Great view. Good staff. Coffee could use more of.

name: Neve Studios
text: Crow's Nest is Amazing.

name: Rick Benken
text: Incredible views, excellent food and service!

name: Dawn Dulebohn
text: The rooms are nice, the location is great but this hotel is SO HARD TO NAVIGATE!

name: Burt Napierala
text: great place for dinner

name: Linda Rusche
text: We have attended to company Christmas parties here and the space was large and nicely decorated. Buffet servers ranged from excellent to -I hate you and this job. The seasonal decor throughout the lobby etc is great for some selfies.

name: Karl Byriel
text: Room was noisy due to lift backing onto it, barely slept at all. Other rooms probably OK.  Room was spacious enough.  Didn't have any view.

name: Paul E. Turner Ph.D.
text: I love the hotel, the options in the hotel, the access to downtown, and when you land a good room, the views can be stunning. are just wonderful.  The hotel front desk is always responsive, solve a lot of problems, and are courteous seemingly to everyone – even rude customers. Solid breakfast, lunch, and dinner options. The health club is first class and separated by gender. The garage next-door makes for ease of parking in the winter.

name: Carl Davis
text: Very nice hotel with great shops & love the decor!!!  Also, folks working there were very nice and helpful and the location is great and close to the coastline along with being nearby a lot of outside shop options!!! Recommend checking out if in town!!!

name: Carl Tiefenthaeler
text: Great location and Nice hotel and staff.  Within walking distance too 49th State Brewery, a must stop for comfort food and Drinks.

name: Terika Kons
text: Finally got a seat at the bar at The Crows Nest... best view in town... and the drinks & apps aren't too bad either!

name: Kitty Nazuruk
text: I loved the stay, the room is nice and big. The view is amazing.

name: Joseph Eatherton
text: Wonderful staff.  Very nice atmosphere.

name: GO-GO OG
text:
Whales tale was a complete disappointment...
Had to send chicken back frozen inside..
Had to send burger back TWICE!!!
LEFT HUNGRY!! FLETCHER'S WAS GREAT!!

name: Jaella Morris
text: The location is excellent. You can walk to all of the downtown attractions and amenities. The hotels restaurants all have wonderful atmospheres, food, and drinks. Their rooms are updated and very comfortable. All of the staff goes out of their way to make your time there a great experience.

name: will shumway
text: This hotel is probably the best in Anchorage, all the shops on the lower level, the amazing barber downstairs, and very capable staff set it apart from their competition.

name: Stephen Blankenship
text: Always a wonderful breakfast at a reasonable price. Great staff, too. All in all an outstanding experience.

name: Nicki Keener
text: Went to Fletcher, quality of food is not good but pricy.

name: Brent Freiburger
text: Great older vibe that modern hotels just don't have

name: Boyd Soule
text: Older building and rooms hit the beds are very comfortable and I got a good night's rest. In the heart of downtown so very convenient. Would recommend staying here and would come again.

name: Julienne Cwidak
text: Great staff and rooms. Restaurants are a fun place with fine dining

name: Catherine Kenney
text: Lovely, historical lounge that looks put over the skyline of Anchorage.  The woodwork alone is worth the trip along with the beautiful art work that adornes the walls.  The service was top notch and we were even able to speak to their Somalia regarding the best of the wine selections.  I absolutely adore the French Wines that are imported my a company out of Big Lake called Heirloom Wines.  Try a bottle, you won't be dissapointed!  Allow extra time to soak up the history and reservations are needed.  Cheers and enjoy!

name: Mandy Gambel
text: I absolutely love the hotel captain cook. It's a beautiful hotel. Rooms are always clean as a whistle and well taken care of. Staff is pleasant and very good at their jobs. We've been going for overnight trips for many years and will continue to do so!

name: Bre Fox
text: Wonderful Hotel, great staff and friendly service. I especially enjoy Fletchers!

name: David Enzel
text: Comfortable hotel in the heart of Anchorage. The decor is dark - too dark for my taste. The bathroom was small but good. The lighting in the bathroom was weak. The bed was comfortable but a bit softer than I like. The location is superb. The reason I gave it 3 stars is the value for money. My room was over $300 a night. I know Alaska is expensive but this hotel I my opinion is expensive for what it offers.

name: matt knowlton
text: Great hotel.  comfortable rooms, great staff.

name: alice bennett
text: This hotel has the best location in Anchorage. We stayed one night before our flight home. The beds were very comfortable and room very clean. This is a classic hotel is a great downtown location. Perfect if you want to stay in a prime spot so you can walk to everything you need.

name: Jessica Rushmeyer
text: Great views!!! Rooms were clean and my room was upgraded because the room i had they didn't have it ready.   This hotel does have room service which is always awesome! Front desk was friendly and helpful.. I would recommend this hotel for families with young children. O yeah before i forget there is  a rather small pool there as well.

name: Kimberly Weber
text: Our annual visit to the Gingerbread village

name: Greg Eschenlohr
text: We have stayed here several times and thoroughly enjoyed it each time. The location of the hotel is perfect. Lots of restaurants nearby. The rooms are clean and comfortable. The views are incredible.

name: Michelle Mitton
text: Nicest hotel in Anchorage with beautiful teak interior and good restaurants such as the Crow's Nest. Also good location for seeing downtown sights.

name: christopher Blas
text: When to have drinks at the bar, service was great and selection was outstanding

name: Ryan Fenn
text: Fun older hotel in downtown anchorage! Robes in every room!

name: Christopher Giron
text: Great breakfast getaway during long layover.

name: Z. S. N.
text:
These two young men were experts of their craft. They held it down in there together like a solid unit.
I was denied oil change service up the street at the other place because they were "done for the day".... at 4 o clock.
I honestly was skeptical of going here but i am going to be a return customer. It was only about 30 minutes, they taught me some neat things about my Subaru too. And didnt push anything unnecessary on me to buy that i didnt want or need. I paid for an oil change and thats what i got. 10 stars will be back next time.

name: GUTTA WAYZ TV
text: The place is legit luxurious, if you spent your money here then you spent it well. They have a great shuttle service for regular guests and flight crew guests ✈️ to accommodate needs.. Rooms are large and spacious. Great view, play piano??? Show off to your lady friends. Exquisite dinning. #YLG #DaTruf (If I wrote it then it's tru)

name: Darwin Feakes
text: Historic Grand Hotel. Room was comfortable and the bed was delightful.

name: Bill Duffey
text: Nice hotel in Anchorage  -- great bars in hotel and within walking distance

name: Frank Trotter
text: First off - this is a cruise ship oriented hotel.  Be prepared for the clientele.  Other than that the location was perfect in downtown Anchorage, and the rooms were nice.  The club lounge had drinks and food with limited hours which was nice.

name: Erika Douglass
text: Went for an event and was dismayed to find that restrooms were on a separate floor from the ballroom. $10 for a glass of wine seemed extremely steep for a catered event, but the bartender was great and recommended a dive bar around the corner. The food was excellent as well.

name: Paul Allen
text: Lovely place to stay and many places are within walking distance. Great views

name: Roger Gaston
text: This is an excellent choice for an hotel and the restaurant here is superb. It is located right in the downtown area, close to the Alaska Train Depot and all of the amenities. The staff is fantastic... Rooms are great.

name: Bo Stahl
text: We stayed here in the winter and we were so hot, we couldn't sleep. There is no AC and we weren't even able to control the heater.  We called staff to see if they would fix it and we were informed, there wasn't anything they could do. We won't stay here again.

name: John McFalls
text: Attended a private event for an annual party.  I've given the hotel captain cook 5 stars for their rooms and other events in the past I was not as impressed by the staff and food as I have been previously.  The event site was impeccably maintained as always.

name: Stefanie Mullan
text: Everyone from the front desk to the housekeeping staff are all very helpful and polite. Thoroughly enjoyed our stay there.

name: Daniel WInters
text: Very kind people. Excellent service.

name: Remona Koop
text: Utterly beautiful hotel! Several shops to choose from for shopping.  Room was a very nice size, and very clean. Staff was helpful and very courteous.

name: Lindsey
text: Swanky steam room/sauna/dressing room. Amazing breakfast at the restaurant there. Neat lil 'nugget of Anchorage

name: Dawn McBurney-Hibben
text:
Fletcher's  Restaurant in The Hotel Captain Cook is excellent!  It's not fancy, but the food is fabulous, and affordable.
The salads, pizzas, meat loaf, pastas, and key lime pie are exceptional.  Yummy food, go get some.

name: ernest howard
text: It's one of our oldest hotels,  kind of dated,  but it's classy and the service is excellent.   If I were spending two weeks in Anchorage and someone else was paying for it,  that's where I would stay.

name: Elizabeth Pruitt
text: This hotel has some misses as far as cleanliness goes and quality service. The rooms are absolutely amazing. I would definitely come back to this hotel for the room quality alone but not so much the people or service. Not the nicest staff and not the cleanist of areas. Pretty good food in the restraunts. Wish the hotel followed through on my requests as well, even after I double checked them three times.

name: Chris R
text: We had dinner at the crow's nest to celebrate a birthday. Service was wonderful and the views were pretty good. I had the Bison t-bone while the wife had the salmon. Overall the food was alright, with some things better than others. We went for the experience and it was satified.

name: Scott C
text: Great hotel. I always stay here when visiting Anchorage. Close to great restaurants. Parking is right next door and the hotel has awesome views. Priced the same as other hotels

name: Patti Armanini
text: The beds were great, room service breakfast was fast and good. Bathroom was surprisingly small.

name: Gradey Iverson
text: A bit pricey but has good food at the hotel.

name: paolo polizzy
text: Continously setting the industry's standards around Anchorage and beyond. Top place in town .

name: Douglas Ryan
text: The best hotel and restaurants in town.

name: Kennedy Myers
text: Had a really nice experience staying 2 nights here. Clean and quiet rooms with friendly staff in a beautifully historic, centrally-located hotel. Would give 5 stars but no parking available -- street parking only.

name: Wilson Cullor
text: An excellent modern hotel with an oldschool Alaskan feel. Weather it's a romantic weekend or a business trip the Captain Cook will treat you right.

name: Nelson Montalvo
text: Never stayed there. Only did a 4K race. Just hung out in the lobby area. Place is beautiful and clean. Legit

name: Lewis Kelly
text: Lovely hotel rooms

name: Joe Stout
text: Upscale hotel, but the price is fair. I did have a few issues like a dirty towel left on the back of the door, and a slow drain in the shower. Things I just didn't expect to happen here. But otherwise a nice hotel. Get a room on an upper floor. The views are spectacular.

name: Elizabeth Brown
text: Enjoyed visiting the shops in the hotel prior to my company's Christmas party. Food at the event was great. Was able to find close handicapped parking on the street. One downfall was the bathrooms which need a renovation.

name: andrea longenecker
text: This is a beautiful and amazing place!! We loved it!! We even had need of two fold out beds on night 2 and they brought the second one with no extra fees, so we had the greatest most blessed slumber party with our grand babies the second night there!! And the pizza place is great, and was so good, we had room service pasta was nice, but the pizza was Amazing!! My granddaughter wanted ice cream late and it wasn't available BUT the bartender suggested the Mississippi mud pie and it was even better than ice cream. And it was not bank breaking, for pizza and pie cost $25 so we pay that for just pizza in Kenai, so value was great!! Great experience!!  Thank you Captain Cook Hotel for a Great Anniversary weekend!!!

name: christa davis
text: Bar area had slow service and food was ehhh,. Definitely not anything to write home about.

name: Lonny Cruff
text: Just the absolute best place to stay in Anchorage.

name: Master Decker
text: We went to the whales tail for drinks and fun after our gender reveal party. Music was good, service wasn't bad.

name: Rebecca Kopperud
text: A wonderful boutique hotel. Great service and location

name: Deborah Trimmer
text:
Beautiful.  Get a room at the top overlooking the inlet. Pay attention to the detail throughout the hotel even if not a guest - an Anchorage jewel.
.

name: Carl Eady
text: great rooms, and shops food is awesome bar and lounge friendly

name: Team Inner Peace
text: Excellent service and food

name: Julia Cazares
text: Went to the Crow's Nest for dinner for our anniversary and had a pretty good time. The food was a bit lacking compared to our previous visits, but still above average. Drinks were fantastic, but the bananas foster felt a bit rushed (it was still delicious, though!).

name: Chris Walden
text: We ordered baked salmon and the grilled sampler plate. Both dishes were outstanding. I usually refrain from 5 stars for those special places, and this is it. Food was delicious and the service was awesome!

name: Phil Hofland
text: Gingerbread house display for 2019 was amazing.

name: steve kennard
text: Great view  room was very quiet and comfortable

name: Cam Kay
text: I went to the Trick or Treat event at the Cook. Kids and parents were decorating cupcakes and having a good time. I was able to take a few pictures of people happy and having a great time.

name: Just Jessee
text: The building itself is quite old and does not appear to have gone under any "refreshes" on the outside or inside lobby/meeting rooms. The meeting room I was in was quite dimly lit despite having a full "chandelier" style light hanging from the center of the room. Everything was slightly yellow in hue due to the lights. I can't recall the color of the walls but I remember thinking that everything might seem less dated if the walls were refreshed.

name: Paul Logan
text: Wonderful staff. The rooms are dated but comfortable. The location and staff make this a great hotel.

name: Joelle Carson
text: I was a part of a tour, did not interact with hotel staff. Can't comment. The two restaurants we dined at were awful. Service and quality.

name: Elvira Morozova
text: In the heart of the downtown of Anchorage.

name: Harold Yutuc
text: Hotel is located downtown and parking can be difficult during busy times. Hotel houses a few restaurants. One is Crows Nest which is on top of the hotel and is considered high end dining. The other is The Whale's Tail wine bar. It's a very relaxed atmosphere which usually has live music and DJs during the evenings with a small dance floor.

name: Ryleigh Slone
text: Crow's nest is amazing!

name: Bill Payer
text: Cozy, lots of old people.

name: kimberly allen
text: Two good restaurants and a breakfast cafe,  several gift stores, an activewear store,  and a chocolate store with amazing chocolate delights. This hotel is used by locals and government regularly.  And,  all the famous people stay here.

name: Jerry Brower
text: Amazing rooms with great views. The restaurants inside the building offer spectacular food.

name: Julia Lessie
text: Its located right in the heart of Anchorage Downtown and close to the 5th Avenue Mall,close to the Museum and more department stores

name: Ginger Hutcherson
text: Beautiful city views. Nice room...carpet a little worn. Terrible parking. Staff a little "snooty".

name: Phil Wight
text: Fine dining and drinks. The price often outstrips the value, but to each their own. Historic hotel that helped Anchorage prove itself as a modern American metropolis after the 64 earthquake.

name: Jeffrey Peterson
text: I went to the Whales Tail to see Meagan Hayes and The Gamma Rays. They are a great band and the bar had a fun atmosphere. Service was friendly and fast enough. I never had to wait for a new drink.

name: Jesse Reeves
text:
Good people. VERONICA THE SERVER. Romanian Yes you rock
Good food. Crab spread. HUMMMMY
Good Drink. And for desert Brandy Ice of course

name: Kodi •&•
text: What an amazing place to go to, I absolutely love this place

name: TinaMarie Chaney
text: Best hotel in Anchorage. Beautiful shops, great restaurants. Friendly help. Nice rooms.

name: Jeffrey Leyrer
text: Great everything besides the pricing!

name: Robert Juckett
text: Great hotel. Really nice rooms that have some good views of the city. Also has some great bars in the lobby area, whale's tail and Foster's

name: Walter O'Hayer
text: Great historic location, very comfortable, and unbeatable location.  Only concern is over the consistency of water temperature in the shower.

name: Pink Anderson
text: Awesome hotel, fun to see the gingerbread village. Requested a room with fireworks view for 12/31. Could book a room, but no guarantee of view. Seems like my cash on hand for a view room would be worth something, but was not the case. Went to Marriott for guaranteed view.

name: Zeinab Takbiri
text: I was at it's restaurant and halibut dish was amazing.

name: Kimberly Fitzgerald
text: Captain Cook is a landmark in Anchorage! GREAT restaurant's, wine bar, and the Cafe has incredible breakfasts! JR. Suite was perfect for pre-party prior to company celebration

name: M Cohrs
text: Showing some age, but a recent refurb helps. Good staff.

name: Sean Ryan
text: This place is definitely 5 star. 5 star everything. They have multiple classy resturants,  mini strip mall inside, giant conference rooms, athletic club, pool, and elegant rooms. The Captain Cook is first class all the way.

name: Ronnie Carroll
text: Fletcher's bar was great, make sure to ask about the pulls on the beer drafts

name: John Hupp
text: The pork chop dinner was delicious

name: Lisa Cook
text: Very good food and service

name: Zachary Washburn
text: The restaurant on the ground floor has superlative customer service and is one of the best places to have breakfast in downtown Anchorage.  Also, during the Christmas season you can find the largest and best gingerbread house display I have ever seen!

name: Doug Early
text: Very nice.  Get the junior suite

name: Chelsea Graf
text: Always a welcoming, relaxing, and fulfilling experience; from the front desk staff to the fresh linens everything about the Hotel is elegant and inviting.

name: Wellness Medical
text: Great staff, very nice traditions, didn't stay long enough. Will book another stay in future summer visit.

name: J Pale
text: I do not know if this is entirely a fair assessment since most of the hotel seemed to be closed for renovations/upgrades.  The mornong and evening room service was unavailable, The Crows Nest was closed as was Fletchers...but the rooms were comfy, if not a little dated.  The price for one evening was fair (we had a junior suite) and the staff was corteous and helpful!

name: Collette Owens
text: Very clean

name: Namiko Asuka
text: Great service, clean rooms, and a beautifully designed interior make this hotel an ideal place to stay. It's close to everything important in Anchorage too, so that's a bonus.

name: paul netzel

Situated at the downtown Anchorage. Walking distance to museum, the theater, the shops, the restaurants, the visitor center, Saturday market, the train station, the Ulu factory, etc.

One of the tallest and historic hotel in the city. We were very lucky to stay at 18th Fl. The view is gorgeous~ The weather is beautiful and we can even see the mountains!!

All the staffs are very professional and friendly. They are always there when we need them.

There are 3 towers in this hotel. There are a few restaurants/bars inside the hotel as well. Basement has the gym but have to pay a small fee to use the facility.

The room is clean and well maintained. Did I mention they have FREE WiFi~

Overall the experience is great!

I had to call serval times as the internet speeds we're not usable, less than 1mb/s (they claim it's high speed). I was finally told it was due to the large volume of guests. If you are considered one of the most high end hotels in Anchorage, you should have enough bandwidth to cover every guest. Another issue is that there is no free guest parking, only valet at $30/24hrs or park on the street where parking is also charged, almost at the same rate. Overall, a wonderful place to visit for meals, but I would consider looking at other similar hotels in the area.

text:
As a travel agent: This is one of the most popular hotels in Anchorage. It gets very crowded & the staff is polite but seem overworked.
This is where large groups tend to stay for the free wifi, Alaskan flare in the lobby and terrific if not the best WIFI in town.
There are many room types including one with 3 bathrooms. Each room has black out drapes since the sun shines most of the summery days. If you need anything there are plenty of shops inside to get your Alaskan souvenirs, or forget your bathing suit and toothbrush. They have art work to tell the history. The view is outrageous and you can watch seaplanes take off!
I stayed here pre-post my cruise and enjoyed the comfy room with just one bathroom.

name: Anna M. B.
text:
(Translated by Google) We were looking for a place to stay in Anchorage on the way to Dinaly National Park. We booked the hotel 3 months before arrival because the price was still ok compared to other hotels here in town, where it cost 280 € / night without breakfast.
We arrived in Seward with the cruise in the morning and were taken to Anchorage for 3 hours with a previously booked shuttle bus.
A TIP: Save yourself the one night in the city and rent a car at the airport in Anchorage or in Seward directly at the terminal. Take a quick drive through Anchorage, eat perhaps the best fish and chips in the world in Humpys ($ 15) and enjoy the more rare nature than the city.
Breakfast at the hotel additional $ 12. However, there is a café in the hotel where you can get delicious muffins. There is a coffee machine with coffee tabs in the room.
The hotel has 3 high towers and thus 500 rooms. Ours wasn't finished until 3pm.
There are a couple of restaurants in the hotel complex.
Air conditioning not to turn off, which is typical for America. Only one socket in the bathroom and with a USA adapter, which you should definitely take with you from Germany.

(Original)
Wir haben nach einer Übernachtungsmöglichkeit in Anchorage auf dem Weg zum Dinaly Nationalpark gesucht. Wir haben das Hotel 3 Monate vor Ankunft gebucht, weil es preislich noch ok war im Vergleich zu anderen Hotels hier in der Stadt, wobei es 280 € / Nacht ohne Frühstück kostete.
Wir sind morgens mit dem Kreuzfahrt in Seward angekommen und 3h mit einem vorher gebuchten Shuttlebus nach Anchorage gefahren worden.
EIN TIP: Sparren Sie sich die eine Übernachtung in der Stadt und mieten Sie sich gleich ein Auto am Flughafen in Anchorage oder in Seward direkt am Terminal. Fahren Sie kurz durch Anchorage, essen vielleicht die besten Fish and Chips der Welt in Humpys (15 $) und genießen dafür die seltene Natur als die Stadt.
Frühstück im Hotel zusätzlich 12$. Es gibt jedoch ein Café im Hotel direkt wo es leckere Muffins gibt. Kaffemaschine mit Kaffeetabs gibt es nämlich auf dem Zimmer.
Das Hotel hat 3 hohe Türme und somit 500 Zimmer. Unser war trotzdem erst um 15:00 fertig.
Es gibt ein paar Restaurants im dem Hotelkomplex.
Klimaanlage nicht auszuschalten, was typisch für Amerika ist. Steckdose nur eine im Bad und mit einem USA Adapter, den Sie sich unbedingt aus Deutschland mitnehmen sollten.

text: This is a wonderful little place to visit. We love visiting national parks and this one did not disappoint. It has a lot of short paths that are perfect for people who aren't looking for a huge hike. It's a nice escape. The downtown area is fun to walk around as well!

name: Mallika Rao
text:
Best place to stay while in Denali. It's a 84 acre property with it's own restaurants, bar, fire pits, live music, gift shops and shuttle. HiFi place to start luxurious in Denali. I only wish their WiFi was better, especially when they charge such a big price per night and boast off as a luxury stay. Sure people come to Alaska for a nature experience but when a place like this hosts bar and live music and fancy restaurant which is already far from rustic experience they might as well invest in better and decent WiFi infrastructure. There is literally no wifi in most of the chalet. It's not what they promise on the website. We had LTE so we were fine connecting with family while on vacation.
Otherwise it's a great place to stay!!!

name: Walter Walker
text: It is exactly what you would expect from a nature preserve lodge, semi comfortable rooms. You probably won't spend much time in your room but the main  lodge is nice, affording numerous eating opportunities. The Serbian restaurant across the street is very good.

text: Great facilities, nice layout, near other restaurants and shopping. We had nice dinner last night and Starbucks this morning.  What more could you ask for.

name: Josh S
text: Awesome little group of restaurants and gift/ photo shops. We went to dinner and a show at the Golden Nugget outside the fire pit area. Surprisingly good food and drinks! They served bottomless bacon mashed potatoes, and all you could eat salmon and beef. Actors were VERY good and interacted with the audience, though not to the point of being annoying or embarrassing. Full 5 Stars for sure! Music was also extremely well done. Again, surprised and impressed!

name: Ankush Gupta
text:
Budget option to stay close to the Denali national park. We stayed at the lodge and the room was extremely comfortable. There is no AC in the room but we got fan. There is also no wifi in room but there is WiFi on common areas. There was a big Creek right behind the lodge with great views. Plenty of places to eat as well and we ate right across the road with fantastic live music.

Totally recommend staying here if you are visiting Denali.

name: Anita Kingree
text:
First of all, let me begin by saying we read reviews and studied up on this trip before booking rooms. With that being said, we got exactly what we expected at McKinley Chalet Resort, if not more. McKinley Chalet Resort is a little older, but this is ALASKA! People expecting to have a 5-Star Hotel experience probably need to go elsewhere. In Alaska most hotels don't have air conditioners. It simply isn't needed. I have seen a lot of reviews of people angry that there is no in-room wi-fi here. You are in ALASKA....the last frontier....wilderness all around you...You are the base of Denali National Park! I, for one, was HAPPY to turn my devices off and just enjoy this amazing experience! With all the complaining, I assumed there wouldn't be cell phone signal, but there was full signal here, so I could still use data to access anything I needed. There was also still wi-fi in the public areas. The only negative I could really see is that we were on the second floor, and there were no elevators in my building that I could find. We had some really heavy suitcases to lug up a flight of stairs, but it wasn't that big of a deal to my husband and I. However, I could see it being a problem if you were disabled, or had trouble walking stairs or carrying heavy loads. If this is the case, be sure to request a room at ground level.
The buildings were also very scattered out (This is a resort, not a hotel, so there were many different buildings). However, the resort provides a free shuttle service to get you from place to place, and I never went outside without a shuttle being there waiting for anyone who needed it. We only used the shuttle once, to go down to the public square for dinner one night. It was waiting for us when we stepped outside.
Our rooms at the resort were clean, and the room was actually broken up into 2 bedrooms which we didn't expect. That would have been a very pleasant surprise if our kids had been along for the trip.
In summary, the place is older and isn't going to look like a fancy new hotel in a large city. Please book understanding that you are going to a remote town in the final frontier of our the United States....a place that wasn't even a state until 1959. Enjoy this untouched land! There's not much of it left in the great scheme of things!

name: Phil
text: We enjoyed are stay and the registration staff were helpful in recommending additional sights to see. We scheduled the Flight to the Denali Summit but unfortunately weather prevented the flight from leaving the airport. We were promptly refunded our fares. The gift shop has a selection of stone and ivory carvings make by Alaskans and Native Alaskans. We purchased a jacket with Denali embroidered and it was an excellent price compared to other shops in the area including their claims for 'deep discounts '. This is the place to stay but book early as rooms are taken quicky. They are also conscious about reducing the amount of plastic water bottles and now sell water in aluminum containers.

text: Great stay. Nice, Neat, and Very Comfortable.

text: Gorgeous resort! If you want to stay in Denali, don’t go to Princess, come here! Great food, beer, wine, signature cocktails, gift shops, entertainment, tours and more!

name: J R
text: Priced as a resort, but relatively dumpy and no parking or WIFI.  We had hoped to have a nice stay outside Denali, and at nearly $500 for 2 nights had splurged for a resort.  Unfortunately, this place was nothing but a seriously overpriced motel...unless you're a cruise passenger on a Holland America cruise.  I paid for a room with 2 queen beds, but on check in was told I was getting a room with a double and a twin and a sofa bed.  Not what I paid for.  When I requested what I had actually reserved and prepaid for, a room with 2 queen beds, I was told baldly that those are given to the cruise passengers, who are given preference since the hotel is owned by a cruise line.  Then the room turned out to be on the second floor of cabin D...no elevator.  It's a motel they falsely bill as a resort. The room was tiny, with a double bed crammed against 1 wall and a twin crammed against the other, with room for only 1 suitcase in the room (the others had to sit on the sofa bed in the other tiny room).  The bathroom is too small for a sink...that's in the bedroom. I asked for either help with our luggage or to borrow a luggage cart, but was told that was a no go.  They did help the hordes and hordes or cruise passengers streaming onto the property by the busload, however.  The parking was also abysmal.  There are not enough parking spaces anywhere near your room if you drive and don't arrive by cruise bus, so they told us to either park at the gift shops on the other side of the highway or to park about 3/4 of a mile away, down a super steep hill.  This stay is a serious waste of money--dingy, small, not very clean, and super unfriendly and unaccomodating.  Oh, and to top it all off, there's no WIFI (free or otherwise) in the rooms.

name: Amy Grace
text: We stayed in the Ridge View Junior suites which opened in 2020. The design and large space is appealing (modern rugged). We were here during a heat wave, so needed to use their ceiling and oscillating fans, because there is no air conditioning. We were on the 3rd floor, but there are no elevators. You walk into the second floor, so floors one and three require walking up or down stairs. Shuttles to the property are available in front about every 15 minutes.

name: Dave Schurman
text: 5 stars isn't enough. Our room is large and nicely furnished.  Not you typical hotel room. The grounds are beautiful and well maintained.  Staff was friendly and helpful. Shuttle service all around the property.  The square has several restaurants and shops plus a large gas fire pit where you could roast complimentary marshmallows and make Smores.

name: Donald Robak
text:
I was impressed by the clean, comfortable room. Food service was nearby, as well as frequent shuttle service to and from the lodging. Sometimes there was a significant wait for service.
It appears that everything was operated under the auspices of Holland America.
We were there in late September and many facilities were, or had already shut down for the season.

name: Ashley Joy Vedrode
text: Ann Marie and Sam provided top notch service. We nearly missed our train due to miscommunication. Ann Marie tried to work it out for us, and got Sam to drive us. Good conversation on the way to the depot. The Chalets are nice - very cute. Convenient location,  good service, clean.

name: Sara McCaffree
text: Lovely place. Great beds. Had a good meal at the brew pub, which was better than the steak house. I think the property shuttle probably takes longer than walking. It's across from a quaint strip of locally owned shops where we ate lunch (Prospectors Pizza) and grabbed snacks for the next leg of the journey. Felt very much like a nice resort in Colorado. Has firepits with smores available. Sadly we couldn't see Denali but apparently that's rare. Excursions sounded fun but we didn't have time. Wish we could have stayed longer!

name: Paul Marshalek
text: Great resort with nice size rooms and friendly staff.  The views are great and a short ride to the ton of Talkeetna.

name: Sheila McDonald
text: Beautifully located property with clean accomodations, nice entertainment, with plenty of dining and loubging options. One of the best features is the knowledgeable staff about sightseeing opportunities, plenty of transport options, and reliable access to the national park. I highly recommend because of their location.

name: Aaron Mason
text: Booked a room with 2 queen beds but got aroom with 1 queen and I twin.  That is challenging with kids. Other than that the staff was great and the hotel is comfortable and well maintained. We really enjoyed nights waking by the river and hanging out by the fires in Denali Square.

name: Vicki Kuhl
text: This place was a perfect pick for my trip to Denali. The beds were soft and comfortable.  The rooms were cozy and well planned. I was in the "cottonwood" building as there are several buildings that house guests. Be prepared to walk but know that they do have shuttles. Music in the p m around outdoor fire rings under the stars, and maybe a s'more or a beverage and dinner and you are set! Dont forget to mingle!

name: Val G
text: The grounds, restaurants and square (center of the place) are beautiful!  Rooms (Canyon lodge) were horrible!  Certainly no better than a Motel 6!  Cheap, and unattractive.  Don't expect quaint, rustic or lodge style rooms or you will be dissppointed like we were.  And we had no view of any kind from our room.  Service was slow and not very good.  The entertainment at the dinner show was good but the food was sub-par.  Owned and ran by Holland America Cruiseline.  They can and need to do better! We would not recommend this place!

text: Scenic location, mix of order and newer buildings.  Rooms can be noisy, maintenance drive ATVs all hours of the day and night.  Bathroom exhaust fans are ridiculously loud.  Service in on site restaurants we're inconsistent.

name: Sharon Chorost
text: This hotel, as well as the Princess Wilderness Lodge next door, is owned by Holland America Cruise line. We stayed in the Canyon Lodge building, which had a nice lobby area, but the room itself had just the bare minimum. There was no desk and chair as you would find in most other hotels. We requested an extra blanket and a refrigerator and the hotel was accommodating. There is a property shuttle that comes around to take you to the different buildings, since some of them are a little ways from the main lodge. There is a "dinner shuttle" that will take you between the McKinley Chalet and the Princess Wilderness Lodge, but will not take you to any of the shops or restaurants across the street (not owned by Holland America). If I had not been on the land/cruise tour, I probably would have stayed at the Princess instead. There really aren't many other hotels to choose from in Denali.

name: Robin Dern
text: There is no place on earth that puts me square quite like Denali National Park. If you are looking to be awed or inspired this is the place. I had read about the park before first visiting 25 years ago and, quite honestly, no words could have prepared me for the size and beauty I came across. Of course the mountain, Denali, along with the abundance of wildlife, are the reasons many people are sure to include the park in their travel plans when visiting. For me though, I’ve come to appreciate the small rocks, abundance of mushrooms and wildflowers, the paths to creek beds and rivers and the sunrises and sunsets. While the Visitor Center and park services are open from mid-May to mid-September only the park remains open to a certain point for skiing and winter hiking...perhaps mushing as well (though you will want to check). I have it on good authority that March is an excellent time to visit is you are Aurora hunting. There is also a Winter Festival each year. In the summer season the area is hospitable to campers, hikers or those who want to bus in. There are several bus options. Cars/RV’s aren’t allowed past a certain portion of the road. The only exception to that is the annual lottery open to Alaska residents. Winners are able to drive the road with their own vehicles. It is an excellent opportunity and I urge all Alaskans to sign up online. Don’t miss this park if you’re visiting Alaska!

name: Rooz Izadi
text: It’s a well-managed place to start your Denali adventure. If you’re gonna wild camp in the park, watching the educational video about camping in bear country is mandatory, even if you’ve seen it before. They give you a bear canister free of charge, and there you should pick which units, and for how many days you are planning to camp. I highly recommend that they stick some photos of the different units on the wall next to the maps, including the highlights of what to expect when getting there (e.g. if that unit offers you views of Denali, number of river crossings, amount of bushwhacking, etc). The man working there was quite helpful explaining each unit to me, however the lady behind the desk didn’t have the right attitude, and apparently had forgotten that her job is to be there, and help the visitors (otherwise I would give the access center 5 stars).

text: Denali National Park is one of my favorite places on Earth. The visitors center here is a great introduction to the park, as well as a great place to ask for tips and guidance to help plan your park adventure. The rangers are always helpful and knowledgeable. One time my husband fell off a rock formation off of Savage River. Split his hand wide open to the bone. We drove back and the rangers helped with emergency Management and directed us to the nearest clinic. The whole time they were administering first aid they were cool calm and professional. That was back in 2012 but it has stuck with me. Long story short this is a great place to help orient people to the park.

A fabulous meal is offered while you learn how people travelled and lived here in Alaska. As well, you may get an opportunity to see wildlife where we saw several Moose through the course of the trip either eating, walking as well running through the Tundra. If you have an option to get a guide on the train, I highly recommend Whitney as she is very knowledgeable.

name: Deanna Schneider
text:
Denali National Park is truly one of a kind. There is no other place I can think of that is so “wild”. What’s great about this place is that there is only one road and there are limited trails. Most of the park is “trail-less” I consider myself moderately outdoorsy and I would say that this is not for me, and probably not for most people. Best to stay on the mostly short trails near the visitor center and savage river. There were also some near to Eielson Vistor center but only like 3. And one by wonder lake but not near the lake (only good for clear days with views of mount denali). Due to the conservation efforts, cars are not allowed passed savage river (mile 15) unless you are camping, and vehicles are not allowed passed Teklanika (miles 29) except buses.

The whole road is 92.something miles, and is worth a visit. The entire bus tour from start to end is 12 hours or so due to the numerous stops for wildlife and general bathroom breaks and rest stops. My particular bus ride from Teklanika was 6 hours one way. You will see so much wildlife and if you are lucky, you will also have an awesome bus driver like Bear (Robert) who will be a great storyteller.

Denali is worth a visit, there are very few places on earth like this and you should catch them while it’s still possible. I am completely impressed the by the number of animals we were able to view in their natural habitat.

name: Daniel Lowe
text: WINTER REVIEW:  I am a National Parks Nerd! I have rated every national park a 5 star, just look. We came down to Denali from Fairbanks to just see what it had to offer in the winter and wow were we disappointed . 3 miles of less interesting views than the drive down. The drive was beautiful and thats were we actually saw Denali the best! The 3 miles of the park were great with small trails to do, but this is a colossal waste of time if you are coming here to experience a park. I have been to many National Parks in the winter, such as Yellowstone and Glacier and I feel that Denali could have offered more than the minuscule 3 mile corridor that you could experience anywhere in Alaska in the winter.  The park rangers were phenomenally awesome as usual though!  We will be back another season.

Very helpful. They also have a place to eat and get a warm (or cold) drink. And the bus stop and train station is right there too. I really enjoyed browsing the bookstore - there were books and stuffed animals and some mugs, etc.
The only thing that frustrated me about the place is the lack of parking. It is slammed packed every time I visit and so hard to find parking. Other than that this place is great!

text:
This is a very well-funded government information center and a necessary point for registering for Outback hikes and trips into the wilderness.
The exhibits are very biased towards Eco extremism but still offer a good deal of information and knowledge if taken with a grain of salt.

The best thing in the information center is the huge topographic 3D map of the park and surrounding areas. You can see that the 65 Mile bus ride will give you a view it's not much better than the free view from the Highway south of the park. If you're hiking the buses are great to get to trailheads but for the view they are quite expensive for what you get compared to the free Highway.

Be sure to notice in the map the portion of Denali park that is owned by the state of Alaska. If this part you can hunt fish and do all kinds of activities freely. This is the opposite of the federal controlled lands.

In the federal lands there are no parking, no camping signs everywhere ,pay money or go away. Once you get to the Alaska control portion of the highway there are free pull-offs south of the park that are ideal for camping overnight in an RV. No facilities but free parking great views and no harassment.

Alaska is citizen-friendly! The federal government is citizen hostile, citizen manipulative, and citizen exploitive!

The Visitor Center is worth going to so you can see how the parts laid out, see the free part you can enjoy on by the state of Alaska and decide whether you're going to ride buses till trailheads, buses for the view, or Joy the Freeview along the highway. If you don't Reserve Advance you're certainly not going to stay in the park with your RV

My 300MM zoom camera only just pics them up, and some Carabou only visable with binoculars. Anyway we saw Denali. Its a shame its the only way to get in there. text: My husband and I really enjoyed our time here. Our room was immaculate. The staff was very kind, courteous and polite.

text: Great lunch and pleasant dining area. The wait staff is fantastic and the food is top quality. A bonus is the fact it wasn't crowded during the lunch hour!

name: Justin Knowlton
text: Our room was new and our accommodations were pleasant. The best part of our stay was the free continental breakfast. It was so much more than a continental breakfast. They had a plethora of hot food as well as your traditional favorites. A word of caution though, they only offer the free breakfasts during the off season in the fall and winter months. They have a nice breakfast for a fee in the summer.

name: Akrose G
text: The room was dirty, I was expecting it to be clean because they were closed all winter. But for $117.00 dollars it should have been cleaner than it was. The beds were comfy.

text: The usual chain hotel but newish and very comfy.

text: Was good visit when last there in October however due to earthquake we had in early January there was some damage and they'll reopen April 29th from what I know.. on premises restaurant is good as serve breakfast, dinner and check on lunch depends on season in many hotels in Alaska. But great location as close to city bus terminal and many places in walking distance for just about anything you could want or need.. certain rooms have great views of mountains or the Cook inlet...

name: Jonathan Rodrigues
text: Rooms are very dated compared to other offerings in the area. Front desk staff member at check in was very unprofessional and at some points rude. Would look for for different place before I stayed here again

name: Steven Smith
text:
Room was dated (which I don't mind) but was very spacious (which we liked).  Mattress was not real comfy and the pillows seemed old and lumpy :-(  Two restaurants in the hotel, but their menus are virtually the same.
Overall, it was fine.

name: Rajasekhara S
text: Very good hotel with well cleaned rooms & furniture with two restaurant very near to airport

name: Warren Feaster
text: Awesome staff, and the room was cozy and comfortable. Very convenient to eatery's and shopping malls, and also give a great view of the mountains in distances. That picture is at 4 a.m. and 7:30 a.m.

name: jaasynergy8
text: Clean spacious rooms. The gift shop was cute!

name: Donald Robak
text:
Our stay at the Westmark was the completion of our cruise through Alaska's Inside Passage along with a stop at Denali National Park. The hotel was clean and roomy and even included a small kitchen, even though our stay wasn't really long enough for any kitchen. It appears that the principal users were passengers from Holland America cruises. They may even have an ownership interest in the property, but this is only a guess.
The toilets are modern with a high powered flush that sounds like a jet plane. The sound insulation in the rooms is no match for the toilets when other guests flush during the long Alaskan night.
I cannot reasonably evaluate the service because most of my contact was with Holland America Representatives. Their service was very good.

name: Josh S
text: Mixed feelings... The room was very nice, spacious and clean. The Staffing here is hit-or-miss. Either you get someone who doesn't know anything or you get someone who seems to be very on top of it and accommodating. A cleaning staff member used their key card to walk into our room early in the morning and ask us, WHILE WE WERE IN BED, what time our checkout was. The front desk comped us some coffee and a breakfast burrito, so that was nice. I do wish our south facing room had better black out curtains since the sun doesn't set until midnight. Overall good experience.

name: Sam J
text: Spacious, modern room interior. Helpful and friendly staff. Breakfast was included which was great!

name: Adrianell Poteet Sorrels
text: Clean amd nice. Offered a $5 coupon to the hotel restaurant if you refused maid service during your stay, which is pretty cool.

name: SHAGGY FBKSAK
text: Love to stay hete even for a staycation.

name: Mark Garrad
text:
Great location within easy walking distance of town centre. The room was spacious, clean and relatively cheap. Staff were always friendly and tried to be helpful.
We watched a rather bizarre interaction between another guest and front desk staff, where the guest enquired about rather basic tourist information. It turned out the staff could offer little insight into tourist attractions around Fairbanks and couldn't even offer any tourist brochures! Perhaps it had something to do with the extensive renovations that had closed the regular front desk?
Don't plan sleeping in on Sunday if you want a complimentary breakfast. Served between 6.30 and 8.30 am only and after that you pay.
Also note that the walls are not particularly soundproof. Fortunately I travel with earplugs.

name: Max Dondo
text: Very nice hotel, with spacious rooms. It's big, and it's easy to get lost around. The rooms are clean, the staff were very nice to us. It is walking distance from downtown and Costco, where we managed to buy dinner and lunch. They also sell breakfast, lunch and dinner there. There is a free shuttle from the hotel to the airport.

name: Ethel Reed
text: Clean, quiet, professional hotel, up to date amenities & friendly staff.

name: Rachael Kvapil
text: The dim lighting always gets me because it'sdark and hard to photograph/film in. Other than that it is a great place to hold a major event. The food is good and the staff pleasant. There is also a great bar and restaurant I often go to even if food is being offered at the event I'm attending.

name: Amelia Hartwig
text: Had thanksgiving dinner here and let me tell you this it was very good we will be back again the staff was very professional and polite they went way beyond our expectations we recommend this place to anyone who wants treated with the up most respect food was delicious and better then we expected we definitely will be back for there next years thanksgiving dinner :-)

name: Julie Helbig
text: Inventory hasn't been too bad

name: Eric Collier
text: So, this review is purely for the convention side of the hotel. This doesn't reflect room accommodations or guest services. Overall a class act for the convention side. This is a great venue for the Fairbanks area and one of the few places that can handle a large function. They cater to smaller functions on a nightly basis and provide full services. The employees provide a fast service and are well adorned to fit the motif of your function.

name: Jason U.
text: What's to say? It's a fairly standard hotel in this price range and area. Our room was clean and the bed was comfortable. No complaints at all. There is some shopping within walking distance and a few restaurants near by. One complaint about the general area is that surprisingly there aren't any grocery stores that we could find. We ended up getting a cab to take us grocery shopping for a hiking trip.

name: Aditi Partani
text: Nice spacious rooms. Great place to stay right in the middle of the downtown. Nice and friendly staff 👍👍

name: T. Frank Box
text: Good morning breakfast, Central location, Head bolt heater plug ins.

name: carrie chomin
text: Heat wasn't working at home needed a place to stay. Nice clean wheelchair friendly rooms. Thank you.

name: Joshua Arnold
text: An other under staffed place. The Alaska cheddar burger combo is great.

name: Paul Robarge
text: Great hotel and convention center. We had an event there and it was very well priced and the food that was catered was excellent and the service was unbelievably amazing. I am really impressed.

name: Darin English
text: Nice place, most of the staff is helpful, counter staff is great, behind the scenes staff need to relax and stop profiling the locals.

name: Chad Sherwood
text: I really like this hotel, free breakfast and comfy beds! The only downfall is the walls are thin and I could hear everything in the rooms next to me.

name: Jasmine Dayton
text: Has good, up to date rooms. Good customer service, and a nice restaurant. Includes a laundry room, work out room, and computer room on the first floor. Nice rooms to rent if you want a big meeting room or a bigger event room. There's also a cute gift shop with a Starbucks in the lobby.

name: Nicole S
text: It is great. Wonderful customer service. Conveniently close to downtown amenities.

name: Alex Bazarsky
text: Nice hotel with large rooms, gym and restaurants. Gift shop is a great bonus. And it's located close to the downtown.

Welcoming staff
Room is ok

name: Michael Vandeventer
text: Went to fund raiser dinner here. Food was okay. Space was large and well lit. Have not stayed or eaten in restaurant that is on site.

name: Victoria Avery
text: I have only gone here for conferences and fundraiser events. They help to host fantastic events, like the Literacy Council spelling bee and the Stone Soup cook off. A valuable part of the Fairbanks community for allowing these events to take place. Again, I haven't used the hotel as a place to stay, but the place is great for non profit and community events.

name: Chad Gomez
text: Good location, good parking, clean rooms, and good prices. Couldnt ask for much more.

name: Kelly Kitka
text: Their rooms are always clean and spacious. The location is great as well! The only thing that a techy visitor wouldn't like is that the wifi is not very fast. Perhaps when I was using it a lot of other people were as well.

name: April Carson Carson
text: This hotel is very big, have great restaurant in/ on the property. Duvets you make reservations! You can walk in but much better if you set it up before hand.

name: André M
text:
This Westmark was a clean, comfortable, and quiet place to stay for a couple of nights. Friendly staff.

The restaurant closes a little early for me, at 9pm. and there is no food available, at all after that. It would be great if there were perhaps 4 or 5 items that a bartender could heat and serve without needing a kitchen staff.

Also this hotel requires your room key to enter the building from the parking lot (not main entrance) and to use the elevator. Extra security and a minor annoyance..

name: Amy Urbach
text: The room was so small and the staff was pushy and unaccomidating. I will never stay there again. DO NOT RECOMMEND.

name: Alexis Fay
text: I enjoy the food and drinks here as well as the atmosphere and ambience. Great restaurant, great for parties and nice hotel rooms if you are looking for lodging.

name: James Morowski
text: Nice place to stay not very far from downtown. Front desk folks were great and very friendly.  Along with that the food at the restaurant was very good.

name: Terry Oakes
text: The Thanksgiving buffet was good and the staff was pleasant.

name: Shannon Skogstad
text: Love the level of service and attitude here.

name: Jack Arsenault
text: Another wonderful hotel in the chain. Enjoyed our stay.

name: Aino Welch
text: Food is good, buffet was refilled service for the conference was keeping up with water,tea and coffee service.

name: Mackenzie Widmayer
text: While I have attended many events at the Westpark Fairbanks Hotel & Conference, my most recent visit was enjoyable. The salad was tasty despite being covered in limp onions and blue cheese. The room was well-decorated and almost large enough for the people who paid to attend. The acoustics of the room were good. I would recommend this venue for other events.

name: Carlos Adair
text: Rooms were clean and well taken care of, I enjoyed my stay

name: C
text: Pretty accommodating. Had some medical issues while I was there and they seem to understand my plight.

name: Eunice Bennett
text: I have 4 kids and they were more than willing to place me in another room because I was next to a daysleeper who complained within the first 5 minutes in the room. The guy who came up for the complaint seen my kids and used my phone to tell them I have kids and there's no problem here and switched my room asap. Red lantern downstairs is a little expensive but the food is SOOOO GOOD, awesome drinks my fave is the northern lights. Super friendly workers when I checked in and had to be moved. (Didn't get their names but it was around 12:30-1pm on 12/16). Nice clean hotel. I love that you need a room key just to use the elevator too. Overall I'd definitely stay here again. ALSO CHOOSE THE NORTH TOWER(BIGGER ROOMS)

name: Cassie Kana Carter
text: Rooms are nice and extremely clean, but AC never really cools them down. Not the nicest staff at the front desk. Also, we verified multiple times that it's still early enough in the year for continental breakfast, but it isn't.

name: Elizabeth Pruitt
text: I was here only for a mother's day brunch.Unfortunately I was unable to spend it with my own mother but I attended this phenomenal meal with a newfound friend of mine and her family. The food was excellent and the service was superb.There was a lot to keep attention on and a lot of work to keep an energized attentive smile but they did it.And they did it. Thank you for a fantastic day.

text: Very big hotel, one of the best hotel gyms I've seen

name: Albina Garman
text: Has great rooms and lots of them. Friendly service

name: Dave Schurman
text: Nothing fancy but still nice. Staff was friendly and helpful.  Food was good at the hotel restaurant but was overpriced in my opinion.  Plus we paid for a  breakfast which in any other hotel would be free.

name: Lorie Schultz
text: Disliked the passed out drunk next to the vending or ice machine right after we got out of the elevator. Blood splattered on the outside of the bathroom door. No windows to open very stuffy.won't go back.

name: Tony Wielgosz
text: Very nice hotel. Pleasant friendly location and good location

name: Colin Moffatt
text: Great stay if your in Fairbanks. 2 nice restaurants a really awesome gift shop and a Starbucks. And tons of other amenities to make you feel at home! Will stay here if I'm ever back in Fairbanks. Stay on 8th floor and you can see all of the city

name: Kimberly Murphy
text: Great place for the staycation it's down town and close walk to shops great eateries  and down town attractions. Clean and comfortable and have great specials like vallentines day we go every year, we are local and love our staycation with them

name: Alexia Hines
text:
Very nice hotel and we stayed here for a great price!
Loved the breakfast of eggs, delicious potatoes , and mm mmm mmmmm bacon! They also had fruit (which was tastey - not unripe or over ripe like many hotels serve for their breakfasts). There was coffee, OJ, water, and pastries and bread as well.

We loved the look of the room. It was clean and tastefully decorated. The hotel has a small workout room and computer room.
To use the elevator or get into the side door of the hotel you need to use your hotel key. Something I really liked. I felt very safe here and the fact that it's close to Fort Wainwright was perfect for my husband (who works on post) and I.

We had an excellent stay and had nothing but great encounters with the staff. We will definitely be back.

name: Whenido Dotcom
text: Hit and miss. Sometimes the night is perfect, and other times it has noisy, tipsy people in the neighboring units. Structure is aging a bit. The beds are fair, but not great. The restaurant is one of the better features. Breakfast is free, but minimal compared to other places. Update: breakfast has improved - eggs and meat added. Bumping up a star, but would give it 3.5 really.

name: Hunter UAS
text: The catering staff here is phenomenal. Brunch is an amazing and enjoyable experience!!!

name: Carol Simpson
text: I have used this hotel for many events for many years. The service is always amazing! The staff is attentive, helpful, and cheerful! The rooms are nice and the food in the restaurants is very good.

name: Jennifer Russell
text: A lot of misinformation with staff, you can ask 5 employees the same question and get 5 different answers. Rooms were a nice size and pretty clean

name: Levi Rollins
text: Accommodations were pretty standard. The staff was well mannered and professional. The room was a bit warm and stuffy but it was quite crowded so I can't exactly fault the hotel for that. Overall it was a good experience. We will return.

name: john watkins
text: I had my Christmas party there last night, awesome place. They make outstanding food.

name: Shayna Lunt
text: Attended the Westmark for an awards banquet and the staff that assisted were amazing. They were attentive to the needs of the guests and they did a great job of making sure there was always food and drinks available.

name: Robert Conriquez
text: I recommend it very nice rooms and the staff were really nice

name: Sharon Hudson
text: Older hotel, but comfortable beds. 2 restaurants on site and Starbucks in the giftshop.

name: Ryan Stonebraker
text: This has become my go to hotel in Fairbanks. They have good in-hotel restaurants, curtious staff, and clean facilities. Would definitely recommend.

name: Sean Doughe
text: Decent hotel. Not great. Decent. Basic amenities, okay-ish breakfast. 5/10.

name: Mike Simard
text: Great place to stay and have meetings!

name: Arlene Acuna
text:
Good place to stay.
.convenient walking location to galleries, museums, historic spots and the river.

name: Julia Haynie
text: A lot of conferences happen here. If it's a busy week, don't expect them to have a lot of rooms or be cheap. I recommend reserving a room early if you want a good deal.

name: Bob Rieth
text: I spend four nights there last week.  Very nice place.  The room that I was in was very small but everything in it seemed to be brand new.  The Red Lantern is a nice place for a drink after the conference.  The only issue that I had was with the bathroom fixtures.  I ended up having to take the toilet tank apart and fix the handle myself after listening to the toilet run for over an hour.  The hotel was 100% occupied for the nights that I was there so I'm sure the maintenance staff was pretty busy.

name: Renee and Jesse Escamilla
text: It was a comfortable stay and the rooms were quiet and clean. I'll definitely be staying again when traveling to Fairbanks for work.

name: Josie Conley
text: If what we stayed in was a "suite" then  I'd hate to see what their normal rooms are like. One lady that helped us was extremely rude, other than that everyone else was nice.

name: O O
text: Very nice, everything was kept very clean

name: Bill Crozier
text: Nice hotel. Clean and modern.

name: wayne bell

name: Astra Catastrophe
text: Excellent customer service. Every worker was clearly trained to provide a good stay to every person that walks through the door. Couldnt be happier !

We were ignored for a while at the counter until a girl stepped up and explained she wasn't on shift for another 10 min but since bo one was helping she would step in. The shuttle to the airport was 30 min late. We were told it was because we had a new driver.

name: Andrea Hulman-Watsjold
text: While the room was lovely, I was woken at 3am by a truck emptying the dumpsters outside, and at 5am by hotel employees loading luggage for cruise passengers. It was incredibly disruptive and when I actually got up in the morning I was still exhausted.

name: Andrew Kaplan
text: Large rooms and hotel seems pretty new. Hopefully it reinvigorated downtown Fairbanks which seems quite depressed.

text: Nice hotel and got a free upgraded room.  Good location close to downtown.

name: Reese Pesata

name: Paris B
text: Im a previous housekeeper so of course I inspected the room first... 😏 Beautiful room.  Great price for 1 night. Clean rooms. No dust ! Everything was placed nice and neatly. There were a few down sides... No tv guides ? I didnt like not knowing what was next or what show I was watching. Cups didn't have plastic on them. No pen or paper to leave a note. And lastly no trash bags ? (I can only think saves them a few dollars not to have to buy them?) Other than all that I had a great stay 💙

name: Martha Ahkivgak
text: A city in a building. Very beautiful.

name: Harold
text: Stay away from the restaurant. They don't know how to serve a whole party. There wasn't room for five of us, so 3 of us sat at a table and the other 2 at the counter. The people at the counter never were served. The only time they were noticed was as they were walking out the door. Dinner they had room for the 5 of us, but the service was terrible. The information we were given said that there was a buffet between 6:30 and 9:30 AM, but they didn't have that, just one sheet of paper with a few menu items.

text: This hotel stay was part of a Holland America tour. The lobby was with easy access to restaurants and a gift shop. The room was nice with the exception that there was no soap at the sink. We called down to housekeeping and requested soap as well as a luggage rack, which was also absent from our room. We went to dinner and returned about 2 hours later to find that housekeeping had not been there. We went to the front desk to try to get this resolved and they had soap that they were handing out to other guests who were also missing soap from their rooms. They were very stingy about handing it out. Only one per room. The water pressure in the shower was also very poor. Other than the poor customer service, the stay was otherwise Ok.
