name: melody smith
text: I have came to this trail for almost 20 years now, and take my children now as they grow up. Always a lovely spot to go, I always take my dog with me so he can enjoy it as well. It is not the most difficult trail but there is plenty of uphill. The first rock is the most tedious to reach, and the 3rd has a lot of that loose fine sandy soil to it so careful if going back down- its slippery !

name: Elizabeth Angel
text: Beautiful views. It can get steep at times but the trail to the top it fairly short. If you go during winter time it will be a little more challenging. There’s a packed trail but you’ll be knee deep in snow if you go a couple inches away from it. Also when going downhill it’ll be steep and slippery so be careful

name: Jennifer Frysz
text: Beautiful day and trail. Quite unique and I kept seeing frozen in time faces. Majestic.

name: Eliana McKee
text: Well kept trail. There is a small picnic area at the beginning of the trail. Bring food and water!  This is a wonderful place for a walk. Nature at its best. Dogs are welcome,  but please pick up their poop. The trail to to top of the hill is a bit steep for very young kids.

name: Philip Unsworth
text: Great hike with beautiful views. We arrived at about 1030am and was not crowded. By the time we finished, parking lot was packed. Restrooms available in parking and were not great. Trail started a little wet, but not a problem. It starts out flat then gets pretty steep, but footing is good. If you're not in a hurry, most people should not have a problem completing the loop. Loved it!

name: Paulness
text: This is a pretty accessible hiking area about 50  miles outside of Fairbanks.  The drive is easy, but Chena Hot Aprings Road can have a lot of bumps and damage due to frost heaves.  Drive with care.  The parking area has a few tables by the Chena River, a latrine, and the fee station  has a digital payment system for cards and fee envelopes for cash or checks.  Parking costs 5 bucks, camping is like 15 buck a night or something. The beginning of the trail is. Ot for the faint of heart, it's a bit more difficult and peolle that brag about how good they are have been humbled here.  So take your time, and be careful as there are area with loose rocks and pebbles. But the views are pretty awesome of the Chena State recreation area and the White Mountains.  The trail itself is about 6 miles if you do the whole loop.  But that's what's great about choices.  Bring bug spray for the mosquitos, bear spray just in case, and rain gear as the weather can cha he by the minute in the interior.  If you're really adventurous, you can hike all the way to Chena Hot Springs Resort, which is about 8.5 miles.  All in all, it's a good.hike to see some scenery and get some cardio in.

name: Ryan Newton
text: Great hiking in the summer.  Take advantage of the sunshine! Find memories and great weather just out of Fairbanks!! Accessabile. This is somewhere is definitely visit again and recommend to others. It's really a place the whole family can enjoy!

name: Michelle Nye
text: This is a flat trail at the beginning and then there are many steep climbs.  The trails are well kept wide and accessible. Bring a lunch to the top as the rocks are a perfect spot to rest and have a picnic. There are gorgeous views of the mountains around and the river below.

name: Joseph Gaunt
text: Awesome trails that are fun and beautiful. If you are in shape, they will be a moderate difficulty and very enjoyable. If you are out of shape, it will be a challenge, but definitely worth it. Absolutely gorgeous view.

name: Westlin Wagner
text: Amazing place! Wonderful views. Well marked trail. Tough climb.

name: Kitsana Dounglomchan
text: By far the best and most accessible hike near Fairbanks. The total journey is around 3.5 to 4 miles but there are some great rock scrambles you can do when you get to the top. There are also some places to rappel, although I’ve never done that here myself. It offers some truly gorgeous views of the area and it’s not a terribly difficult hike. I recommending taking the trail counterclockwise, which is what the signs recommend anyways. I really can’t think of anything negative to say about. The only downside would be if you came out during breakup and the trail was either super muddy or still had snow on it.

name: Vasin mohcharoen
text: Best hiking place for beginner.♥️♥️

text: This trail was recommended to us by 2 locals.  We were not disappointed!  For a Friday afternoon, it wasn't crowded at all.  In fact we were the only people on the descending part. text: This place is amazing, my kids love it and the trails are groomed regularly which makes for easier skiing for my 4 kids who are barley getting into the sport.

text: Birch Hill is incredible for year round outdoor activities. The disk golf course is amazing! Lots of ski trails for winter and hiking trails in summer, highly recommended place to visit any time you arw in Fairbanks, Alaska!

text: This is such a great place anytime of year. The summer is great for walking and enjoying the sunshine, the fall has spectacular views of the changing colors of the foliage. The autumn yellows and oranges really pop against the hill and it’s great for family photos. Winter and spring are fantastic for cross county skiing. Good for all levels of skiers. Nice warming hut as well. Lots of parking but can get busy during peak season.

And of course everybody knows the ski area in the winter time. A beautiful safe place to take the family and enjoy some wilderness for the afternoon!

A service tech broke our dashboard foam, in our Sedona van, right before we were leaving to come to Fort Bliss. We have a hand signed letter that Kendall will and replace/repair our broken foam.

It has yet to be fixed. My next review will be to "our" Kia dealer here. As well as reviewing Kia on Facebook.

There's a lot of finger pointing, and my family's safety is dead in the middle of it. Excuses: oh the time difference, what's the most cost effective method. Kia is privately owned and are franchisees so they have to work it out. So, who exactly fixes this and whenm

I've come to a conclusion it will most likely not get fixed.  Each entitiy can continue to point fingers We plan to keep our Sedona until it breaks down. It's a great van. My greatest concern is, what if we got into an accident, Mr. Bushke? I thank God it hasn't happened. Yet. I mean, anything can happen at anytime.

That broken dash will instantly come through it's leather encasement, impailing the front seat riders. Then what, Mr. Bushke? Then what?
All we want us our dash fixed, and sooner rathet than later.
fulfill your obligation and stick to your word.

Nicholas got me in to Kendall Anchorage for the radio.

text: We bought an '06' Mazda Tribute in April of 2011. They redone the engine - took care of that problem but this last time called for a steering arm then a few days later said the rack & pinion needed replaces. I think they just got in a hurry to get rid of it after they took it in on trade. It had been in a little bender and we had to wait for a new front bumper before we could have it. We have hardly put 8000 miles on it since we bought it. We retrived our vehicle and have taken it to another shop to do the work ourselves with the help of another mechanic. I hope we won't ever be dealing with these people again and will not recomend any one else to.

name: Sterling Campbell
text:
Had an pretty good experience with few speed bumps up to the point of boarding our flight.  There were mechanical concerns that led them to move us to a different gate, which is perfectly understandable.  However on three consecutive occasions, for multiple reasons, we were told that we were boarding only to stand there for 5 minutes before eventually being told that something else happened, there was another delay and so given yet anothe another time which would again come and again pass.

I'm sure they were doing there best, but it was frustrating and just a little communication would have saved a lot of trouble.

Beyond that, the building is nice and clean and the floor format was intelligently designed.

text:
*UPDATE*
The food was much better and room 203 was beautiful. I moved this rating from 4 to 5 stars after my second visit. Staff is accommodating and covid procedures were followed.

------------------------------------------------------------
The room was cozy and clean. There is a jacuzzi tub in the room which is a nice treat. The room had good lighting and was very crisp and fresh. You can expect to see the usual items one finds in a hotel such as soaps, face towels, folded washcloths, laundry bag, hair dryer, luggage holder, keurig, ice bucket, bag for the ice bucket, vending on second floor amenities and etc... The regular dinning is covid restricted so it is in takeout containers dropped off at your door with canned oran ge juice room temperature.

I heard that one can hike to the waterfall - but our tour did not allow the time for that.  If you can do the Whale Watching without the Mendenhall Glacier at a lower price - I recommend that. text: This place is absolutely gorgeous! The glacier is vibrantly beautiful with waterfalls nearby. On a sunny day you will not be disappointed. Be careful when walking out on the lake during the spring and early winter. The ice can fracture and break. Even during the dead of winter terrain be sure not to walk too close to the face because the ice is not as thick being that the water is moving against the face. Another thing to be wary of is the fact that during the warmer weeks the glacier will calve, as in break, and icebergs will fall into the lake creaking a wave of breaking ice. Enjoy the view!

name: Cassandra Yeh
text:
Only one word to describe..... "WOW!"

I have never seen anything like this in my life!! There are thousands of glacier in Alaska, only a few that you can see it by car... others you have to take the planes.

Once we got off from our cruise on Juneau cruise port. Tons of local vendors selling excursion. YES, way cheaper than the excursion package on the cruise. We did whale watching and Mendanhall Glacier for $110 compared to the cruise charging $210. That is a big saving!! If you just want to see the Mendanhall Glacier, round trip bus $20.

When we go off the bus, we could see the glacier from far.... THE COLOR IS JUST GORGEOUS!! The sky blue color makes it so dreamy and unreal. The bloating ice look like cotton candy~

There is stairs to go all the way down to the water. YES, you can really touch the icy cold water!!

Then there is a path way to guide you to as close as possible in front of the glacier. OMG!!! Now I truly appreciate what nature have created this amazing view!

There is a waterfall right next to the glacier, about 1 mile walk.

If you are in Juneau, DEFINITELY have to check out Mendenhall Glacier! You won't regret!

name: Maxim Culacov
text: This is the best business ideea I have seen in years. This is such an amazing store with amazing employees and service that you forget the purpose of this endeavor is to make money. This is the ultimate tourist trap and I love it :) And when you get there, make sure you send a post card from the North Pole to your family or friends.

name: Terrance Aldridge II
text: What a wonderful place to go and see Santa Clause, Mrs. Clause, and their Reindeer!  Everything in there is adorable and you end up wanting to buy EVERYTHING!  Kids had a blast and there is so much to see!  If you have time, make the trip!

name: ShibaKitti
text: Pretty fun. Been going here almost every Christmas of my life. Things are pricey. Love the reindeer 🦌

name: David Claar
text: Santa Claus House is an iconic North Pole destination. Obviously, visiting Santa tops every child's Christmas list, and his jolly self sits ready to bring a huge smile to those good children. The store feels like Christmas. From the comforting food at the snack shop, to the festive clothes, to the unique, beautiful decorations, and of course the the perfect holiday toys to brighten any child's day. The magic of Christmas awaits your visit year round. I love Santa Claus House.

name: Eric Collier
text: Pretty sure this is the best Santa/Christmas store in Alaska. This is a must see if you are traveling the Richardson HWY through the interior. Atmosphere on the inside is spot on, big tree and Santa near the parking area. There is an area within the shop where you can sit and have coffee and homemade fudge. Everyone very friendly and helpful. Note: There is a sales tax in North Pole.

name: Trent R

There are plenty of photo op's and gifts for the whole family. BTW - It's HUGE - So be prepared to enjoy yourself for a little while.

name: Ola Alhammami
text:
COVID-19 review/
Really nice place to visit, specially for kids.
You can see all Santa place and toys.
Also it’s great place to get souvenir.

name: Shannon Houser
text: I went with a bunch of friend & had a great time viewing all the different holiday decor! Christmas is my favorite holiday and made me feel like a little kid again. Definitely a must see!

name: Robert Piekarski

name: Debbie J
text:
This is a wonderful place. Definitely puts you in the mood for Christmas!
My husband is from Peru. We were looking for products made in USA to send back to Peru. Sadly, there are not many choices. The staff said they are working to get more products made in the US but it is difficult.
The products made in Alaska are stunning. We purchased several to send to family.
Thank you Santa Claus House!

Was nice to be able to go this year and see they had expanded, quality of merchandise is high end, prices were fair, staff was very friendly they still had Santa and Mrs. Clause for pictures (with masks) they enforced social distancing and highly encouraged masks. An absolutely amazing place!

It was so nice to walk into a place that wasn't afraid to celebrate Christmas! No grinches or anti-Christmas bullies up here!

They actually  play real Christmas music too and decorate with Christmas trees and even have manger scenes! I will probably order online every year...the gifts are that nice!  It's awesome!

Being in Alaska makes it way out of the way for the lower 48 folks but it is really worth visiting if your in the area.

Beautifully laid out store! I spent more than an hour there just looking...and I hate shopping!

name: Paulness
text: As usual, the review has to begin with the Alaska disclaimer.  Prices here are higher than most other places.  Why?  Because the cost of living is high in Alaska.  Bottom line, it doesn't matter where you are around Fairbanks, things are expensive.  That being said, this a cool place to stop in any time of the year.  Where else can your kids (or you adults) meet a very real-looking Santa in July, in North Pole?  Nowhere.  This place has a great selection of Alaskana items and souvenirs, as well as toys, books, and other Christmas items.  There's also a little coffee stand inside, very good during the winter events.  You don't have to buy anything, but if you venture into the Fairbanks area this is a must-see place.  It's a neat little shop that helps lend to a holiday, year-round.  I recommend everyone that visits the area stop by and check it out.  You won't be disappointed.

name: Sonia Revolorio
text:
We made the trip to Fairbanks just to visit the Santa Claus House (Dec 22-23). I must say that I was very disappointed that it didnt feel like xmas, at all. In my mind I thought they'd have a large open space, decorated with xmas lights/decorations, for the kids to be out in the snow. The parking lot was small and dark and the store had little to no lighting around it. There was no light shining on the large Santa, in the front, so we couldnt take any good pics. I really thought they'd make an effort to make it look like Christmas inside and out since its supposed to be Santa's House, after all, but they didnt. There were no xmas lights anywhere. The only lighting was to the front, of the store, to show the facade. Going inside, I thought it'd feel like xmas too (cozy with warm feelings and all). It didnt!! It looked like any other gift shop except this one is filled with xmas ornaments (ranging from a few bucks to over $1000). Its pretty crowded, enough to make me paranoid about accidentally bumping into a shelve and breaking something, especially when we're all wearing our huge winter clothes. I didnt even enjoy myself because I had my 3 and 5 yr old children who I had to keep super close to me and under eagle eye supervision because the store is filled with expensive ornaments on the bottom shelves where kids can easily reach and break them. Not sure why anyone would call a place Santa Claus House and make NO attempt to make it kid-friendly. Its almost like they purposely planned for children to NEVER come inside. Unless its a business strategy "lets fill this store with expensive breakables, call it something kid-friendly to trick parents into bringing their children, and maybe they'll break lots of things so the parents are forced to buy them". If so, I guess it works. 🤣
Oh, I almost forgot... the only space for children was a 2 adult bench that was situated 4 feet from a wall-hung TV, that played the Polar Express movie. In other words, a max of 7 SMALL children (toddlers) could fit in this space (3 on the bench and 4, on the floor, at the feet of the 3 benched children). Again, no planning whatsoever since the TV was up high (about 5-6 feet from the ground) so the floor children had to bend their little necks to watch the movie.
The only thing I enjoyed was being able to buy deeds to own a square inch of the North Pole (still not sure if theyre real but super cute). I also liked how Santa was there but we didnt get a chance to take a photo because they werent accepting any more people. We showed up around 4:30pm and they said they had enough people, on the wait list, to last them until closing (6:30pm). They did mention that its never busy at opening (10am) so we planned to go back the next morning. We got there at about 10:30am and we still waited about 1.5 hrs. I guess you have to be there before opening time so you can be the first in line. I guess I hadnt noticed, on the first day, that Santa didnt have much of his own space. Like everything else in the store, Santa's space was very crowded too. His space backed up into another aisle filled with ornaments. I guess they dont make more of an effort because it IS free to have your photo taken. Note: you have to bring your own camera but they do have an employee that takes the photo for you. Also NOTE: the employee taking the photo is no professional. She cut the feet off our photo so it looked a little awkward. Overall, it's definitely not a trip worth making (unless youre really into xmas ornaments) if this is all you plan on doing. You'd be better off visiting a mall Santa!! At least, there, your kids are more free to roam.

A very large decorated Christmas tree was in the yard along with huge statue of Santa. Reindeer were in pens nearby.Inside the house had a large array of Christmas related items as well as Santa holding court for the patrons. Since there was a possibility of an extended visit they also had a small food counter serving desserts and sort drinks.

text:
Meh...I have lived in North Pole for three years and I think this place is kind of a tourist trap. It’s certainly not bad and Santa Claus, the gifts and deserts are legit. But what you pay for is going to be severely marked up as opposed to what you’d buy online. And in the end, the city of North Pole is just named that (no special meaning or reason why they called it that as far as I know) and the only thing Christmasy in town is Santa’s house and the reindeer in the parking lot.

So if you’re SUPER into Christmas or have young kids then it’s definitely worth your time, but if not I think there are so many other things you can see when you come to Interior Alaska that would be worth your time.

name: Jacob Statler
text:
Santa's house is the cutest little place. They have so many cute and ornate ornaments to buy. There are letters from Santa that you can get to give to loved ones. You can even send the letters from Santa's house so they will get stamped from the North Pole.

Another cool thing you can get is a deed to 1 inch of the North Pole! It is really cool! There are some cheaper gifts that you can get too. There are some wooden post cards that you can actually mail to people. I have never seen such ornate postcards as them. If you don't want to mail them they do make quite a  neat souvenir to keep.

When we went, Santa was on Fall Break so sadly I did not get the chance to sit on his lap and ask him if I made it to the nice list this year. But I will have to come back in November so I can ask him.

Something that you must get when you go to Santa's House is their fudge. It is the best fudge I have ever had! They have so many different flavors and all of them are so good. They are a little pricey but definitely worth it if you are a fudge lover.

name: Robin Dern
text: Every city has eateries that are locally iconic and Lucky Wishbone is that for Anchorage. Simple in their approach, diner fare, they do what they do extremely well which is why they have remained in business for 65 years as of this year (2020). They are known especially for their fried chicken and their milkshakes but everyone has a favorite on the menu. They have drive-thru service as well but, in non-Covid times, it is worth dining in just to look at all of the history they have hanging on their walls.

name: Griffin Hagle
text: Lucky Wishbone scores perfectly on the WYSIWYG meter: it serves up juicy, crispy pan-fried chicken and it doesn’t put on airs in the process. Much of its charm is in its quirks (looking your way, right hand drive thru window) and status as a time capsule. There are better fast meals out there, frankly (their chicken sandwich was just alright), but as institutions go, Lucky Wishbone is without equal: a true American classic.

My favorite place to eat  PAN - FRIED - CHICKEN !
I've been dining here since I moved to Anchorage back in 1997.  I always order the Pop (5 piece) chicken meal with a corn bread muffin.  If I want to make my dinner extra special I order a large Pineapple Malt.  If you want to complete your meal then order a side of coleslaw.  If reading this doesn't make you hungry then read it again and immediately drive to Lucky Wishbone.  You can place an order now and pick it up in about 15 minutes.  You won't find a better place in Alaska for Pan-Fried-Chicken!

If this review was helpful please click the Like button.

name: Charlean Lee
text: Loved the fried chicken and chocolate milkshake!! They are quick and food was fresh.

name: Sharolyn Wyeth
text: Simply the best friend chicken in Anchorage. It doesn't get better than LW. The staff is always friendly. The shakes are great. The food is always consistent, (My son in law is addicted to their Cole Slaw.) and they make the best onion rings! Supporting small, local businesses is easy, when the food and the service are this good!! :)

name: K A
text: Only stopped by for dessert this time. It was a busy Saturday night but they managed to seat our party of four very quickly. The service was excellent and we were served quickly. We all chose different malts and they were very tasty. There is a lot of parking available.

name: Damon Schaeffer
text: Food was amazing but the person on the phone was very rude.

name: Marcia Pegram
text: Went for chicken on Thursday.. fried chicken NO FLAVOR. Tired milkshake  friday..the flavor is good BUT IT WASNT COLD..OR COOL IT WAS ROOM TEMPERATURE. Put flavor on the chicken, make your milkshakes cold. Do these things and Everyone will luv u again.

name: Elizabeth Maxson
text: I heard the milkshakes were amazing and I was craving one. Drove out, got a butterscotch milkshake, and omg....friggin delicious!!!! My SO got chicken and fries that smelled amazing..he said they were great. Ill get those next :)

name: Kati Tunnell
text: They're slightly pricey, but their milkshakes are the best and their food is always fresh and steaming!!! I've been going there since I was a little kid and will continue to go until I can't anymore.

name: D'Lany Nichols
text: I can never knock this place. Lucky Wishbone is a family favorite.

name: Can ACIKEL
text: You will love chicken again, I tried most of the options and each one is great. Onion rings are huge and a lot 🙂

name: Amber Sluss
text: Very good but some items were pretty greasy

name: Artie Reekie
text: They've become pretty proud of the food there

name: Justin Fleming-Brown
text: Great food.  Adapting well to current social distancing standards. Great customer service

name: Nick Pestrikoff
text: Still a delight, Missed George, but the cheer of our server, Storme S was delightful and very welcoming back oriented. Had Gizzards and Navy Bean with Ham soup, was so good. My friend enjoyed her meal to. Won't NOT go there anymore ever. First time there since my Dad went "home" (died). He and George were good friends.

name: K.
text: best chicken in town

name: Rhett Paulson
text: Great fried chicken, great milkshakes. An Anchorage classic

name: Betty Tunnell
text: Be food. Best service.

name: Alaskan Brighteyes
text: Tiny burger for $10.25. At least the fries were good.

name: Conce Rock
text:
Excellent fried chicken, juicy inside, crispy outside. All the sides, slaw, corn muffins, and fries, very tasty. Still have super milk shakes after all these years! Chicken noodle soup, very salty this day. I'd never had this soup before, so can't compare to other times.

This place is always packed. It's an institution. It speaks to its tasty food and great service which brings back long time loyal customers. Lots of free parking.

name: Truth B Told
text: The best tender gizzards you will find and priced accordingly at $9 for a plate of them. The expensive fried chicken is average flavor and on the small side. The drive through is strangely on the passenger side. Fries are also average to less than. Go to Popeye's for better chicken.

name: Matthew Muir
text: Classic and greasy.

name: Theron Biglow
text: Great fried chicken

name: T Reed
text: Usually they are very good but every once in a while it seems like they're serving left over chicken which seems hard to believe considering the amount of business they do. You also have to check your to go order carefully lately they have been forgetting things.

name: Jeffrey Roddy
text: Excellent as always, and they're absolutely pro at six foot distancing.

name: Alaskan Wanderer
text: I stopped in there about six months back and I don't know what was going on but their Fried Chicken was not on point. Today I'm very pleased to be able to say that that has changed and that they're classic high quality of fried chicken is back to its standard. Seriously this is one of the best places in town for fried chicken and for any types of shakes you may want

name: Rebecca Bronczyk
text: Cute, little place downtown, historic for Anchorage. Food left something to be desired, but the service was good (even had a gentleman run out with our forgotten leftovers to make sure we took it home). Not a place I would incorporate in my typical restaurants, but would go back with friends, if this is were they want to eat.

name: Lecon Chuitt Jr
text: Great take out. Quick. 10 min wait

name: MeZ
text:
Great food but I have to say, when you call to place an order the service is pretty much ZERO. After 100 rings (gotta call your order in) and finally someone answers "Lucky Wish Bone, please hold" and BAM you're on hold. I wouldn't call our experience "on hold". It was more of a "You're Forgotten" experience for us. We called back a couple of times with the same Lost in Space process.

Look, I love to support our local businesses and as a family we try do that every day right now but this service is extremely lacking a quality customer experience. A real bummer and a real let down, LW.

name: Elena Bartman-wallman
text:
The service was great. The amount of customers in and out of there was a bit overwhelming, but the waiters were composed, polite, and quick.
Food was delicious. If you haven't been, I highly suggest you make time to stop in.

name: Chris Soule
text: Fantastic food as normal but the new menu started today. And the prices went up!  It loses its charm with change.

name: Rob Stapleton
text: Great service, good food, fair prices. Old time family diner atmosphere with great WWII photos. Good place for fried chicken or a cheese burger and a milk shake!

name: Kyle McClanahan
text:
Honestly the BEST fried chicken I have had in Alaska, and I’ve been here 3 years - born and raised in the south. Tastes just like how my grandmother used to make - grilled cheese, fresh cornbread, perfectly fried chicken, and the salmon chowder was AMAZING.

Will be my weekly cheat meal for a long time.

name: Patrick Simons
text: Best chicken in town. The real deal.

name: Erin Price
text: Best fried chicken and shakes in Anchorage!  I recommend the raspberry, it has real raspberries in it, and salted caramel shakes. I will say the fries and cornbread are a bit bland but the chicken more than makes up for it. It's a very casual diner style restaurant. The staff is always fast and friendly. Give it a try!

name: Alex Favaro
text: If you want good chicken come here. Trust me. The location is rough but worth it. The people here are great.

name: timothy chavis
text: Best fried chicken in Anchorage.. I ordered a chicken sandwich. and it had too much honey mustard on it, so next time I asked for no honey mustard.

name: Pig Pen Shen
text: Love this place. Very kind knowledgeable staff. The ideal place to eat & relax. 🤗💞🎶🌈

name: Dennis Morris
text: Great food just have to do take out.

name: Sakura Sano
text: They would get 5/5 if they had indoor seating....

name: Mr Bacon
text: Great chicken & service

name: Tiffany Briggs
text: Yummy chicken. Good burgers. Good shakes. Chill atmosphere, a bit dated. Would go again if nearby

name: Mitch Andrews
text: Awesome local place with classic eats and incredible milkshakes! Worth a visit again and again.

name: AkGrown71 Alaska
text: Always an excellent choice. Best fresh fried chicken in Anchorage. Another option is the jumbo Cheeseburger, order of fries, and fresh strawberry shake. Service is excellent.

name: Marge Chord
text: Ordered a fish sandwich to go...got to work and could not believe how bad it looked. One bite told me it tasted better than it looked. Because it was a total mess from brown lettuce to funny looking patty of fish.

name: Pepsi LaMar
text: Love the Onion Rings... a bit pricey

name: qbagcal
text: Best pan fried chicken in AK! Hamburgers made with fresh ingredients and home made Onion Rings makes this my favorite place in AK!

name: Jen Downs
text: A blast from the past!  The peanut butter shakes are amazing and why would you ever get anything but the chicken and onion rings is beyond me.

name: Richard Slaw Severson
text: Looks like a place where locals eat. If you like fried chicken, this place is a must. Also, great salmon chowder. And don't forget to have an old fashioned ice cream soda.

name: Brian Watts
text: This place is the BEST. First, you walk in and wait for seating, but not really because the service is super fast. Then you sit down at a nice table and are immediately served by the best people in town. You order, and it's there within 10-15 minutes, and they are always packed. I would go there everyday if I could. The area of town isn't the best, but the Lucky Wishbone brightens it up.

name: Aaron Mason
text: Had a breakfast burger that was ok.  Wait staff was really good.  Would recommend the fried chicken and fries.

name: Brian Malone
text: Lucky Wishbone is an iconic Anchorage restaurant. Very casual dining. Definitely no pretentious dishes here. Great fried chicken and burgers. For healthier options, the salads are huge and are always fresh and I've never gotten wilted lettuce. One of my favorite, quick go-to spots.

name: Gregory Hartley
text:
I have mixed feelings about Lucky Wishbone. On one hand, it's a long-standing pillar of the Anchorage dining community. Locals eat here more than tourists, which is good. Many items on the menu are scratch-made and delicious; the pan-fried chicken stands out as the obvious example. The milkshakes, too, are fantastic.

On the other hand, the menu is hit-or-miss. Step outside of their standard turf of burgers and fried chicken, and you're in a minefield. I ordered a fried fish sandwich that was just a store bought frozen fish. (It's Alaska . . . fish is a big deal). The iced tea is not freshly brewed. The fries are exactly like McDonald's fries. Those little annoyances add up, I'm afraid.

Still, if you want fried chicken and an amazing malted milk shake in a truly Alaskan environment, look no further.

name: Deborah Conroy
text: Love the place. Great burgers, and malts.

name: Paul Cohen
text: Great food, quick service, made the love of my life happy

name: Seth Weaver
text: Original hamburger and fried chicken place in anchorage. 1952. Still has the best burgers and homemade fried chicken in town. Truly an icon.

name: Alan Pongratz
text: Busy, iconic Anchorage lunch spot, famous for their chicken (which I will try on a subsequent visit). I got one of their full-sized burgers, which was plenty by itself, without their highly praised fries. Leaving here hungry doesn't seem like an option!

name: D Westlake
text: Small menu so they can concentrate on doing those things well.  It shines.

name: Barbara Hrubes
text: Lucky Wishbone Restaurant has been around for ever. If you love fried chicken its the place to go. Great burgers. Service is really good. Milkshakes are to die for, ok almost.

name: Melissa Moody
text: A classic stop.  The milkshake offerings and onion rings are my personal favorites... And the always pleasant service!

name: Roberta Stevens
text: Had the daily special, one of 8 soups daily & a tuna sand.  I cannot wrap my head around the chicken there, it looks deep fried, not pan fried.  Had a brownie sundae, was good, just a little to much whipped cream.  Server was pleasant.  VERY busy at lunch hour.

name: leslie haskins
text: Great food. A little spendy but great servers. Really friendly atmosphere. They make you feel like family

name: Jason Harrell
text: There best chicken

name: Karen Marlise Cowles
text: I’m gone to this restaurant for over 20 years for the quality of the food and it’s absolutely made well and affordable. This is an Anchorage institution of quality

name: Scott Griffin
text: Good homecooking!

name: Shane Mecham
text: First visit in years.  Food was really good.  Had the mom lunch, which was a breast leg and wing.  Chicken was moist and tender, while remaining crunchy.  Sides were good.  Rings and fries can feed 2 people, so order for what you want.  Rings were not bad at all and fries were good.  Couple people in our party ordered shakes and could not stop complimenting them.

name: Evan Koonce
text: Best fried chicken in Alaska. Great menu, service, and prices. Gotta check this place out

name: Annalise Strong
text: Great fried chicken. Try the campfire sauce!

name: BLYAK
text:
Fantastic food and even better customer services!

Just FYI the small order of slaw isn't worth the money. Csnt seem to post of pic of how small the tiny little palm sized dish is but it isn't worth the $3, just upgrade to the pint.

name: Dana Jara
text: An Anchorage institution not to be missed! Exceptional fried chicken, burgers, and shakes. Everything is made fresh and to order, so be prepared for a wait.

name: Tayma McClain
text: Love the Alaska zoo! Such nice trails and educational info about the animals. Im a lifelong Alaskan and I still enjoy going!

name: Colin Ossiander
text:
It's everything you want from a Mom & Pop diner: delicious food, low prices, and great service. They've been around since basically forever, and it's because of consistently great casual dining. I've also spoken with a APD family member (who has seen the inside of many cheaper restaurant kitchens on account of getting called in) who specifically mentioned Lucky Wishbone as having a spotless kitchen, even at the end of a long workday.
I recommend ordering the chicken 'extra crispy'.

name: Lisa Birnel Douglas
text: Good family owned restaurant, reasonable prices and love Grandma style homemade Fried Chicken... Handmade Milkshakes are so delicious!! Super friendly staff🤗

name: Sharon Miller
text: To be honest, the burgers tasted exactly like McDonald's does, even the onions were cut the same and the cheese was the same taste as McDonald's. I haven't tried anything else, but the coleslaw and I liked it. I ordered the Swiss Bacon Burger. I heard this place is famous, but am not sure why, do I was actually disappointed. The service is like any other place, so they take care. The hostess waited to seat us until she put drinks, silverware and the likes on the table, which didn't make logical sense to me. I would've rather sat down first. If you're looking for a diner in the style of a road trip film, this is it. With the pale colors, green booths, nostalgic photos strung on the walls and a homey feel. I did enjoy that because it's unique. I won't come back though.

name: Ka Vang
text: They are quite the spot in the evening, so prepare for wait times. I had their chicken with coleslaw and it was delicious. Their coleslaw had pineapple pieces and is a must try! The service was great, they got people in and out pretty fast and everyone looked and/or was happy.

name: alana melin
text: I've been eating St lucky wishbone since 1968. Went high schools with kids if the browns. Best food fir over 45 years I lived here.

name: Larry Green
text: great as ever

name: Alexis Mattson
text: I ordered the cheeseburger and a peanut butter milkshake. Absolutely delicious. Low prices, amazing quality. Larger portions, definitely worth the stop!!!

name: Robert Schwartz
text: Excellent burgers, fries, shakes, chicken! Friendly staff. Been on my places to eat list for 40 yrs!

name: DjChonga AK
text: Very nice fried chicken and burger

name: Rick Feller
text:
One of Anchorage's oldest eateries and still among the best. Easily the best fried chicken in Alaska.

Service is always friendly and top notch. While many patrons come here for the burgers, I've never tried one here because I can't not order the chicken.

I've introduced the "Bone" to all of my grandchildren, and it is their new favorite restaurant. Despite the recent passing of its founder, the place continues on with its excellent service and delicious food.

name: CA G
text: This is definately a old time cafe with a lot of cool history and great food. If your looking for a good burger, fried chicken or malt this is the spot for you. They have a number of great items on the menu I plan on trying in the near future. It may not look like much from the outside but it has a nice diner feel on the inside. Make sure you beat the rush, sometimes a line of people will run out the front door waiting for a seat. Very good food!

name: Michael Spear
text: Lunch at the Bone will bring a smile to you face and a warmth in your heart. The place has a history that is worth a listen because it explains why you get a feeling of home here. Not a bad server or attitude in the building.

name: Island Girl
text: excellent home quality made  friend chicken!! juicy and phenomenal!! Home style cooking with a 5 star rating!!

name: Brenda Valley
text: Milkshake u eat with a spoon..EVERY single spoonful is just as good as the first. I had pineapple-strawberry and can hardly wait to go back. Chicken and coleslaw was real good too.

name: Niles Laschober
text: Great burgers and pretty damn good fried chicken. Their onion rings are the best I’ve ever had. Get the ranch dip for the rings it’s homemade and awesome. Great local burger joint!

name: Emery Bowles
text: Really good fried chicken.  I like dark meat.  Well done.  Live the Cole slaw.  Has chunks of apples in it.  Nice touch

name: Traci Gleason
text: Awesome milkshakes and burgers

name: I AM JJ Walker
text: If your hankering for some fried chicken this is the spot, get there early. Fast friendly service...

name: Sarah Greenwood
text: Batter is wonderful, and the service is friendly. First time I had it to-go and it was flavorful and amazing. Second time I dined in, it was definitely fresh and well cooked, just under seasoned and a bit bland. The corn muffin was great, the fries were nothing special. I'm going to lean towards the first experience being the norm since they've been around since the 50's

name: Cynthia Street LeTourneau
text: Besides chicken they have to be one of the best places for a burger and fries that I know of. I'd rather go there than anywhere.  There is a reason why they have been around for over 50 years.

name: Allan Pickett
text:
Go here to get a burger and fries for lunch occasionally. The hamburger is handmade and the buns are homemade or local. Its impossible to keep your fingers out of the basket of fries they give you.
The food is good and the price is fair. Show up early if you want to beat the line at lunch.

name: Kornthida Sittithamsakul
text: Awesome!!

name: Michael Buck
text: This is THE PLACE to go in Anchorage if you want fried chicken. The chicken is always delicious and the way the cook it, it turns out super moist on the inside and crispy on the out They also have shakes which are good to.  The atmosphere is an old fashioned restaurant that is family friendly. It's usually got a steady flow of customers. Sometimes there is a wait, if you go at peak dinner hours, but it is usually not a long wait. Highly recommend!

name: Kodi •&•
text: This place is sweet, love to go here for something good to eat.

name: Joseph Biondich
text: The Jumbo burger just wasnt that good, and the fries were hard.

name: B. F.M
text: Everyone recommended this place "best fried chicken" well I was disappointed with my food. It was soggy and seemed a bit undercooked. Honestly KFC has better fried chicken.

name: Perry Albright
text: Its been 5 years, same great chicken.

name: Michelle Wagner
text: We met for lunch reunion. Great service, wonderful food.

name: Jeffrey Kempff
text: Outstanding fare. This is our new diner in the area! Prices are very reasonable and their 63+ years experience shows. Excellent chicken and burgers. This is a must stop for foodies and non-foodies alike. Even our toddler loved it! Family and group friendly.

name: Brad Roche
text: It's been years since I have visited.  Still the same... gives one a good feeling that some things stay the same.

name: Tina Mullins
text: Tastey chicken but poor customer service.  We waited in their drive through... Nothing like " We will be with you"  We left to KFC

name: John Moraco
text: The best Chicken and fries in town! I love eating there one of my favorite places in town for a fifty's style dinner with awesome food and people who serve you with a smile on their face.

name: donna farrell
text: Fantastic milkshakes! Place to go if you're looking for a finger licking good chicken! Would definitely go back and try something else on the menu.

name: Leland Jones
text: Best classic burger and chicken you can get! Won't let you down. Be sure to get the fries and a shake for the best experience! Love this place.

name: Jack Daniels
text: There drive through is backwards and the line is usually a little long but like any good restaurant there's a reason, and if you haven't had there chicken gizzards and fries you've been missing out on the best snack in Anchorage AK. hands down the best!!!

name: Pete Donahoo
text: Growing up near Omaha in Nebraska it's hard to find food quality with down home comfort food. This is the best I've had outside of the Midwest. Nothing beats fresh pan fried chicken! Slaw and rings are pretty hard to beat also. Opt for the corn muffins over the rolls. Little bit of fresh ground salt on the chicken, a meal you won't forget... In one of the seafood capitals of the world.

name: Stephanie Douglas
text: The best crispy fried gizzards and strawberry shortcake.

name: Joseph Jeffrey
text: The milkshakes are second to none honestly.

name: Bryan Hawkins
text: This is a historical spot in Anchorage and it's long tenure in the city becomes apparent when you visit. Pictures of it's history is all over the walls, and their food is the pinnacle of comfort food in the city and It ranks among the top eateries in Anchorage. Quick and friendly service with a "southern hospitality" like charm make Lucky Wishbone a must visit for locals / tourist alike.

name: Gia Jean
text: Historic my uncle John pannick always took me here when I was a kid great chicken I love it and I love the milkshakes to I applied here hoping to get a job soon Angela Idzinski

name: David Okitkon
text: Should be known for its pan fried chicken,  but it was just decent. The batter was ok, and  the chicken itself should have been tastier.  The cornbread muffin didn't seem fresh but made yesterday and kind of dry. The blueberry milkshake was tasty though.

name: Adeline Leung
text: I love the drive through.

name: Evelyn Posala
text: They have drive thru and customer service is usually great. The fried chicken, fries, and milkshakes are delicious! Cornbread was dry. Overall delicious food.

name: Colin Rastall
text: One on one service, good food very relaxing

name: Kyle Hampton
text: The fried chicken is the best we've had in Alaska yet. They are sure to get a good crunch on the chicken without overwhelmingly thick breading. The shakes are also pretty deadly...

name: Chris Tadda
text: Great food andservice. 5 stars..

name: Jennifer Madsen
text: Super yummy food! Love all of their foods. Try one of the malted desserts! And the fried chicken. Serving sizes are larger than what is supposed to be an average amount of food, but not extremely so.They are a little pricey but worth it.

name: Hokulani Fritz
text: My num Dr 1 favorite fried chicken. Always will return for the good stuff and fast service with a smile.

name: Scott Pessetto
text: Best place to stop after coming in from the valley for a nice meal.

name: Derik Dorgan
text: I've been going here since I was a kid, the food has always been great. Love the onion rings, Fries are always great, but the burgers! The burgers are my favorite, double jumbo Swiss bacon is my go to. Aside from the crowd that always seems to be there the service staff always is great and the food always comes out quick and hot. The only complaint that I have and I believe merits a lost star, is the place is too small to accommodate the crowd that always seems to populate this wonderful burger joint. I know the owner is getting up there in age and probably doesn't want to put the money in a remodel, but that's all this place needs!

name: Craig Aitchison
text: Fried chicken and a chocolate shake. Avoid if on a diet, but don't avoid it really even if you are. Excellence!

name: Always4u Today
text: Definitely NOT delivery friendly!!!

name: Bruce Marshall
text: Great food, wonderful staff and very friendly atmosphere.

name: Howard Diamond
text: Always good chicken!!!

name: sugeily morales
text: The best place to eat. waiters are super friendly and  professional. the food is fresh and delicious ...EVERYONE STOP BY AND TRY IT !!!!

name: Andy Gilda Jr
text: Delish pan fried chicken. Fair price for what you get. The staff are nice and friendly also very helpful

name: Dustin Moses
text: I got my meals the way I ordered them it was delicious

name: Elizabeth Taylor
text: Service  was average,  quality  of food was very low, and quantity of portion of food low compared  to last visit.  As a veteran  I would not recommend  this restaurant for this item ,chicken  gizzards.  Thanks Mike Taylor

name: Radu Croitoru
text: Great food, good atmosphere, reasonable prices, staff very friendly and helpful

name: Barbara Frey
text: Loved their fried chicken!!  Super busy place and large portions.

name: Saundra Johnson
text: This has become a go to for my husband, who loves chicken, during our stay in Anchorage.  The only negative is the price. They are pretty pricey.

name: Theresa Philbrick
text: Always delicious. Milkshakes velvety smooth, second only to Arctic Roadrunner's. Moist, tender chicken. No pretentiousness. Just good cooking like my grandma did.

name: desiree matter
text: Still great food! Interesting that they now open on Sundays!

name: Hugh Perry
text: My chicken was totally over cooked! It was pretty expensive for a two piece meal, and the sides were blah! Seriously disappointed! :(

name: Old Skool E
text: Anchorage landmark. Pan fried chicken and fries. Old time airport pilot spot. Best chicken in town. A lot of history and memories. Drive thru options. Fries or slaw. Busy but affordable has other menu items. Delicious.

name: Steve O
text: Always the place to go for fried chicken and make pretty good gizzards too.

name: Thecla Greenlee
text: Chicken is delicious, fries are salty enough and smoothies are good for sweets. Thank you!

name: Lynda Lewis
text: The  best  chicken  in Alaska. Take out or eat in lucky wishbone has incredible fried chicken and mikkshakes. If you have not been to Lucky Wishbone you are missing out!!

name: BRETT PIERCEFIELD
text: Burgers, fries and shakes are very good. They're "famous" for their pan fried chicken 🍗, but I don't know what the big deal is. There's no seasoning on it, none at all. It's just chicken fried in oil! That's all you taste, chicken and oil.

name: Chief Reviews Everything
text: Great chicken, great service and great prices!

name: Amy Lieb
text: Funny set up situation

name: Lisa Haney
text: I have been going to lucky wishbone for a very very long time.  Had not been there in quite some time but was in the area so I stopped in with family. Not a thing has changed busy busy awesome service and fantastic eats and shakes! Cheeseburger,fries, onion rings and Fried chicken and a couple shakes it’s all still so great served fast and tastes awesome.

name: Jason Davies
text: Lucky Wishbone is an old style diner throwback to the 50s, where the pilots came in for a quick bite before protecting the the Nothern most part of the United States during the cold war.  Menu mainly features burgers, sandwiches and unfrozen chicken.  The star of the show is the milkshakes.  So good.  The memories of the old days are there, but it's fading slowly.

name: Katherine Barrios
text: The food there is really good.

name: Carl Olson
text: Good fried chicken and shakes.

name: Ashley Chuitt
text: The servers are always so lovely

name: Farid Sanouvong
text: One of the best restaurant diner in town! This place gives a great settings for meet-ups and family outings. The crew is definitely friendly and brings joy to the locals when I first entered the diner. Pretty good atmosphere - I really digged it! And if you know some locals well.. there are secret menu items.. 🤙😏

name: Saralan Ruth Hancock
text: Onion rings were not done.

name: Jeff Willis
text: Good clean place, great service.

name: Thomas Greenman
text:
Great local fried chicken joint that has fried gizzards and livers.  If you're from the south and you enjoy that sort of thing - this is the place for you!  If you're into fried chicken, it's also good too but for those looking for spicy or savory fried chicken, you may be disappointed.

Fantastic shakes & malts as well!

name: Sandra Syrup
text: Sooo Yummmy!

name: Tony Tiranno
text: Very good food and good price. Highly recommend

name: Glen M. Allen
text: Always great home made foods! Longtime original family run business in Anchorage! Always busy;...fast food delivery, worth a visit!!!

name: Rebecca Phelps
text: Best salad ever.  delicious homemade Croutons

name: Justin Fleming-Brown
text: Great chicken, fries, shakes and more.

name: Natalie Cardenas
text:
food was good! everything was good except for my
cup. there was a lip print from a previous customer...

name: Nichole Banks
text: Friendly service and delicious,  old fashioned milkshakes!

name: Bishop David
text: Fantastic chicken and wonderful staff.  They all work hard to make your dining experience the best.  You feel like family.  If you've never been here, you need to go.

name: Michael Tierese
text: This restaurant has been in anchorage since I was a child the taste has always stayed the same, simply amazing.

name: GenHazard
text: A truly classic establishment, quite delicious food and excellent milkshakes. Highly recommended.

name: Mike Brown
text: The Brown family is the best.  Been going to this restuarant my entire life.  Best chicken in town!

name: Marguarita Marion

name: Michael Forte
text: I love this zoo, and animal refuge.  Every exhibit in the park is alluring and fascinating. My kids love it so much.  I love that they are always interested in going.  We go just about every Sunday. Porcupine, tigers,  wolves, wolverine, snow leopard and Llama (rest easy Caesar) are our must see every time.

name: bethany rosendahl
text: A great way to spend an afternoon. They have daily critter chats where they show you the animal if the day up close with a few snacks. We had a lot of fun I definitely suggest it!

name: Kelley Soper
text: Zoo Lights was fun, though not amazing. It was nice to have something festive to do in the evening, especially with so many things closed down. We were able to see some animals, though most were hunkered down for the night.

name: Mat Pyles
text: Great day with my family

name: Stephen Wood
text: It is a great time for the kids. There are all sorts if animals. The only things missing were polar bear, wolverine and moose.

text:
It's a zoo and it's nice
Nothing super exciting but it's nice

name: Michael Padgett
text: Very nice zoo. Exhibits are laid out with trees between them, giving it a very wooded atmosphere. A great selection of animals on exhibit.

name: Maranda Powell
text: A nice little zoo with lots of beautiful local animals! Easy to see all the creatures within 2-3 hours.

name: Stacy Hawkins
text: Everybody loves the zoo! I just didn't know when I took my mother, who is in a wheelchair, that I would be pushing her in gravel. Leaving and having to push uphill was excrutiating. This was the first zoo I ever went to where the walkways are not paved. To see the seals, we had to go all the way to the end of the display area and cut back to be able to reach it in a wheelchair. Just a little disappointing.

name: Jace Olsen
text: It was really fun for the most part. Wish there were more animals to see, a lot of them we couldn't even see cuz there were so hidden. Besides that tho it was pretty cool.

name: Lawrence Goodrich
text: Nice little zoo, but the special behind the scenes tour was $28! Too expensive for very little knowledge you gain. Just walk it yourself.

name: Angeline Whitman
text:
Great place to go with the kids. They enjoyed every moment. Wow, one if those bears was playing in the water with a boey.
We enjoyed the experience. Thank you Alaska Zoo for being open, and such a positive experience.

name: rachel stein
text: Very Awesome! I was so happy to see the polar bears together finally! Watching the Grizzlies was amazing. Very clean, very kid friendly, and they take AMAZING care of their animals.

name: Autumn Paris
text: Anyways educational and the staff is great.  I miss face painting for them. I always did a froggy on this woman's face and she was always the best model

name: Holly Green
text: Didn't get to see very many animals. Might have been a timing thing. Such a lovely place and walk through that I didn't mind much.

name: Evan Nunley
text: I love the Anchorage Zoo! Especially Little Rock the Musk Ox. Hes the best! I'll come back every year to say hi to him! The Zoo is doing everything it can to keep people safe during the pandemic. When we went, on a Thursday, there were not many people there at all making it very easy to social distance!

name: Kim Murphy
text: Great Zoo Lights Night. We had a lot of fun despite rain, hail, snow and Wind. Lights were beautiful.

name: Joe Eklund
text: Nice animals. The enclosure could be better.

name: Serena G
text: I really liked the layout of it how it was like walking through the woods & seeing animals. The gift shop is awesome too. I think it needs more play areas for the kids.

name: Patrick Simons
text: Really appreciate the zoo putting this together this year. Not a huge display but we'll put together and worth the trip

name: Dimitra Kourtesi
text: Cute zoo! My first time seeing muskox and yak and really up close!

name: Conner Erickson
text: Nice zoo for Alaska.  Decent array of wild animals, both native and non-native.  Gift shop and snack bar available.  Plentiful parking.  Friendly staff.

name: Ryan Jensen
text: I love this zoo. I love animals. Most of the animals were resting. It was nice though. Not very much people there.

name: Austin Langford
text: Incrediblely fun i reccomend for a date or a family day out ♡♡ the animals are well taken care of and the docile friendly attitudes reflect it the show offs ♡♡♡

name: tlchenvt
text: Polar bear was not there. Watched bald eagle, snow panther very closely. The brown bears don’t live in very good condition. They looked bored.

name: Brian
text: Great place to take the family!!!  Small but enough to occupy the kids for a bit!!

name: Evelyn Blandino
text: There are a lot of good exhibits of animals that are native to the far north. The walk from one exhibit to the next is very enjoyable. The forest setting feels natural to what you are here to enjoy. I do wish that there were more detailed learning opportunities. These are seriously the most fun paint jobs I've ever seen in a public restroom, though.

name: Jeff Stetz
text: Great setting, a nice variety of native and exotic species, and good educational information about the residents.  Certainly better than any indoor activities like watching idiots on television!

name: Deanna Pushruk
text: Animals were finally talking today. Lots of fun as usual. I sure miss elephants being there. Just as well, they dont need to he caged. Lol never smelled camels before 👃peeww!

name: Thomas Greenman
text: Really amazing zoo for its size with all sorts of things for kids to runs and do.  Lots of hills so be ready for some exercise.  Fun place to get out and escape the hustle and bustle of town.  Gift shop and snack bar inside, as well as ample parking.

name: Amie Kirby
text: Very small zoo, great for smaller kids. Several of the areas didn't have any animals. Spent about an hour or so there and saw everything. The staff seemed very friendly and nice.

name: Felicia Judge
text: Fun and the right price. The polar bear decided to not grace us with his presence but all the other animals were out and about. Cutest baby seal ever!

name: Kristina Fidler
text: We like the zoo enough that we got an annual membership despite living an hour away. We enjoy seeing the bigger animals there,  but there are quite the selection! Moose, caribou, yak, deer, grizzly bear, polar bear, black bear, musk ox, tiger camel... so many more! My daughter's current favorite is Cranberry, the polar bear, however, I really enjoy the seals and otters.

name: Chris Betts
text: Very nice zoo showcasing a lot of native wildlife to Alaska as well as playing an important role in conservation efforts. Staff was very friendly and informative.

name: Teresa Brown
text: Great hidden treasure! Close-up, personal views of the animals.

name: Sean Ling
text: Had a wonderful time with family

name: Tayla Jones
text: It cost a good amount if money and there is hardly any animals. It took maybe an hour to take my niece who is 7 and my nephew who is 10 around to every open exhibit it was definitely better before covid. Now it's a little disappointing

name: Jennifer Pittman
text: Great local zoo to view bears and wolves.  The wolves always catch my eye and the exhibit is built nicely to view them pretty closely.

name: Michael Rosebeary
text: Always a great time!

name: Ryan Bish
text: Been coming to the Alaska Zoo to view the polar bears since 2002, went to the seminar about the declining beluga whale population in cook inlet on 11/13/2019, super informational with great speakers. Highly recommend the wildlife Wednesday series

name: Lucy Moose
text: This is a great place for kids to walk around and get rid of that winter energy. Animals well cared for. Clean and friendly. Christmas lights are fun too.

name: doris hernandez

text: Small but that's ok. The zoo does not receive any public funding. Most of the animals there are rescues but a few have been snatched. Overall it was a good visit.

name: David Bozard
text: My family loves this place. Beautiful place to spend in the summer and winter. My daughter loves going back often, especially for their perfectly salted popcorn.

name: Cheryl Wirkus
text: A lot bigger place then I expected.  Very clean.  Nice zoo.  Zoo keepers were awsome!

name: Katie Weniger
text: Always a good experience when I visit. It gives everyone a chance to get an up close look at animals found in Alaska and some from other parts of the world. I like supporting the zoo because they do great rehabilitation work and educate the public a out wildlife.

name: Becky Noyes
text: Very nice zoo with lots of really nice exhibits and plenty of animals to enjoy!  Actually now one of my favorite zoos!  We actually visited later in the day, so it wasn't very busy and it was a cooler day so many of the animals were out front and center.  I hope to return someday when I make it back to Alaska someday.

name: Colby
text: Would have been better if we had been able to see the polar bear. But besides that it was a good little zoo.

name: Steven Kosmicki
text: Really nice facility and the animals were active with the cooler weather!

name: Michael Crismon
text: Awesome place to visit. Loved it.

name: Parker Helble
text: Plenty of mammals and birds, but be aware there aren't reptiles or amphibians. Totally worth $15 admission. Great trip for both kids and adults!

name: Elvira Morozova

text: It's quaint, but has a great selection of Alaska's most fun and dangerous animals. Lovely walking paths and good displays of animals that mostly look happy.

name: Victoria Avery
text: We did the zoo keeper for a day and it was amazing. We got to make diets for some of the animals and feed a handful! Of course, we had to um clean up after them too. But these up close encounters I will remember for the rest of my life!

name: Amber Sluss
text: Many areas are blocked off im assuming due to covid, but the prices are still the same. Would be better if they told you that ahead of time or offered lower ticket pricing due to that.  Everything is also overgrown and makes it harder to see the animals.

name: Ashmeet Singh Rekhi
text: Have seen better zoos. It wasn't bad.

name: Yellow Jacket
text: Anchorage, Ak zoo is a great place to take the family and enjoy the day. Lots of animals to see. My favorite being the tigers but all animals are awesome to see. My advice would be to get there earlier in the day to enjoy and take your time cause the zoo does close at 4pm daily.

name: Yeva S-yan
text: Excellent place! And very educational place for our little ones.

name: Emma P
text:
The zoo is a nice place to go. It's small but with a lot of amazing animals.
But the cages look small too and the polar bear seemed very alone to me...

name: Just Jessee
text: Always brings a smile to my face. It may not be the biggest zoo out there, but it's Our zoo.

name: Hannah Wentz
text: We had a great time at this zoo. We went on a weekday and it wasn't too crowded. They have a wide variety of animals and open enclosures. We watched the wolverines and coyotes run around and play. The wolves also gave us a howling a acapella to enjoy.

name: Rob Moriarty
text: It's a relatively small zoo.  But it was fun.

name: Kyle Green
text:
Been here before in the summer. Great activity to bring little ones on nice days. Tonight (2018 Black Friday) we attended the opening of Zoo Lights. Fun event where various Christmas lights are displayed through the zoo as you visit with the animals that are still up and moving at night in the cold. For use this was the seals, leopards, tigers, cyotes, muskox, and a few others I'm not remembering.

TDLR: Zoo Lights was a great event and always fun to visit this place for the littles to see a variety of animals.

name: Amanda Graves
text: It was Great. Staff answered a bunch of questions. Watched the bears be fed. So fun.

name: aaron donham
text: Nice zoo , very clean, animals seemed well cared for. The animals seemed very old...especially the wolves

name: Ka Vang
text: Finally found us some parking. I did expected more animals. A lot of the cages were empty with no animals to be found. But overall experience was good. The walk around was very tiring on my leg, but that just means I'm out of shape. My second time there and will continue going back.

name: Scott Carpenter
text: Small and just right for a few hours of walking around...most animals were out wondering around....

name: Rakshanda Visave
text: I had really good time in here. It was fun watching Alfa  and also beer .

name: Nephrym
text: Very clean and well maintained! The staff are friendly and knowledgeable. The animals seem to sleep in the middle of the afternoon though, so I will have to try going sometime earlier in the day when next I visit. My daughter's favorites are the seals and the petting zoo!

name: Melissa Moody
text: One of my favorite place in town to take visitors, because the animals are great, the mission of the zoo is an important one, and the walking paths around the zoo are enjoyable all on their own!

name: Michael Jenks
text:
I go here several times a year, and for the past 3 years it's been excellent.
Was cool to come and see the wolves shedding their coats and going white.
Great for kids and adults.
Only 4 stars due to unclear signage. I've been going here for YEARS and still have trouble finding the cafe...

name: J. J.
text: Such an awesome place. A must-see. Got to speak with some of the staff that manage the Bears and The Wolverine

name: Wynona Mills
text: They were amazing. The wolf keeper was so amazing. He made sure my husband had his dream come true. Keep up the good work. Love you guys.

name: Lorrena Terry
text: Always a fun time at the zoo. Great trail to walk. All kinds of animals, friendly staff, nice cafe, and a small playground all hidden within #GetOutandPlay #Everyday #Anchorage #Alaska

name: Makayla Suttle
text: I feel like I wasted my time and money. Most of the animals weren't out and it was the middle of a nice day...

name: Mike Grauf
text: The zoo provides the ambience of walking through the forest to see the animals.

name: Andrew Nowa
text: Lots of great animals. Perfect size for small children.

name: Adriana Fisher
text: Fun outing with kids, good safe covid practices in place!

name: B D
text: Love the zoo!  They have some great animals and take good care of them.  Some cages are empty, which is a good thing for the animals :)

name: Peter Nussbaum
text: For the price this is one of the coolest zoos I have ever been at.

name: Sean Ryan
text: Not a lot has changed since I was kid going here over 20 years ago. Most of the same animals and a lot of them are local animals to the region. Small compared to other city zoo's. It is worth checking out but not a place you would pay to go in again and again.

name: Rob Petrie
text: Nice local zoo. Many of the animal exhibits are outdated and cramped. Trails though the zoo could use better signage.

name: Matt Houser
text: The Zoo was nice. Recommended for seeing some Arctic wildlife.

name: Lunch Lady InAk
text: Small but very cool zoo! Wide assortment of creatures! Cute food and coffee shop! Playground for the little ones! Also they go all out for several holidays... Halloween is really cool!

name: Keegs Sah
text: Really cool. Never expected to ever be able to see a living Snow Leopard but they had 2 there!

name: Alex Slaght
text: We went here yesterday for our sons first birthday and we all loved it. I adore that it is a rescue/rehab zoo and they have informational plaques that tell you the story of each of the inhabitants. Great prices and amazing people!

name: Zac Keyes
text: Was able to walk around in a hour, went during a snow storm so there wasn't many people there. My toddler loved it. Only wish it was a little bigger.

name: Franny Yeates
text: Not physically the largest zoo we have seen, but very likely the most amazing collection of animals. All of Alaska’s and Canada’s bears, wolves, and moose, plus tigers and various yaks from Central Asia, and Snow Leopards!! One of the rarest animals on earth, and they have two! They are unbelievably gorgeous. A devoted, dedicated and very friendly staff. Absolutely delightful place to visit.

name: Kerry Hall
text: Its ways fun for the family to go to the zoo. My mom took me and my sister almost every week when we were kids.

name: Alene McDermott
text: Its a great little place to walk and look at local and northern animals with family.

name: Marc McCuen
text: Kids loved it, all that matters.

name: Nunyo Bidnez
text: Just a great place.  The Zoo Lights are worth going for alone.

name: kristina elshoff
text: What a fun small zoo! We visited on the 50th anniversary when it was half price, and the staff were doing lots of scheduled visits in the pens with the animals. The staff was great at answering all of our questions while working with the animals. Some animals were not present that were shown on the map - I found out some had passed on. Most of the animals are rescued. They had an infirmary and orphaned area section which I thought was nice to have. However, the petting zoo was only a goat and 3 chickens.

name: Malachy Moran
text: A really fun way to spend a few hours. Small, but they have a great selection of animals, most of them native to Alaska. Favorites are the seals, bears and owls. Not too expensive, and definitely worth the 15 bucks.

name: Kelsey Moore
text: The polar bear was the best!!! Loved all the informational signs too.

name: Ursula Pico
text: Was fun for me and the kids, nice walk.  beautiful animals; The Tigers were my favorite

name: Dave Cossairt
text: As always staff were friendly and helpful

name: Shari Gilbert Mitchell
text: Neat, clean, easy access and animals are well cared for!!

name: Lynda Gauthier
text: Beautiful day for a visit to the Anchorage Zoo. Love all the critters

name: Joel Johnson
text: Not a large zoo but respectable.

name: Chris Bering
text: Our 6 year old had a great time. We liked the wilderness feel of the zoo. The coffee shop was a great resting point and the gift shop had a nice variety of items to choose from. Overall, we spent about 3 hours there and saw everything in the zoo.

name: Pam g
text: Very nice Zoo.

name: Russell Durkee
text: Not a huge Zoo. Nothing new is Zoo. For what they have is really clean. Animal seem well cared for. Definitely not over the top. Give yourself about an hour maybe an hour and a half.

name: Gary Poppe
text: I thought the zoo was okay.  My biggest complaint was some of the pens were quite small and there was no sun relief.  It was warm the day we were there and some of the animals, with heavy coats of fur, had no protection from the sun's heat.  Shade and/or water relief seemed appropriate.  On a positive note, they did have a large variety of animal species and it was an overall positive experience.

name: Norman Payne
text: Relatively expensive to maybe see 8 animals and a splattering of birds. Can't recommend this place, at least not at the moment.

name: Deborah Romani
text: Great time!  Loved all the animals, and learning their stories.

name: Randy Rienth
text: Great place to spend a day. Fun day for all. Go to the 12:30 discovery tour, well worth the extra money.

name: dan geno
text: Not many animals an they didn't look very well.. cages overgrown with brush.. kinda sad

name: Patrick House
text: Had a great time, wonderful place.

name: Simon Carpenter
text: This is a very nice small zoo. I like that many of the paths are not paved (like say, the San Diego or St. Louis zoos). The paths are natural material and it makes it feel like you're walking through a forest full of beautiful and interesting animals. The zoo has a very nice gift shop too.

name: L V
text: Great place to view all the Alaskan animals. Easily spend half a day there. Do the behind the scenes tour for an awesome experience.

name: Brad Bliton
text: Great place to take the kids and spend a day. There is always something unique and the animals are amazing. The snow leopards are beautiful and are a true rarity to see.

name: Evotia Taliulu
text: It was our 1st experience w/sum of of our famz from out of state.  We didn't see no polar bears nd it was too pricey but not worth it!!!

name: Nichole A
text: Great zoo. The paddocks are cool and you get closer to the animals than any zoo I've ever been too. Good collection of animals. The wolves are the best! And Cranberry of course.

name: Amber Ausdahl
text: Wonderful, educational zoo with a beautiful wooded trail and lots of animals! Such great memories here!

name: C Lippert
text: The night lites were pretty and colorful. Few animals as the cold should have kept us in too.

name: Christopher Zamora
text: Went to a church dance here, it was very fun, and exciting, I fell down while kidding with someone, and injured my back! Let me say best injury yet!

name: Louis
text: This zoo has some nice areas and ideas. The animals generally looked well taken care of. The facilities and condition of the zoo were poorly kept, and the total lack of on-screen signage directing customers, especially tourists was disappointing.

name: Chelsea Graf
text: Not your average zoo and that's what keeps the animals happy! A delightful stroll along the gravel trails, under a rustling canopy of leaves! No elephants or other large, southern hemisphere animals. Here you'll experience wolves, owls, eagles, and a few surprisingly content camels; who knew they'd like the Alaska climate! Always educational joy as staff takes time to teach us about their animals and various programs. Our favorite visit is always to the orphan bear cubs as they are rescued ans cared for until re-release!

name: Joe Barron
text: We had a really good time. It's a smaller zoo but a lot more animals than I expected (especially during the winte) and I thought it was played out very well.

name: Clayton spann
text: Was ok. A lot perhaps 20% of display s were empty

name: Melodious Merri
text: Always a great place to visit for Alaskans or visitors. I have an annual pass and go often with my son. Lots of rescued animals and sometimes they are baby bears.

name: Lauren Newton
text: Love the zoo! I am local but enjoy taking the kids frequently as we see different things each time.

name: Emily Clarrey
text: Nice little zoo! Staff was very friendly! Very cool to see animals you cant see at other zoo's like polar bears, eagles, Grizzlies, ox, doll sheep!

name: Tyler Pendergrass
text: Went for zoo lights. Was very impressed with the displays and attention to detail

name: Kyle von Bose
text: Great for kids that like animals. There's a small playground here too for little ones.

name: loretta mcgee
text: Love the animals! They are so always happy to great people. The workers are so helpful and help with people with disabilities.

name: Savanna Piekarski
text: The staff was very helpful, professional, and knowledgeable. The two women working at the petting zoo were willing to assist with questions from my eleven year old brother. Another female worker was able to answer all of the groups questions about the caribou. And there were a lot of little kids bursting with questions! The zoo itself was clean, welcoming, informative, and fun!

name: Cinderwolf 05
text: Great place!

name: Cas

name: Linda Maywald

name: Julia Lavin
text: Fun to see in winter with no crowds, but definitely missed seeing the bears. They offer a lot of great programs for locals and the staff were friendly. Wish there were more spots to warm up during the walk, but otherwise a lot of fun!

name: Casey Renteria
text: This place is a maze in a good way. My daughter loved getting lost on the paths to different animals. We spent 2 hours here and didnt see everything. Great place to take toddlers to kill an afternoon.

name: GenHazard
text: Great zoo to explore. Wonderful exhibit's, though could use some better amenities as far as food goes. Just a small coffee shop with minimal snacks.

name: The Roaming Rosiers
text:
Nice, clean, gives a good feel of local wildlife.
Paths are rocky and steep in some places. It is easier to have a jogging or trail stroller or pack little ones. It was lots of fun for my 4yr old. Enjoyed the information stations.

name: Ty Kon
text: Still an amazing place to visit. I haven't been in 10 years but took my neice today and had as much fun as ever. The wolf enclosure is amazing. My niece wanted to "start a howl" while all the wolves were asleep. Not only did she wake them up, but they all came to see her. Always worth a trip and if you've never been, you simply must.

name: Anthony Mosley
text: One of the best location in the town to go with family and enjoy your time. I really like this place. Will surely revisit here.!!

name: leslie

name: T. Frank Box

name: Tasha Skolnick

name: Sharon Palacios

name: Connor Priest

name: Brian Malone
text: The only zoo in Anchorage. Easiest place to guarantee you will see many of the wonderful arctic and sub arctic animals that make Alaska famous.

name: Melody Mcdaniel
text: It's a great set up. They give homes to animals from all over the world. Most have been rescued and would have died. It is a must way to spend the day. And so very affordable

name: Daniel Moseley
text:
Alaska Zoo is a great place to take the family for an afternoon outing.  It usually takes our family about two hours to see all of the animals.  We bought an annual membership since we're a pretty large crew.

(Admittedly, we were spoiled years ago by the Saint Louis Zoo; I still can't believe that place has free admission.)

name: Keith Watson
text: Great zoo for Alaska!

name: Suman Pandey
text: I saw lot of animal neglect and poor living condition. Especially bears and birds. They don't deserve caging. It was sad to see bald eagle cooped up in such small area. And three grizzlies in a small confined area. Coyote has no business in zoo. It is not even endangered. Overall area given to animals is very small. And that is abuse. I didn't expect this from a 50 years old zoo.

name: Linda Friend
text: The nachos were gross. But seeing the brown bear up close was so cool. And the wolves..

name: Mark Jensen
text: All zoos get 5 stars from me. Instead of a walk in the park, take a stroll in the zoo! Grab a coffee midway and get some gifts too!
