name: Elizabeth
text: Nice place.  well kept and good for kids to come and learn about animals. Wish the coffee shop hours matched zoo hours

name: James Morowski
text: Great place to check out. Cool animals to see up close and the staff was super nice. Has an awesome gift shop that will make you wish you had an extra bag to bring stuff home.

name: Nicole Fuster
text: I loved this zoo I wish their were more animals though and was handicap friendly it's not paved and because of that wheelchairs and dirt don't really work out that great but it was very beautiful and I did enjoy the animal's I did see though

name: Angel A
text: Great time with family and kids. Thank you!

name: Jerry Quinn
text: Great spot to see Alaska's critters plus a few "out of state" visitors. An easy one hour walk can pretty much cover the grounds or a little longer if you're escorting the kids. Well worth a look

name: Michelle Winchester
text: Kids loved it.

name: Bruce Marshall
text: This is worth the visit while visiting Anchorage. It's a wonderful place with friendly staff that really do care about the animal guest they are hosting.

name: Teresa Preston
text: Good place to spend in Anchorage! Is cost effective.

name: KK6WGO Rollins
text: They know what will survive here.  Friendly staff, good food on snack bar, priced fair; food and admission.  Had raindeer dog, good and spicy.

name: Gerie A
text:
The zoo is a lot of fun to me and I love animals. The zoo is small and easy to walk around winter or summer. The animals are all Alaskan except the camels, lamas, yaks and the tigers. However they were all rescued from the wild and it is a fun way to see the devirsety of animals Alaska has.
Lots of fun for little kids too, they have a small playground and a petting zoo with farm animals
In the summer the zoo offers free shuttles from Downtown and in the winter the Zoo Lights are a lot of fun to see.

name: Brianna Eisenbacher
text: Adorable little zoo. Majority of animals are indigenous to alaska, but a plenty of outliers. Took us approximately 2 hours to see everything at a moderate pace. Admission is reasonable  with a cute coffee shop and gift store. There is a small petting zoo area with chickens, a rabbit and a few goats. Lots of good informational plaques with lots of staff around to ask questions. Polar bear was sleepy today, but the brown and black bears were lively. Very cool 5-dog wolf pack that was also fun to watch. Easy to accidentally drive past as the sign kind of pops up behind the trees, so watch closely as you get near on the road. Will definitely be back!

name: Amber Davidson
text: Small zoo with multiple construction projects going. A couple of new bear Cubs which were adorable playing outside. Not a great day to go probably since most are Arctic species and it was too hot for them! The snow leopards were down close to the gravel trying to chill off which was quite cool since they were so close.

name: JD Smith
text: The tiger experience is amazing!

name: Christian Jacobs
text: Great small town zoo! Great place to see the animals of Alaska without going into the bush. It is very well maintained and has exceptionally friendly staff. I go here every time I visit anchorage and thoroughly enjoy every visit.

name: Tayma McClain
text: Delicious homemade burgers with special sauce and homemade french fries. Love this old time restaurant!

name: Darcy Boerner
text: Awesome experience! One of my kids wanted to see a moose while we were in Alaska.  The zoo offered that and so much more.  Great day at the zoo but wear walking shoes

name: Grant Hartwig
text: 4.5 out of 5. Just got done seeing the zoo lights. Great time and awesome animals. They have all the Alaskan animals, only reason it gets 4.5 and not 5 is because the AWCC is 40 min away and has almost just as many animals but is more of an Alaskan experience.

name: drago main
text: Love to spend my time here and see all the animals and scenery. They also have a lot of pokemon go stops which is super cool.

name: Mike wheeler

name: david webb

Don't forget to check their website for the live polar bear webcam.

name: Dave Williams
text: Surprisingly great zoo for being in Alaska. My girlfriend and I had a great time. If you find yourself in Anchorage it's worth the visit and ten bucks.

name: CA G
text: A good place to see exotic and alaskan animals. They have a great gift shop and petting zoo for their goat population. It's a great place to bring your family if they have never seen these types of animals.

name: Kaity Eliz

name: denis S

name: Jeff Brasel

Nice to see some animals, unfortunately the petting zoo was closed.  With the cold weather several off exhibit signs.. which is good the animals are being cared for.

name: Becca Hill

name: David Brown

name: Adam Booth
text: I love our zoo.  It's smaller and more simple than others I've been to, but I think it's authentically Alaskan while throwing in a couple of surprises (like Amur tigers for one example). The amount of bugs that bothered us while visiting was minimal.

Family friendly and a small area to picnic made this better.

name: Tom Tunnell

name: m. w. brooke
text: this is tough for me. i think i'm growing less fond of zoos these days. i found myself fairly depressed while walking the grounds as i noticed the very small, dirty enclosures, with most of the animals huddled in the corners of their enclosures or anxiously pacing the perimeters. they didn't necessarily look neglected or in major distress, but i definitely felt like my presence there wasn't exactly doing any good for these poor creatures. while i fully understand that most of these animals were born into captivity or were in some way injured and cannot survive in the wild, it's difficult to be able to justify putting them on display. still, it was pretty wonderful to get to see a snow leopard, polar bear and amur tiger up close. go early (9-10am) or in the evening, or you risk visiting when they're all sleeping.

text: Gotta go in summer. Gotta go especially Italy in winter.  The extra bucks for a tour is worth more than you expect.

name: John Albee
text: This zoo is different than most in the lower 48 in that it's smaller and seems to have a different focus.  We we lived in Phoenix we used to go to the Phoenix Zoo which is nice however I prefer The Alaska Zoo because the walk is so much more enjoyable even if there is overall less exhibits. We ended up getting seasons passes as its a quick outing and like every zoo, is going to be a different experience based on time of day and time of year.  We have our own stroller that works well on trails however it does appear that they have loaner strollers that would do better on the paths than city strollers.  The paths aren't perfect level cement paths everywhere which is nice as I think it makes it feel a bit more natural.

name: Christie Cox

text: The crab was so delicious! Everything was  great! Great waiter, bartender! 👍

name: Mary Farnstrom
text:
Unfortunately poor service and poor quality food when we went the other night. They forgot our drink orders and staff didn't communicate between each other at all.

They were were friendly, but poorly managed their time and customers. :(

Used to enjoy going to the Turtle Club, but that visit has made it to where we no longer want to go back. We hope they are able to improve in the future and get back to what they used to be.

name: MaryJean Fischer
text: Very good and fun atmosphere.  Remember that Alaska fine dining is not the same as San Francisco fine dining, i.e. paper place mats with the menu printed on them. We started with a chilled Kendal Jackson Chardonnay. The salad bar is worth getting. We all ordered the all you can eat salad bar which was very satisfying and fresh.  Mom had the halibut appetizer lightly battered and deep fried.  Plenty generous, the halibut was thinner pieces as opposed to the fat chunks we enjoy when we catch our own.  I had the same but steamed with drawn butter. Very nice.  Our young man had the prime rib.  Cooked to medium perfection and very tender.  We all had dessert.  Outstanding dark chocolate cake, rich with 7 layers.  Chocolate mousse light and smooth. Creme brulee very thick served cold.  Better if room temp maybe.  Total bill almost 200 for 4 people.  Worth it.

name: Bao Cheng
text: I ordered the combo of lobster tail and foxy cut of prime rib. My husband ordered halibut chunks and portabella mushroom fries. It were really delicious.

name: Evan Nunley
text: By far the best Prime Rib I've ever had. This place has had the hand of god touch their cooks, because it is unreal how amazing the food is. Also has the best salad bar in town! I will keep coming back here time and time again, there is no place like it anywhere else in the world. If you haven't been, plan your next outing at the Turtle Club. I promise you it will be worth your while.

name: Gerard Ellis
text: 9-5-16, the BEST prime rib ever! Seasoned to perfection, salad bar was ok, bread was very good. Lobster tail was fair. Service was decent but place was packed. Reserve your seating early.

name: mike bruner
text: Always delicious, very well done prime rib that leaves you wanting more. You get a hold delicious salad bar and baked potato with your order. Only thing is dont drink the water. Seriously I grew up in Alaska and will never get over that super iron almost blood taste that lingers in the water. I had a lemonade it was delicious.

name: Manuel Colon
text:
First of all the staff were excellent from the moment we walked in. There were also some local folks that helped us out immensely. More about that later. The food was prepared perfectly to order and the wait staff was very professional. The salad bar was very very good with a great selection. We had the prime rib with baked potato. Perfectly prepared. I thoroughly enjoyed my dining experience at Turtle Club

Now to the local folks. We arrived about an hour and a half early. I decided to turn around and go for a ride to kill some time before our reservation. Well I got stuck and could not get out no matter what I tried. So we walked down to the restaurant figuring we would have to get a wrecker during or after our meal. Unbeknownst to us someone from the wait staff in the bar saw what happened and was ready to assist us before we even walked in. Then some of the sweetest folks just pulled me out and said that now I could enjoy my evening which we certainly did. It says alot about  the local area. I was very appreciative.

name: Michaela Higgison
text: Expensive but worth the price! Perfect for special occasions or just a tasty meal. Their prime rib is everything I wanted and more.

text: Heard great things about them so tried them for my anniversary. Not impressed. Salad bar was messy and seemed like old lettuce. Food was not cooked well and had little flavor. Wait staff was short of attention and seemed to be hurrying us out. It was during Christmas party time, so willing to try again, some day.

The toughest thing after dinner was picking a dessert. I highly recommend this place. You won't be dissatisfied.

A small area for those asked to wait for their table would have been nice. Something in between being directly seated and having the time to pull up to the bar.

But bottom line, the food was delicious and it is a great place to make a special night for someone.

They have packed so many tables and chairs in the dining area that people are bumping into each other. Way to crowded.
Not a place to go for a romantic dinner!!!
The food was ok but had to take it home to eat it, couldn't eat there for all the noise, could not talk across the table could not hear each other .
One more thing in a place that charges that kind of money, one would think they would serve a good glass of water but no they served some awful sulfer tasting water!!
With all the bottled water out there, they serve that foul tasting stuff.
No I will not return there and would not recommend it to anyone else.

name: Ryan Stafford
text:
If you're in the Spenard area this is the only Wendy's near you.

The food tastes great, but I have two suggestions that will make your visit even better.

1. Avoid the shift change time between 5-6 PM. If the night shift employees are not on time then you'll have a 5 minute wait until an employee takes your order and a 15 minute wait to get your food. During the shift change the manager is doing inventory, so this also slows things down.

2. Use the Drive Thru. The Drive Thru is the priority over dine-in guests.

I noticed one employee had his music playing through his earphones while making the food and packaging it.

In my opinion this was the slowest service of all Wendy's restaurants in Anchorage, but the food tasted great.

text: I went in as a large group with my family and I was really disappointed by the lack of vegan options. :/ I was able to significantly alter the taco salad though. I also was told that they couldn't substitute the lettuce (which is just water and has no nutrituon) for any other kind of greens like spinach or something. But I don't see why not, if they did have them on hand. But the waitress made it sound like it just couldn't physically be done?? And as I knew it would be so bland, I asked for some dressing as well and she didn't bring it until I was halfway through my meal. She also came off as rude and almost snapped at one of my family members. I understand that she's only human, as I am a server. But I felt that my family wasn't rude or demanding (and believe me, they can be, but they weren't in this case) so I don't feel she had any justification for being rude. name: Shannon O'Hara
text:
Whatever you do, don't order the prime rib and eggs at lunchtime! The meat was grey and bland. I waited for the server to ask how everything was but she saw me inspecting the meat and avoided our table. I was hungry so I ate the hash browns and eggs, which were delicious, but then I tasted the meat.

The "prime" rib was grey, bland and flavorless. I tried salt, the horseradish sauce, A1 (a sin on meat in my opinion). I finally stopped the waitress as she tried to pass the table yet again. I asked how the meat was prepared. She said "cooked fresh every morning". (I suspect it was microwaved, you know the flavor) Having been a server myself  I explained the grossness in the nicest and quietest way possible. I told her it tasted "off". She said 5 others had ordered it that day with no complaints.
I said maybe some au jus would help??
She got some and it didn't.
She did offer to replace it but if it was disgusting...why would I get another?

We received the check and I got a go box for the dog since there was no discount.

My suspicions were further realized when I got in the car and the dog wouldn't touch it.

Not much longer after that, in a busy store, I started getting tummy cramps and you can imagine the rest of the story.

My husband had the club sandwich. It was very light on meat, only had one meat and, per his words, was dry. He removed the middle bread and ate it.
The fries were excellent!

In closing, with tip, I paid over $40 for a sandwich, fries, hash browns and eggs......not to mention the embarrassment that came afterwards.

(I know, I shouldn't have ordered prime rib before 4 pm)

text:
My stay was okay, not bad but nothing special either. The room was big, had a refrigerator, microwave, flat screen TV, and the standard amenities.

They advertise online as being newly renovated; this is misleading. They may have slapped some paint up here and there, but I wouldn't call it renovated. The bathroom caulk is pealing and dirty, the tile grout is cracking and missing in places, and overall the place feels "well lived in". It's not a bad place to stay, but it was very disappointing to be expecting something that was updated to find it really needs to be renovated again.

I feel what I paid, $65 for the night (out the door), was a reasonable value for the room; I expected more because I got it 50% off regular price on special from Travelocity. I wouldn't pay anymore for this place than I did. For less than their normal prices you can get a motel in the same area with the same feel and amenities.

If you're expecting a renovated hotel, you'll be disappointed to find yourself at a typical motel. I'm not saying it's bad, just don't pay more than I did for a room.

Staff was either somewhat helpful or looked annoyed when asked basic questions at night. Many spent a lot of time sitting on their phones or engrossed with their computers.

name: Dawn Sievers
text:
This hotel received a 3 star only because the staff are 4 and 5 star ratings. The restaurant isn't much more than a grill and fry cook setup, everything is served in styrofoam or on paper plates. My French Dip was better than expected although the au jus was a bit thin and I loved the huge fries that accompanied it. I ordered the chicken wings to have for lunch the next day. When asked if I wanted plain, barbecued, or buffalo, I ordered the wings plain and asked for ranch dressing rather than blue cheese. When it was time to eat lunch the next day I was disappointed to find that the plain wings had been battered, pleased to find the batter was still crisp and tasty. Interestingly, the ranch dressing tasted dilly enough to be tzatziki sauce.

Everything was clean and tidy but it was quite obvious that it has been a long time since that Alex has been renovated or redecorated. The furniture in the lobby is too low to be comfortable and the only accessible power outlets I could see were at tables that we're technically part of the restaurant.

My room was a 2 queen bed room and was exceptionally large. I suspect that it would have appeared much smaller if it had contained the desk and easy chair that I am accustomed to finding in quality motels. It was necessary for me to move the night stand between the beds in order to plug in my phone and charge it. I was unable to find any other outlets available, other than those in the bathroom.

The drapes in my room were in need of repair and the control panel for the HVAC system was impossible for me to read in the room's night lighting.

On a more positive note, the beds were comfortable. I slept on one and Mikki, my service dog, slept on the other. The sheets smelled fresh and clean but the chenille bedspread were faded and outdated.

The bathroom was large, well lit, clean, and a bath bench was available. I loved the bath linens and would like to have some just like them. The thick, white, soft, cotton towels were fantastic.

All of the staff were kind, considerate, helpful, generous and understanding. I will stay there again just to be where there are people who are as nice as they and for their continental breakfast. The link sausages were cooked just as I like them, the scrambled eggs weren't runny or dried out and the coffee was strong.

resp.text: Dawn, We appreciate you taking the time for such a full and complete review of the services you received. Thank you for staying with us and we hope to be able to accommodate you in the future. name: Hayley Cobb
text:
Found a great rate on this place through a third-party hotel booking site. Considering the price, I wasn’t expecting much, but was surprised that the rooms were large, and "reasonably" clean. There was some rust/grime around the drain in the bathtub, a stain on the carpet, and a messed up wall. For the price, I'd say these are all minor, aside from the issue in the bath.

My biggest issue was that the Wi-Fi was not working on my floor during my stay (March 16-19). This was a pretty big deal for me. The front desk acknowledged the issue and suggested that I try connecting to another floor. Unfortunately, I just wasn’t able to get a good connection by doing this. I ended up burning through a ton of data on my mobile, and had to drive elsewhere to avoid missing an assignment deadline.

I was also pretty excited about the free continental breakfast, but they stop serving it at 9, so I wasn’t able to take advantage of it. 9 am seems early to stop serving breakfast, especially for people on vacation and coming from different time-zones.

Also, someone had very clearly smoked pot in the elevator, which I realize isn’t the hotel’s fault, but maybe something to consider if you’re traveling with children, or if you prefer to avoid staying in a place that attracts those kinds of guests.

All in all, I’d say if you’re looking for a cheap bed consider here if you don’t mind a rougher crowd, semi-clean rooms, and aren’t depending on reliable Wi-Fi. Personally, I won't be staying here again and wouldn't recommend it  to others.

text: Everything is always very neat and clean. Things are usually pretty easy to find and the produce looks amazing usually. There have been a couple of misses with the produce... I bought the already cut containers of melon chunks and half of them were soggy with an "off" taste while the other half was hard as could be with barely any flavor at all. Another time I bought the pre cut/washed container of stew veggies in produce near the salad bags and melon containers. Everything looked alright but when I got home and took the saran wrap off, my God there was this dreadful odor coming from the package. I don't know what was causing it but I can tell you that the texture of the orange bell peppers was a bit  slimy. Then we get to the onions, potatoes, etc. They all had a thin layer of goo from the peppers coating them from being wrapped together. Obviously I ended up putting the stew meat in the fridge for the next day and ordering pizza but the whole experience made me not buy ANY of the pre cut produce items. Someone needs to absolutely make damn sure that the food in the saran wrapped container has the right date on it. I don't see how 3 seperate items were off tho. Maybe they're trying to stretch days to sell more things... Just be careful in produce, everything else is great!

name: Richard Ferris
text:
Pretty nice hotel with decent rooms. The beds and pillows were okay.
The bathroom fan in our room was horrible! It was so loud that you couldn't run it except for an emergency circumstance.

Management of this hotel was another matter. We sprayed our room is Ozium when we left and got assaulted by a clerk accusing up from smoking in the room. We told him we didn't smoke in the room but I'd use Ozium. They didn't care they said they had to put a ozone unit in the room and charge us $250. The room had for Windows that all opened and had screens. If they wanted to remove the smell of the Ozium all they had to do is open the windows for 15 minutes and the road would be probably purged of any and all odors. Management in patiently explained they had procedures and that opening the windows is not what they did. What they did was put an ozone machine in the room and charge the client $250

We talked to the manager and told him if the room didn't are out and he was going to charge us to call us so we can come by and check out the room ourselves. He said he would call us if he was going to charge us but never did and then the next day you put a charge on our bill and would not discuss it. He did not call us allow us the opportunity to inspect the room as promised!

We read the terms of the contract and we had violated none of them as there was no smoking smoking apparatus signs of smoking or smoking paraphernalia in the room according to the manager and yet he still charge this rather than just opening the windows to remove the air freshener weed put in the room.

Management attitude seemed to be if they enjoyed gouging their customers rather than providing them with as good a service as possible.

This management needs to go to customer service school cuz they think the object is to destroy their relationship with customers rather than to try to make things agreeable and to even honor their promises to call us before building our room.

3 star rating was based on the quality of the premise I would have given this a 0 or 1 star rating based on the quality and professionalism of management

resp.text: Thank you for providing a review of the property, however as addressed in the email to you the smoking in the room is not permissible we are 100% Smoke Free.  You admitted to smoking/vaping in the room.  You were provided the property policy at check in.  Which you read and signed.

name: Roy Conley
text:
Historically I find I get the best price quality ratio at Safeway. They have an extended selection of each item which I appreciate. Not one or two but sometimes as many as five or six different brands of the same product. I like quality and I will pay the difference when there is a difference. I have been using their Safeway app and do find it difficult for me to use. I am not a pre planner so I end up bouncing from one end of the store to the other I'm looking for the discounted prices all items I usually buy. I am told I could just pre flag them and then go about my routine of going up and down each aisle. That might work might not. I was so pleased to find large catfish fillets Frozen at 699 a pound directly from Baton Rouge Louisiana area. In the past these has been as much as 1899 a pound. That is difficult for a boy raised in the swamps of Louisiana to pay. Just goes against my grain. I am 70 and my dad raised us selling catfish for 50 cents a pound. The Times They are changing

I went to Safeway again yesterday and was quite surprised to see a change of their marketing strategy. They are offering many items much lower than they normally do especially their fresh meats. I love to buy at Walmart there 10 lb bag of chicken leg quarters to make soup with. They are usually eight or nine dollars for a 10 lb bag. Lo and behold Safeway had them in their frozen section for $4.99. That's amazing for being in Fairbanks and it was not a one day special. They also advised me they are going to have untrimmed tri-tip on sale this week for $4.99 a pound. Again that is spectacular for Fairbanks. Stock up your freezers

text: Had a blast, many animals and learned a lot.  Look forward to visiting again.

text: What a very fun experience! It was awesome how much they let you do! It was totally worth the price. My three year old had an absolute blast. It’s so cool to see such awesome animals up close and to interact with them. The tour guide was so friendly and knowledgeable and funny! Definitely worth it!!

name: Crystal Collett
text: Super fun, they paced it perfectly for even the littlest walkers. Learned a lot about the history of the farm, the area it was settled in, and the animals were all super sweet. Couple of them started getting a bit cranky, and they were quickly put into another pen so visitors would be safe.

name: Rachel Jordan
text: We had a great time at the A-MAZING tour yesterday!  Everything was perfectly timed, lots of fun interaction with the animals, slides, a maze, buggy ride for the young ones, hay bale jumping and a tractor ride.  We all had a lot of fun

name: Rebecca Wilson
text: Did the Christmas/Santa experience. Amazingly orchestrated! Got to feed reindeer and kiss a moose 🥰

name: Nephrym
text: Super neat place. Great for kids. My 5 year old loved it. Friendly and knowledgeable staff. They are taking lots of precautions due to Covid and I felt totally safe here! Highly recommend!!

name: Allison Capps
text: Their A-MAZE-ing was truly amazing! Took two kids, ages 12 and 9, they had an amazing time, and so did us adults. The whole Taff was wonderful. The activities like the maze and reindeer train were a blast! All of the animals were very well taken care of and very friendly. I HIGHLY recommend going. We will be back

name: Lauren
text: What a wonderful experience and location we had a fantastic time can't wait for the summer activities

name: Ryan R
text: The 2 hour tour was perfect for our family. The activities were well timed and spaced to keep my children's attention (I felt the price was cheap for all the activities included, even a snack was included). Our group consisted of children from 1-12 years old, and they all seemed entertained the entire time. The lessons we learned about each animal group was nice. There was just so much to do, but we never felt rushed. We will be going back!

name: LeeAnna Bohnert
text: My family and I always enjoy coming here! Such great people taking great care of all of their animals. You can tell they love them all and are so knowledgeable. Love kissing Rocky💋😄 We bring everyone who comes to visit here! Always a hit!

text: Great family fun. Especially for the little kids. Quite informative presentation given at the beginning of the tour.

name: Ryan Stafford
text:
A great place to bring visitors and family.  Take a tour and see the horses, elk, reindeer, and other animals here.  There are horse rides and pony rides for the children.

During holidays there are events here too, so checkout their Facebook page for updates.

name: Dorothy Rogers
text:
We called the morning that we wanted to visit, which was really late notice!!! The owner worked with us. We made the trip to the farm and enjoyed the experience. We fed the reindeer and the reindeer, Carl, loved on us!!! So enchanting!!!!
We also met and fed Rocky, the moose. Wow was he a big boy, but sweet!!!
Loved the experience!!!!

name: Kimberlee Kenyon
text: This is a fun place to stop on your travels in the Palmer/Anchorage area. My husband and I came upon this reindeer farm by accident and decided to stop and check it out.  It is a short tour, but long enough to stretch your legs.  I would highly recommend for young children.

resp.text: And such beautiful surroundings to stretch your legs! I love your adventurous spirit. So glad you found us, even if by accident!

name: Loren Breshears
text: We took the guided tour and it was amazing! The guide was engaging, informative, and funny too

name: Blair KC
text: This place exceeded all expectations. We could not of had a better experience. Amazing animals, amazing staff, amazing views.

name: Brad Wuerer
text: They are so nice and welcoming.   The grandkids really  enjoyed Santa, the reindeer and other animals they have at the farm.

name: Macy Farmer
text: Awesome place to bring the kids. They loved it!! The tour was fun, interesting and very informative. Definitely recommend and a great spot for tourists to hit.

name: Alex Kreilich
text: Really fun place, highly recommend even if you don't have kids.

name: Josh M
text: Overall a great experience. Wish they would have enforced a mask policy.

name: K S
text: Went to the Reindeer Farm today and our Tour Guide was a 13 year old, I think his name was Camden. He was very polite and knowledgeable about all the animals on the farm. It was a great experience, we even got to pet the baby moose they're taking care of and bottle feed him! We will be coming back and I can't wait!

name: Aaron Mason
text: Went to the haunted house and it was pretty good.  Not very long but entertaining.  Purchase tickets online, the wait if you don't is long.

name: haylee hays
text: Had an amazing time out at the farm. We are from Alaska and I did this as a kid. Extremely excited as an adult as well to go and pet some animals. Our tour guide was really friendly and for the life of me I can't remember his name. But everyone was nice . From the girl at the gift shop to the woman who made our milkshake to the guy who saw us wanting to pet the big white dogs. We thought he was upset but nope we pet everything that they would let us! Fun little hour tour on a beautiful day. Suggestion go in the morning first or second slot of day . Reindeer are more hungry. They might run up on you don't be afraid.

name: Sagar Bansal
text:
The tour was an amazing experience, and the farm is beautiful.

The tour guide was humorous and informative. We started with feeding the reindeer, then saw the bison and baby yak. There was also a baby moose, and the tour ended with looking at and feeding elk.

The tour lasted around 45 minutes, and we learned a lot of basic information about these animals.

resp.text: Wonderful! I'm so glad you had a good time. We appreciate you leaving a review. I just love to hear feedback from people. They are very unique arctic animals. We love to show them and talk about them!

name: Annie Feliciano Rivera
text: What an awesome experience, in all my 11 yrs in Alaska first time in the reindeer farm had a blast with the kids and they have the best haunted house !!

name: Leah Hercules-Jandres
text: Our plans got derailed due to Covid and we had to make some adjustments and stumbled on this gem! We brought our visiting family including our 5 year old nephew and 17 year old niece. They both loved it! The staff is friendly and funny and it's a bonus to support a family run business. The prices are reasonable and I'm excited to bring visitors in the future.

name: Auddy Groom
text: Cutest farm I've ever been to. The animals had a lot of love and trust for the employees. When I have kids I'm bringing them here. Great family experience.

resp.text: Thank you! So glad you had fun! We look forward to seeing you with your kids, and maybe even again before that happens!

text: Really good guides, family farm experience. Loved our visit!

name: Jeremiah Allen
text:
Basically they have all the reindeer! We really enjoyed the experience with the Reindeer, Bison, and especially the Moose! The guide Camden was wonderful and if his future plans to attend school to be a chiropractor fall through, I think he should go into comedy. He really knows how to handle a rowdy crowd with ease.
Definitely a great place to visit.
Cheers,
Lucky the Clown

name: Benjamin Bell
text: Awesome pre Christmas experience for kids and adults alike. This family run farm brings the fun back into Christmas. Please keep doing this, you do an awesome job.

name: Jessica W
text: We’ve been here so many times since moving to Alaska and they are always friendly! We love the reindeer and getting to kiss Rocky!

name: Chris Moore
text: Fun place to visit, great piece of history. Got to walk with reindeer and pet the moose Rocky.

name: Linda Wall
text: Learn about the domesticated cousins of caribou, even feed and pet them, and interact safely with a moose, bison, yak and elk on the walking tour of the farm. Other attractions include horseback trail riding and a small animal 'petting zoo' for the kids. Very fun family experience!

name: Todd Grivetti
text: A true working reindeer farm. Great for families with and without kids. Interactive farm where you can feed Reindeer and even kiss a moose.  Well worth the trip if you’re in town or traveling through to Denali or Fairbanks.

name: Aditi Partani
text: Must go place if you have kids. Our guide was good and had fun feeding all the reindeer. Me and My kids went all crazy with the furry reindeer. My kids went crazy for the little cat Leo that was wandering in the farm. They give a good sight of how they manage this big group of animals and how they interact with them. Moose , Bison , yak was fun too.. it’s a good place to visit if you are in Anchorage.

name: Gary Poppe
text: Fun place to visit.  Many different animals there and visitors are encouraged to go into the reindeer pen and hand-feed them pellets.  It can be a short 'filler' activity if looking for something quick ... we spent just over an hour there.

name: Amanda Franklin
text: Very nice and helpful staff with cute sense of humor and very good experience for our family ❣️

name: shannon brumlow
text: Helpful, respectful staff. Laid back, Alaskan atmosphere. Great for small children, very family friendly.

name: Terrenna Giles Brown
text: Very friendly staff. Liked being able to interact with the reindeer. Babies and adults were easy to pet or feed. Our guide was very knowledgeable. We saw a bison, a yak, a elk, and I got to feed and pet a 1 year old moose. Really family friendly. Would recommend this day 1. Laid back great way to start your vacation.

name: Oscar Oneill
text: Is good...

name: Abi Dove
text: The tours are really short, kinda gimmicky, but designed for tourists. Driving by is just as entertaining as paying for the "tour" (and saves you a few minutes).

name: Michael
text: We live in the Butte and we visit the Reindeer Farm a few times a year. We feel really lucky to have it in the area and to have the Hardy family as neighbors. My kids love it and can't get enough. Great for new visitors to Alaska and a fun place to take visiting family, especially those with kids. There isn't another experience quite like it in Alaska. If you haven't gone, be sure to check it out.

name: Preston Edson
text: If you ever wanted to feed a reindeer with sprigs of leaves from your mouth this is the place! Worth a visit but they don’t sell reindeer steaks!

name: Ryan

name: Marcus Biastock
text: Informative and friendly staff.  We took the tour of the farm.  Presentation was very interesting.  Had the opportunity to feed and interact with several different types of animals.  Great for kids!  Beautiful setting with awe inspiring mountain backdrops.  Museum and gift shop on premises.

name: Shawn Tu
text: Great place to take the family, engaging and friendly staff and you get to see reindeer and moose up close!

name: peace_love&muzic
text: My family and I absolutely loved it here. What a great and fun experience for us all. I might have loved it more than the kids. :) Coming from Michigan... :)

name: Nicki Gore
text: First time we have ever been to the Reindeer Farm was yesterday (10/14/2017)for their Fall Festival.  It was very well planned and handled. Will do again in future years. They have well cared for animals that the kids can interact with, great games, very well thought out. Thank you for such a great experience!

name: Dawn Brooks
text: No fake front! They are sensitive to the emotional well-being of their animals and are given opportunities to pet and feed what would be undomesticated reindeer, elk, and even baby moose. Casual run at the pace of the guest for their enjoyment. Wonderful pony rides at a low cost.

name: Jim Hall
text: It brings out the little kid in you.

name: S B
text: Such an awesome place! Take the tour, experience the animals. Great for kids. Will definitely be back!

text: Super fun family activity farm!

name: Scott Carter
text:
We had a great time at the Fall Festival, and it was a pretty fun experience. They did their best to provide just about every attraction/booth you could hope for, including live music.

Kind of pricey once we got through the gates, but would be great every now and then for different events.

text: This place was so fun for all ages

text: The best fall festival I have ever gone to! The rest can't even compare or compete at all!

name: Amanda Stewlow
text: We had my son's 4th birthday party here, and it was an excellent experience for all the attendees! The kids got to pet bunnies, a pig, hold chickens, feed reindeer directly in the pen surrounded by a herd, see a bison and a baby moose, and pet an elk. They also got a ride on the "train" and my son received a gift from the staff. There was an area with tables for our use to open presents and eat cake. Also, our guide was very knowledgeable!

name: Tammy Kosusnik
text: Very dissatisfied with the fall festival today!!! I had a toddler breakfast myself did not offer to put stroller on wagon so we could go back to the field where everything was!!!Wagon ride was good,  but back there with no stroller with baby who did not want to walk!!! How are you suppose to enjoy if you can't get stroller back ther!! Then went to get in reindeer ride so my granddaughter could ride said I could not ride said I could let her. Are you out if your mind she is only 16 months!!!! Maze was not baby friendly at all spent 30 minutes lost in maze with toddler who did not want to and got very heavy, sure wished I had my stroller!!! Every thing was in field and only way back there wagon,  suggestion, if you can walk to pumpkin patch, surely make a path so that people with strollers can get back there, or let people put strollers on wagon!!! I really don't know if I will be back!!!!!!

resp.text:
Hi Tammy, Thank you for leaving this constructive feedback. As the owner, and the people that create this event, it is certainly not what we hoped you would experience here! I can see that we have some areas to improve. Running events we have helpers that are either volunteers or we only see once a year to help us with our Fall festival, so I have no doubt, there could have been some better training.
I would like to address some of the situations you pointed out in your review.
1. Stroller on the wagon. I don't know why they wouldn't help you get the stroller on the wagon, especially if there was room. On occasion, if the day is busy and hectic, obviously we just don't have room for strollers, but from what I understand you were right there in the beginning of the day, and there should have been room. Did you happen to ask for help? Or were you told no? Also, there IS a walking path down field. Many people used it yesterday. We actually widened the path this year. I believe we could have more signage to help direct people, and the wagon loader, could have pointed it out if he realized you needed to keep your stroller.
2. It is not safe for people greater than 100 lbs to ride the reindeer train. Due to the strength of the frame. We are planning to rebuild it this year before Christmas to allow for more weight in each of the cars. Even if you are under 100 lbs, because some of the staff has not used good judgement in the past, we have made a rule that no adults are allowed in the barrel train. However, I wish they would have thought to offer your toddler could sit with an older child that was riding on the train.
3. the Maze is tricky, we need to challenge people, or they complain. However, my 16 month old grandaughter has been through it with us many times. She was willing to walk, I can only imagine how hard it would be to carry her through it, and we made it stroller friendly, with parents in mind. (Yes, I know you didn' t have your stroller)

We have an information trailer set up right at the entrance/Exit of the farm. Hoping to help direct and answer questions. I am confident it could have been a much better experience with a bit of direction. One of my grand daughters FAVORITE things is the wheat box in the big barn. It is under cover from the rain. Its like a giant sandbox they can play in. Also in the barn are bunnies and family photos.
I truly appreciate the time you took to leave this review. I also truly appreciate the details you put in it, giving us some things to work on, and talking points for training for next week. I would love it if you could give it another chance, and put us to the test to see if my staff learned from this experience. Please email me at reindeertours@gmail.com to discuss further. Denise Hardy

resp.text:
So Sorry you feel that way. We live here year round. We have these animals as our pets and our business. By opening our farm for tours it helps us to feed them year round. I guess when I think of a tourist trap, I think of a pop up business specifically placed in a location to lure in tourists.
While we welcome tourists, we also welcome locals, schools, churchs, and many other groups of people. This farm has been in our family since the 1950's. It has been many things over the years, and has been a Reindeer Farm since 1987 when my dad decided he would like to try farming reindeer. We have tried many things with our reindeer over the years, and one of the things we do with them, is open our home to allow visitors to enjoy them as much as we do.

name: Kathy Hayes
text: Claire gave us our personalized tour of the Fortress of the Bear.  She was very knowledgeable and answered our many questions.  She shared with us the story of this center and the resident bears.  We witnessed the bears use sign language to communicate (they learn this so the care givers can provide health checks while the bears remain in their enclosures).  The new building was first class and the enclosures the bears reside in appeared to have been created to provide the best experience for the bears, their care and for the visitors.  There is nothing else I've ever seen like this - it's no zoo.  It's an immersion into these bears lives!!!!  Thanks to the team for doing this amazing work!!!

While closely-cropped images on the facility's website showcase the animals, in person, we couldn't not see the dreary environment, with trash floating in the water and busted tired strewn across the landscape. text:
Preface: this is only my second time visiting Sitka, so this is not from an in-town local experience, but a southeast local review nonetheless.

Excellent establishment. Food & drink: the exceptional thin crust pizza is complimented by a diverse cocktail menu - using seemingly fresh & handpicked ingredients, fruits, & spices. My bartender had a wealth of knowledge to help pick a drink that fit my preferred tastes and seemed to guide me through the range that it fell under. For those who don't do carbs & meat; the salad that I had had as much attention with ingredients and flavor as the pizza & drinks.

Conclusions: Mean Queen is a must if you're looking for a local dive that can provide great food, drinks, atmosphere, and people. I'm over the moon being here

name: Joseph Dutko
text: Located in the Tongass National Forest is the Saxman Totem Park which has many different totems from around Alaska.  There is a repair shop that overhauls these totems as they weather from years of exposure.  It is fascinating watching the craftsmen labor to restore these totems to their previous glory.   As you wander the park grounds you get to see and enjoy the different sizes, styles, shapes and intricate carvings of the native Alaskans.  You finally begin to appreciate the hard work that was put into the making of these pieces of art, visualizing them using nothing but muscle power,  patience and primitive tools to make these incredible totems.  We attached a few photo's for you to enjoy and perhaps spark your interest to see them in person.  Enjoy.

name: Ryan Stafford
text:
If you're looking to launch your boat or watch some wildlife then the Seward Boat Harbor is a great place to visit.

The Seward Boat Harbor is a great place to launch a boat or even a kayak.  The boat launch is located near the Kenai Fjords National Park Visitor Center on 4th Street and the kayak launch is located at the Northeast corner of the Seward Boat Harbor.  Parking is a pain, so you will need some coins or a credit card to pay for time.

The Seward Boat Harbor is home to wildlife including sea otters.  If the sun is bright you can see fry swimming in gigantic numbers below the catwalks.  Occasionally a bald eagle will sit on a tall light pole looking for fish too.

The Seward Boat Harbor is a great resource, but the sad reality is the expansion many years ago removed a significant amount of beach.  The beach was a great place to snag King Salmon.  While the fishing near the Seward Boat Harbor isn't the same the expansion did modernize and expand the Seward Boat Harbor capacity.

name: Dan Wilding
text: Chena Hot Springs is Well with the drive. We spent the day and had a great time. The hot springs was fabulous, it was 20 below zero and entering the spring was comfortable sure to the speed walls and covered tunnel. The ice museum was fun, lots to see. The restaurant was excellent.... Wirth the drive itself.

name: Alyssa Norris
text: I enjoy going to Chena Hot Springs for a full weekend, or just an evening. Much better to go in the winter when it’s cold. The rock pool is my favorite and is a great place to relax. The food is good, and if I’m spending the night I try to stay in one of the geothermal cabins for a more rustic and quiet experience. I recommend doing the ice museum tour if you have the time, and be sure to try an iced appletini.

name: Elizabeth J

The drive up the Chena is beautiful, we spotted a beaver and moose along the way. The hot springs themselves were really nice and relaxing.

I would recommend being hydrated because they drain a lot out of you.

(Bring some water shoes if you have tender feet) the rooms were clean with the basic needs. The staff is very knowledgeable and extremely friendly and helpful. Will be returning.

name: Susan Bretz
text: What an absolutely beautiful place! I've always thought people were crazy to go into the hot springs when it's subzero. Now I understand. The ice coating the rocks and trees makes everything look absolutely magical. Admittedly, it's cold getting into the water... But once you're in it really doesn't feel cold anymore... When we finally pried ourselves out... It actually felt good being in the cold for a bit. My only recommendation is to bring your own towel... The one they rent you is small and not very absorbent. It was definitely worth the trip out. I'll be back.

About 30-45 minutes into camping out, Aurora lit up the sky!  That experience made my ENTIRE trip!

text: A place that's a pretty long drive from Fairbanks.  In the winter the road can be dangerous, so be careful.  The main attraction is the "hot spring". Though there is a spring on the premises,  the water is actually pumped into the rock pool from the spring.regardless, its not a bad way to spend the day.  The pool and indoor hot tubes are pretty lame, so just use the outside pool. There are lockers available for $.50 each use, and they're pretty small so dont bring any unnecessary items.  Plan to spend at least half a day here.  The food at the restaurant is like everything else in Alaska, pretty expensive.  So eat there at your own risk to your wallet.  Never stayed there, so I can't comment on the rooms, but the prices are up there.  There have other activities as well, just be ready to pay out for them.  All in all, not a bad way to spend a half to full day.

name: Brent Freiburger
text: Chena hot springs is a complete mixed bag that i could probably write a very long article on. But to keep it short the hot spring itself is great. Very relaxing with just the right amount of sulfer and heat to do a body good. The restaurant and bar are all top notch. Now for the meh. The ice hotel is ok but never changes and could easily be better. Everything about the hotel just seems cheap, with loud rooms, no refrigerator or microwave and you have to pay for substandard wifi. The parking is terrible. On the weekends its very hard to find a spot and parking is sporadic and confusing. Parking areas are also unmaintained for the most part being very icy and packed down snow everywhere. I see someone slip and fall in the parking lot almost every time i go. Overall take the good with the bad and have a good time. I like the small improvements but they have much more to go

name: Teva Wiese
text:
Beautiful location and great activities, but the lodging leaves much to be desired.

The hosts at the check-in counter were rude and disorganized, and the room itself was unacceptable. We stayed in one of the Fox rooms, and found that the room smelled like urine, and the windows were frozen shut so we couldn't even bring in some fresh air. There were stains in the shower and on the bed, hair on toilet seat, and the lights went out about a minute after we walked in. Other than that, the fit and finish of the room is comparable to a Motel 6.

After that unpleasant surprise, the resort did much to redeem itself. The hot springs themselves are comfortable, and although not luxurious, are a nice place to relax, especially first thing in the morning when there are fewer people.  We also took advantage of the late night Aurora tour, which had some great views of the stars. They drove us up to a hilltop in a caravan of Hagglund BV206 Arctic exploration vehicles, where we found a couple of yurts, hot chocolate, and the northern lights waiting for us. If you've never seen the stars away from the city lights or the aurora borealis, you owe this trip to yourself. My only recommendation is to take the 9:30 trip instead of the 10:30, as we all started getting pretty cold and sleepy after 2AM or so.

We also took a look at the low temperature geothermal power plant. I'm glad they are making the effort to educate the public on renewables and to implement this technology themselves. They also have hydroponic greenhouses, which we unfortunately didn't get to tour because we left before the 2PM tour start time, but it's great to see Alaska embracing food independence and sustainability. A morning tour would be a great addition to the program.

With some key improvements to the quality of the facilities, I would be happy to recommend Chena hot springs.

Relive history and study the various tools and machines used by miners of the past, or simply take a relaxing walk on one of the surrounding nature trails. Chena is a wonderful place to relax and unwind!
