name: Ania M.
text:
Very remote spot but close enough to the city.
If you want to relax for a weekend or come foe a day of spa.

name: John Burgoyne
text: It was well maintained and organized! Was there for Thanksgiving and enjoyed the delicious buffet! Polite and friendly service! Loved the hot springs!!

name: Nabil Al Nahin Chowdhury
text: Had a great time. Totally different experience in summer and winter. Only disappointment was it wasn't cold enough for my hair to freeze 😂

name: Erica Stoner
text: Really nice place with great service. My review is for the restaurant located at the resort. The gentleman who took our order and served us was very friendly and welcoming. They definitely know how to cook a filet mignon, it was perfect in my opinion. I also loved their tomato soup. Would visit again, thank you.

name: Glenn Marlin
text:
Fairly disappointing. The facility is nice and a beautiful setting, but the service was horrible. I brought 4 adults to a suite set up for 6.  The room had 2 towels. I tried 3 times to get more, but was ignored every time. Finally bought some from town so we could enjoy our dirty room.

I recommend that management do some spot checking. I get it that the buildings are a little older and require maintenance, but it doesn’t  cost you any more to clean it and sweep it.  Try empowering your staff to make a great experience for your guests.

name: Dee Hend
text: all i can say WOW..just wow the view so much to offer with hotel on site..restuarant great food...staff not up to par .priced a little high...but they DO grat... so double check your receipt... omg the clam chowder though...

name: Gracie Ramirez
text: Nice relaxing spot. Good price. Customer service could be improved.

name: Jessi Scott
text:
This place is a tourist trap.  The pictures make it look like a 5 star resort when it’s more similar to a motel 6.  The room was alright, basic.  Two sunken in queen beds.  The room was HOT when we got there with no AC. Had to open a window to cool it down and the window had no screen so...hello mosquitos. The worst part was the water that came out of the bathroom sink. It was brown. And I mean dark brown, couldn’t see through it at all, and had so many particles in it it seriously grossed me out.  It took a minute of letting the water run before it turned into somewhat normal water.  I can get around the sulfur smell because it’s to be expected at a naturally occurring hot spring, but wow.  Ate at the restaurant which was mediocre at best. Dry, what tasted like frozen fish and chips.  I will give our waiter kudos because he was bar tending, seating and serving multiple sections and doing a great job.  Tried to buy some stickers at the gift shop but no one would check us out so just put them back and left.  The only cool thing about this place is the hot spring lake itself, but it’s not as nice as the pictures make it look either.  Not worth the money, or the hour+ drive from Fairbanks.

Edit:
Forgot to mention the WiFi. It awful.  Works for 2 minutes, then quits.  Nothing ever loads.

name: Aleks Krysa
text: Stopped to visit and look around. Nice gift shop and restaurant. They are adding on a new wing & entrance, so there is some construction. The rental cabins and campgrounds are dry, with no water or sewer, but they have electricity. Rooms in the lodge appear clean. Very nice...well kept.

name: Emily Accipiter Stewart
text: A very nice place to relax with family. The staff is wearing masks, but sadly they are not enforcing or asking guests to wear them.

name: James Stafford
text: Amazing trip, rooms were small and expensive, food wasn’t very good. The wings were dry and the pasta wasn’t good, the sauce was like water, could of gotten better pasta from Olive Garden for a fraction of the price...

name: Robert Duke
text: What's not to like about a mineral hot spring.  It was very relaxing and clean. The hot spring water is wonderful to feel.  This is a great stop in the Fairbanks area.

name: Becky Noyes
text: We visited the resort to tour the ice museum, but as we arrived rather early for the next tour, we decided to explore the grounds.  The resort has many hiking trails, we took a shorter one that takes you out and around a beautiful little pond with crystal clear waters, as well as a dog kennel that does tours and cart or sled rides depending on the season.  They also have plenty of places which to camp out and a very nice restaurant that we felt was very reasonably priced.  Plus they grow all their own vegetables right on the property, so you can't get much fresher than that!  Of course they also have the ice museum, which was super cool (pun intended) and, of course, the hot springs, which we kinda ran out of time and didn't get to experience.  Someday, I hope we'll get a chance to return to this beautiful location with lots of fun and relaxing experiences!

name: Stanley H.
text: We spent 3 wonderful days at this resort, the hot springs were crystal clear and toasty warm to hot depending where you soaked at. Just a heads up don’t forget to drink as much water as you can, the hot water dehydrates you very quickly! Bring your water bottle, you can refill it in the building where you checked in. There is a lot to do if you want or just relax and unwind. To cool off visit the Ice museum on the property a cool 26f. And very beautiful and unique. This resort is off the grid only Verizon and ATT cell coverage works here what I have been told. We were very blessed to meet the owner Berni sp? And his family. Unfortunately he lost his wife in January and they were having a celebration of life for his wife. What a wonderful man he is and his family.  Sending prayers to his family.  The resort is a work in progress, and progress takes work what he said.  The new hotel covered entry way and drive way was getting paved when we were there in mid Aug . The hotel rooms are nice like camp rooms, don’t expect 5 stars here maybe 3. The restaurant has amazing tasting food, 40 % of the food is grown in the green house and garden.  Ooh, bring shoes that you don’t mind getting a little dirty, paved and in paved areas if you walk around a bit. And hiking shoes if you want to do some hiking.  Lastly friendly staff .

name: Anthony Ludwig
text: Beautiful place and friendly staff. The rock lake is super relaxing. Accommodations are a little pricey but comfortable and the food is great.

name: Tom Witteman
text: Awesome experience.  Swimming in the hot springs when it's 20 below zero was just amazing.  Thank you CNLAstro for showing us the wonders of an amazing location.

name: Another DeJa Vu
text: I really enjoyed my time in the hot springs. The mens locker room is very small and awkwardly limited space.    Bring a towel. They are $5 to rent. Also bring flip flops or something to protect your feet while walking in the locker room and pool areas

name: Jeff Stetz
text: Be sure to look into the geothermal greenhouse and power plant.  It's fantastic to see a place like this working to reduce their reliance on outside energy sources.

name: Clairese Yuhasz Austin
text: Smashing place to rejuvenate after a few days of driving a motorhome from Anchorage! Worth the trip.

name: Shailesh Soliwal
text: Great place to watch northern lights and enjoy hot springs. Food was delicious!

name: Faith Summerlin
text: What a peaceful calming experience! Three days of pure pleasure!

name: Jose Carrasco
text: Good place to see the northern lights, and have different things to do while you wait for the spectacle. You can see the museum and drink a cocktail in the ice bar, amazing ice sculptures. Later  you can have a dinner in the restaurant (great food) and the you can relax in the hot water while you enjoy a clear sky to see the stars. And around 11 go and enjoy the northern lights.

name: Amanda k
text: Nice wooded campground.  No hook ups.  Campsite was beautiful. Right by a stream and very quiet.  Hot springs are very natural and do smell strongly of sulfur. Ice hotel was beautiful. The northern lights tour was fun but be prepared for a rough ride up the mountain. We had great views of the lights. The yurt was heated and had hot drinks and cup of noodle included.  The bathrooms are out houses next to the yurt.

name: Debbie Stewart
text: Go to this place every time i go to fairbanks area. Love the natural lake hot springs and drive up. Saw 7 moose this time.

name: Y G
text: We visited last summer and we just brought my friend last month! It is definitely nicer in winter because the hot spring is pretty hot. It was nice to see the ducks taking bath too. Very cute. Ice museum was fun too!

name: dan geno
text: An amazing experience..staff is so nice water is perfect 104 degrees Fahrenheit. Great food wonderful atmosphere

name: Lauren
text: Great day trip destination from fairbanks! There are a lot of pretty hikes surrounding the area. There is very little/no reception around, sadly, unless you have verizon. Even then, the reception is very spotty and only 1x. I couldn't purchase the wifi at the resort (it wouldn't load) but my friends who did said it was bad since it comes from a satellite. The restaurant was also pretty good. I tried the alaskan salmon and duck tenders. Both were pretty good, but the salmon was amazing!! Definitely recommend!

name: BreeAnna Erickson
text: Springs, hot tubs and pool are all dirty. Smells like wet dog. Service at Restaurant was TERRIBLE. Food wasn't awful, but wasn't amazing. Let's just say the Dry Calamari and Flavorless Halibut were the highlight of the trip.

name: Rudi Pennington
text: This was the first time I had ever been to a hot spring. I thought it was a crazy idea to go into a body of water when it was below zero and snowy, but this was a magnificent experience. I've visited 3 times and loved it every single time. While driving back to Fairbanks late at night, I witnessed the most beautiful lights in the sky. I hold this memory dearly in my heart.

name: Ronald Smith
text: Fun get away...

name: Swathi Swathi
text: Nice place... hot springs are really amazing. indoor pool is there for kids as they are not allowed in the hot springs. 2 Jacuzzis are also there. we had a good time. Seen the ice museum. the sculptures are really great.

name: KK HH
text: Must visit place. You can escape the ice museum if you already visited the ice museum in Fairbanks downtown. Try the hot spring in the morning cause there will be very few people. The restaurant is very good and the price is very fair

name: Adena Gwirtz
text: Visited the Ice Hotel as seen on the travel Chanel. What an experience! Literally everything is made from ice. Yes, don't worry you are given a warm parka to wear. Spent an hour going through the hotel rooms and watching ice being sculpted into various furniture. Don't be shy grab that special ice drink on your way out!

name: Dennis Rollins
text: Very much improved over the past several years. Wonderful place to spend a day or more.

name: Dawna Myers
text: We had a great time and the staff was so kind in offering suggestions. . Definitely will be back. .

name: Galaxy Gamers
text:
Nice place. lots to do. There are dog sleds and snowmobile activity’s that are very fun.
But if you have teens or kids they can’t go into the hot springs which is a little disappointing since that’s kind of the selling point so just be informed.

name: Paul Cohen
text: Had a wonderful time with my man. It was one of the most unique experiences of my life.

name: Bacon & Cheese Productions
text: Great day trip out of Fairbanks.  Good for families with Kids, hikers and hot springs enthusiasts.

name: Abhijit Naik
text: Need more activities...good place, good foods..hot springs are good. Cant spend more than a day though.Geothermal plant and greenhouse is excellent as well.

name: Iddet Milian-Prada
text: Far drive with the tour guide. Def worry going and getting in the really hot spring water.  Must go in the winter for me though just because of the experience with the cold temp of the snow and the hot water.  Locker rooms with showers and hair dryers inside.  Gotta pay 50 cents for a locker.  They rent towels for 5$. So just bring your own like I did from my hotel.  There’s a gift shop. There’s a pretty good restaurant.  Bit of a wait time but really good food.  Also a bit pricey.  The ice museum is there too. Only got one girl working there so once you’re in there pretty much stuck in there for 40 minutes until she’s done serving the drinks.  They should add more staff.  But over all it’s a good area.  The spring is really big and at night it’s dark with colorful lights around. Def a must do if your in Fairbanks because it’s one of those things you just can’t not do if you’re here.

name: Amanda Nutter
text: Our room was dirty, the hot tubs were dirty. The service was ok, long wait times for someone to take our food orders. Cable was out and the internet would not work. The Activities were amazing though.

name: donna hill
text: People were extremely kind and place was super clean.

name: Rick Benken
text: Outstanding food and chance to see Northern Lights! Hot springs are great!

name: B. Tamm
text: Definitely a place to visit when in fairbanks.

name: JL Skeptic
text: The hotsprings rock lake alone is worth the drive! Get your suit on, ignore the indoor pool and head out the back door! The restaurant has good food. There are tons of outdoor activities in summer and a few in winter. There's cabins to rent, camping sites and RV lots too. I have yet to go in the ice building.

name: Keanu Henry
text: It's a fun place to be. I played beach ball in the pool, soaked in the rock pool, and ate some good food. The employees are also pretty nice

name: Daniel Lowe
text: We did not stay here because of the higher cost of rooms compared to Fairbanks hotels, but we did visit. The ride out here in the winter was easy and beautiful (moose spotting along the way).  We liked the set up of the 'resort' and the hot springs were great as well. There were plenty of activities to sign up for even if you were not staying at the hotel also.

name: Cara H.
text: There's nothing like being in a hot spring at -20s or -30s (F).  The rating is for the experience.  The facility, however, is poorly maintained.  I suggest bringing your own swim shoes.  There are flip flops for sale at the desk but the swim shoes will protect your feet in the spring better.  Bring towels too so you won't need to rent them.  I would keep them in the locker until needed after shower.  If you keep them hanging by the spring entrance they will only get damp and freeze.  We dined at their restaurant once.  The food was ordinary.   We did not stay at this resort due to the negative feedback in TripAdvisor on cleanliness and customer service.  The latter is quite lacking.  They have an ice museum that has scheduled tours.  They also have tours to see the aurora borealis.  Get gas in Fairbanks before driving out here.  There are no gas stations open at night.

name: MaryJean Fischer
text:
The hot springs for $15 / day are worth the 1 hour drive alone, but we enjoyed the geothermal plant tour, the ice house, appletini, and dinner also.
The wait at 7pm was 30 min.  The food was surprisingly good despite looking like it was mass produced.  We had "grilled salmon" burger.  It was a pre made patty with ground salmon and fillers but tasty.  The king crab cakes were also pre fab looking, but sweet and delicate.
The carrot cake was delish and the coffee correctly brewed strong.   The restaurant could work on their seating process and food presentation for a big impact at a low cost for the improvement.

name: Angeline Whitman
text:
Chena Hot Springs Resort is an excellent place to go, to unwind, to hike, to just plain experience.
You will not be disappointed.
Go visit, and maybe plan a several days' stay. There is so much to experience at the Resort.
There is a restaurant/gift shop. The food is top notch. Warning: The big bowl of clam chowder is gigantic, you may just want the bowl, rather than the big bowl. It was super-delicious, but way too big to get half-way through.
There is an "ice castle", the hot springs, that you can soak in, hiking trails, a duck and moose pond, and most likely much more that I missed.
Go check it out, you won't be disappointed. Well worth the time and effort to visit.

name: Ivy Marcella
text: Hotsprings is amazing! Ice museum is cool as well

name: Walter Analoak
text: It was great I would love to go back sooner than later.

name: Michael Smith
text: Ice museum operated and overcharged

name: Andrew Radtke
text: Wonderful visit. Planning to come back again as it gets colder.

name: Ellie Nicole
text: Have a alot of fun everytime I've gone, food isn't great. Hotel aren't clean nor worth it but the hot springs its self is great just make sure to bring food and water with you.

name: 39 Pizza
text: Don't go there for the cable TV. But the pool is pretty nifty in -50. There's quite a few tourists, in addition to your self. But it was beautiful.

name: Orren Wilkinson
text: The water was amazing. The scenery is beautiful. You must go and see this place if you are in Alaska. Locals should go about every month

name: sylvester sanchez
text: Stayed a few days here on our move from Juneau to Kodiak. Yeah I know it was out of the way. It was worth the extra miles. We stayed in n a two bedroom condo and too advantage of all it had to offer. The restraunt had great food and amazing service. There were four wheelers for rent and trips up to the Arctic Circle. There is also a class on renewable geothermal energy. There was a great petting zoo and always something to see and do. But the most amazing thing for me as a parents, was how my son fell in love with the Caribou. That made the trip for me. And the pools were nice too.

name: Robbie Tindall
text: I brought my Fiancé to the hot springs for a little get away and I was not impressed. I heard they had an ice bar which sounded fun?? But it’s not a bar it’s part of a tour of the ice museum. You have to buy a ticket to the tour and then your allowed 1 ice martini -no thank you. The door is closed and you can’t even look in? You can only go with a tour guide. We spent the night and the rooms were not updated like I had heard. Your phone doesn’t work and there’s are a limited amount of tv channels. The rooms are old and it wasn’t very comfortable. 1:00am someone pounded on our bedroom window so I’m thankful we were armed. Because good luck finding help if you need it out there.  The hot springs were relaxing but could stand to be updated. They grow vegetables in the green houses up there so the salads are fresh and delicious I highly recommend the salad. Go visit the hot springs have a salad and leave.

name: Kevin Koch
text: Nice and acomadating lots to do. Springs are hot.

name: Ruby Paquette
text: One of my most favorite places ever!

name: Dirty Thirty
text: Great place to relax and rejuvenate. The rock pool is really awesome when it is cold out. The hot areas of the pool compliment the cold. A very great place and a must when visiting the Fairbanks area.

name: Mary Hoy
text: Only visited the hot springs and ice museum but omg it was so worth it!!! Hot springs felt amazing and the ice museum was beautiful

name: Orren Hyatt
text:
This review is only for the hotspring and pool. I did not eat or stay at the resort.

My friends and I really enjoy coming here. The hot spring is a great way to relax and enjoy the beautiful sky. The Jacuzzi outside was great as well offering a more tolerable heat while still being outside.

The only downside was that the locker rooms are not always the cleanest. My wife had said that she found feminem hygiene products on the floor of the shower.

name: Tyrone Callaway
text: What a treat to relax in a hot spring after being out in the back country camping.

name: Arsal Nawaz
text: Cool places but too many masqitos , did enjoy hot springs, friendly people. Will probably go back but in winter!

name: Kaylynn Balcom
text: Wonderful experience everytime

name: Jacob Proffer
text: Little pricey, $15 a day for hot spring access. And if need cell reception for work etc, plan accordingly or pay $8 a day for Wi-Fi on site (it is not free). Bring a towel as well, its a nice day trip and it was a nice break from work.

name: sandra shephed
text:
Very friendly staff with excellent customer service. Restaurant has a great choice of food and prices are good. The souvenirs are also reasonable with authentic Alaskan craftsmanship. The ice museum is the crown. A must to see and the guide was very informative.
Accommodation was comfortable and casual.
Great place for the family to come and enjoy or a weekend getaway.

name: Roya Rakhshani
text: Food is good, but it better for the younger crowd.

name: Fawn Silas
text:
I love the hot springs. The night time is the best you can see the stars at night.
Warning it is a ways off the highway but well worth it.

name: Misti Dople
text: Very nice. Love visiting here

name: john watkins
text: The ice museum and the lunch was amazing.

name: TheWasillamike Tarr
text: Nice. Alaskan style. Best maintained hot spring that I have visited. Natural flow through spring pond, stays fresh. Crushed rock bottom.👍🏻

name: Dillon Matson
text: Lots of activities, and good times.

name: William Butler
text: Great place to come relax and really enjoy the amenities !!!

name: wanphen Tee
text: So Nice!! Feel good after that.

name: Kathy Karpin
text: Take a relaxing hot bath among happy, people also soaking and bobbing around the pool with varying degrees of heat. I lasted about 40 minutes. After a while enough,  but quite enjoyable.

name: John Pearson
text: It would be nice if their busses would turn off their bright over head lights when meeting them on the road.  Other then that everyone is fairly friendly.  could use some locker room maintenance at the pool house a little more frequently.

name: Mallika Rao
text: Entry for non guests is 15$ and worth every penny. There see two indoor hot tubs, one outdoor hot tub, one hot spring and one indoor pool. Very neat and clean maintained. Restrooms and shower is great and clean, staff is friendly. Bring quarters or dollar bills to get quarters. This is helpful for lockers. The hot spring feels really good. Bring water and Gatorade as you will get dehydrated in the hot water.

name: David McAdoo
text: Burgers are cooked to order but they don't ask how you want it done.

name: Laura Cipielewski
text: I had a wonderful scallop dinner at the restaurant before we went into the hot springs. The water in the springs felt awesome. The locker rooms were pretty nice. This was my second visit and we did not stay the night this time. Last July I had an overnight visit where we rented one of the small cabins. The cabin's do not have a bathroom so if that is important to you I would stay in the hotel.

name: Polar Remedies
text:
What a great place on earth. The resort is situated in such a remote setting and over the years has integrated sustainable eco living with techno modern life.

They always have an interesting crew of workers there and always friendly! The food and drinks in the restaurant and bar are so good too - everything fresh and with a nice pour.

Make sure you check out the aurorium there which is for watching the aurora borealis.

name: Mr_Promsit_ Channel
text: Beautiful place but long drive.

name: Petru Crucian
text:
Awesome place for relaxing your body and soul
Great place to see aurora

name: kp masonry
text: Love it out there! Especially when its -20! A great way to weather the cold and the food at their restaurant is top shelf!

name: MISFITsKABOOKIE
text: I live in Fairbanks Alaska and come here at least once a month in the summer and twice in the winter. Excellent place to visit for a day or more if you like. You just can't go wrong.

resp.text: Thank you very much for your review! See you here and let me tell you that we love our regular folks!

name: Per Harald Pettersen
text: The rock pool is very nice, big and warm, massage shower, cold spray to cool you down, and terrace with sunbeds too. The indoor pool is not so big, very ordinary. Jacuzzi and hot pool is nice. Pretty good package. Must be super on a cold winter night.

name: Tammy Helf
text: Beautiful! No matter the weather, this is a majestic natural wonder. There’s a restaurant, cabins, a lodge and greenhouses that are open year round. We went in December when it was -10, decorative lights around the grounds, the springs were hot, icicles on the wet hair. So much fun!! Love this place!!

name: Standa Pilař
text: Nice place for relax and rest. The place is located near by Anchorage city approximately 50 miles. I can recommend that's. I spent very pleasant day there.

name: Eric Davis
text: Great place for sore bones after a long trek

name: Kelley Soper
text: We greatly enjoyed our time here. We visited the Ice Museum and then went in the hot springs before taking a walk around the property.

name: Tricia Harrington
text: Yes yes loved it

name: Gloria Smith
text: Beautiful place

name: Fred Lamont
text: Great spring with fair prices.  Didn't stay in the resort so I do not know about it.

name: icussdemise _
text: Only hot spring I've ever been to, so it's great! Clean facilities, quiet, peaceful very relaxing environment. They have an indoor pool and hot tubs, and an outdoor hot tub in be addition to the hot springs. The cafe and restaurant on site are both pretty good places to eat as well

name: Richard McGuire
text: The hotsprings are awesome. They can be somewhat hot during the summer. Still fun though. They are easy to access. The price is not bad. Drive to the springs is easy enough.

resp.text:
Hey R,

Thank you very much for your visit and your review. We are happy you had an overall good time.

name: ANTHONY MARTIN
text: We always take our visitors here never disappointed the colder the better and we got -20, always enjoy the bar too:)

name: Krystle Anderson
text: My favorite place

name: Derek
text: Awesome,  enjoyed everything!

name: Padee McCrery
text: Clean and just what I needed. Burgers are always perfect too. Thanks for the Hot Soak

name: Victoria Avery
text: We took a tour here with one of our classes. They are powered by geothermal energy, which is really cool that they can be off the grid like that. They also grow a lot of their own food in the various green houses. A place like no other in Alaska. It is self contained and worth the visit.

name: Kerra Peavey
text: Great fun and good service.

name: Dean Barnes
text: I love the outdoor pool.

name: reese bunch
text: Super pretty, knowledgeable guides and employees, incredibly interesting, definitely worth the trip!

name: Zeng Sunshine
text: Great hot spring. If you what to observe aurora, you might need to walk a bit further away from the buildings: they don't always put down curtains when turning on lights 9n the room And cars are driving around. It's nearly impossible to see aurora light 8n the hot spring. Too much fog above the pool

name: Leland Collins
text: Hot Springs feels good.. food is good.

name: Moriah Norris
text: Oh my goodness, where to start. Delicious meals for all 3 of us, followed by the hot springs under the northern lights. Such a wonderful experience!

name: Tim Wilson
text: It was nice. The ice house bar is a must see. The hot spring was pretty cool also.

name: Eljay Koomba
text: Great sight seeing and hike trails. Amazing views once you're up there on any of the trails. The spring looked amazing but we didnt do it. Those in the water looked very relaxed and warm! It was about 35 degrees that day so it looked well deserved. I wasn't happy seeing the dog kettle area as to all the dogs on chains to a pole. It felt very sad like a concentration camp of many dogs.

name: Daniel Harris
text: We very much enjoyed a soak in the spring,  but this place could be so much more.  Nice RV spots,  but no hookups (for $20). No WiFi accessible from RV spots (though they claimed it was in the lodge).  Ice Museum can only be accessed on a tour (we just wanted a drink).

name: Michael Smiyun
text: Very nice super hot springs. Sucks the ice museum requires tours.

name: Adriana Pellegrini
text: This place is so amazing. I would highly recommend going in the winter. The rock lake is so lovely, relaxing, scenic, natural feeling, and perfect for pictures. Lodging is a bit expensive, but if you drive over from Fairbanks, access to the hot springs is actually quite affordable. Good food at the restaurant, as well. An absolutely lovely weekend trip. Don't let the frigid outdoor temps scare you off, because that just makes the hot springs that much sweeter.

name: Robert Taylor
text: Clearly for most of us the highlight is a soak in the hot springs. Zero out but hot in

name: Todd Christensen
text: I recommend the hot water neck and shoulder massage at the far end of the rock pond.

name: Jamie Burchfield
text: We just kind of stumbled onto Chena hot springs so we didn't swim or have planned activities here. Next time I would like to stay here. We walked the grounds. Looks like a great place to stay.

name: Casey Tobia
text: Clean, enjoyable, affordable.... No matter what time of year

name: Austyn Vaona
text:
I would highly recommend spending a day there
Bring a water bottle with you into the hot springs
And also get has before you go as you are really heading out there

name: Amanda Franklin
text: They've got you because you at the end of the road but springs and restaurant are very nice

name: ElPaco Taco
text: What a special place. Period

name: Ted Booth
text: Hot springs are great, hotel is so-so; no refrigerator or microwave, very basic. Though the mattresses are pretty great.

name: Yoni Ryabinski
text: An awesome spot to relax.

name: Keita Bodrogi
text: Indoor pool is small, limited hot tub space, hot springs are nice but too crowded. Rooms are nice, but you must pay for wifi. 👎

name: Pamela Cook
text: Outdoor pool is nice and bonus because it's over 18 (there is an indoor pool for kids). The outdoor hot tub is a work in progress. Would be really nice if you could order snacks and drinks while using the facilities, but instead you have to get fully dressed to go to the restaurant. We probably would have went back into the pool if that weren't the case. They have a cafe but it's very lacking in options. Restaurant food was good and prices weren't bad at all.

name: Jacob Singleton
text: There's so much to do here! Swimming in the hot springs, enjoying Appletinis in the world-class ice museum, petting the donkeys, touring the geothermal plant and greenhouse, and eating in the restaurant are just a few of the things we did during our afternoon here.

name: Robb Geesen
text: A fun place to spend a day

name: Brennan Lyle
text: Chena Hot Springs Resort is a great place to visit in Alaska. The outdoor rock pool is an awesome place to relax, and the prices are very reasonable. For a day pass (which is the entire time the pool, hot tubs, and rock pool are open) it's only $15. You'd probably pay more for open swim days at a regular pool, and not get nearly as much variety as out there. Only downside is the drive, but it's easy cruising on Chena Hot Springs Road to get out there.

name: Shay Denton
text: Lovely resort! The more expensive rooms are absolutely worth it.

name: Hovercraft Steve
text: Superclean hotspring pond

name: Sheri Schoenberg
text: I love the Springs at 20 degrees and below because it's magical.  The summer though is lovely as well.  I was pleased with the quiet atmosphere.

resp.text: Hey Sheri! Thank you so much for your review :)

name: Avaiyak Brower
text: Open 7am to 11:45, and worth the drive. Talk about relaxation

name: Rugged spartan

Even the water from the faucets smelled weird. Maybe old pipes?? I can understand why the internet was terrible cause we were literally out in the middle of nowhere. There was only one channel that was working on the TV and it was fuzzy. Adding a DVD player with some movies to check out would have been nice. The coffee at the activity center was ok. Had to pay with cash because there internet was down.

name: Tanya Wychopen
text: Interesting site.  Loved the runway and the planes.  The office staff would be more knowledgeable if they actually knew the layout of the RV spots. We encountered one that didn't. The restaurant was a long wait, which we would have understood if the host had taken time to say that they were short staffed, rather than us discover on our own. Didn't see the hot springs, thought it was a bit odd to go through the pool, but maybe next time.

name: Garima Mishra

text: It needs an upgrade, the front desk holds your deposit for 30 days (keep that in mind), but overall it was nice. Either way I'm sure some of the bacteria is due to humans. But the rooms were clean, and restaurant food was delicious.

name: Gary Dorgay
text: Great place in the Fairbanks wilderness to relax in the hot springs..Great restaurant..

name: Patrick Woolery
text: Chena hot springs is about an hour out of town, and the pool is only 15 bucks per adult. Its a good place for a day trip, and while there are other things to do there I cannot speak to how they are. The pool is worth visiting though.

name: Bridger Kimber
text: Fun place for a weekend getaway. Very neat seeing all the self sustaining technology.

name: R P
text:
Cool spot. Nice natural hot springs in the Alaska wilderness. Quite a few buildings make up this "resort". It's will built up. We started y in a dry cabin and it was pleasant.
A couple issues: inside every building is incredibly hot. Super hot. The restaurant was unbearably hot. The cabin was so hot we had to open up the windows to let it cool down. I guess it's hard to regulate the heat source, seeing as it's all naturally heated by circulating spring water. I wish the restaurant had windows to open.
Speaking of the restaurant, prepare to wait. I'm not sure if it's due to inadequate staffing, or just a nonchalant approach. Either way, takes about 15 minutes to be acknowledged, another 10 to 15 to be seated, and yet another 10 to 15 to get a server to notice you. After all the waiting, the food was good, beer selection was pretty good. Don't get mixed drinks. Moscow mule was not a mule.

The hot spring is cool. But the locker rooms are filthy. Super gross. Wear sandals, or flip flops. Do not enter barefoot.
The pool (outdoor) is big, and hot and wonderful! Sand bottom is a nice touch.

name: Jamie m
text: Love this place! They have made a lot of improvements in the last year too. The springs are so relaxing. The restaurant is very delicious. The ice museum is awesome too. Highly recommend on your visit to fairbanks!

name: Andrea howard
text: It's great at night time and great place to bring family of all ages! There's a restaurant, gift shop, tours, a pool/hot springs, massages, and a hotel. The hot springs is so nice:)

name: Bryan James Blehm
text: Way too touristy.  Not somewhere to go if you want hot springs in the wild.

name: isabelle stebler
text: The Hot Springs are rather small and the outdoor area is limited to one bigger, more natural looking big pool and a whirlpool and the inside area was another pool that looked kind of dirty (even though it was adviced as being chlorinated...). Overall the facility seems not too well mantained, or at least looks that way... camping in the campground was nice.

name: Eric Benz
text: The drive to Chena Hot Springs is worth the visit.  Great views of the Aurora and Sunsets.

name: Queena Gandwa
text:
If you're visiting Fairbanks, you should never miss out on this hot spring. $15 for adult admission on the hot spring and you can stay till midnight! Some stay here to watch the northern lights while in the dipping in the hot spring. They have towels here too for 5$ and a swim suit, swimming trunks, etc. If you forgot to bring something.

You need 2 QUARTERS for a locker. It fits an average school backpack. Just bring 2 quarters. They ran out but restocked after 30 mins.

If you don't want the outdoor hot spring, there's a heated pool and a jacuzzi indoors. So, choose whatever you want!

name: Mayra Stender
text: You need this in your life.

name: Misty Johnson
text: LOVE chena!!! I have zero complaints! Everything to do there is so fun!!

name: Emma OA
text: My absolute must visit place in alaska. One of my favorite places to visit. Definitely give it a try. Restaurant makes delicious food, cheap camping options and of course the lovely hot spring.

name: Edward Santillan
text: Very interesting.  Love soaking in the lake.  The WiFi was great and reasonable - $1an hour. Don't miss the reindeer. Wear warm clothes so you can enjoy ice museum.

name: Elisabeth Nyang
text: Great place to spend the day. I usually come every few months. Have never spent the night, so can't comment on the accomodations. I ate twice at the restaurant and drinks are good, but dishes are average. I give this place 5 stars because the experience is epic.

The place was surprisingly upgraded that room

name: Gay Herve
text: I paid  for an apple tini before going into the ice museum, didn't have my ID, wouldn't serve me,which is fine, but then wouldn't refund my money, not good customer service 😡 they should ask for ID when paying.

name: Robert Carpenter
text: Great food.

name: Nathaniel Terpening
text: Natural hot springs in a truly Alaskan setting. Miles from anywhere, the resort offers a wide range of activities year round. The ice castle is fun with a special adult drink for an extra charge. There are sled dogs and trails and all sorts of Alaskan outdoor activities to enjoy.

name: James Farmer Jr
text: Amazing place, very romantic. The room was adequate, but we didn't spend much time there. The Ice Museum is a must see and the springs are a great place to spend time with your significant other.

name: Cassandra Yeh
text:
This review is for the activities on site.

The Service: The service at the Activity Center was okay. The staffs have to take care both Activity Center & Convenient Store.

The Activity: They offer several activities.

Ice Museum - $15 admission (45 minutes). So-So. Very dark inside so hard to see & take pictures. Kind of small. $15 addition for Apple Martine in ice glass.

Dog Sledding Ride - $60 (15 minutes). BEST ADVENTURE ever~ Super fun on the sled & enjoying the gorgeous view.

Snowmobile - $65 (45 minutes). They do stop in the middle of the trip so you can take photos.

Aurora Snowcoach - $75 (9pm-2am). No guarantee if there would be northern light, all depends on the weather. They do post weather forecast at the Activity Center. If it is cloudy.... don't sign up. Because you will end up waiting inside freezing cold bungalow up in the mountain for hours and see nothing. Waste money & time.

Hot Spring - $15 admission (all day pass). However, every time you leave and open the locker, you have to pay again when you re-enter the hot spring. Bring your own towel, save $5.

In winter, the scenery is super gorgeous! Walking on the trail and enjoy the winter wonderland (FREE!).

The Transportation: They do offer tour package including shuttle from the city. I personally prefer getting a rental car. It is only about a little bit over one hour drive from the city and I can spend all day at the resort enjoying all the activities & facilities.

name: Brian Rohan
text: Always fun, in the summer or winter. Was lucky enough to be here when they were making ice glasses

name: Chelsea Ramirez
text: Open until midnight,  had a great time,  waters HOT.  Bring your own stuff! Several different hot tubs to sit in outside the springs. Great place for a date! Worth the drive♡

name: Derek S.
text: Nice place to enjoy hot spring.

name: Boogles Johnson
text: I give it 3 stars, we stayed in the the king salmon cabin and the unit needs some electrical work shoddy extension cords for the lights.  For the price I would like to have a light switch.  The water was great and my kids skin sure liked the water.

name: C Lippert
text: Nice, nite trip up mountain had a wonderful guide Joe. Excellent chef! Rooms need a through clean.

name: Jen Lee

name: Lee Hunt
text: We love the natural springs...and benifits it gives us health wise! Blessed to have it near us

name: Chloe Allan
text: We went to visit only the hot springs. The water is probably deepest and hottest in the rock pool (ages 18 and over because the water is not processed). They have 2 small tubs and a warm pool indoors. The outdoor pools are the rock pool and one hot tub. Good place to bring tourists and friends.

name: Jim Steward
text: This place is a over priced dive! Sorry but true.The hot springs I remember is long gone. The pool was clear and you was greeted at the front not asked to leave. I think a open minded owner could do so much better. But I love going there damn you front desk pool guy. You my friend suck at customer service. Should try cleaning the pool and hot tubs.

name: Hazel Sunshine Hall
text: Beautiful place to go. There is no internet connection out there but there is WiFi you can pay for at community lodge. The hot springs are nice and comfortable. Locker rooms get crowded quickly. Great place to go and relax and watch the stars

name: William Lemos
text: Not a Ritz Carlton, but that's not why you go. You go to get as far away from your every day life as possible. With that said, they have everything you could ask for. We stayed at the Moose Lodge. Clean and comfortable rooms. The staff was exceptional. The owners are amazingly involved in the running of the resort. The hot springs are ridiculously therapeutic. We loved the ice museum, the horseback riding, the bike rides, the geothermal tour, the sled dog kennels, the restaurant, etc, etc. I would highly recommend you stay at this resort. The 2 days we spent here were the highlight of our week in Alaska.

name: Van Strebe
text: It was a nice hot spring and no drama. Nice staff and well kept premises.

resp.text: Thank you very much for taking time to write this review!

name: Sonja Heuscher
text: Worth a visit, wonderful hot springs in a remote location yet accessible by road

name: James Haag
text:
Way out in the middle of nowhere you will find an incredible getaway boasting numerous opportunities for recreation of all flavors.
We stayed at a super cool spot in the campground which was great because they don’t take advanced reservations for the campground so if you get there early enough you can get a nice spot unlike many campgrounds that are booked solid all summer hours after booking opens.
The pool house had a warm pool and a couple jetted hot tubs but my favorite was the “rock lake” outside that was natural water.
We also took a tour of the ice palace which was a true palace full of incredible ice sculptures made by a world renowned artist.
If you’re in the Fairbanks area this place is worth the side trip for sure.

name: Ryan
text: You come here for the hot springs (better than whitehorse IMO, not anything as good as laird), riding bikes, horseback riding, canoe or kayaking. Everything is reasonably priced. Rooms are not fancy, but they work. Captn n coke at the bar is $7.35. Renting two fat tire bikes for an hour was $10. Sandwiches at the restaurant for $12. Candy bars are only $1.50 which is cheaper than a convenience store. All the employees are friendly, typically your out of state employees smile a little more but that's with any Alaska business you visit. They seem to constantly be improving the place which shows care from the owner.

name: Keith Nicholas
text: Great place to visit in the summer and winter... they got a hand full of activities for everyone to do.. its a must visit!!

It is about 1.3hours drive from Fairbanks. Watch out for moose is you drive yourself. Take bug spray with you, the mosquitoes there are just hungry for a piece of you.

text: There's only one hot spring pool and they don't enforce the 18+ only rule. The rooms have paper thin walls and we heard kids screaming and running around well past 11pm. There is plenty else to do there, like an ice museum, flight seeing, ATV tours, and more, but the hot springs were the reason we went. Overall not really worth the price and the drive out there for me.

name: Mike Maltese
text: It was a great day with friendly staff and great service. We took the Ice museum tour, snow machined, and swam in the hot springs. The prices are comparable to other attractions in the area. The location is remote but still offers all the luxury amenities of an in town resort. We would recommend it at the tip of the list of things to do in Fairbanks.

name: Stephen McQueen
text: This place was one of the best experiences I've had in Alaska. I'm going back ASAP.

name: FERIANTO Liem
text: Fresh air, beautiful scenery, plenty of activities, just don't expect city's toilet.

name: Andrew Scott
text: Chena hot springs lays about an hour from Fairbanks, down a winter worn road. When you get to the resort, the road ends, and a small one car bridge ushers you into the resort. They have a restaurant and bar serving on site grown salads, potatoes, and other vegetables, as well as seafood, lamb, and burgers that's open until 10pm. They also have a commissary serving coffee, oatmeal, basic soup and sandwiches until 12pm. The rooms are clean with firm beds, and have hard wood floors in the unit I stayed in. The bathroom was a shower stall and a toilet, with the vanity and sink outside by the front door. The indoor pool area has 2 hot tubs and a 5 ft pool. The outdoor pool area is a large spring fed pool with a ramp leading into the water. It's surrounded by large boulders of local stone that is comfortable to sit or lay on. The water has a sulfuric smell that's akin to an active volcano. The water makes your skin and hair soft. The water will tarnish silver really badly, so make sure you take off anything you don't want to turn brown. They offer laundry facilities for $4 wash and dry, a dining area, and internet for $8 a device per day or $12 for 2 days.

name: Marie B.
text: Hey friendly staff, clean facilities and a nice spacious outdoor pool, as well as several indoor pools. The nice thing is that the outdoor hot springs pool is only for 18+, so no kids allowed. Very nice restaurant also as well as options to get a massage or a few souveniers.

name: TishAnne Steele
text: Clean locker rooms, good food in the restaurant. Bring cash, all of their credit machines were down

name: Anne Komac
text: After reading the reviews we almost didn't go to the Hot Springs, but I'm glad we did. The facility is dated, but the changing rooms and showers were clean when we visited. Yes, there is algae on the rocks in the outdoor pool, but the water is clear and for heavens sake, it's an outdoor hot springs! If you don't  want to experience nature, go to a heavily chlorinated indoor pool at a Ritz Carlton.

name: Lindsey Rising
text: I always love coming here. The hot springs are amazing, the temps vary throughout the pool so you can get in a super hot spot or just warm. The restaurant is a must for me every time I'm there, they have the best burgers!

name: Aaron Majors
text:
I try to give each business the benefit of the doubt when considering leaving a negative review as sometimes it's due to a new employee in training.  As a resident in the area I've been here several times and normally it's a great place to soak in the hot springs.  This visit we decided to stay the night and I was less than impressed from the time we parked until the time we departed.  The mosquito and no-seeum population is unbelievable! Bring coils to burn and repellant! Previous years I did not notice this as a problem but was obvious during this visit and made it impossible to enjoy anything outdoors. We stayed in the "Bear Family Suite". It was a step up from a tent but don't expect a 3 star hotel quality. The room was in working order but less than standard workmanship was obvious in glancing at the room from the entrance that was slanted so bad a sober person would feel drunk walking on. The finish and cosmetic appeal was borderline terrible. Half of the beds had pillows extremely hard. Plan to bring your own pillow. The room looked to have been cleaned in a hurry several times but there was a ring of dirt around each room. I'd rate the room as a 1 star and the employees as 3 stars as a couple were great and a couple less than great. A few concerns; no air conditioning, phone, Wi-Fi, stuck in the 1960's, the shower was scolding hot or extremely cold, pest control, parking was difficult because the building is located away from the parking lot. They did make an exception for us to park closer.
The restaurant was good but expect to pay a little more than in town.
The ponds were good for watching a moose calf and ducks and the birds nested into the balcony kept the mosquitos at bay at the room only.

Considering all aspects of the stay I would consider this value to be around $40 not including a swim pass. You may want to consider camping instead.

name: Jon Robichaud
text:
I'm torn on what to give here. The hot springs are nice, but not great. The washroom was less then desirable. A bit dirty for the price you pay. The one down side is that if you camp here for $20 a night you still have to pay $15 to use the springs.

For an hours drive from Fairbanks it's a nice place if you want to and plan to stay for a few nights. But for a day trip or just for 2 nights I'm not sure I'd return given the price of admission.

name: Nate Stalzer
text:
They get you to drive to the middle of nowhere. No cell signal. The upper management probably saw that as a money making opportunity, so they charge for use of wifi. Fail. Nickel and dime people like that and you get a 2 or 3 star rating. We had an ok time, so 3 stars.
Also, for a place that people visit to see the aurora, you sure have a lot of lights on. We had to drive 10 minutes away to get a better aurora experience in almost complete darkness.

name: Larry Montgomery
text: Nice place to visit definitely not to miss

name: Kim Traud

name: Michael Johnson
text: Loved it! Managed wonderfully for all there traffic it gets. In previous visits, the drinking and tap water was alike to the water in the hot spring, but it has drastically increased. Food and service is amazing, and beautiful surroundings.

name: Kenyatta Moreland

text: Had a great time staying and visiting the springs.

name: Will Elver
text: Nice place and the hit springs were great! Rooms are so so but not too bad for the price. Be prepared to spend money if you want to do the other activities they offer.

name: Steve Parkinson
text:
At the restaurant we waited for 10 minutes at the 'wait to be seated sign'. Since no one came I stepped in to the dining area to be seen. A waiter asked if we had been helped then rudely told me to wait outside by the sign.

We sat for dinner about 6 PM. The waiter brought our water and menus, but that was the last we saw of him. After 15 minutes we left. If the water was indicative of the meal that could have been, then it would have been foul.

Annoyed by the restaurant we didn't buy shirts at the gift shop.

We did wade in the hot spring. It was nice, but I think a great tagline for the hot spring would be 'the less you know about microbiology, the more you will enjoy the water.'

Finally, we wanted to have a drink at the ice bar. As it turns out, it is only accessible by taking the ice museum tour for $15 a head.

name: Patrick Barbier
text: Definitely worth the trip for the hot springs alone!  I would bring your own towel to avoid the $5 charge to use theirs.  We spent the money to go into the ice museum and as it is interesting I think the price doesn't matchup with the experience (the additional charge for the cocktail was a letdown too).  I would go back for the hot springs or if it was a weekend package that includes activities.  Plenty of stuff to do there and unfortunately we didn't get to do the Aurora chasing, kennel tour, or snowmobiling.  During the summer they have comparable activities too.

name: Courtney Marchesani
text: We made the pilgrimage to Chena after having attending a week long kids camp in Fairbanks. Unfortunately there were some really wild patrons in the pool making it virtually impossible to enjoy it. We spread our time out between the individual pools on the upper deck. If you don't have kids and you avail yourself of the deep adult wading pool you'll feel like you've died and gone to heaven. I laid back and let the steamy heated bliss emanating up from the waters take away the stress of the week. It is well worth the time taken to get there.Somewhat on the expensive side so make sure you allow plenty of time to meander, enjoy, and get your money's worth. Hopefully you won't have the party crashers ruin your vibe.

name: Rebecca Bronczyk
text: Stayed in one of the fox rooms, very comfortable. Decided to do a guided atv tour, which was to tons of fun and our guide was super nice! Had dinner at their restaurant which was yummy! The hot springs are of course fantastic, and extremely relaxing. Service was great, all the employees are super nice. I would definitely come back, but recommend bringing a cooler if you don't want to rely on the food they have here.

text: We stayed 1 day and night at Chena. It's a place great for getting away from the big cities with no internet. There's no reception at the resort. They're ice museum was beautiful and cool to see! Don't forget to bring bug spray during the summer! The hot spring looked clean and was very refreshing. However, not so much for the pool. Food at the restaurant wasn't so great, just needed improvement for their items on some of the entrees we had. There were 7 of us and had to wait 45 minutes or more before we were seated. (Though understandable because they were busy) Customer service was great at all places (Hot springs, Reception desk, activities desk, Cafe shop, and even the restaurant) There were many activities we didn't have the chance to do. So it's recommended that you stay more than 2 days.

name: 金山劳模
text:
(Translated by Google) Chena Hot Springs is famous for its hot springs and is also a resort that provides accommodation. NorthPole is located on the south side of Fairbanks, 60 miles from the airport and about an hour and a half on snowy road. This one-hundred-year-old Chena Hot Springs was built by a pair of brothers who dig out a gold mine. The reason why the two brothers discovered this hot spring was to help his brother Robert, who suffers from rheumatism, find a place to soothe the pain. They finally found this hot spring in the barren land of inland Alaska and built 12 cabins to entertain guests from all over the world, and it became one of the most popular resorts in inland Alaska.
The American Agricultural Service once sent people to analyze the hot spring water here and found that the water quality here is very different from the water in other parts of the United States, which has special benefits for the human body. Soaking in the hot spring here, you can feel the temperature difference between 30 degrees in the hot spring and minus 30 degrees and up to 60 degrees outside the hot spring.

In a light-free environment, Chena Hot Springs has become a good place for chasing aurora. If you are lucky, you can see the beautiful scenery in the picture outside the cabin.

Friends who want to live here can book here in advance. In addition to the hot springs, there is also the famous Aurora Ice Museum to visit, all of which are made of ice, just like the palace of Elsa in Frozen. The ice sculptures inside are exceptionally novel and dreamy under the light, and there is also an Ice Bar. Don’t forget to order a glass of "Appletini" made of Vodka and apple juice and placed in an ice goblet to warm up!

(Original)
Chena Hot Springs 以温泉著名，也是一个提供住宿的度假村。位于 Fairbanks 南边的北极村 (NorthPole)，距离机场 60英里，开雪路约一个半小时。这个一百多年历史的 Chena Hot Springs 是由一对掏金矿的兄弟一手打造。两兄弟之所以发掘这片温泉，是为了帮患有风湿的哥哥 Robert 找到一个可以安抚疼痛的地方。他们最后在这个阿拉斯加内陆贫瘠的地找到这座温泉并打造了12个小木屋招待千里迢迢来这的客人，应而变成阿拉斯加内陆其中一个最热门的度假村。
美国农务所曾派人来分析这里温泉的水，发现这边的水质跟美国其他地方的水十分不一样对人体有特别的益处。在这里泡温泉，你可以感受到泡在温泉中30度及温泉外零下30度高达60度的温差。

无光害的环境，Chena Hot Springs 成为了适合追极光的好地方。幸运的话在小木屋外就可以看到图片中的美景。

想住这的朋友可提前网上预定点这里，除了温泉这里亦有著名 Aurora Ice Museum 可参观，这里全部都是冰做的，仿佛冰雪奇缘中 Elsa 的皇宫般。里头的冰雕在灯光照射下格外新奇梦幻，还有一座 Ice Bar 冰冻酒吧，别忘了点上一杯以 Vodka 和苹果汁调制而成，且装在冰制高脚杯的“Appletini"暖暖身！

text: Best tacos in Fairbanks.  Great people who work there.

name: Brian Won
text:
The owner does a great job keeping the employees authentic, and the menu certainly seems authentic.

However the execution isn't the greatest, but to be fair-- this is Fairbanks. The fact that they attempt something authentic at all deserves them a lot of credit!

FWIW stick to the tacos, the menudo was a bit too salty. Tacos are only a bit too greasy, and oversized-- like they're on soft taco flour torillas instead of proper street tacos. Although considering the price, soft taco-sized tacos is about right!

text: Good food for the price. Had the carne asada and lengua combo. Both came out very good. The carne asada was seasoned very well. Also had the chicken soup which I highly recommend. Soup was a little bigger than expected but definitely had lots of   chicken and vegetables.  Finished the meal with a flan which was ok.

name: Brice Wilbanks
text:
As far as Taco King goes, this one ranked pretty low on my list. The normal Taco King feel I get back in Anchorage just wasn't present at this location. The dining room was dirty, musty, and grimey. Tables were uncleaned and the overall experience was not up to Taco King standards.

The tamales were VERY dry here. I can see why they were a "Special". Unflavorful and dry. I had to add moisture to it by drinking more Pepsi. On the positive side, the staff here were awesome.
They were very open to accommodating our request to substitute the rice for chips. Once we sat down, they finally came over and wiped the table for us.

Overall, food wasn't great and it just didn't feel like the traditional Taco King experience. I'll be keeping my Taco King eating to my usual Anchorage location.

Pretty good spot for some good Hispanic food.

The ordering system is a little weird - you order at the counter and then sit down and they bring the food to you.

The rice and beans were very yum. I also appreciated their little salsa and sour cream bar. I love me some sour cream so it's nice to be the dictator of how much goes on my plate. :)

Overall, our experience was good. Nothing crazy but definitely not bad by any means.

We were not disappointed at all. We are vegetarians. We got everything that we wanted. The food was super delicious. The service was super fast as well. The owner was kind enough to circle back with us to see if we got everything as per our liking. When we were waiting at the counter to pick up the food they asked us to seat at the table and they will serve there. I really liked their service and the human touch. Finding the Taco King was not at all difficult, the on air ad gave you the directions.  I was not really hungry (that turned out to be a good thing), I just wanted to sample a simple item from their item; so that I could say that I had been.

I ended up ordering a carne asada taco at $3.45 - yes a regular-size taco for over $3!  So, how was the taco?  It was like any average taco and therefore, no worth $3.45.  I am sure there is a reason for tacos being $3.45 in Alaska.  The good thing, is that I did get the need to go out of my system.  Darn, when in Alaska, local advertising does indeed work.

text: I always enjoy the meals I have here with my family. Its a yearly birthday pick by my sister. We used to go more often, but with family’s growing up they start to get busy and live their own lives. They service is always great here, they check in on us often and refill our side dishes quick too. I would give it a 5 star but its more expensive then other restaurants around wasilla. $12.50 for a bacon burger with fries no soda.... But I always look forward to coming and eating here. We don’t drink so I have no comment on that side of their business. Worth going and checking it out. Good Date Night in Valley too.

text: Went with family. The service was so much better than other Red Robin's! Jessica was AMAZING! She was super nice and you could tell she was smiling even though she was wearing a mask. She was super joyful and polite! 10/10  definitely recommend going and ask for Jessica!

name: Ryan Stafford
text:
You can't beat the variety of food at Red Robin Gourmet Burgers and Brews.  I personally enjoy the burgers the most.  The cheese burgers are great for those who like dry fingers, however many of the other burgers can be real juicy and messy.  The garlic fries are great and I think they're worth the additional cost.  Fountain drinks are endless, so you won't leave thirsty!

May 2019
(1) Cheese Burger: $12.59
(1) Soda: $3.19
(1) Black & Bleu Burger: $15.59
(+) Garlic Fries: $0.99
Tax: $0.97

text: I love the atmosphere of red Robin,  it reminds me of being a kid. Their food is absolutely delightful,  but it is sooo expensive. I've had great people serve me most times and only twice that it was poor service. Sadly I have to keep updating this review with less and less stars...Red Robin's delivery service is terrible,  you might get fries or you might not, they often forget entire parts of the order, a burger or sometimes all of the beverages. Their answer is to put your name on a list and you can get a free burger next time because it takes upwards of 2 weeks for them to process a simple return. When I tried to redeem my burger they didn't know who I was. This time I opted to wait 2 weeks for the return, we shall see...

name: Marvelous Massage
text:
Nine times out of 10 you will get a very great burger here. Because I have special dietary needs I choose to have the lettuce wrapped burgers the majority of the time. Will they do a lettuce wrap they typically wrap it in a rapper so that you can still pick it up with your hands and eat it like a burger. Well one time we didn’t do that and it was basically this laid out deconstructed burger on a plate it was a bit disappointed because I could not pick up my burger and eat it like I wanted to. It was dry and frankly lacking in taste as well.

I do really really like their garlic fries with extra garlic of course!

Most of the time the wait staff is exceptional
(Tikatnu location only)

They always give you a free birthday Sunday regardless of your age!

Excellent value for the money

name: HighExpectAsians
text: Party of 6, and each with their own problems. I ordered a Smoky Tavern burger and halfway through I realized that I had forgot what I ordered because it tasted like a regular burger, probably because it was, except a large pump of barbeque sauce at the very end. The grilled cheese shouldn't even be called a grilled cheese, it was barely cooked at all and drowning in butter. The avocado burger didn't have avocado on it. The chips from the nachos tasted stale, and my water glass was shattered on the bottom, not to leaking point but very unprofessional. The only thing that could have made it worse was the service, so it's appreciated that the service was good. Not the most helpful but it was pretty busy and I'm sure everyones trying their best. In the end, we haven't been having good experiences on our last few trips and we won't be coming back.

Past 3 times I have been here the food hasn't gotten better. I also don't get the bottomless fries. I only eat the first serving that I get but it really bugs me when I get only 10 fries with my burger. Please just give me a proper order. I don't want to order a second set of fries. Time is money and sitting at red robin waiting on my free fries is not how I want to spend my lunch break.

name: Kristen Donchess
text:
I was never a fan of chain restaurants until I moved to the Frozen North aka Wasilla aka the good food wasteland.
Red Robin is something that I love the consistency of here in Wasilla!
I don't come expecting to be totally wowed, but the consistency of great wait staff ensures that I always leave satisfied. I've had cold food, undercooked food, and food that was totally not what I ordered, but the waiter staff always rectified the situation.
So first off kudos to you guys!!

The only real complaint/issue I have with Red Robin in Alaska is the fact that they allow children to sit anywhere. I'm from Washington which has strict laws as to where and when minors can be places, it was always a sacred thing getting dinner in the bar. It makes me upset that the host staff will seat children in the bar...but I guess it's an Alaska thing. It's it because I really dislike kids either, it's because the parents don't work to keep their children quiet and they don't care if their kids are ruining others dining experiences.

Anyway, rant over....

I love the bottomless root beer floats and I love the onion rings. As always, I will keep coming back Red Robin, just keep the root beer flowing and the onion rings hot!!

name: Pete Sandor
text: Food quality has gone down hill serverly... I had family member go by while they were out to grab me a burger  (big mistake)... I wanted to try the new BBQ ranch burger but have the ranch n BBQ sauce on side so the burger didnt get mushy by time I got it... My family member arrives and double checks (constant thing no matter where you go now adays) and the ranch and sauce were on it... So after blaming that they are busy,  they had to redo it, also asking to make sure it's med rare... The employee gets into an argument stating "we have to cook it more then well done", even tho we never had this issue before, after sometime (longer then should require) she says she will tell the person making it... After 40min a new burger arrives again blaming on them being busy... So now I get my burger and it's so dry it's disgusting and inedible, we call them up to complain to the manager who again blames them being busy, but refunds the money to my card... This is just pitiful to use being busy as an excuse and then to argue that they can't cook a burger to med rare taking 40min to make a dry disgusting thing, are you kidding me... McDonald's would have been cheaper and tasted better then this burger and they are 10x busier then Red Robin... The quality of their food has gone down that I won't be back and I feel bad that if people around here accept this as a quality burger place (been to many across the US), Red Robin is great, but just not this one...

name: phillip chandonnet
text: My wife and I stopped mid day for a brew and some food.  They were serving brunch, and was very very good.  I had the eggs benedict and my wife had the biscuits and gravy.  Both as stated before were very good.  We ending up having some friendly chat and the server showed us their dinner menu.  We decided to come back for dinner, and glad we did.  We split some clam chowder and two entrees.  One was the braised pork shank, and the other was the roast. We also had an appetizer of the sea scallops.  The meals that we had were over the top, perfect size and infused with different flavors.  I will highly recommend anyone going to Fairbanks to take the 15 minute drive to the Silver Gulch and have a meal you will not be disappointed.  Cheers to our waiter Jamie and chef Robin can't wait to come and enjoy again.

name: Cyrus Collier
text: Took my family out last night to the Silver Gulch Brewing and Bottling company I have been there a few times before and enjoyed my time, however the last two times including last night were very poor! I brought seven people in my group with me to dine, we were seated promptly, however it took them 38 minutes to even come to our table to give us water, and that’s only after I got up and walked over to the waitress station and ask for somebody to come to our station. Four people came in after us were seated were welcomed and given water and drinks before Us. I am an Alaskan I work hard and I don’t look rich however that shouldn’t matter when it comes to service. If I come to your facility it means I can afford to pay what’s on the menu. My daughter was up from Texas to visit and I wanted her to have a nice night out for her last night here however I was very very disappointed. My bill was over $230 for my group. I believe that we should’ve had better service. And I just can’t believe the disappointment for my daughter.

name: Matthew Lee
text:
I really want to like this place. We've been 3 times and the food is really good. However, no one has ever greeted us when we walk up to the counter and the hostess is either not present or acting very flustered.

Our first trip there was good, second trip was better, third trip ended an hour after we arrived but left without getting our food (had somewhere to be so we left and just called in pizza):

Third trip: waited 5 min to be greeted (literally no one was at the hostess stand and multiple employees walked by and said nothing to us) then got our table and were not greeted by wait staff for another 5-10 min and waitress seemed annoyed when she finally came over. We ordered and 40 min later we did not have our food. Manager came about 20 min in and apologized, saying there was a large party upstairs, which was appreciated, and assured us our food was "on the way" soon. Waitress came by and asked if we wanted an appetizer (why would that suddenly come faster than the food we already ordered...?, we said no thank you but appreciated the offer). 20 min later, still no food. Asked for a refill on a soda we ordered and 10 min later it was still sitting empty on our table... that did it for us, we just left a few bucks on the table and left. This was clearly a kitchen problem but front of house staff was very unprofessional. They seem understaffed and poorly prepared. We weren't upset about the slow food necessarily but we didn't have all day to wait around and it was just so poorly managed from start to finish.

name: Whysay
text: Not a great experience. The place was so cold we had to keep our coats and hats on. Everyone else in the restaurant did too. Someone must have finally said something because a waitress brought over a portable heater and put it near them. We ate our food as fast as we could so we could leave. Spent over 100 bucks for 3 people trying to eat and get out. Not a great night out. Only reason I'm giving it 2 stars is because our host Doug was outstanding. Truly disappointed.

name: William Lemos
text: We had an excellent time here. The staff was friendly and hard working. We had buffalo burgers and a pizza crust club sandwich. All were quite tasty. Great local brews on the menu as well. Gift shop and beer store was taken advantage of. Try their homemade root beer for the kids.

name: Tyler Cunningham
text:
Potato "encrusted" halibut

This was a delicious dish despite the overcooked fish. But the thing that gets me about this dish is the wording. The menu claims potato encrusted, so I would assume the entire piece of fish would be wrapped in some sort of potato crust. Nope, my assumption is wrong.... What The Silver Gulch claims as a piece of encrusted fish is 4 very thinly sliced slivers of potatoes set on top of the fish. I would call this a garnish at best, but I'm not a chef at The Silver Gulch...

Im really big on misleading menus, simple words to describe a dish and yet something else is served to you. Just leads to a disappointing meal no matter how good it might be.

Beer is good, some very tasty appetizers as well... It's worth a trip to eat and drink though. But if I'm driving out this way it might as well be Turtle Club, best prim rib ever!

name: Olga Gold
text: First of all, take extra cloths, you might get wet:) I took my daughters to this gold panning facility. They had great experience. We were 4 including a 1.5 yo toddler girl. I didn't want to pan myself, but I didn't mind to get 3 bags of dirt, kids loved to do extra more gold densed dirt for panning :) We were taught how to pan and adviced first to practise with free dirt, which is a huge pile. The stuff was very attentive and kind. One of my daughters was less successful and seemed to lose interest, and thanks to one of the stuff members, she regained her confidence and managed to find enough golden flakes and even a nugget for her new gold locket and necklace. We spent 2 hours there, the time passed quickly . One of the girls , could hardly leave, she would stay much longer.  Overall we had positive experience. Thank you!

resp.text: Thank you so much for writing a detailed review of Gold Daughters! I'm thrilled to hear you and your family had a great time. Playing in the dirt while looking for (and finding) gold is addictive!

text: Great fun for all. The ladies who own and operate Gold Daughters are awesome. Lisa and Zoey were super helpful ensuring we find as much gold as possible. We found enough to make beautiful gold earrings for my daughter that same day. Again, very polite, helpful ladies. My 3 kids had a blast!!!

name: Amandeep Godara
text:
The Tanana Valley is a lowland region in central Alaska in the United States, on the north side of the Alaska Range where the Tanana River emerges from the mountains. Traditional inhabitants of the valley are Tanana Athabaskans of Alaskan Athabaskans.

The region experiences great extremes of temperature during the year. During the winter months, the air is prone to stratification due to temperature inversions, leading to thick fogs. During the summer, the surrounding plains are generally boglike, and include much permafrost and many pingos.

The Tanana Valley is the most populated area of Alaska north of the Alaska Range. Its largest city is Fairbanks.

According to James Q. Jacobs, Tanana Valley has the earliest evidence of human occupation in Alaska.

More recently, Tanana Valley sites have been dated to pre-Clovis period, or 13,000–14,000 cal yr BP.

The Broken Mammoth site, the Swan Point Archaeological Site, and the Mead Archaeological Site are the earliest dated sites in Alaska. They are located along the Tanana River.

name: Hugh Miller
text: One of our favorite spots in Anchorage. The staff is always friendly and helpful. The in house brews are fantastic. There's sure to be one for you, if not, they have a fully stocked bar. The food is equally impressive. Try the crab stuffed jalapenos! If you're really feeling Alaska try the various yak dishes they offer. 49th State should be on top of your list when visiting AK.

name: Elizabeth J
text: This place is great. The staff was friendly, the beer was great and the food was good as well. Oh and the view wasn’t bad either!

name: Kim P.
text:
We loved this place! We especially can’t wait to return when it’s warmer and can’t sit outside on the patio and see the view.
We ordered the Bavarian Pretzel for our appetizer and loved it! I ordered the king crab legs, while my husband ordered the crab grilled cheese, and we both said, we’d be coming back to try more dishes! Restaurant was clean, waitress was friendly, and food was great!

text: Great atmosphere and great staff.  The food was great.  Be careful of the caramel popcorn as it has a spicy kick to it that I did not know was there.   The Yak-a-dillas were very large and filling.

name: Ben Snellgrove
text: Incredible desserts, incredible brews, typically good service. Definitely a regular favorite due to their consistency. Amazing spot for evening drinks in the summer.

name: Tayler Burgess
text:
Under cooked (medium well came 80% pink), $25 Yak burger on a dry, crunch bun (see photo where I cut out a quarter and tried a bite).  Nope, not again.  Not their kitchen at least.  Beer is good though.  Reubens have been dry in the past, not the first burger I haven't enjoyed but the first one I've paid $25 for.  Wife's impossible burger didn't get labeled either. Kind of a deal for a vegetarian.

This is one man's opinion so please draw your own but I'll not be giving this kitchen any more chances.

name: bethany day
text: Amazing food. I got the halibut tacos, avacado fries and Brussels sprouts. Everything is amazingly good. However, be warned if you order the avacado fries they will only give you 6 fries for $10!!!!!!!!!! That seems pretty insane to charge that much for so little fries, but they are avacado after all..

name: Cindy Main
text: We thoroughly enjoyed ourselves. Marie was our server and she was awesome. She's on the ball. Food was amazing. My husband had the Halibut and fries. I had the chicken cobb salad which was huge and oh so delicious. We had the pretzel and Brussel sprouts for appetizers. The pretzel was huge and the sprouts were to die for. We highly recommend this place.

name: Jon Perry
text: Absolutely some of the best fare in Anchorage. Fresh seafood, pizza, American and continental cuisine. Generous cocktails, wine and craft brews. I first visited here about a year ago and it has only gotten better. Great prices and excellent service - thanks in part to Darrel and a team spirited crew.  Pictured are halibut tacos.. superb. For an appetizer sushi grade tuna and fried wanton chips and accoutrements of sauces and avocado with toasted sesame seeds. 49th State Brewing is a destination.

text: Food was excellent, service was a bit slow, but they are very clean and organized. Beer choices we great! Great views from the roof top

The crab grilled cheese was as good as it sounds, served with a delicious bowl of seafood chowder. The Parmesan and Asiago crusted halibut was cooked perfect and so full of flavor. Amazing meal.

text: The Christmas Market is intimate and fun. The vendors were friendly and hot apple cider was yummy.  Thanks 49th State Brewery for hosting this, looking forward to future events.

text:

Friendly service and a huge range of beers on tap. The popcorn also has its own spark with a balance between sweet and jalapeño heat - too good!

resp.text: That is a high compliment! We'll be sure to let the chef know. He put a lot of love into that recipe so your comments are really appreciated. Hope to see you again. name: Nancy Winters
text: I would highly recommend stopping by for a meal. Our server was Hallie B. she was outstanding! The food was amazing, everything we ordered was delicious. The views from the bar area were of the inlet and nice.

name: Terps Madison
text:
If you're a fan of local brews and food, this is a place to check out. The mac and cheese options are delightful, and always leave you with leftovers.
They have a great appetizer menu with options like a yakadilla, nachos, and even fried avocado.
A good place for tourists to check out while in town!

name: Jennifer Pittman
text: This is a great local place with a cool atmosphere, delicious food, awesome beer and scenic views in the summer off the rooftop patio.  The pretzel with beer cheese is superb and always draws me back.  I have to cheat on my low carb diet it’s that good!  It’s also a neat place to buy local gear from the gift shop to send to the craft brew loving family back in the lower 48.  Lastly, the event staff is awesome and took great care of my dental offices for our staff’s holiday party.  They were very accommodating for our vegan and gluten free guests also.

name: Robert Rago
text: The NY steak special was awesome. The beer cheese pretzel is an absolute must order every time!

name: Ka Vang
text: We had roof top dining and the experience was amazing. The waiters were great and knowledgeable, the view is a must-see and the food was delicious. I sat at the table not speaking to anyone but just enjoying the jalapeno poppers and my burger/fries. It's basic, but so good.

name: Sagar Bansal
text:
