text: Really good with maybe just a hair of hype. Their smoothies are excellent, though be warned you have a limited amount of time to drink them before their biodegradable straw disintegrates. Food is above average and likely the best brunch/breakfast in town, though it wouldn't be considered the best outside of Alaska. Service has always been excellent though.

name: N R
text: The stuffed French toast was awesome!! It was perfect balance, not overly sweet and lemon zest made it. The staff are extremely friendly and helpful. Will definitely be back!!

name: Ali zeee
text: Maybe I get the wrong stuff. Maybe I’m just not feeling the breakfast hype over expensive eggs. Either way, I’ve never been impressed by the food and Ive always been mega hungry when I get to sit down following a huge wait (avg 45min). Again, maybe I’ve been super unlucky the few times I’ve gone. Service is quite pathetic for price point. I honestly wouldn’t recommend. Breakfast shouldn’t be this complicated.

name: Angel Gonzales
text:
Snow City Cafe is hands down my favorite breakfast/brunch/lunch restaurant in town!!! Everything from the food, to the customer service is superb. My husband used to work here as a line cook, and they treat their employees like family. Also, because he worked there, I know how meticulously clean they are, and they will not serve a dish to a customer unless it is made right. If you don't want to sit and eat, you can order your food to go. Or you can just pick up a cup of coffee, smoothie, or pastry from the coffee stand. There is even a whole hot sauce bar for your spicy pleasure. Snow City merchandise and art by various artists are also available for purchase. It is definitely advised to reserve a table online prior to coming, to ensure you don't have a long wait time at this highly popular cafe.

They are also taking all of the COVID-19 precautions to keep their employees and customers safe. There are sanitation stations, masks, sanitation breaks, a side door for to go orders, and outdoor seating is an option.

name: Billy Ready
text: The wait was long, but it was really worth it! Coffee is great, food is tasty and the overall vibes of the cafe was chill. We will be going here again soon!

name: David Abram
text: Pretty nice breakfast. Good bacon, good options, I wish we could have eaten in the dining room (coronavirus).. La Marzocco espresso machine

name: Brenda Hill
text: They have a best of both eggs Benedict that is so good. Perfectly cooked eggs. I love this place.

name: Dale Moore
text: How can I tell about Snow City that hasn't already been mentioned? Definitely get a reservation because of the reduced seating or you'll have a long wait. It appreciated it very much. Parfait for yoghurt and granola is Fantastic. And if you just have to wake up then go to the Sludge Cup.

name: Maria Miller
text: I have waited for years to try the crab eggs benedict here! Reading reviews about how great it is. So finally today I got my chance to try it. Not that impressed! The person that brought it out could not tell me what kind of crab it was. Looked like tanner or snow crab. The crab was cold which then cooled the eggs and sauce. I wanted it at least warm. Would have told the waiter, but he didn't come back to see if everything was ok. The hashbrowns were so crusted on the bottom I could not cut them with a knife. Not what I was expecting. Kinda bummed. Waited 20 minutes to get a table for 1. Good atmosphere. Good music playing. My breve was awesome!

name: Mat Pyles
text: Great food and drinks the staff was so nice to me and my wife ☺

name: Paul Sokolowski
text: Great place to eat not overpriced for the area at least when we were there.

name: Todd Adams
text: I had heard about this place and finally was able to go and try their food. Great, friendly staff with delicious and good portions. It was a great experience over all. Im glad I gave them another shot. There isn't a wait all the time. Even if there was, its worth it.

name: David Maddison
text: I could not fault the service here! Great recommendations from the waitress and found the crab and salmon patties with hollendaise sauce to die for! The eggs were perfect and the sauce has that right amount of tang. Get in early to avoid the queues because this place fills up quickly and early!

name: Aurora A
text: Lovely spot downtown. Only downside is how quickly they get packed with people. Hope they do alright through all of this.

name: Renee Tatusko
text: Food is always good.  And I love when Emily waits on me.... she's such a sweetheart.

name: Sarah Dalarah
text: Delicious food! I cant wait to eat here more. Food was perfect, and the service was friendly.   This place is amazing. So flavorful. Loved their lavender coffee.

name: sylvester sanchez
text: Great place with great staff. It can be busy, best time is always early in the work week. Parking can be rough and dont forget to pay as I was warned the parking meters are well watched. Food is amazing, great Eggs Benedict with many options.

name: Sephora Allen
text: Nothing short of amazing! The food and service was great, one of my husband and I favorite spots in Anchorage now. Try their Royal Mimosas!

name: Nancy Widjaja
text: Love the Salmon Egg Benedict (Ship creek benedict) the most, but the rest of the foods are tasty as well. Fast & quick service. The weekend wait was too long and limited available reservations that we came back on weekday with reservation. Definitely need to reserve earlier & even so you may not get to be seated right away.

name: Matthew Ray
text: Food was nice but it felt very rushed. We had to wait outside for 30 minutes when the waiting area was empty. They seemed a little overwhelmed and stressed out.

name: Richard beck
text: Food was excellent. The raspberry dream was delicious.

name: Duke of Curb
text: I ate here for lunch one time, I did not enjoy it enough to go back. The food was ok not good just ok. There is a place across the street way better, and behind it is another place that over shadows the food here.

name: Vinny Valosky
text: They offer a great menu and delicious options. The amount of delicious coffees and lattes they have is also impressive. The staff is great and they always have some awesome recommendations. Even if I have a short stay in anchorage I make it a priority to come here. Also, if you catch them on turkey chili day you definitely need to give it a try. Snow city cafe is wonderful and worth it!

name: Lee Anne Roquemore
text:
Excellent!!! Had the eggs benedict on biscuits. Delicious! Super friendly staff, great service, minimal wait time.

My 9 year old says, “6 out of 5 stars.”

name: Brian Bowen
text: Everything looked so good as I watched food coming out for the other customers. It was hard to choose with all the great options. I ended up going with the Cowboy Meatloaf sandwich. It had a very generous portion of meat loaf and thick cut bacon. I substituted the rye bread for sourdough and it was so good. The pecan sticky roll... again, so good.  The staff were all very friendly making it a great experience.

name: Alexander
text: One of the best meals I had in Anchorage so far, amazing quiche and crab cakes. Loved the bacon and syrup as well from the meal. Had the root beer float as well.

name: beau mccay
text: Stopped in for breakfast. Food was very good and reasonably priced. Ordered a steak breakfast. It was tender and well seasoned.

name: Abigail Black
text: Spectacular place to start your day! I love their breakfast foods. The staff assisted me very well!

name: Shawn Tu
text: Great food, great atmosphere, excellent staff, quirky hot sauce bar where they have a selection of, you guessed it, hot sauces to choose from. Biscuits and gravy are phenomenal and the Kodiak scramble was delicious!

name: Brian Boehringer
text: Coffee was really good and stuffed french toast was well balanced with sweet and tart raspberry flavor. Also got the "deadliest catch" benedict, which left something to be desired. Both eggs weren't runny, and the crab and salmon cakes weren't very good

name: Mel G
text: Amazing breakfast food and super cute restaurant with great ambiance! The stuffed French toast with orange cream cheese and raspberry butter are O.M.G.😳 and the reindeer sausage! YUM!! And the coffee mugs are nice and big. Have ordered the Polar Bear breakfast to go as well and it was just as good as dining in!!

name: Melody Willis
text: This place is so goooddddd. Their breakfast and coffee is amazing!

name: Drew Raught
text: Breakfast, Lunch, and Dinner. Excellent Cafe style food! Grab a cup of coffee or custom esspresso from the coffee bar while you wait to be seated. The wait is decent at times, but as expected for a must visit restaurant.

name: Andrew Elegante
text:
Pretty good food,  service started off slow but got better. It's very popular so expect a wait. The have a way to reserve a table online. I suggest looking into that if you have a big party.

I had the deadliest catch Benedict and their snow City (white chocolate & vanilla) mocha. The mocha was good, not particularly memorable. The deadliest catch is a salmon cake Benedict and a crab cake Benedict. The crab one was very good. Muffin was very flavorful. Benedict sauce was like the mocha, good but not memorable.

I didn't care for the salmon cake. It had a gritty texture to it and the flavor was so so. I am not a huge fan of salmon so that may be why I didn't enjoy it as much as the crab.

name: Ivone Sanchez
text: Another fabulous breakfast. They never disappoint me. And the service is wonderful

name: Ken Rowlan
text: Super long wait but the food was amazing! Had some smoothies, eggs benedict, turkey melt, and a BLTA. Everything was awesome. Service was great too.

name: Drea Jo
text: Great coffee.. Consistently great food. Casual atmosphere. Lovely. She asked that her hash browns were well cooked.  Curry carrot soup. Loved it

name: Ed Blocker
text: Food was pretty good, espressos were good, prices were within reason, service was very poor! They seemed to be short staffed in the kitchen causing most orders to take about 45 minutes to be cooked then the staff managing the "to go" window allowed orders to sit on their racks, getting cold, before calling the customer to get their order. Very poor operations, regardless of the COVID-19 restrictions.

resp.text:
Thank you for your feedback, Ed. It's very helpful to hear from guests during this unusual time. We make frequent changes to operations as things change due to COVID requirements, and we will keep working on perfecting our systems so situations like you mention don't occur again
. We're sorry that your experience with us was less than perfect, and we hope that you'll give us a chance to make it up to you!

name: Mike Stevenson
text: Out of the 9 days we were in Anchorage we ate their every morning on or first two times we made the trip we tried a lot of decent places but nothing came close to Snow City.

name: Louis
text: I loved the atmosphere and music they played. The wait to be seated was reasonable and I loved that you could get a cup of coffee while you waited. The wait for food was a little bit long, but the service was excellent. The food was delicious! If we are ever in Anchorage again, we will be coming back.

name: Emery Omiak
text: I tried the Country Meatloaf and it was great, even though it came as a sandwich.  My wife loved the Bacon Burger and Tomato Soup, tried a spoonful of the soup myself and it was as great as my wife it was.  Highly recommend when given the chance

name: Zakary Hartford
text:
Food was amazing!
The COVID mitigations were easy to navigate and the service was friendly. Definitely will come back!

name: Trevor Williams
text: Busy breakfast spot downtown. Didn't wait to terribly long on a Saturday morning. Pricey and nothing to write home about. French toast, stuffed or not was regrettable. Should of tried the eggs benedict...most likely won't return to try it with plenty of other places to try.

name: Bryon Skiver
text: A great place to go. People treat you right.

name: Niki Scott
text: Great hot beverages and food! The breakfast burrito hit the spot with the green chili being mildly spicy with good flavor. Don't expect a smothered green chili burrito from NM but this one here is pretty darn tasty for an Alaskan version. Excellent service with a pleasant atmosphere.

name: Kelsey Allrich
text: Great food. Pricey.

name: Stanley H.
text: We had a excellent breakfast here, great tasting omelettes and egg Benedict’s. Outdoors eating or take out, we had a 15 minute wait when we went. There is one small covered area, we got lucky to get it and it started to rain out.

name: Margaret Sales
text: Soup was tasty, smoothie was nice, service was good, friendly atmosphere. Went in close to closing time, felt welcome.

name: Chelsey Curry
text:
Very busy place, i reccomend getting a reservation
Food was good, hashbrowns are amazing

name: Neil Gillian
text: The Deadliest Catch was super delightful. The service our waiter provided was very well mannered and did not rush us. Anytime I have went there I have never been disappointed. Food and service is unbeatable. I can only imagine if they had a dinner menu. Thank you to snow city cafe.

name: Fabiana Kirtley
text: My number one favorite breakfast restaurant in Anchorage. Their food is absolutely wonderful! I ordered a wild mushroom burger with a side of rye toast and my husband a burrito. A few other dishes to try are the stuffed French toast, their huge pancakes and their cinnamon rolls!

name: Vicente Panizo
text: Best breakfast in Alaska! Great service and food options.  The staff is superb and the atmosphere is awesome. You doesn’t like waking up to 80’s 🎶 😎

name: Alexis Fay
text: Cute breakfast/lunch place with delicious food. The place can get packed, even on a weekday. They have a coffee stand where you can annoy coffee while you wait for a table which is nice. It’s downtown so free parking can be tricky.

name: Kahdija Imari
text: Very very crowded establishment. The Marionberry jam is tasty. The quiche of the day was quite delicious as well.

name: Alexia Hines
text: I had the opportunity of dining here thanks to some suggestions from my Alaskan friends. An adorable cafe located on a street corner in downtown Anchorage with a charming and colorful interior. There is plenty of seating (and plenty of spacing - thanks COVID). I got a good, hot coffee with cream to sip on while waiting for my Stuffed French Toast. When my French toast arrived it was like looking at a masterpiece. The portion is definitely worth the $$$ and soooooo tasty. The dish itself is not very sweet so if you're less of a sweet tooth this is still a good option. The raspberry butter is a nice touch and brings more freshness to the dish. I really enjoyed every aspect of my time here and would definitely come back. 💜

name: Allen
text: Selena took care of my BREAKFAST desires CONSCIENTIOUSLY.. Yummy Chuck Norris special.

name: Alex Statz
text: The one thing that I love most about this place is it's consistency. Snow City has yet to disappoint me in any shape or form. Love coming here for breakfast!

name: Cara H.
text: Awesome food and friendly service.  No free parking close by.  Call to make a reservation.  Queue could be long during peak hours.  They have all natural smoothies without sweeteners or ice.  Great for breakfast, brunch or lunch.  They have packed salads and freshly baked goodies.  Tried their cream cheese brownie--heavenly 😁

name: Landon Bell
text: Amazing breakfast spot.

name: Julieta Mendez
text: Perfect place for a great brunch with friends! The food is amazing and the service is great! It's a very homey diner and a local hot spot.

name: LeeAnna Bohnert
text: Extremely disappointed. Only good thing I can say is our server was good. Food was so bland it was ridiculous. 1 biscuit and gravy was $8 it was seriously so bland. Husband got the Polar Bear breakfast, reindeer sausage was OK a little spice to it, but the French toast tasted like just plain toast? He paid the extra $1 for "real" maple syrup, which definitely didn't taste real to us, and was super runny. Coffee was blah too. Overall seems to be just an overpriced tourist trap and we will not be back. So disappointing!

name: Patrick Newman
text: Great good and great service

name: Deon Oakley
text: Waited over 45 minutes for an order that got missed and wouldn't have known if I hadn't called this happens alot this needs to be addressed!!!!!!

name: Joshua Dobson
text: Breakfast burrito was good, could hardly taste the chorizo though.

name: Semian Arquette
text: I came here with my two sisters. One of which came with me to Alaska to cost the other. Tonight is our last night but I had to write this review... THIS PLACE IS UTTERLY AMAZING!! From the time you walk in you are greeted with warmth, our waitress was so kind and funny. The artwork on the walls was beautiful and THE FOOD WAS AWESOME! yes I just screamed because I’m still drooling. It’s a bit pricey but I don’t even care! I need all of their food in and around my mouth! I wish I could put you guys in my pocket and take you back to Virginia Beach. Thank you for an amazing experience!

name: Agnes Lawson
text: Delicious food! Great gluten free and vegan options plus also food options that are neither. But the GF and V options are so tasty it caters to those who don't normally look for that. Friendly quick service. There was a 30 minute wait for a table because it was a busy Saturday morning but there was water and coffee to sip while waiting. It's an easy walk from 5th Ave Mall with a lot of cute shops to window shop on the way.

name: Eric Collier
text: Just a run of the mill breakfast. Honestly could have gotten the same quality of food at Denny's. Very packed on a Saturday morning. Wait staff was overwhelmed. This is evident in the 20 minutes we sat at the table before we asked if someone was going to take our order. Food was hot and fresh. Took another 20 minutes for us to get our check after we had finished eating. For a place that is trying to move customers in and out of the door, you wouldn't know it.

name: Michael Forte
text: What a great breakfast joint! I had the stuffed French toast, the raspberry butter is really great!

name: Ralph Segock
text: Excellent service, caring people no matter what race you are, and very prompt!

name: Bob Chan
text: The restaurant is extremely hip! During brunch hours there's usually a relatively long wait so make sure you call ahead to reserve a seat. There's a good amount of families that eat their morning brunch there. The only reason why I don't have this restaurant as five stars is that the menu is kind of expensive.

name: Christopher Gibson
text: Delicious food, quick and quality service. Get any of the scrambles.

name: Ryan Mirl
text: Visited on a Sunday morning before 8 and we were sat immediately. The service was great and the food came out quickly. I had the Kodiak Benedict and it was fantastic. By the time we left the place was packed with a line waiting to be sat. Really enjoyed this place and would definitely visit again.

name: biggbran77
text: A bit of a wait to get in but the food was good and the staff was friendly. Has a very hospitable atmosphere.

name: Heven Demo
text: I love the tomato soup so much. Next time I'm taking photos. I was so hungry this morning I just dug in. Just trust me on this place being worth it. It's always packed so it's good to reserve or the wait will take a bit. Their coffees are good, and cocktails. So frickin good.

name: Iryna Tsyngalova
text: Seems like the usual wait is about one hour but  worth it! The food is amazing, stuff members are friendly and nice.

name: D Ro
text: Friendly staff, fast service, awesome food, and good coffee. Get there early to avoid the wait!

name: haylee hays
text: Best hash browns.... And literally their eggs Benedict is to die for, I mean all of them. I always get a side of country gravy as well just to add a little zazzz to them. So yummy!

name: Andrea Fergus
text: Excellent breakfast place. Can expect a delay at certain times, but the food makes it worth it. They do take reservations, next time I will make them. I had the breakfast burrito smothered with a green chile sauce. Made my nose run. My husband had an eggs Benedict with a crab cake and a salmon cake. The salmon cake was better, but he enjoyed them both.

name: ohmyheck31
text: We waited 60 MINUTES to be seated on a Friday! Our server was very nice, but the meal was not. My Ship Creek Benedict of smoked salmon cakes was very fishy and not very good. There was no smokiness, needed more hollandaise, and I put a lot of hot sauce to try to make it better, something I don't do. I was sorry to have ordered it. My husband's Wild Mushroom Omelet seemed to be made with regular mushrooms and the amount of garlic overpowered the experience. Also, he doesn't like garlic, so it ruined it for him, too. There was less tea than in a store-bought teabag in both of our cups, so they were very weak. Our favorite part of the meal was the sourdough bread (not really toasted, so not really Toast) with raspberry jam. Very disappointing and in no hurry to go back.

name: Katherine Lewis
text: One of the best breakfast places in Anchorage! Their food is fantastic and well worth the wait. I recommend making reservations when possible because it's no secret that their food is so good

name: Pudu Creative
text: Have had breakfast here twice and both times everything tasted great. Service is fine, but parking can be hard to come by and wait times can be long during breakfast/brunch hours. I have recommended this place to visiting friends and family and they all have had good experiences. This place is a safe bet for an  above average meal at a fair price.

name: Yeva S-yan
text: Delicious food 😋

name: Caity Madskills Weld Inspection
text: Crispy hashbrowns and crab cake benedict!

name: Ashley Godbold
text: Gluten free sandwiches are delicious! The tomato soup is also good but the best thing is the customer service 💯 outstanding! Great experience

name: Cheryl Dilgard
text: Loved it! My daughter picked our breakfast spot and it was amazing! The food and service was great. Filled with locals, this little beauty had some thing for everyone.  Great coffees and coffee drinks as well as chai. The monkey bread looked amazing but in an effort to fit into my jeans, i went with the harvest hash and fried egg, my daughter had the spicy green chili breakfast burrito.  We left stuffed! Great experience...i will be back.

name: Blair G
text: Fantastic food and service

name: Xavier Orozco
text: Best biscuits and gravy in Anchorage. The bacon strips are perfection as well.

name: Robert Kaleak
text: Great coffee and great breakfast. Have to pay for parking tho

name: Israel Siria
text:
We wanted to check why the buzz about this place. The waiting time was 1 hour and 15 minutes, too long for me but we found something else to do meanwhile.
Once was our turn we were very pleased with the food and good service. Definitely one of the best places in Anchorage to have brunch.

name: david webb
text: Delicious vegan scramble and excellent service as usual.

name: chelbie garcia
text: Very good food, great art and excellent customer service. The pecan sticky buns are a MUST!

name: Annie Bi
text: The vibe of this place is so colorful and busy, which is fun. We went for lunch to-go, and had about a 30 minute wait for the food. They have a nice bench set-up outside which is nice. We got the Fourth Avenue Special sandwich, fiesta and Mediterranean bowls, and the Impossible cheeseburger. The Impossible burger didn't taste like meat, but it was good. I also loved the Mediterranean bowl. The fiesta bowl was a bit too spicy for me though.

name: Kris Anderson
text: Very good food and drink. Excellent service.

name: JT Stanley
text: Very good breakfast. Probably the best “modern breakfast” in Anchorage. By modern I mean not exactly old fashion, home style cookin’. Everything on the menu is amazing. Smoothies are expensive but very filling and it makes me feel healthy so I get one occasionally. Hollandaise is on point. Make reservations or come early and be patient. This place is BUSY.

name: Izaak Philip Bruce
text: Great place for breakfast food. The omelettes and hash browns are excellent.

name: Carolyn
text: As good as snow city cafe you have to be prepared to wait. We always are but not like today! 1 3/4 hours to wait for a table for seven is ridiculous! Poor organization, continually seating smaller groups of 4 or 2 is no excuse! We had one person to had to leave and skip lunch or maybe call it early dinner! It will be a long time before I go back to Snow City Cafe and even longer before I recommend it! Service was good, food was alright.

name: Colin Martin
text: Make a reservation or expect to wait for a table. Consistently busy tourist spot. Excellent food and coffee. Never had a bad meal, just would never show without a reservation. Stays busy winter and summer. Limited street parking.

name: Tyler David
text: Fantastic breakfast options... You can't really pick something wrong here. Gigantic pancakes and french toast is amazing. They're both served with some great raspberry butter, which i find that i can't live without now. Every time that i have went the service has been wonderful and the people very friendly, even when it's jam packed and they gotta be fast, they still make you feel welcome.  The wait is long, but take a walk around the area and it's not too bad. 👍👍

name: Casey Tobia
text: Service was poor...ended up leaving... hopefully service will be better if and when I try it again...

name: Shopping Bag
text: Locals know: this is one of the best breakfast joints in the city. They also know: don’t try to get a seat during the rush of tourist season! Simple American breakfast done right, and a decent lunch menu.

name: Chris Bering
text: Be ready for a wait. But boy is it worth it! Great food, great staff, great atmosphere! The hash browns are so fantastic! Highly recommended!

name: Molly Woo
text: Very busy in the morning, average waiting time is about 20 minutes or more for table. Try to seat in the bar if not large group, usually no wait.

resp.text:
Hi Lola,

Skip the wait by making a reservation at snowcitycafe.com or calling us at (907) 272-2489!

See you soon!

name: Josh M
text: Make a reservation and be prepared to still wait for a table. It’s a formality. Otherwise, I’ve never had anything I didn’t like. Great food and drinks.

name: Lyn Schrader
text:
Oh heck, this place is to die for! Anything and everything is superior and so worth the wait. They even provide self serve coffee while waiting.
Just go.
There will only be happiness, as a result

name: Ty Jun
text: Best breakfast joint ever! Great pancakes, eggs, an bacon! Good service and they kept my coffee full

name: A Male From Day 1
text: Great food always crowded

name: Sarah Allyn
text: Lots of wonderful eggs Benny options! Plus free refills on organic drip coffee.

name: Darwin Feakes
text: Known for it's breakfast mine eggs benidict with crab cakes was great. Highly recommend.  Also not a long wait to get in when I went.

name: Dewitt Mcnutt
text: First, and foremost, make an online reservation. Otherwise, you will wait for an undetermined time. Even a resident didn't know you could make reservations. He and his family have always shown up and waited. Street parking is limited. There is a lot across the street that requires a credit/debit card to park. It was $6 for the 1st hour. Now about the food. It was very good, and you won't go home hungry. Their pancakes are larger than the plate. There is a great selection of foods. Note: They are only open for breakfast and lunch. Plan accordingly. And I recommend starting with a homemade cinnamon roll with their cream cheese icing. Consider sharing or save for later. Btw, I am not a coffee drinker (don't judge). They have a coffee and espresso bar with some baked goods for there or to go.

name: Daniel Grimes
text: Snow City Cafe is packed every morning for a reason! Quality food, plenty of it, unique dishes, healthy choices, fantastic wait staff, and the time it takes to get your meal is blazing fast! Unlike a lot of breakfast spots, they do take reservations, so it is worth calling ahead if you can. When they are slammed, they reserve rhe right to bump your party if you aren't all there when your seating is called. Give them a try, their tater tot quiche is ridiculously good, as are any of the eggs benny options❤

name: JMark Johnson
text:
My wife and I had been trying to come here for a few years. Every time we try and come it's always busy always with a ridiculous wait time. The one time we actually come the food was cold, and people that had arrived well after our orders where taken, got their food first. And $3 for a small childs juice is asinine!!
My first time will be my last time.
Thoroughly disappointed.

name: Sherman Sabie Jr
text: HELLO, number one breakfast spot during our short week stay. Place booming with smiling, satisfied customers and happy serving staff. Breakfast Menu filled with great, hard-to-choose-from meals, it all hit the right tastebuds just looking at the menu. Wished I could have fit most of it in. Crab benedict was awesome. So was French Toast.

name: Cody Eagle
text: Amazing place for breakfast I would definitely recommend this place the food is great and the location is easy to find

name: Olga Moza
text: Great place with awesome breakfast! We had a Family breakfast before some of us headed to airport. Very fast service. But very loud place. Be ready not to be able to hear person in front of you.

name: Chris Jones
text: Amazing place with delicious food. Super busy, so be prepared for a wait time unless you make a reservation.

name: Michelle Mitton
text: Delicious food and I'd highly recommend, though expect to wait, it's a popular place.

name: Hugh Perry
text: The food at Snow City is awesome! I had the wild mushroom omelet and hashbrowns. Delicious! The hashbrowns are the best I have ever had!

name: Pink Anderson
text: Based on reviews, I am sure it is a great place.  However, I may never know.  They accepted my reservation and even sent me a confirmation for date and time.  Guess what...they weren't even open on the 4th, the date I scheduled.  Disappointing way to start the holiday weekend.  I hope they fix this on their system.

name: bublehed
text: Great place for breakfast with a large selection

name: Krissy Redwine
text: Nice building, very busy expect to wait about an hour. Coffee pots, sugar, variety of different milks and creams available for you  while you wait (bring coffee with you when you're seated, waitress will add to your bill).Lots of Benedict choices including crab and salmon looked great. Reindeer sausage best my husband had this week. I ordered polar bear breakfast with multigrain French toast, bacon, eggs and add  blueberries for a dollar, it was surprisingly tasty !

name: nt. Templin
text: Always tasty!😋

name: Daniel WInters
text: Friendly staff, love the food. Great for when you have business at the Court House.

name: Brett Kirk
text: Yum. Yum and Yum. Eggs Benedict was great. Enjoyed every bite. Hollandaise was perfect. Coffee was HOT! Just the way I enjoy it.

name: Ralph Barnette
text: Friendly staff and excellent food

name: Vincent Rogan
text: Not much parking

name: K.
text: delicious!

name: Project Cosplay
text: It's great! There is most likely going to be a line of people but that's because the food is so good! Prices are also very reasonable! I love it. 💜💜💜💜

name: Madison Clark
text: Yummy food! The wait is always worth it! Creative rotating drinks!

name: David Sanders
text: As a former employee, I would highly recommend this place as a "must see" for anyone visiting Anchorage. Good food, great service! Vegetarian, and vegan dishes available. Also, the building across from this restaurant is  the site of the only "car bombing" in Anchorage that I can think of.

name: Racahael Lowe
text: Good food, friendly staff

name: Jeff Hamilton
text: The food was fantastic.  I had the apple pancakes and they may have been the best pancakes I've ever eaten.  I just wonder if they've become too popular for their own good.  I asked the server if they had blueberry muffins, and was told that it would take him 10 minutes to walk back there and find out, otherwise I could walk up to the counter and look for myself.  My buddy was waiting for a coffee refill; eventually he left the table and walked up to the self-serve coffee station near the front door.  I would go back again, but only if I had made a reservation so that I wouldn't have to wait an hour.

name: Richard Eaton
text: Did not think it was very good for the hype. Flo's pancake house or the noisy goose is way better.

name: Kateri Candee
text: This is a must if you are in town. There is always a wait, but completely worth it. Service was great. Food was amazing.

name: Zeke Hilsinger
text: I've been going here for 15-20 years and the food is always amazing but the service is always horrible nobody acknowledges you and they all seem a little bit irritated.

resp.text: Hi Zeke, thank you for sharing your feedback. It has been shared with our management team. We are sorry to hear that you have not had good experiences with our staff. We have a great team, some of whom have worked with us for years. We have high standards for service, and to hear that we haven't met them is disappointing. We try to do our best, but certainly there are times when we miss the mark. Please continue to let us know when we fall short, and we will keep working on bringing our smiles, friendliness and great service to our guests. We take guest's reviews and comment to heart, and we appreciate your business.

name: M Croz
text: Great food, but long wait times to get a table.

name: Sharolyn Wyeth
text: Love Snow City in the winter. Lines are stupid, during tourist season, but things are back to normal now. The food is always consistent, the service is always good, and the coffee is always fresh. The crabby omelet is my favorite & they have the best hash browns in town!

name: Zahby Ellis
text: Genius waiter upsold my husband a $10 pancake. I thought it was hilarious

name: Jill Moody
text: Love their food! We go for breakfast most of the time. Stuffed French toast, or build your own omelet...oh yes please!

name: Julie Cresap
text: Good food and service. Make a reservation to get in faster during lunch. :)

name: Staci Duquet
text: One of the best breakfast places in town but make sure to get there a little early on the weekends because there will be a bit of a wait. One of the things I love is you can order from the bakery while you wait and they have self serve coffee too! Love this place.

name: Wayne Paliwoda
text:
The ambiance was one of the most welcoming that I have experienced since I moved to Anchorage. It was busy, but the waiting area has plenty of space and self serve coffee.

I had the deadliest catch and it was delicious, especially the salmon.  The service was perfect and they even offered a to-go coffee!! I will definitely be back.

name: L B
text: Crowded on Saturday before Halloween. 45 minute wait. Cheerful crowd. Creative, flexible menu. NICE food! Attentive service. We'll be back.

name: Cami Pena
text:
Thank goodness for being able to make reservations online! The wait is a little rough but I can see why. The atmosphere, the customer service the decor ... a great place! I had the B.O.B. eggs Benedict with a pomegranate mimosa and j tried a grapefruit one - yum!! I've has their stuffed French toast before too and that was the best I've ever had.
Such a fun spot!

name: D
text: Nice spot to go to for breakfast. I always like how they change up the art on the walls which are created by locals. The atmosphere is welcoming and laid back. Their pancakes are huge but well worth the price. Definitely like going there every now and then.

name: Conce Rock
text:
Very popular eatery in Anchorage. As my friend from LA describes it, "a place for hipsters". I still feel it's more of a "granola" hangout, healthy food with an in vogue twist. Come early for all meal times, or be prepared for a wait. Most costumers are willing to do some.

Today we had 4 person's for breakfast. One had eggs and hash. The hash was yummy, including turnips and parsnips with the usual potatoes and nicely flavored corned beef.

Two had Benedicts, one regular with Canadian bacon, the other with salmon cakes. The poached eggs were perfectly cooked, (drained of all cooking water). The salmon cakes were tasty; I'm guessing Pink Salmon, rather than my favorite Sockeye. The Hollandaise was excellent, smooth and even, no separation.

The fourth had the Polar Bear Breakfast: a pair of eggs, Black Forest Ham, and French Toast. Ham & eggs were fine, but the French Toast were overly chewy. I think they used sour dough bread and not enough egg dip. Each of us tried the French Toast, but none of us liked it. The server was kind enough to give us a break on the cost of the French Toast without us mentioning it. For the most part, we were very satisfied.

I've eaten here a number of times, usually breakfast or lunch, and we've generally enjoyed the meals. Services is always friendly and efficient regardless of the crowd!

name: Landis Loftin
text: Good food and a busy brunch crowd made this a fun place to have some tasty eats. Portions were large and food was comfort style. An Anchorage institution.

name: Tim Mathews
text: This place is so dang good.  I ate so much there.  Its really good for vegetarians or other diet restrictions.  Great place to eat and hang out.

name: Priscilla Velarde
text: The food was good but not anything to run and tell your people about.  They have bar seating is first come first serve and with the wait being 35 minutes it made it really handy. They also have a coffee bar where you can order drinks to go. I ordered a latte while I waited to be seated.

name: David Harper
text: We went here based on all of the positive feedback and awards. When we arrived at 10:30 AM we were told it would be over an hour wait. We decided since we had time to go ahead and wait. We went for a walk around while waiting. It ended up being about an hour and 15 minutes wait. Once we were seated we waited about 10 minutes to be waited on and another 30 before the food came. The waiter was very nice and took off the charge for the coffee (without any comment from us) due to noting the long wait for us to get our food. The food was great - I had the deadliest catch which included a crab Benedict and a salmon cake Benedict with a side of reindeer sausage. My wife had the crab Benedict. We both loved the food and the coffee was also quite good. Prices are a little high. this place would be so much better if they added some staff and put in a few more tables by removing some of the wasted space in the restaurant. I would recommend this place with the caveat that you need a lot of time, or put in a reservation as for us - breakfast ended up being lunch at about 1:30 by the time all was said and done.

name: Julia Spehalski
text: Delicious stuffed French toast!

name: Nancy Minnick
text: Delicious food in casual neighborhood atmosphere. Good sandwich and soup place

name: Austyn Vaona
text: The salmon cake Benedict was amazing and was definitely a great first meal in Alaska

name: Diego Rodriguez
text: This is a regular go-to place for me. They have so many tempting options and good vegan choices too. The blueberry coconut latte was delicious, I hope they make it part of the regular menu. YUM!

name: C Lippert
text: Short wait, wonderful waitress excellent food.

name: Carl Davis
text:
First time going and thought was pretty good. Giving four stars instead of five because after a 40 minute wait to get seated it took another 20 minutes or so before we were approached by a waitress and that was after we had to flag one down.

The food was very good and the serving was very large but the long wait on both accounts (before being seated and after) put a damper on things. Still recommend giving it a try.

name: CHERYL Bowlin
text: Great menu and food, very popular place. Always seems to be waiting line for tables. Good protein smoothies. Cheerful service.

name: Boogles Johnson
text: We had about a 20 min wait, it was nice to get a cup of coffee while waiting.  The food was worth the wait.  I had "deadliest catch" Benedict and it superb!

name: Lori Salyers
text: Yummy stuffed French toast!

name: Nathanael Kupczyk-Gregory
text: Our favorite place to eat when in town. Great service and delicious food. Gluten free options on the menu. Never had a bad experience.

name: Justin Knowlton
text: We went in early April around 10:30 am on a Monday and had to wait 15 minutes for a table. But it was worth the wait. The stuffed French toast is heavenly but very rich. We also had a breakfast burrito that was really tasty, and full of good things. Most of the wait staff were very friendly.

name: Nickolas Warner
text: Snow city is an anchorage institution but not exactly for that good of a reason. They’re food is fine, but more like upscale diner food than anything else. All three times I’ve eaten here my hash browns weren’t crisp and the omelettes completely dry on the inside. The prices are also very high for what you get. Unfortunately there’s not much else in Anchorage so you might as well eat here anyways.

name: George Case
text: A cafe that also serves high-quality breakfast meals. Make a reservation or be prepared to wait a while unless you're just getting coffee!

name: Elizabeth Dostert
text: Not too much to say except I was bummed out it was closed on this holiday when my mama and I wanted to eat brunch!

name: Susian P
text: Cozy. Good food. Great service!

name: Angeline Bigley
text: Food and service cant be beat

name: Boyd Soule
text: Nothing worth waiting 45+ min for. The food was ok but I felt it was similar to Village Inn. The waitress was amazing and very friendly and I got a hot chocolate while sitting there for a table and it was amazing. I would not recommend this place to my friends for brunch as I feel there are many other options with better food and no wait time.

name: Brianne Belford
text: Stumbled into this place for breakfast.  The service and food here are excellent!  Ended up coming back for breakfast the next morning as well!

name: Reyna R. Tapia
text: Servers here are amazing. Very patient and willing to work with dietary restrictions. Some good options if you're on a vegan options

name: John T
text: AMAZING!!! All the egg Benedict’s are incredible. Great coffee options too.  Our favorite breakfast place in Anchorage. But make reservations or you will be waiting outside for a hour. That is how good this place is. Great atmosphere too! Highly recommend Snow City Cafe.

name: Troy Turner
text: Great place to eat.  I would definitely go back!  Their omelets are out of this world!

name: Erin Michele Reese
text: I love this place! Great food, lots of fresh options, gluten free, & vegan too. Employees are friendly and helpful. I wish the prices were a little lower, but it is local so I don't mind so much.

name: Ana Owczarzak
text: Excellent food and beat value in Anchorage! Had a bit of a wait but enjoyed the coffee bar before being seated. Enjoyed salmon cakes and a breakfast biscuit sandwich for under $30 which was probably the cheapest meal our entire visit to Alaska and the flavors we're phenomenal. Highly recommend, totally worth the wait!

name: Dan Apsley
text: Skip this place and go to the taco stand across the street. Snow city was a 45min wait to eat something that tasted like a Costco re-heat item. The taco stand was less than half that for some legit Alaskan styled huevos rancheros and breakfast tacos.

resp.text:
Hi Dan,

I am sorry to hear you had a disappointing visit with us. I would love to hear a bit more about your experience. We take feedback seriously and use it as an opportunity to improve. Would you mind emailing me directly at kathleen@snowcitycafe.com to give me a few more details so I can follow up with my team?

Hope to hear from you soon,

Kate Boyd
General Manager
Snow City Cafe

name: Randy
text: Very impressive. Well worth the wait.

name: Nathan Elliott
text: The menu is a bit "new age", so may not be everyone's cup of tea. The restaurant is clean, and service was very good. I enjoyed my meal and would visit again.

name: Jack Albrecht
text: Cool atmosphere and good food.

name: David Brown
text: Go for the eggs Benedict. You'll be surprised at how good they are. I dont usually get them, but they were great. Get a big pancake on the side too.

name: Tom and Roberta Hurt
text:
Very bad chai latte.  Please try another brand, BIG TRAIN is yummy.
Friendly service, though.

name: Kenneth Scherer
text: I got the crab and salmon benedict, and they were both amazing. There is a large coffee selection, and it is great. It may be a long wait at times, but the staff and kitchen are quick and very friendly.

name: Dakotah Steele
text: Pretty sweet hippster breakfast spot. Probably the best breakfast spot in Anchorage. I recommend the stuffed french toast and raspberry cream coffee

name: DL Hereford
text: Excellent, original and eclectic Alaskan menu. Downtown and great for visitors!

name: David Stock
text: Big portions and very tasty food. Staff was great and quick. This place is always packed if you don't want to wait make a reservation.

name: Paul Allen
text: Very busy and popular. Food good. Waiting 40 minutes to get a table.

name: Michelle Miller
text: The food is fantastic. Maybe the best bacon I have ever tasted. Five of us ordered eggs 5 different ways and all were cooked to perfection. My breve was so yumny. Service was equally good. If you need to wait for for a table I promise it's completely worth it. Our only complaint was the music was too loud. It was difficult to converse.

name: Eric Cardozo
text: No matter what time of day be prepared to wait at least 20 minutes. That being said, the food is fantastic. The service staff is usually running around and might be hard to track down due to the high number of customers, but in my opinion the food is worth it. You can't go wrong with any of their breakfast items, but I personally recommend the meatloaf and mac and cheese.

name: Sara Tall
text: Snow City is great!  There's something for everyone:  people who love a traditional plate of eggs and bacon to the vegan coworker.  The wait can be long if you go during peak hours tourist season (the only reason I gave four stars instead of five) but you can grab a cup of coffee and walk around downtown while you wait.  I highly recommend the stuffed french toast and the McNeil bar!  So good!

name: Amanda West
text: The food was amazing and the staff was friendly. It was incredibly busy when we went and there was a long wait time but it was worthwhile for the food. The staff was very friendly and understanding of small children. They even have a bin of toys for the kids to play with while we waited to be seated. I ordered the fruit plate with cottage cheese for my kids. the cottage cheese came with a large piece of hair sitting nicely on top but the waiter had a great sense of humor about it and quickly for us a new bowl. I got the eggs Benedict with the salmon and my Mom got the one with crab. Both were done perfectly and were delicious. I highly recommend both for the great food and the pleasant atmosphere.

name: Joanna Eppler
text: Delicious food, great service, great coffee. There's a reason this place is always so packed, you should always get a reservation.

name: Christopher Cole
text:
I had breakfast there with a friend. I had the Eggs-Benedict and he had the breakfast burrito.  We were both really happy with our meals.

The wait staff was very attentive, and the atmosphere was enjoyable.

I definitely will consider returning for future meals!

Thank you for a good experience!

name: Talia Green
text: We loved our breakfast here! We got the stuffed French toast with cream cheese and oranges and it came out with raspberry butter which was a wonderful compliment to the dish. The wait is really long here though so that keeps us from coming in as often as we would like

name: Matthew Scott
text: A great breakfast place in Anchorage. One of the best by far. The biscuits and gravy are amazing. The gravy is creamy, the pancakes are fluffy, the eggs benedict on point. I would recommend to anyone visiting the downtown area.

name: Brittany Tripp
text: Good food! Good vegan options, which I am always looking for. Could be more, though! Wait times can be a little crazy. If you have some time to spare, overall a good place to check out.

name: Jennifer Carpenter
text: Oh, BEST BREAKFAST in Anchorage!!! Loved the meal I had with my daughter!! Best to call for RESERVATIONS a good while before you are hungry. 😆 There is definitely a long wait time otherwise, but it's worth it!!!

name: Amanda B
text:
The food here is good, and their soups really shine. It's always busy, but they take online reservations if you plan ahead. They have baked goods, which include at least one vegan option. I have been here several times with friends and every single time someone ends up missing a small part of their order-- toast or a condiment. Despite being exceptionally busy, the staff are always friendly.

Today, we asked about the specials and our waitress grabbed the menu, flipped it over, and showed us where the specials are listed. Then, she walked away and left us to read over the specials ourselves. They have a lot of specials, but I feel like she could have at least mentioned one or two of them.

This is one of the few places in Anchorage that will keep your water glass filled, too!

It's not very handicapped accessible. The space between tables isn't really wide enough to accommodate a wheelchair or a scooter. The doors to the  building and the restroom do not have an automatic opener, and the restrooms do not have bars to help move from a wheelchair to the commode. Often, the tables are crammed with people, so even if you did manage to get a wheelchair in, you'd have trouble getting very far, and you'd constantly be in the way of the wait staff and other patrons moving between tables.

name: timothy chavis
text: My wife and I love this place! The only complaint I have is that it's too crowded during tourist season, but they always have coffee available while you wait. Food is great and the staff are nice. I also like the location downtown.

name: Yader G Sequeira
text: Amazing place with great food and friendly service, though don't be late for breakfast or there might be a slight wait..!

name: Raymond in AK
text:
My favorite diner anywhere may be Silk City in the Northern Liberties neighborhood of Philadelphia, so I have been thrilled to find Snow City here in Anchorage.
This is for sure top 3 faves in ANC. Despite the telling long waits for a table on weekend mornings, this a first choice treat for late breakfast.
Like any favorite, Snow City has fabulous food and excellent, professional servers.
Love Snow City!

name: C E
text: Staff were kind and helpful.  The food was reasonably priced and well made.  Enjoyed both of our dishes as well as our coffee.  Plan ahead!  This place is extremely popular and the wait can be LONG!

name: Scott Horton
text: Very busy, long wait, call ahead, great food and service.

name: Mark McElroy
text: Friendly servers, a big warm dining hall, and inventive breakfast burritos combine to make this eatery at the top of the world one of my favorites in Alaska. An easy walk from the Captain Cook Hotel, Snow City offers coffee to those standing in lines -- and lines will form, and the wait is worth it. On a dark morning in Anchorage, there's nothing quite like walking up to the golden glow of Snow City and feeling instantly at home. Highly recommended.

name: Kimberly Arthur
text: The Vegan Hash was very greasy. Great toast and jam though!

name: Sarah Greenwood
text: This place is awesome! The Cook Inlet Fog is spectacular, and the chicken salad BLT, with the tomato bisque won't disappoint. My husband got the biscuits and gravy, and it was incredible as well. The staff is top notch, and willing to give suggestions too. Go here!

name: Chief Reviews Everything
text: Delicious Breakfast Options very fresh and filling. Definitely a must have while in Anchorage!!

name: Victor Rodriguez
text: Breakfast for the ages.  1 hour wait and after my meal was over I would have waited 2 or more hours.  This is one you have to try if you are in Anchorage.

name: Tim Newton
text: My family loves this place. They make me go. The food is good & service too, but kind of high priced for me. Often a long wait to be seated, as well. A fine establishment, but doesn't quite suit my personal tastes. You might like it a lot. Lots of folks seem to.

name: Randy Windsor
text: Very good food and service

name: Kasindra Van Meter
text: We've been several times and never been disappointed! The menu is varied from healthy (they make their own granola and will substitute egg whites if you like) to classic pancakes and biscuits and gravy. I love that if there's a wait,  which is always the case on a weekend they have a coffee station set up in the front so you can at least have a warm cup of coffee or tea. The staff are eclectic and friendly. I plan on being a regular. There is also an espresso bar, juice bar, and after 10am they sell adult beverages.

name: Angelo Russoniello
text: Pretty nice place and good food

name: Tiara Light
text: Best brunch in town! They also have this cool lil coffee box that will hold multiple cups of coffee if you're trekking around downtown in the winter. Good selection of various mimosas and beers. Try the polar bear breakfast.

name: Wilson Cullor
text: Trendy crowd. Great menu. Can get really busy and leave you waiting.

resp.text:
Hi Wilson,

Thank you for taking the time to give us a review. Being busy is a great thing for us but of course leaving people waiting when they are hungry is never ideal. To help with that, we started taking reservations!

You can visit our website at snowcitycafe.com or give us a call at 907-272-2489 and speak with one of our hosts!

We hope to see you soon!

name: Keri Hutchins
text: Delicious breakfast, friendly staff, quick service.

name: Brian Won
text:
Make sure you come early to beat the crowds-- which get ridiculous!

Some rave about the benedict, I was not impressed. Service is pretty good-- very homey feel despite the size and light of the place-- and holy cow, the cinnamon roll is worth the hype. I'd honestly skip the rest of the menu, get a hot drink and a cinnamon roll early in the morning, and then enjoy the rest of your day!

name: Jade Catalano
text:
Didn't eat there, was busy, looked like a typical diner. Not much in Alaska, in the way of good food/breakfast. Went to mexican food truck next door, which was amazing.

Updating since we didn't eat: seemed like a typical diner, did look decent. Thank you to the owners response - very nice option to make a reservation if you know it will be busy.

resp.text: I am sorry to hear you couldn't stay and dine with us but I am glad you visited our neighbors. They have great tacos and our a staff favorite! We do stay busy, especially in the summer, but you can make reservations. Try to visit us again and make one by visiting our website or calling us at 907-272-2489. We hope to see you soon!

name: Bryan Blakstad
text: Good food good service

name: Dylan OBrien
text: Great breakfast place stuffed french toast is awesome, the Riendeer sausage could use more flavor. There can be wait if you like late Sunday breakfast.

name: Jeffrey Kempff
text: Fantastic food, fabulous staff, phenomenal atmosphere. Heck, even the prices are not bad! Reservations are available but mostly only required 'in season' or earlier in the day...just call or expect a short wait. That said, it is well worth a wait!

name: Ellen
text: The food is always good, the service can be a bit slow.  You might need reservations in the summer.

name: Lynda Lewis
text: The hash browns were heavenly. I loved my Sams scramble. My daughter ordered the lemon blueberry pancakes. When they came out they had no blueberries. We were informed they were out of blueberries. Even though they gave her strawberries when they saw she was unhappy. It would not have been ordered if we had been informed of no blueberries. Service was slow and not real friendly.

name: Ashley Plante
text: I recommend making a reservation here, it's always busy. Despite how busy it was we were seated right away(we had a reservation), it didn't take long for our drinks to come out or our food. The crab cake with eggs Benedict was amazing, everything else was great as well. Service was awesome, we were done within an hour.

name: Janl Wieber
text: Fun!  Noisy!  Great menu selections!   Worth the wait!

name: Ana
text: Food was good. Good service! In 30 min we ordered and ate our food.

name: derek murphy
text: I bring my family here at least once a month. We always make a reservation to cut down on wait time. The staff is always courteous and attentive and the food is always good. I've never had a bad meal here.

name: Nat Luengnaruemitchai
text: Good coffee, good food.... just a bit too crowded.

name: Christopher .Jordan
text: Always love eating here for brunch and coffee. Great service and great food

name: matt knowlton
text: Great food. Good coffee

name: John Noland
text: This place looked amazing and everyone we talked to or overheard talk about the food were very complementary.

name: Bennie Good
text: Very warm and welcoming.  Great spot to grab a bite in downtown Anchorage.

name: Tony Azouz
text: Good food but be prepared for a long wait until you're seated.

name: Danielle Clifford
text: Make a reservation, but this place is totally worth the wait. Best breakfast in Alaska. We had a stuffed French toast and smoked salmon omelet that were perfect. Their espresso was perfect and my husband loved their chai tea.

name: Tso Pigu
text:
I would rate it a good to not-bad place.  As someone who is from Seattle and coffee is in our blood, Snow City's coffee was quite burnt and charred to the point of repulsive.  I am sure someone likes that coffee.  So I wouldn't judge.  But seriously tho...wow, burnt and ashy taste like that bottom of the communal coffee pot at work that was left on the burner all day long.

The signature dish, the salmon and crab cakes Benedict was so-so and had some technical flaws.  Instead of that meaty  flaky crab and salmon meat, they ground up the meat or pulverized it like a meat mush and then formed into cakes.  The result is a dried, meat paste of a cake that's devoid of the original beauty of salmon or crab meat.  Might as well use crab powder to make them.

Eggs on the Benedic were overly done.  The yolks were half cooked and half runny.  Classic Benedict requires the yolk runny.  While this aspect is of personal preference, it was unexpected to find Benedict with half of the yolk cooked on its way to become a hard boiled egg.

The reviews say "prepare to be blown away"... I guess that depends on the standard of being "blown away".  Today's performance was nothing close "blowing away."   But hey, every day is different.   Today's failure will be tomorrow's success.  Better luck another day.

name: Margaret Wiltfong Tovrea
text: A real "Go To" for friends, family, and visitors. Excellent service, reliably tasty food, great coffee.

name: James Wilson
text: Incredible food. Smoked salmon cakes were to die for. The sausage gravy I got on my hashbrowns was the best I have managed to find in anchorage. My only regret was not starting eating here sooner after moving to anchorage.

name: Caleb
text: Usually this place is really good, sometimes it is a little disappointing.  The Deadliest Catch is great, but their hashes, pancakes, everything is good.  Sometimes it just feels like they are having an off day and your crab/salmon cakes dry.  Definitely a bit too expensive for the quality of food you get, and it seems over hyped... make sure to make a reservation.

name: Ft Gray
text: Spectacular baked goods, great breakfasts.

name: terry crossley
text: Stuffed French toast is great.  I wish it was bigger.

name: J Lmm
text: This is average food. Should not be more then 3 stars. Taste is ok to I can eat if hungry.

name: Ricky Bakker
text: Very good food and excellent service!

name: James M
text: You can expect a wait, but one that is well worth it. The food was absolutely amazing. I sat at the bar and was able to watch the staff quickly work together to make beautiful dishes and drinks, it was a great experience and my food was delicious

name: Antonio de las Traviesas
text: Great place for breakfast!

name: Aditya Salunke
text: Excellent place for breakfast if you are in Anchorage anytime. Service was amazing. Everything we had was so good. Would definitely recommend anyone and would ourselves love to visit again.

name: Pamela Wigandt
text: Our first breakfast in Anchorage was here. A little bit of a wait, but so worth it. Menu has so many great dished. I had the stuffed french toast with rasberry butter.  Yum

name: Natalie carlin
text: This place is excellent! Breakfast sandwich with a cappuccino.

name: Eddie Williams
text: It's was open during pandemic

name: JJ Cavins
text: Always good. Go at an off time or off day or be prepared to wait. Good different kinds of eggs benny and good coffee.

name: Robert J
text: Good food allways busy place with a line most days thats a good sign of a restaurant.

name: Paul Burns
text: This place is always busy and service is always great. Only came in for coffee didn't have time to grab a bite but their food is delicious!!

name: David Enzel
text: Great place for breakfast. Fresh ingredients and super friendly. Locals really come here. Highly recommended but be prepared for a wait. Counter seating is first come first served.

name: Chelsea Spaulding
text: It’s good, but I don’t see what all the rave is about. Location is what makes it so nice.

name: Jim Barker
text: Wonderful lunch spot. Tasty food and excellent service. Expect to wait, but well worth the wait.

name: Pamela Proffer
text: Saturday and Sundays are pretty busy but weekday mornings aren't too bad.

name: celticdenefew
text: Everyone knows this is the best breakfast in town. Where else can you go where they're nearly full 15 min after open?

name: Ian Lee
text: Good coffee, Pink Floyd, Reindeer sausage... all located downtown in a cozy, well lit corner cafe.

name: Eugene Burke
text: Best breakfast joint in downtown Anchorage, worth the fourty minute wait if you're in a group, or stop by the bar if solo for faster seating

name: Blanche Sheppard
text: Best place in town for breakfast. Try the stuffed French toast

name: chris clapham
text: Best brunch place Ive been to in a long time. Helpful staff.

name: Kevin Pike
text: Consistently good food over the 8 years I have been eating here. Yesterday was no exception. Can be a long wait in the summer, but in the winter it's pretty easy to get seated. Service is good. Only complaint is the price, but it's on par with the rest of Anchorage.

name: Bene C
text: Great food and service, always busy so expect to wait.

name: Royce Thompson
text: Great breakfast cafe. Very popular. After eating the red we could see why it has such a good reputation

name: Tony Weber
text: Amazing breakfast and or brunch if you dont mind the wait if you're not there before the rush

name: Adrienne Keck
text: Best breakfast in anchorage. Love the fried egg sandwich and stuffed French toast! Worth the wait!

name: amy graham
text: Love the food. Location is good. Servers are relaxed.

name: Mark Kirven
text: Good food.

name: James
text: the food is delicious and the service was great! It is a very popular dining location (for good reason), and it was very busy. We were seated right next to another group of people,  so there was no chance of an intimate or private conversation.

name: Carrie Murray
text: Delicious unique food combinations.

name: Logan Herrera
text: The food was good. Nice for small parties of less than 4, but I don't reccomend larger as it's so busy. They do take reservations for larger groups. If you come to Alaska it is a must at least once.

name: Steven Carner
text: Wait time was incredibly slow the kids running the show didn't seem to know what they were doing. the food was good. though but I don't understand why the president of the United States stopped here

name: Cathy Fisher
text: Good food. A bit loud, but very busy place. Seems popular with the tourists in downtown Anchorage.

name: Sharon Palacios
text: Delicious food fun atmosphere

name: Carol Brown
text: Oh my goodness, what a cute restaurant.  Large portions of French toast where we could have shared so unable to finish.  Live this place!

Hi Shanon,

Welcome to Anchorage!

I am sorry to hear you did not stay to dine with us as it was crowded. We would love for you to give us another chance. We know it is tough to avoid the wait with us sometimes and unfortunately our local guests feel the brunt of that. We started taking reservations a few years ago so our locals would have a way to get in without a long wait. You can make one by calling us at 907-272-2489 or going to our website www.snowcitycafe.com.

We hope to see you soon!

Happy New Year!

Biscuits & Gravy: The biscuits taste like cardboard, they're also flat like English muffins--

The Ship Creek Benedict: I found this lacking in flavor and completely bland.

The Kodiak Benedict: ... Was actually pretty delicious. I have no criticisms about the Kodiak, their crab cakes are on point.

The items on the Lunch menu are really great! Try their Cowboy Meatloaf. The Love Potion smoothies are good and so are the milkshakes.

The chunks of chicken in the peanut soup are usually dry. I think the soup would be better without it.

My favorite restaurant in town is Glacier Brewhouse.

text:
Thanks to the Visitors Center in Anchorage, I found out about this local favorite breakfast/lunch spot.

Tip: Maker reservations; otherwise, expect to wait about 20 minutes for a table.  While you wait, you can get started with a cup of coffee which will be added to your bill.

Expect your traditional breakfast favorites, some with a twist such as the Kodiak Eggs Benedict (Crab Cakes in lieu of Canadian Bacon).

On this visit, I selected the chilaquiles.  Traditionally, the tortilla chips in chilaquiles are thoroughly cooked in a chili sauce.  These chilaquiles were more like tortilla chips with tomatillo sauce poured over with a helping of scramble eggs.  Not traditional - yet yummy and satisfying (see picture).

text:
As a travel agent: No one wants to get up early in the morning!! Right? Uhm no, get in line with the rest of the Alaskans and enjoy breakfast at the SnowCity Cafe.
Meals are made from scratch, and with plenty of love. Do you love a fresh healthy meal to start the cold wintery days of AK Idiatrod week?
I had my stuffed french toast baguette, with mandarin orange cream cheese, toasted walnuts, syrup, raspberry butter. I was licking my fingers at the hot cocoa. Ok...I had to cups!!! But don't look at me and roll your eyes! Next they were selling the Idiatrod collections and I purchased gifts for my dog loving friends.
Next time you are in Anchorage--Join the line-it's worth the wait.

name: Cerena Gonzalez
text: Visiting Anchorage and found this was a must-try place via the interwebs.  Even though we went on a Tuesday, we took others advice and made reservations.  We were there a bit early for our reservation, but was sat down the time we made our resie for.  Our hostess sat us and quickly brought us some waters.  Enough time had passed that I actually had to look at my phone to see how long we had been waiting... about 7 minutes until our server came to greet us.  He was nice and thanked us for our patience.  Ordered the Almond Joy drink, which was too dark chocolatey for me.  I ordered the stuffed french toast, which was so so soooo good. I am not the kind of person who usually orders pancakes, french toast, waffles (carb focused), but the description of the french toast sounded delicious so I had to try; I was not disappointed! :) My boyfriend got the Alaska king crab cake benny, which was good.. we had shared plates and he was disappointed that his egg was more soft boiled than runny, however, my egg was runny so no complaints here.  Check came out to be a little under $30 - reasonable. I will definitely come here again.

name: Brian Won
text:
Oh man. Really wanted to like this place-- staff are great, ambiance is super appropriate for Fairbanks, and the menu seems very appropriate. The cinnamon roll french toast was very tempting but seemed like sugar overload...

The chicken fried prime rib was just okay, not salty enough, while the corned beef hash was the opposite-- not bad but too salty until you mixed it with the eggs!

So. Hard to knock, but hard to sing its praises either...

name: Jennie Ramirez
text: The food was AMAZING. We tried the cinnamon roll since it was mentioned a lot in reviews and it was great. The ham, eggs, French toast were also great. Fast service, there are a lot of tables available even though it was busy when we got here

resp.text: Thank you Jennie. Glad you dined with us and enjoyed it. Thanks so much for the review.

name: Sole Professor
text: Best breakfast in Fairbanks period.  Portions so large you’ll get a back ache from being so full.  Steak and eggs are incredible, the Nolan, pancakes, everything is over the top good.  A true family environment like your in some American family next door kitchen.  Really enjoy this place.  If your wanting breakfast or brunch this place should be your #1 choice, period.  Fairbanks does breakfast well across the board but this is the spot that doesn’t have a weak item on the menu.

name: Donald Gerhart
text: The food was excellent! If you have a big breakfast appetite then try the chicken fried steak made from a slab of prime rib. Sadly, the service was poor. Nice people, but the drink orders were wrong and simple things like the offer to bring napkins being forgotten detract from the whole visit. I could understand it if they were busy, but there were only four groups of two to three people each.

name: CA G
text: This is the place I look forward to when I get to fairbanks. It is a down home country breakfast restaurant worth trying at least once. I haven't had anything on their menu I didn't like but what I would recommend is trying their corn beef and hash. They slow roast it in their own spices and it is one of my favorites. If you are looking at baked goods they also sell pastries and cinnamon rolls that are huge. One of my favorite breakfast joints.

name: Jamey
text: Far from impressed.  We tried the Cookie Jar while visiting Fairbanks.  I tried the homemade bread ham sandwich on sough dough.  The bread sandwich arrived on stale white bread and the cheese was shredded like you'd expect on a quesadilla.  It was gross.  Kids got pancakes and they were tough to cut and chew.  Wife got a burger, it was decent.  Overall the restaurant was dirty.  There were a few families dining in, but far from busy enough to justify how dirty it was.  Bottom line, we had high hopes and were very disappointed.

name: Tricia Pry
text: I heard so many good things about this place. I was excited to try it but my food was a little below average.  I had the quiche of the day.  It was a meat lovers with mozzarella.  It was dry overcooked and very bland. Not alot of meat and I couldn't find any cheese.  I also tried the corn beef hash and biscuits with gravy. They were both a little better but still a little bland. I got a blueberry muffin, chocolate chip with nuts, oatmeal raisin and peanut butter cookies.  The muffin was burnt, and the chocolate chip cookie has 2 very small nuts. The other two were absolutely delicious.  I will try this place again but I think it will be for lunch or dinner.  I heard too many good things so maybe they were just having an off day.

We felt uneasy when we walked in, but our server was overall great, so the service balanced itself out.

The problem was the food.  Mine was just below average for what you expect from a place like this, but that puts it at maybe Denny's level, which isn't good.  The husband's was clearly awful, though.  I have never seen such a dried-out brick of egg in my life.  He barely touched it, and he'll eat anything (really, almost anything).  I just posted a review that I'd go back if someone else was paying, but I don't think that's even true here.  There seem to be some edible things on the menu, but certainly not all of it.

text:
Had breakfast on the 24th and lunch on the 25th.  This is a great place that we couldn't find at first, it is behind the dealership.  Great local place that severs up some big breakfasts and lunch.  Had the bacon, sausage, and cheese omelet and boy was this thing stuffed with meat.  You get your choice of home fries or breakfast potatoes and toast.  From lunch had a chicken bacon cheese steak that would be right up there in Philly.  The roll was fresh baked and softer than in Philly, but I think it would do Philly proud.  When you go ask for Jennifer, she was great, friendly and full of smiles both days, never let our drinks get empty and also checked in with us.
This is a must if you are visiting Fairbanks.

name: Mel Jenkins
text: This place is so cozy and cute. It's got gifts, cookie jars and cookies/yummy treats in the front area with cute little tables and chairs. When you walk in the door, you're greeted by a wooden moose chef. The waitresses seat you at a little table. Very small little restaurant but very inviting and nice and quiet. The food is like classic American food... Burgers, cheese steaks, root beer floats, meatloaf, pie, lemonade, etc. Also a few things like noodles, soups and salads. Typical drinks like sodas, milk, chocolate milk...a few drinks offer refills. They also offer the breakfast foods all day. All meals are a good helping sizes and taste home made. Even the kids meal was big! We love taking our kids! We prefer this place over Food Factory. Oh a fun note... Guy Fieri visited once for his Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives show. A big poster with his autograph is on the wall!

name: David Matz
text: The Cookie Jar is one of the more popular breakfast places in Fairbanks. That said, they also serve lunch and dinner - although there is no dinner service on Sunday. Be aware that peak times on weekends you will likely have to wait for seating, and the entry area does not have copious amounts of seating. However, the food is worth the inconvenience. The food is good and fresh, with unique items on the menu. The French Toast made from cinnamon rolls is a family favorite, whether regular or stuffed. They offer the best country fried steak in town, with their house version being a breaded cut of prime rib (although a traditional version is available). The home fries are a great potato option. Portions are ample. The one thing to be aware of is that it can be loud during peak times. If you have people hard of hearing or sensitive to noise in your group, you may want to ask for a table in one of the alcoves or their large party area as they are quieter than the main dining room.
