name: Traci Dale
text: So, my husband and I went there on a Friday night and I was shocked how empty it was. We have not been there in quite a while but every time before they were packed. After eating there, I'm not sure if I'm correct but I think it's because of the food and the service. Our waitress, even though she had a great personality, was slow and a little forgetful. The food was not as amazing as it has been in the past. It was not horrible by any means, just not like I remembered it. I hope they are still doing well and it was just an off night.

name: DAWN CURTIS
text: Burned the roof of my mouth on the first bite of quiche and the mushrooms tasted very old...well I only ate three bites...burned mouth!

resp.text:
Dawn,
I can assure you our food is fresh though if it was as said, I hope you spoke to management because we would want to make it right. We feel awful that you weren’t satisfied.

name: Dana Ziskrout
text: Really neat place. Food was very good. Great selection of food choices. The server was the weak link. Polite, but a bit confused. Would return.

name: Timothy Worley
text: This place has such great food. It's always busy which tells you that people know how good it is. If you like french toast, try theirs... They make one out of cinnamon rolls! Whaaa!!!!!???? It's delicious

name: Kimberly Murphy
text: One of the best breakfasts you can get in Fairbanks. Lasagnas are so yummy. And I can't get out with out at least one price of those delicious chocolates. Try them all.!!!

name: Colin Harasti
text: Large helpings of delicious food, solid service, and a clean if somewhat crowded establishment. Prices are moderate, but not unreasonable.

name: Patrick Prentice
text: Had such an incredible experience here! Great food (get the cinnamon roll French toast) and excellent service! You can't ask for anything more 😊👍

name: Sheryl Ann Turner
text:
Service is great and food is even better. Coconut cream pie was to die for.....
Nice relaxing atmosphere and my husband said the biscuits and gravy were very good.....

name: Leah Jean
text: Took us a while to get our food, but the food was really good and the portions are huge, so I ended up taking two lunches worth of food home with me. Friendly service, cute place, little touristy items you can buy if that's your fancy.

name: Zeng Sunshine
text: Large portion, tasty food.

name: KC T.
text:
Delicious food for a good price!
Even the kids menu is filling - I recommend the mac n' cheese.
The wait staff is very friendly and helpful, and the food is even better!

name: Atila Đurik
text:
Delicious food, quick service, nice.
Would eat here again.

name: Rachel Titus
text: Ordered my Corned Beef Hash and Scrambled eggs with white toast as always. My friend had the 3 piece French Toast and aside of Bacon. He didn’t get his bacon till after we were all done eating. Our waitress reassured that it’s still coming but won’t be charged because of the long wait. And our coffee was always filled if empty. I love that their breads are fresh made daily for their menu and who doesn’t love fresh baked bread? Great breakfast place hands down.

name: Elvira Morozova
text: It's a good breakfast place. Nothing out of ordinary. Simple food and good service.

name: Chad Baxter
text: Eggs over cooked or sat to long under the heat lamp. Portions have gotten alot smaller than I remember also. Won't be back

name: Alfred Ketzler
text: Sunday midday, so service is slow but food quality makes up for slow service. Enjoyed the meal.

name: Rebecca White Wolf
text: The Halibut burger is amazing and the Philly cheesesteak as well. Reminds me of hometown cooking 😊

name: Lisa Vogt
text: Long wait, slow service, cold yet over cooked food, and RBF on almost every server. Usually one of my favorite places, but not this year☹

name: Kristopher Ashton
text: One of the more popular spots in Fairbanks for breakfast, and featured on a popular television show. I decided to try The Cookie Jar while in town for a few weeks. Wonderful, friendly service and large portions. Way too large for me to finish. The country fried steak was decent, but certainly not the best I've had. The wait can be a while at certain times of the morning. Overall a pleasant experience.

name: Kimberly Gormly
text: Gross food, horribly outdated decor. I had Stromboli that was disgusting. The filling was just bland sauce and hamburger meat. It had the taste and texture of something that had been microwaved. My daughter's fries also seemed reheated and buffalo chicken nuggets were soggy. Don't go.

name: Isaac Osborn
text: The location and building are great, feels like grandma's dining room in a good way. Food is awful. I've been here multiple times and I have never enjoyed my meal. Such a shame, this place seems to be loved by all.

name: Cameron John
text: Really good food. I've had some of the best breakfasts of my life there

name: Erin Goodlett
text: So cute and cozy! I had the meatloaf sandwich which was incredible! The fries and potato salad were fantastic too. My wife had the roast beef and she really liked it. I also had the veggie soup which was so delicious and warming. We were visiting out of state, wish we lived closer because we'd go here all the time. Lovely place!

name: John D Knott III
text: Pretty good food. Great service. Well lite dining area.

name: Michael DiSarro
text: Amazing burgers!

resp.text: Thank so much!!

name: Victoria Avery
text: Great place for breakfast! My only complaint is that the tables are a little close together for large people like me, but the food is so good the place gets packed so I get it. We bring fam here when they travel from Outside. They all crave the biscuits.

name: Susana Luna
text: 10 out of 10 would recommend. Since the first time I went I have gone back about five times. The staff is great and friendly. The food is absolutely amazing it can get full but even when they are full the food still comes out at a reasonable time and the food is great. Definitely going back.

name: Kevin Kearns
text: Service was not good and food was just okay. I was expecting better from the reviews and word of mouth. I would go back again, but it wont be my first choice.

name: Daniel DeLuca
text: Less than stellar experience. Wasn't greeted at the door, and when I was seated, it took about 10 minutes for someone to come serve me. Food was decent enough, but server rarely came to check with me, talked maybe 3 times. It wasn't like it was busy either, restaurant was at half capacity.

name: Amanda Blanchard
text: Always great food and friendly staff.

name: Kyla Phillips
text: Delicious breakfast! We came here twice on our vacation. I love that they give you the option to have your meal as an omelet or skillet. I had the skillet and loved it! The pumpkin spice latte was also perfection. It’s hard to find a good breakfast spot that also serves a good latte! The only dish that wasn’t a “win” in our book was the biscuits and gravy (a bit bland).

name: Scott Thompson
text: The food was good for Fairbanks. They were very understaffed. The staff that was working needs to multitask. Just because it's your job for the night to seat people does not mean that's all you do. If your tables are taken care of help the servers out. In the big picture all employees will make more because happy and full customers tip more and return often.

name: Per Harald Pettersen
text: Great cafe, serving breakfast, lunch, salads, cakes and cookies. Diverse menu, special treats. The staff was friendly and efficient. Recommended.

name: Deborah Mulcahy
text: Friendly service but very slow. Restaurant was not busy and we waited 20 minutes for our food. Food was just ok. One piece of candy was $4.50. We would not go back.

name: Katie Wells
text: Really great place. Food is good. Service is a little slow even when not busy so dont come here for a quick bite. Prices are a little high in my opinion, but nothing to discourage me from coming back

name: janean colburn
text: Delicious....as always!

name: amy graham
text: The food is plentiful, and tasty. Real size lemonade. Reasonable prices towards spendy, but worth it!

name: Linda Larcom
text: Great as always

resp.text: Thank you so much!!!

name: Sierra Huffines
text: This place is beautifully decorated! The staff was very friendly. The food was kinda pricey but it’s a great atmosphere. The food tasted great and the pastries are delicious. Great place to go for a nice date!

name: Sherri Long
text: Great food, went their as a guest for a Christmas Party and met the entire staff. Everyone was awesome. Really respectful. I would recommend it to everyone.

name: Adriana Pellegrini
text: Very good food. Very good service once at the table. Wait was quite long to even get my name on the waiting list. More expensive than I expected.

name: Alexis Fay
text: I enjoy the food (only been here for breakfast but on many occasions) and I love the quaint decor with all of the cookie jars. But this place gets packed and food can take a long time if you go in the weekends. I don’t mind waiting because they refill your coffee but if you have hungry littles ones, be warned. Lol.

name: Matthew Denakis
text:
Good coffee, great breakfast.
A little crowded on the weekends. But well worth any wait.

name: Bill Payer
text:
Surprisingly bad. Omlets made with boxed eggs not fresh. Asked for crispy hashbrowns got exact opposite. Toast was not! Butter on toast is not butter! I was surprised when i arrived on a Friday at 640 there was 2 tables full. Now i know why. There used to be no better place for breakfast, no longer true😡😡😡😡😡

Shame, on triple D years ago. Not the same anymore. Freaking margarine bull💩💩💩💩💩💩💩

name: Johanna Desbiens
text: Good lunch and breakfast! Everyone was so nice. They also having amazing home baked cookies and treats!

name: Chris Heering
text: Great food, most staff didn't seem to want to be there as thier attitude reflects such. Felt as if I was a burden.

name: Chad Gomez
text: Amazing breakfast food! Havent been for anything else since I dont live in Fairbanks but will definitely try another meal next time I am in town.

name: Judi
text: Delicious! We stopped here for a late lunch and everything was great! I had the French Dip with fried onions and Swiss, it was.perfect to say the least. To top it off, the bun was grilled, a nice touch mostl restaurants miss.  My daughter had the cheessteak which she said was great.  We took dessert home,  even though we did not yet eat it, we know it's going to be out of this world good, just based on appearance. Two thumbs up for the cookie jar!

name: shahab aria
text:
Simply the best restaurant in Fairbanks!!
Quality of the food was great, great taste and  great and healthy produces( it is very hard to find a resturant in Fairbanks with tasty foods and great quality materials,
Staff was great, we were there almost at 8pm and they were closing but we had a great service with friendly server.
I recommend this restaurant with 5 stars.

name: Levi Blalock
text: Good price. Lots of good food. Some things weren't too good like salad and ranch. Finding entrance was hard, could use some signs. Seating was cramped. Waitress was good.

name: Muriel Toole
text: THE COOKIE JAR is a friendly and warm environment. The device is usually ver good. I would like and have suggested the add back some of the previous menu items especially the Sylvia's salad. I know it was not only mine but others I've talked to favorite plate.

name: claudia Wright
text: Great customer service

resp.text: Thank you so much. We’re so glad to hear that.

name: Joshua Arnold
text: I have been there twice, and I am baffled at how they made it on DDD. It is okay food at best for a diner, but there is better in Fairbanks AK

name: James Wells
text: The Cookie Jar restaurant is a comfortable local eatery where we can get a good meal and relaxed atmosphere.  The food is generous portion sizes and service is friendly.

name: Fronty Parker
text: I've never seen cinimon rolls so big!  I like breakfast here.

name: Evan proios
text: Great breakfast spot.

resp.text: Glad you liked it! Thanks for coming.

name: Ryan Stonebraker
text: One of the best breakfast restaurants in all of Fairbanks. Frequently crowded and might take a little to get seated, but worth the wait. While great, this is probably not the place for people on diets as they have an extensive menu of unhealthy (but good) dishes.

name: Carol J Garcia
text: Cute place, Nice lil gift shop Great breakfast, awesome service

name: Anthony Ludwig
text: Good food for dine in but very disappointed with the delivery service.

resp.text: Sorry to hear that. Please call us to let us know how we can improve and what happened that shouldn’t have. Ask for Bob or Gloria

name: Vida Horsfield
text: Great for a cup of coffee and quick bite. Clean, convenient, friendly staff, quick service, outside seating available.

name: Hazel Sunshine Hall
text: The food is delicious. The best muffins I've ever had. Fast service and clean establishment.

name: terri bowers
text: Good food, friendly staff.

resp.text: Thank you! Very kind.

name: Andrew Radtke
text: Love the all day breakfast. Sometimes you just need an 8/9pm breakfast.

name: Jessica Butchar
text: So so so so so good!!! Highly recommend EVERYTHING and great service!

name: Debra Segers
text: The rating would have been 5 stars, but...Interesting that this was on both ends of the spectrum - great and horrible. The horrible was being seated, having our drink and food order placed at the same time and 25 minutes later having to ask again for our coffee. We had a training team of waitress/waiter and we understand the newbie maybe forgetting, but the trainer too?!?! Almost left the restaurant to look for food elsewhere but she finally showed up at a nearby table so we could ask again for coffee. We got our first cup just seconds before the food came to the table. The food (Meat lover's omelet and Corned Beef breakfast) was excellent. Cooked to order, flavorful ... Simply wonderful. The Corned Beef breakfast was actually corned beef, not the canned hash stuff. Totally delightful. So the kitchen has their act together, but not the service. Will try again just to see if service improves - the food is that good.

name: Chelsea Arnold
text: Great food, nice people and a good atmosphere.

name: Bao Cheng
text: Their foods is delicious. It come with a big platter . I can't even finish my food .

name: Eric Collier
text: For the most part a good breakfast. Not sure if the owners are saving a buck or two by having limited servers. Could have stayed home, raised a few hens, took the eggs, cooked them, and then my service would have started. Once we had service, it was great, up till that point..... We were just water drinkers.

name: Queena Gandwa
text: Were so glad they're open on New Year's day. It's a cute place and you should TRY the CORNED BEEF HASH. I'm very glad i chose that. It is so good.

name: Brenda erlich
text: Very excellentservice and food. Attentive, courteous and friendly staff. The beef strogganoff was very good.

name: Rye Adrianos
text: The prime rib country fried steak was delicious! A little hard to figure out how to get into the parking due to construction.

name: Jarek Halat
text: Great servers and great food. Will return again soon!

name: Elizabeth Pietryk
text: Not great, but not terrible. Convenient if you are getting your car seviced.

name: Kimberly Bridges
text: This has to be the very best place "EVER" that Robert & I have had breakfast! Delicious Home Cooking! You feel like you are sitting at your Grandparents kitchen table!

name: Pamela Tapert
text: Food was pricey, our poor waitress needed more help with 45 of us, but she was great

name: Ellie H
text: My fruit cup wasn't very fresh, and my friends biscuits & gravy wasn't the best. But I must say, the atmosphere is so friendly and uplifting. Service is quick, food is usually great, and the restaurant is kept tidy.

name: Walker Wheeler
text: Great place to get a meal. Just as good for desserts. If you have a breakfast sweet tooth try Nolan's Own, a fresh made cinnamon roll cut in half and made into french toast.

name: Emanuel Mavres
text: This restaurant is a hidden gem in the Fairbanks area. On our visit from Florida we ate dinner here one night and it was phenomenal. The beef stroganoff was very good and the egg salad sandwich was also delicious. So good in fact we decided to try this place for breakfast. Well it was so good the first morning that we decided to go a second morning as well. We had eggs benedict, biscuits and gravy, Denver burrito, and their coffee was amazing. Highly recommended place for you if you are visiting Fairbanks or live here.

name: Christopher Beegle
text: Great food, amazing treats!

name: Mr Bacon
text: Great food and service. May have to wait for a table but it's worth it

name: Ron Baioni
text: Cozy restaurant, large portions, friendly staff. Good casual dining.

name: Mike Sewell
text: Service review only- after waiting 10 minutes for someone to take our drink order we got ahold of the hostess who said someone would be by. Another 5 minutes went by without seeing anyone. So we left. Let the front of house know on the way out and nobody seems to care. Wasn't that busy. Plenty of blue shirts standing around.

name: Yi Wang
text: Great cinnamon roll breakfast.

name: Eljay Koomba
text: Good ol fashion comfort food! Was an amazing treat to eat there. So good!

name: Matthew Meagher
text: Very nice and clean. Walking in you instantly get a small town feeling. The service was excellent and the food was great. Prices are reasonable. Great family restaurant. My family's must stop any time we are in town.

name: Ali Ko
text: Always busy, and the tables are all within arms reach of each other with hardly any room for wait staff to get through. The food is okay but very overpriced. The owners are rude, but the wait staff seem nice enough. I only come here if I have to.

name: Aino Welch
text: Think this place is over rated. Service is not up to par any more. Food quality has gone down hill. Had my favorite stroganoff, and it came out floating in grease, sauce separating. After that every other meal has been so so.

name: Robert Carpenter
text: Great for large groups, service is great too.

name: Reese Pesata
text: Decent home style food. Service was slow but overall experience was good

name: Rhonda Martinez
text: Wow what a place! I loved all the things on the walls I love the decorations I was amazed at how quick we were seated even though they said it was a long waiting list it didn't take as long as we thought it would. Everyone was so friendly and helpful and the food was outstanding!☆☆☆☆☆

name: Constance Smith
text: Well, I wish I could say that I LOVED this restaurant as much as everyone else in town seems to. I ate here a couple times for lunch meetings with others. Tried a couple different items. The first time I came, it was around 10:30 and all I wanted was one of their signature cinnamon rolls, (after all I had seen Guy making them before I'd even come to Alaska!) but they were already sold out?! Then I tried to order something else, and they were out of that as well. I ended up having quiche...meh. Ordered a mocha...not that great either. I did come back at a later date for cinnamon rolls. My kids loved them because the cinnamon rolls were bigger than their heads! (as they said) but honestly, I wasn't terribly impressed with the flavor. I wish I loved this place, because I love supporting private/family owned places, but I have to be honest. It's okay.

name: Karen Page
text: Very good food. Loved the fish taco.

name: Dorlen Gasaway
text: Very good food and staff.

name: Eli Mitchell
text: Pleasant, bright environment. Friendly staff. Good food. Reasonable prices. This is one of my favorite places to eat out in Fairbanks.

name: Debra Cyphert
text: Yummy breakfasts that are hot and fresh. Cinnamon rolls the width of a basketball that can be shared by 4 people.

name: J.Kraig Smyth
text: They double booked the space for our party's reservation, so we were seating was suboptimal. They were understaffed and service was very slow. Food good, as always.

name: chris hamblin
text: Absolutely loved this place!  Will be back again during this trip!

name: Jesse Lentz
text: The food is always fantastic and the staff is always super friendly. It's definitely a treat to go there, the only thing I wish was different was how packed the tables are. It can get pretty hard to even turn around at times.

name: Matthew Millsaps
text: I went there for breakfast. Good portions, friendly service.

name: Austin Gibson
text:
Good food, nice atmosphere, clean and usually quiet.
Also a great place for groups.
And you can't go without trying one of their deserts. They're awesome.

name: Sandi Snow
text: Great food, great service, excellent desserts.

name: Carl Eady
text: I am the bus driver, had 29 elderly, service was great food was very good.

name: Ben Nove
text: Great place to grab breakfast, but make reservations. They are a very busy restaurant. Highly recommend trying their cookies!

name: Nicholas Vandermunnik
text: Wonderful food. Biscuit was delicious 👌

name: Jennifer Frysz
text: Very good food. That is most important. The second most important thing to know is if you do not want to wait for a table for breakfast, then you must get there by 900 or you will have to wait. They are busy. The other issue is if you are in the back rooms. It is way too loud to hear each other, so it makes it less appealing. I do enjoy this place, despite these two minor challenges.

name: Ashley Wear
text: Weirdly, it's not a bakery. This place has some of the best home made food. I really enjoyed the beef veggie soup and my vegetarian lasagna. They give you a lot of bread with your meal, as a heads up. Inside is a little sparsely decorated, but over all a little Fairbanks jem.

name: Matthew Lee
text:
We came here as our first restaurant experience in Fairbanks when we moved here. Overall it was delicious but the cinnamon roll we ordered was actually slightly raw in the middle. However... our waitress noticed we had left some on the plate and SHE was the one that asked if it was raw and offered to take it off our check. Excellent service!

We gave it another chance a couple weeks ago and everyone in my party really enjoyed what they got. We actually had the same waitress again! Surely she didn't remember us but this time the cinnamon roll was cooked perfectly. Definitely one of my Fairbanks favorites.

name: Kyle George
text: Love this place! Best breakfast in Alaska! Also the best BLT I've had almost anywhere.

name: Mary Hoy
text: Food was phenomenal... that's the only reason I gave it 2 stars.  Props to the cook.  However the service was EXTREMELY slow and when asking for certain things they never came.  We sat with our water glasses empty for 20 min. Waited another 45 min for the check.  We also went at 2pm so they weren't all that busy.  Pretty disappointing.

name: Angela Spear
text: Excellent baked goods and candies. Nolan's French toast (uses a homemade cinnamon roll) is beyond delicious. Espresso and hearty variety of breakfast, lunch and dinner options for the whole family. Gets busy quick so come early

name: Tyler Cunningham
text: Place is good, prim rib chicken fried steak is where it's at! Good coffee, but the OJ served here is a little upsetting. Let's step it up a notch and serve some real Orange Juice. Orange juice from concrete only does OK when made as a screw driver. As for my OJ with breakfast Simply Orange or Tropicana... That to expensive or what?

name: Karen Best
text: Super fantastic food. Sundays are really  crowded so be sure you go before the church crowd gets there.

name: neal gregory
text: Great food..great bakery..great gifts

name: Marshall Sims
text: Good food and friendly service. Great for breakfasts, lunch, or dinner. Can be very crowded with long waits depending on the time of day. Lovely gift shop by the entrance.

name: Rose Gueco
text: I love their country prime rib steak. I get it every time, it's so good. Can be hard to get into because the food is good.

name: Daniel Martolano
text: I had the country-fried steak breakfast with prime rib with gravy on the top, hash browns and onions fried hard. All food was delicious, hot, and was a good portion. Left happy!

name: Mandi Herr
text: Delicious food!

resp.text: Thank you!!

name: Michaela Higgison
text: One of the better breakfast places in town but still has room for improvement. My waffle wasnt very crispy so it was a bit soggy with syrup. Service was quick but expect a long wait time.

name: Bruce Andrews
text: Good service and food.  All day breakfast.

name: Ariel Newby
text: Good prices and food food. It can get a bit busy but we've never had to wait long for a table and the staff have always been super friendly. The kids portions are on the bigger side which is nice since it means we'll have leftovers for our son for later.

name: Scott Fisher
text: Always good food and service.

name: Nicholas Key
text: I'd come here simply for the cinnamon rolls. Soft, warm, and sweet.

name: Peter Noreen
text: The food and service were quality. I think it is a bit over hyped. I avoid it at peak hours, especially brunch timeframe on the weekends, because it is a bit of a drive for us and waits can can exceed fifteen minutes, which I don't love. Also, if your waiter offers to take care of the check instead of taking it to the register, let them! We were trying to get out of the way so they could bus our table and said we had no problem cashing out at the register. We ended up behind folks cashing out and buying from their bakery and spent another ten minutes after our meal waiting to pay....

name: Bishop David
text: Great restaurant and friendly staff.  Wish I could eat there every day.

name: Cyrus Collier
text: Great food and very friendly atmosphere and staff. Great place to go for lunch and dinner to enjoy.

name: Marie B.
text: One of my favorite lunch spots. Friendly and attentive. Gluten free option for their burgers (lettuce wrap). I love this spot

name: natasha J
text: I lived here 12 years ago and I loved the cookie jar.... I have recently returned and I am pleased to say that it still serves great breakfast and the best cookies!!

name: Carl Jacobs
text: Good, but hard to live up to the reputation. Go for the cookies and burgers. I've heard breakfast is solid too. Locals love it - usually pretty busy.

name: J. J.
text: The morning of Friday March 25 2021 about 7 or 8 am. An elder 58yr went in to eat some breakfast drink some coffee read the news paper at the cookie jar. The staff brought him to a table, so he waited for a menu Well others came in and they were seated with menus. Eventually Their meals showed up. So the Elder attempted to ask one of staff about a menu, the staff walked pass and continued to Ignore him. So after the other customers Finished with their meal he decided to get up and leave.  That's a sad way to treat your elders. Majority of Fairbanks restaurants take care of their elders.Please help us bring attention to the situation by either pressing the like or any other action on this comment. No Elder should go through this. Thank you for taking the time to read this

name: Ariel Howard
text: Horrible service and food. Maybe it was an "off" day for them. All in all-- disgusted.

name: Tom Weissgerber
text: Had the BLT, it was good, but I was not overly impressed.

name: Shayna Lunt
text: Their cinnamon rolls are AMAZING! And even better, they had homemade caramel that was life changing! I've been for dinner and lunch.... But I'm hoping to make it there got breakfast soon!

name: Makayla Suttle
text: Their food is ok, the waitress was a little snippy with us. I wasn't done ordering and she interrupted me a few times. The cheese on my burger wasn't melted all the way. They were also out of cinnamon rolls.

name: Brian Stoltenberg
text: I absolutely love the cinnamon rolls

name: JAMES Bailey
text: Always excellent food

resp.text: Thank you James, we appreciate your taking time to comment.

name: J Grunder
text: I really enjoy the Cookie Jar. I’ve only been for breakfast and everything I’ve had so far has been made in house and is super fresh. They also have an excellent baked goods selection to take with you.

name: Dagoberto Perez
text: Fantastic food great portions

name: Jennifer Tanner
text: Three words: Corned. Beef. Hash.   OMG!!! FRICKIN AMAZING!!!! The chicken fried steak is awesome too. I'm a fat girl so my word is my bond.

name: Vincent
text: Very good. The prices really aren't that bad, and the food is excellent. The cookies they have are also great, which is a good thing considering their name. We had no problems with the service, and will most likely return

name: Pam Gresehover
text: Excellent Food, large portions, very nice waitstaff!!!!

name: Sheri Schoenberg
text: Clean, good service, great food

name: Cameron Stevenson
text: Delicious food, favorite place in Fairbanks yo grab some breakfast. Nice staff

name: Jonathan G
text: The chicken fried prime rib is to die for. Their cinnamon rolls are also some of the best that I've ever had.

name: catherine chamberlain
text: Great food and even better service

name: Mary Leith
text: As usual, we had a good lunch with cookies and coffee afterward. And it was decorated for the holidays with all the Christmas cookie jars out on the shelf.

name: Isaac Lendore
text: Good people. Service took long. But the servers were flexible. Didn't like the foid though.

name: Marilyn Bellows
text: Great food,wide variety of food to choose from. Large portions.

name: Faith Summerlin
text: Loved the cinnamon rolls

name: Jean Garry Antoine
text: Great service, greater customer service. So far one of the coolest place I've eaten at

name: Adrian Johnson
text: I have to get a cinnamon roll every time.,... Oh and breakfast too.

name: Bobby Patterson
text: Food was ok. Service was not. And they have added way to many tables. It's like sitting in an airplane

name: Michael Bushke
text: Always a great place for any meal.. warm atmostphere.. great alaskan hospitailty.. enjoy!!

name: Katie Brock
text: Never had a bad meal or bad service. Food is always the same and awesome. Love that it has sweet tea and amazing desserts

name: Will Lentz
text: Simple yet sophisticated fare for a good price. Make sure you grab a cookie on your way out!

name: Myra Powers
text: Great breakfast place. The cinnamon rolls looked wonderful but I ordered something else not so sweet. I was jealous of the roll that came to the next table, haha

name: Ashley Godbold
text: Fantastic breakfast. Timely service. It got busy fast and we were still taken care of. We will be back

name: Erez Kennan
text:
Very good food, kind service.
Not the cheapest option, but I think it's worth it. Might be too busy during rush hours.
Watch the opening hours on weekends.

name: Aria Gerbus
text: We've gone here twice and both times we were all very happy with the food and the service. It's American good and they do it very well!

name: Alexia Hines
text:
My fiance and I came here for brunch ~ I was especially excited because this diner had been on the show "diners, drive ins, & dives".
When we showed up the place was quite crowded but they said the wait for the table was only 15 minutes so we stuck around ~ and sure enough within about 15 minutes we found ourselves seated.
The diner was big - which was great. No cramped seating and yet there was an abundance of tables and chairs. Lots of windows gave the place an even more wide open feel. It was nice, wouldn't say cozy, but it had that good diner feel.
Gage and I ordered our drinks and food and then waited
And waited
And waited.
For about an hour and 20 minutes we waited for his montecristo sandwich and I waited for my side of house fries and stuffed nolan's.
Finally they came and boy oh boy did they look GOOD.
Big portions, AMAZING French fries, good house fries...
The montecristo sandwich was more like 2 French toasts with some meat on it. Good idea in theory. We didnt really see or taste any powdered sugar on it and it was a bit too much bread to meat ratio.
The Stuffed Noland was yummmmm - massive. Though it was more like round cinnamon french toast things sandwiched together with cream cheese filling between them (mmmmm ) and strawberries on top. Boy oh boy between those strawberries and the mountain of whipped cream on the side I thought I was in heaven. The only thing that disappointed me was the middle part of my Stuffed Nolan was undercooked and doughy.
Gage didnt mind and ate it anyway  but I cant say I'm a big fan of undercooked bread.

It was a pretty good experience over all minus the incredible wait times for food and the fact that we saw our waiter like 4 times in the 2 or more hours we were there.
I'd love to go back and give the place another try.
I think it's a great place with lots of potential and I'm hoping we will get the better end of the stick next time.

name: Kathy Hayes
text: As a vegetarian I had a very disappointing experience.  I didn't want greasy potato skins (the only item visibly vegetarian) so the waitress suggested jambalya.  It was $35 and was enough to sever 6!  Ridiculous!  Rice and veggies.  Seriously.  The service was slow and when we asked for bread while we waited we were told "no" you'll get it when your meal is served.  I was really disappointed.

name: Rachel Heath
text: My boyfriend and I came in for dinner and an $85 bottle of wine on 4/3/21. We were seated at the bar which we are usually fine with. The bartenders ignored us extensively throughout the night. The bottle of wine was opened incorrectly. The food runner slammed our food down and walked off. We asked for a to-go box for our appetizer and the busser cleaned the entire table including our silverware. It took 10-15 minutes for us to get replacement silverware while our entrée sat in front of us getting cold.  We were ignored until we asked for our check, at which time all of the staff suddenly started being nice to us. It was apparent that the staff wanted to flip the bar seats as quickly as possible. We were treated inhumanely and as cattle-- not humans who had come to this restaurant for a pleasant experience. Yes the blenders at the bar were running occasionally throughout the night but that did not bother us-- what bothered us was how extensively we were ignored the ENTIRE time we were there. The service was terrible from start to finish. I contacted this establishment after we left and they offered us a free dessert. We do not want dessert, we just want our money back and to never come to this restaurant again. We were not treated well and this is unacceptable. I personally feel like this is just theft. Additionally-- this place is completely packed out and there's no way this is following the state advisories for COVID safety.

name: Mat Pyles
text: Great food and drinks 🍸 the staff there was great to they treat us like we where family

name: Jake Klusewitz
text:
Very tasty food! We wrnt last weekend and arrive just before opening at 4:30. We were seated and got drinking within probably 20 minutes, and food within probably an hour. The food was great!! My pepper steak was cool fabulously, and the girlfriend got crab stuffed halibut.
The only downside is that if you’re looking for a nice, quiet date, this won’t be it. The staff are super quick, but it can be pretty jarring as you’re trying to have a nice conversation, and several times we had people reach in front of us to refill or waters without saying anything. It was good service and I didn’t mind, but it definitely made the girlfriend anxious.
Overall, we both liked it, but I wish we didn’t feel so rushed. :)

name: Brandon Hipsak
text: Cajun food is really good. Steak was fair, I've had better for cheaper.

name: DAVID PEASE
text: I will drive the hour and half just to eat here. A perfect mix of Cajun and Alaskan.

name: Lenett Trueblood
text: Previously had a bad experience with Double Musky, but decided to give it another shot and had a very pleasant experience the second time around! The food was great, the server was excellent and their Cajun delight (I think that’s what it’s called?) dessert was sooo good. Not sure if they were having an off night when I had visited before, but the food was fantastic this time!

name: Mari Rueter
text:
I love the Double Musky Inn! It's a gem located in Girdwood. They do Cajun cooking along with great steaks. I have enjoyed everything I've eaten there, well-known for their pepper steak. They have amazing jalapeno cheese bread, which you can take home so you have room for your main course. My favorite part is when they bring you the dessert tray at the end so you can see how delicious your choices are.
The atmosphere is unique with beautiful stained glass and treasures everywhere to give you that vibe of an Alaskan hang out. The staff is super friendly and very attentive!
They don't take reservations, so sometimes you have to wait for over an hour, but it's definitely worth the wait! They let you look for an open seat in their lounge so you can enjoy a drink and appetizers, makes the wait time fly by.

name: Fred Abell
text: Best Cajun food in alaska!! Crawfish dip and peppered steak are always delicious

name: Sean G
text: It was worth the drive down. Good food but I could tell that the staff was feeling the stress of the covid restrictions. Our server was not really present at all. She actually walked away from me a couple times when I was trying to ask her about something. I asked for a med/rare steak but got a med-med/well steak. Not wanting to add to their stress, I didn't complain or send it back. I'll give them another shot another time. Apps were delicious though and so was dessert. Those were home runs

name: Racahael Lowe
text: Absolutely delicious! Authentic Cajun food! Huge portions don't be afraid to share.  We ordered way to much but glad we did because we got to try a couple different things! Left stuffed!!

name: John Thain
text: One the best restaurants in Alaska, this place has excellent cajun style food. Arrive early, or be prepared to wait, especially during the peak of summer. The pepper steak is very popular. Seafood choices are also good. This place might have fancy food, but you won't look out of place if you are dressed in jeans and a t-shirt. The portions are huge, my wife and I both took home enough leftovers for a another meal.

name: Chano Williams
text: Very natural-feeling atmosphere with lots of wood and low-lighting. Somewhat crowded seating. Loud volume since everyone sits so close. Cluttered decor. Excellent serving staff. Delicious menu items that are fresh. Good dessert and appetizers. Expensive, but high quality experience.

name: Lorena Hendricks
text: Great service. Unique ambiance. A must try if you're in the area.

name: Hartsock Homestead
text:
Loud and annoying, but amazing food and service!

Bargain priced appetizers. ( Stuffed mushrooms ) included huge jalapeno cheese biscuits.

Generous sized steaks.

Kitchen and wait staff was accommodating to special requests.

If you are like me . . . A good steak does not need gravy, so might order gravy on the side for pepper steak :)

name: Tiffany Mann
text: AMAZING food! My steak was perfect and huge. So was my Hubbys. Salad was perfect. Hidden gem in the woods. Cant say enough. WE WILL BE BACK! and we will bring friends too.

name: Rexann Bassler
text: Best food ever! Fresh, hot, yummy. Wait staff is second to none. They are friendly, efficient, attentive. Worth the travel to girdwood.

name: Bobbi Jo Conner
text:
Intimate but not intimidating.  Service and food was top notch.
Will be "popping" in more often.

name: Cara H.
text: Service was excellent.  The host was quite organized and very friendly.  The place was packed on a Saturday evening but we didn't have to wait at the bar very long for our table.  Come early because they can run out.  Rack of lamb was all gone before 8pm!  We ordered a couple of appetizers--halibut ceviche and escargot stuffed mushrooms.  Enjoyed both but I can make better ceviche.  My shrimp and scallop cardinal had the right balance of spices.  Hubby's Alaskan crab stuffed halibut was pleasing.  Would come back to get that rack of lamb ;) and maybe the Jambalaya.  Riesling was unimpressive.  Overall had a great dining experience.  The lady who attended to us made sure our dinner was perfect.  They're closed on Mondays.

name: Kevina
text: One of my favorites!! It's always a pleasure to eat here, whenever I make it out to Girdwood. Great food, great service, great atmosphere. The wait time is totally worth it :)

name: Jason Williams
text: My favorite steak house on the planet.  By a long shot.  Get the Filet Mignon or the Pepper Steak.  I have been to a lot of steak houses all over the country and none compare to the Musky.  THE GREATEST!!

name: bublehed
text: Cozy little restaurant in Girdwood. Service was good as well as the food. We had the king crab legs and crab stuffed hallibut.

name: Theresa Philbrick
text:
Don't be put off by the wait. There are no reservations. So, if you arrive between 430-5pm on an evening when DM opens at 5. Just get in line. And, please, don't be a lazy butt and sit in your idling car next to the door. That's just tacky and rude.
Once the doors open, the line moves quickly.  Plus, the food and service are worth the wait. All the menu choices are delicious.
The fish is never overcooked, and the beef is tender, moist, and if you want it rare, you get it rare...slightly cool in the middle. I think the cook would probably NOT cook your beef to shoe leather...even if you asked nicely.
The side dishes such as the rice and vegetables are average. I suspect the vegetables are frozen as every now and then a broccoli floret was pretty cold. And, I'm less a rice eater these days so not so impressed by it.
We've eaten peel and eat shrimp in the bar, slurping down cold beers. At our various visits, we've supped on pepper steak, crab legs, and the salmon. We have savored etoufee and shrimp scampi. Pina coladas are delicious, as are martinis.
Desserts are predictably scrumptious. The only quibble I have about dessert is this...too much "cake" to "frosting" on the carrot cake. I'd like another 1" of frosting to go along with the 3 inches of cake.  The Musky is worth the drive from Anchorage or just down the road.

name: Michael Vanhorne
text: Food is good. Long wait to be seated. Son ordered steak medium and it came rare. By the time his steak was finally returned every one had eaten. Compared to other visits this was disappointing.

name: Dimitrios Alexiadis
text: Probably my favorite restayrant in Alaska, will be back.

name: Simon Denton
text: Amazing food and great service! Definitely worth calling ahead but was able to get a drink from the bar and wait outside for a table to open up. THE spot for dinner in Girdwood.

name: D Haas
text: Tried the peppered steak with gravy sauce, didn't really like it. But, customer service was excellent. Cleaning after every customer's table with disinfectant spray is an A++

name: Putz
text: Excellent food.  Huge portions.  Great atmosphere.  Be prepared to wait because of no reservations.  The peppercorn steak can easily feed 2 people in my opinion.  The creme brulee was very good as well.

name: Paul Markoff
text: Fantastic. My father would take me out to Girdwood and we would go out and eat at the Double Musky. Now I take my kids out to eat at the Musky. Excellent food and memories.

name: Jason Brunelle
text: Great everything

name: cathy b
text: It's ok.   You should arrive at least a 1/2 hour BEFORE they open and be prepared to stand in line. If you like cajun, spicy, large portions and super crowded you will enjoy.  It is eclectic to say the least.

name: Wes S
text: The peppered steak and carrots cake are amazing, I can't bring myself to order anything else

name: Benjamin Carney
text: Totally awesome,  very nice and friendly and top notch service and food..

name: Brandon Wheeler
text: Always terrific. Been years since we've last been, and was still fantastic! Shrimp in the Etouffee is still the only shrimp I've had that tastes like fresh spotted shrimp on the back of my dad's boat in Prince Williams Sound.

name: Kris Sisseck
text: There are no reservations at this classy cajun restaurant so come early or expect to wait. Good food and great service. I always enjoy my meal here. Check out the interesting decorations that litter the walls.

name: qbagcal
text: Food is excellent! Tasty and big portions, even for the people who can eat a lot. Not your typical high end appearance of fine dining But is a great small ski town feel. The 'Pepper Steak' is the best. Heads up on wait times because of the popularity. Got there before they open 45 minute (closed on Monday) and another 35 to 40 minute for food (party of 6).

name: Jeanne C.
text:
Great food. Excellent service
Steak is always great.
Carrot cake is the best in Alaska.

name: Judy D travel_andbeinspired
text: Very interesting place. Food was amazing and staff was great.

name: Justin Kjellstadli
text: Haven't had food that good in a long time

name: Matthew Muir
text: We only had appetizers and desserts in the lounge because the dining area was full by 4:45pm (the 430pm dinner crowd appeared to be bigger than the 6pm set). They were good, but nothing that memorable. Love their cookbook, but I expected more based on their reputation.

name: The Carlson Peeps
text:
Get there early, ideally before it opens. Otherwise, expect a wait.
The building doesn't look like much, outside or in, but...

Pros: Possibly the best service we have gotten at a restaurant. Ever. Bus-people and wait staff are constantly circulating, ensuring that glasses are filled, food is as expected, empty dishes are removed. They manage to be attentive and unobtrusive, a significant feat in and of itself.
The food is freaking amazing. Hubs had the Saturday only Prime Rib special, and said it was in his top five best steaks ever. I ate off the appetizer menu - beer batter halibut (with pecans in the batter) and hot crawfish dip. Amazing. Portions are large - we had leftovers. Dessert was also amazing.

Cons: None!

name: Andrew Thomason
text: Amazing food, beautiful location. There is sometimes a wait-list always worth it. AMAZING COCKTAILS. Get the signature drink.

name: B D
text: They serve very generous portions and the staff was was very attentive.  The restaurant has a very Alaskan backcountry feel, and the menu has a lot of Alaskan options.. we had the prime rib, pepper steak and the jambalaya.  The prime rib was cooked well, however was missing flavor below the rubbed crust.  The pepper steak was also cooked well.  The most flavorful dish for us was the jambalaya.

name: Catherine Kenney
text: Loved this place!  Super local, awesome experience.  Food was spot on and the service was impeccable.  Expect a wait time even at 5 pm.... Lovely evening with new friends!  Enjoy.  Oh and for you wine enthusiast, there wine room is fantastic as the wine list.  Enjoy!!  Great job Double Musky team!!

name: John Palmer
text: This is always the first place I try to eat at when visiting Girdwood. The atmosphere here is unlike any other. Food is expensive but I’ve never had a bad meal. They’re famous for their pepper steak but if you try it make sure you’re sharing with someone. It’s huge.

name: Shane Mecham
text:
No reservations makes this a real gem.  Come early and stay a while.  Grab a seat in the bar while waiting for a table.  Its standing room only most times, and don't hesitate to share a space.  Alaskans are friendly after all.  Lots of options in the bar with appetizer menu and drinks.  Staff is great about shuffling you, drinks and bills when time to seat in dinning room.
The Muskie is a always lively.  Its made more so by having a good attitude and being patient.  Once seated, service is pretty fast.  Portions are large, so plan to being food home.  If you are in Girdwood at the hotels, use a shuttle or carpool.  Parking can be a hastle, so reducing cars in the lot is nice where you can, plus this also promotes responsible fun.
Deserts are great and they have many, so save some room.  Drink options are really good if a little limited, which is understandable for the location.  But I've never had a bad drink in my many visits.
Definitely worth the wait in my opinion.

name: Steven Kalmes
text: Always great food

name: Melody Willis
text: The pasta was superb and our waiter was fantastic!

name: Tiffany Su
text: Food is always great hit the spot.  They raised a lot of the price on the food.

name: Gregory Adrien
text: This place is amazing as usual!!! Steak tips are the best I've ever had in my life. Lobster is too nitch and the carrot cake is to die for!

name: M & E Walsborn
text: The food is amazing! Well worth the drive and you definitely get what you pay for. We will be back!

name: Charles Case
text: Not many vegan options which is completely understandable but otherwise the rest of the food and alcohol was pretty good. Waitress was incredibly thoughtful and well-briefed with the contents in the menu.

name: Tom Tunnell
text: Great steak. Prime rib was a little tasteless. It's like the piece we got was missed by the seasoning. Staff was awesome.

name: Shannon Nysewander
text: Amazing as Always

name: Pete Donahoo
text:
One of the best meals I've had in Alaska! The pepper steak was done to perfection and cooked so perfect! The Alaska king crab was killer and as a bonus being pre-split it was so easy to enjoy! The stuffed halibut is so flaky and flavorful it's well worth the market price! We started with the Cajun popcorn and it was well worth it! We didn't end up getting our salads but that was all right because the meal in the service was stellar!
Also be sure to enjoy the homemade rolls and butter!

name: Cinderblock907
text:
Come for the decor and stay for the food!

Fair warning, this place does NOT take reservations and does NOT split checks. So first come first serve and better keep your parties small if you enjoy having money in your wallet.

This is a hole in the wall restaurants that every Alaskan knows about and will most likely make a pilgrimage to at least once in their life. If you're a first time visitor, you'll probably notice the line going out the door, and for good reason. The food and service here is fantastic. People say you can never go wrong with a prime rib, but I say why have something you can get at any steak house when you can get what they are famous for. The peppered steak! Now just because I recommend the steak, don't let it detour you from trying anything else on the menu. It's All good. Don't forget to try dessert while you're there. The Cajun Delight is out of this world.

Though with that being said be prepared for a hefty price tag for your meal. For 2 adults, expect to see a $100 or more on the bill.

So if you find yourself in Girdwood around dinner, then I highly suggest to swing by and treat yourself to some great food.

name: Mariah Henson
text: Must visit! Best restaurant in Girdwood. Creole meets Alaska seafood, yum!

name: Grace Hudson
text: Friendly and helpful and polite and the food is the boom

name: Sarah Jeter
text: What a cool restaurant!  Amazing food, as well. So happy they were able to easily accommodate our large group and were such lovely people to dine with. We'll definitely be back, probably more for a quieter, more romantic meal.

name: Mark Jensen
text: Not impressed. Sorry but my food was too salty and the service was not hospitable. I felt like I was just another ticket. The three stars is because I saw locals there that I know and they seemed to enjoy the place.

name: Jw Douthitt
text:
I loved the atmosphere and the smugness of the place. We saw an episode on a food channel that went to Alaskan venues. So we finally made it there. We are from Ohio and had  heard all the rumors and yes, They were right!
Great service, staff was very courteous,  the food was great! Total satisfaction.
We will return!!!

name: Dean Balzmi
text: Large portions and creative Alaskan dinners make this a great place for your plans.  Their water comes from glaciers

name: Erik Molby
text: Needed a wheelchair after. Portions are HUGE. And food was amazing!

name: Bonnie Wall
text: Best meal in Alaska! The Marti Gras theme surprised me but the food--amazing!  Most entrees are $31 - $45 which is high for my budget, but we would totally do it again and again. It was that good. The portions were Alaska-sized, meaning huge, so you can split a meal and still be full. Word of warning: don't fill up on the delicious jalapeno cheddar rolls before your food comes. The servers are happy to wrap up all the leftovers including rolls to take home. If you don't order their signature Pepper Steak for your entree, get the Pepper Steak Tips appetizer so you can get a taste of the award-winning flavor. Plan ahead to order dessert 'to go' because you don't want to miss the carrot cake or other scrumptious items. One order will feed 4.

name: Andy Rodriguez
text: I was very excited about going to Double Musky, everyone that had been to it had nothing but great things to say. But! I'm sad to say i was very disappointed! Normally I'm not over-critical about food but when I pay $30-$50 a plate and the food is terrible, I have to be straight up. All the seafood was overcooked we paid $197 for overcooked food (3 entrees, 3 appetizers, 1/2 lb of crab legs, and some drinks). The avocado in my and my friend's ceviche was brown i cant believe that was served. I suggest you take your money elsewhere. The only reason I gave it 2 stars was because the customer service was pretty good and the free bread was good too.

name: Erin Scott
text: The Double Musky is a place everyone tells you that you need to go in Girdwood. It definitely is and the sooner we had was a lot of fun. The problems are huge, especially the pepper steak the size of which could feed a small family. While the food was good it wasn't amazing but the wine and atmosphere made up for the "only pretty good" good. Would definitely come here again and order smaller plates.

name: Brandon Randall
text: Only open for business for a few hours. You ad better be early if you want to get a table. Service was decently fast, and very friendly. The steak is phenomenal, melt in your mouth delicious.

name: Cas Rudy
text: Service was fantastic, atmosphere was perfect for a big birthday dinner. All the food (appetizers, meals, and desserts) that all 7 of us got were AMAZING. The only thing better than the food was the drinks. The hot buttered rum was the best I've ever had, and all the other cocktails I tried were delicious and a decent size for the price. Decor was great too!

name: Traci Lennox
text: This was a very interesting experience.  I had heard mixed reviews prior to my trip so I wasn't sure what to expect.  It was really good!  I wish there was a rating for 4.5 stars because that's what I really wanted to give it.  Service was fairly slow (likely because it was pretty crowded), but that's the only knock I really have.

name: Andre Alexander
text: Great food, great prices,  limited seating mitigated by pre- seating.  Often times restaurants neglect their waiting customers,  but waiting here is a social meet-up and appetizer experience where you eventually move to scenic tables and delicious food prices moderately compared to its portions. Staff is busy but attentive and polite. Food 5/5, overall experience 4/5 because im impatient.  Wouldn't recommend in a hurry,  but perfect for a weekend evening meal or special occasion.

name: Dean Moberg
text: Best in Alaska period! Don't go there enough & never could!

name: Bruce Templeton
text: Service is excellent. Food is excellent. Been here many times and never have had a bad experience. I strongly recommend the Jacked Up Shrimp appetizer. It's awesome.

name: Peter Newman
text: Long wait to be seated, crowded, noisy, uncomfortable chairs, overpriced, food is not bad but is overrated. Service is good. Few vegetarian options.

name: rick h
text: Great Cajun spices but if you want to get a table at the first seating you should show up around 4 o'clock and wait on line. Otherwise you can usually get a table around 6 when the first tables start leaving. If you do a later seating the specials are probably going to be gone though.

name: Noah Miller
text: Always fun going there it opens at 5pm but it is wise to get there beforehand. A long line is usually forming by 445pm. Food is very delicious but expensive. Warning they bring out a tray of desserts and if you say yes they just put in on your table (whichever you choose). Very hard to resist

name: Deena Opiela
text: The best smothered steak I have ever had. Great atmosphere, excellent food

name: Dow Jopp
text: Alaskan standard that keeps with it's tradition of great food.

name: Brice Wilbanks
text: The double musky is a great place to have dinner. The only down side is always the amount of people in the restaurant. It is packed! This leads to longer wait times for a table, but it is totally worth it! Food is  spot on and The Double Musky offers many different flavors for all tastes. Servers are always nice and friendly. Although, sometimes attention to guests is minimal. It is understandable seeing how busy it is all the time! Overall great food worth the visit.

name: Mandi Ward
text: Wonderful experience from start to finish. The decor is eclectic and fun. We sat in a corner booth drinking a bottle of wine people watching. The food was a bit pricey but when it came the large portion size didnt disappoint. The scallops as nf shrimp dish was packed with flavor. My date said his pepper corn steak was a beautifully seasoned and a perfect medium rare. We will return! Desert is also a must here!

name: Don Moore
text: Our drinks and appetizers were amazing, especially the scallop mushrooms. And the service was top notch too.

name: Justin Savage
text: By far the best food we had during our visit. Be prepared to to wait, not a good place for but parties, it makes the experience so much better!

name: Rose Gueco
text: Loved the jalapeño bread, big and soft. First time there and ordered the peppered steak, it was HUGE I could only eat 1/3 of it. Ate another 1/3 the next day and my son finally helped finish it. Staff was very friendly. I love these kinds of eclectic places. The owner of the place went to visit tables and at a group of 6 near us I listened to his story and he's a good story teller and he gave all 6 a free book about his story. We'll be back for sure, want to try the lamb.

name: Jason Nesslage
text: Excellent food, excellent service! Have been going here for the last 20 years and everything is the same! Even some of the staff have been there for ever. You can tell owner/mngt take care of their personnel.

name: Travis drewry
text: Long wait but worth every minute of it. Food is always on point!

name: YK E
text: I love their food

name: Jon Kotwicki
text: Good food, lots of butter

name: Erik Ottosen
text: Some recipes have changed, but the overall quality hasn't. The gumbo is still the real thing, the pepper steak is still the best in the US, and the atmosphere is still very active. Be aware that the owners still do not take reservations - ever - so be there before opening if you want to be sure to get a seat.

name: Cindy Bishop
text: Great local feel, quaint decor, very good appetizers, friendly service

name: Martin Bargo
text: Best escargot I ever tried

name: storm heames
text: Great food, fun atmosphere, really good people

name: Cal Craig
text: Kinda funky place. Some people are crazy for this place. Its good, but I don't get the craze.

name: Nicholas Conrad
text: Quite possibly the best restaurant in the state. Everything on the menu is absolutely delicious, but with a decidedly "Alaska casual' decor that invites you to eat amazing food without worrying about getting dressed up. The prime rib routinely runs out, so get their early if you're craving some horseradish-y goodness.

name: Diana Banks
text: Fun place, great bar and and good food. Try the Coconut salmon appetizer. My Musky Mule was good.

name: Sharolyn Wyeth
text: Can't beat the Musky, for great food & great service! Every time we go, I say I'm going to try something new, but how can you go to there & not get the pepper steak? It's OUTSTANDING! Thankfully, my husband always gets the cajun fried game hen, so I can steal from his plate. Don't expect to have room for dessert...Thank goodness they'll pack your dessert to go!!! :)

name: Rose M Meneses
text: Great food and great service

name: Sue Miller
text: Food was excellent as always, we had a large party that ate there, 19 in our party so they made good money off us. One waitress was extremely rude to one of our tables plus we were rushed with our meals. Very disappointing for the service

name: William W
text:
Not sure what people are talking about with dishware cleaning, from what I seen from the bar -  they used a dish rag to scrub each glass in a hot soap bath before a double rinse.

The food is absolutely amazing. Best in Alaska, especially the pepper corn new York.  Their coconut salmon is epic, as the plum sauce is the winner here.

Wife had the fettuccine and it was alright, 8.5/10. The peppercorn steak tho, 10/10.

Bomb drinks too. Love it.

Minus the wait. Screw the wait. (personal rant)

name: Aeronca Chump
text: You'll most likely be seated or greeted by the owner and not even know it. What a great host. Great food and great atmosphere

name: Tim Sorenson
text: Great place to eat if you find yourself in Girdwood around 430 PM. My favorite is the pepper steak but everything is really good. Sometimes we just order a mix of appetizers with drinks, they're large enough servings to be a dinner. They don't take reservations so if you're on a time budget arrive before 430 and get in line for first seating. If you don't arrive there's a bar to chill in. Our kids love to play I Spy. You could play forever at Double Musky. We've been eating there for 30 years and enjoy it every time we go.  As with any restaurant, food quality and service can vary a bit but overall we find both consistently very good.

name: Kymberly Coffey
text: Great service... Food and drinks... Thanks for my 🎂 🍨

name: Mike
text: Fantastic Peppercorn steak and stuffed Halibut! Shrimp in cheese sauce app was amazing. Excellent service for our large group of 18!

name: Gabe Gonzalez
text: Great food! Great atmosphere! Highly recommend a Steak or the Halibut!

name: William Burton
text: Food was great service was ok food portions were just enough bread was good but probably will not go back what you get for what you pay is off its been 2 years and still no desire to go back

name: Chris Rac
text: Amazing food and drinks.  Wished they were open on Mondays and wished they took reservations.  It sucks making that two hour drive from Palmer not knowing how long of a wait you're looking at.  Who cares though... pepper steak and carrot cake are the best in the country.

name: Chris Breck
text: Great food and a cool atmosphere. Always a treat to go to the Double Musky. Had the game hen with mashed potatoes and it did not disappoint. Can't wait to go again.

name: Matt Richardson
text: Great service and I think everything on the menu looks amazing! Had the pepper steak, very good...

name: Linda McLendon
text: My only favorite restaurant in alaska..except for golden corral. Oink oink...my only favorite meal is the pepper steak. They no longer include a salad in the meal price. You must order separately. Their pepper bread is phenomenal.

name: Woo Tang
text: All I can say is it's well worth the wait. Outstanding food and attentive staff.

name: Lili Gulsby
text: Good food. Nice atmosphere

The pepper sauce itself was mediocre, the menu boasts that a food network personality named it best steak in America.  I've had better steaks at casual diners in Italy and France...understandably the steak supply chain is probably not the greatest in Alaska.  At the end of the night, the food wasn't amazing and just not worth the +100 we spent after food and drink, nor the drive.

text: Unfortunately, it was our first time there and we had the worst server since moving to Alaska. Truly unfortunate because we brought family visiting after having the best day on Girdwood. Terrible ending to an awesome day. We only got as far as the appetizer, but we will say that if the stuffed mushrooms were any indication of the quality of food, the rest must be amazing! We also had drinks. One of our drinks, the crown and water, was very watery. When we asked that it be fixed or changed, that server rudely told us that it was because it was a crown and water and that they are strict about making sure the crown is exactly 2.5 oz. We then asked for crown without water and mixed it with the same amount of water and it was significantly darker in color than the watery drink. We highly recommend Seven Glaciers Bar instead. We had the exact same drinks there and they were tons better. Thankfully, the manager apologized and reassured us that she would address the issue head on with the server. We hope so in the event we dare chance bringing people there again. She even made some recommendations to other restaurants in the area we could try insteaf. The ambiance was fun and family oriented. name: Ryan Stafford
text:
In my opinion this IS the best restaurant in Alaska for a steak dinner.

There are many restaurants in Alaska that claim to have the best tasting steaks, but I doubt you'll find a steak as amazing and original as the French Pepper Steak! If you're early to dinner then order the Prime Rib. The Prime Rib is sold out often and like the French Pepper Steak the cut is huge!

My favorite appetizer is the Scallop Stuffed Mushrooms Rockefeller. There are 6-8 upside down mushrooms with a scallop inside and covered in a tasty butter sauce. I recommend you spoon some sauce on a piece bread because the sauce will make the bread taste amazing!

I miss the dinner rolls they had like 10 years ago. The bread was softer and there were actual pieces of jalapeño and melted cheese in the rolls. These dinner rolls were just as large as the ones you can get today. At one time you had to pay extra for these dinner rolls, that's how filling and tasty they were. Today these rolls are complementary again, but the tops of the rolls are burnt and there are only small pieces of jalapeños and cheese.

Finally some helpful information:

1. Get here early!
2. No reservations!
3. Parking is limited
4. Seating is very tight
5. This place gets very loud, seriously.
6. Parking lot is rock and mud, so walk carefully.

Enjoy your dinner!

name: Brandy Willett
text: As one of the only sit down restaurants in North Pole, Pagoda does a good job keeping up with demand. Service is typically prompt both from the wait staff and the kitchen. Portion sizes are huge, so bring a big appetite, someone to share with, or prepare to take home leftovers. Try the House Broccoli with shrimp, beef, chicken, baby corn, carrots, mushrooms, and of course, broccoli. Enjoy!

name: Laura Cipielewski
text: This is the hot spot in North Pole, Alaska. The food is very good and the portions are generous. Two of us split the Happy Family dish which was plenty for us.The parking lot is always full. The service was prompt and pleasant. You can often find the owner checking on tables and asking if his patrons are happy or need anything. They have a well stocked bar. Overall great place to eat.

name: Mike Hector
text: Best Asian cuisine in all the land.

name: Cody Fox

Food is delivered very fast after ordering, all of the staff operate in a professional and friendly manner, making their rounds to each table, far more frequently than other restaurants in the fairbanks and north pole areas. name: Terry Oakes
text: It is always a pleasure to go to the Pagoda restaurant.  The only thing better than the service is the FOOD!!!  If you get a chance to go try the Mongolian Beef, it is the best.

name: James Perrizo
text: I have never had a meal at Pagoda that I didn't truly enjoy.  The quality and abundance of every meal means you get to enjoy it more than once.  Benny's longtime staff are always pleasant.  A couple of the must try items on the menu are the walnut shrimp, dragon steak (any meat or fish with dragon sauce will be great) and the ribeye.  You can't go wrong at Pagoda.

name: John McCain
text: Great food (in my opinion). They will always make sure that you have refills on soda and water. It is a good place for family dinners, going on a date, or even if you are just craving Chinese food. They also offer delivery to North Pole and Eielson AFB. The meals are decently priced and you get a large amount of food for what you pay for. Customer service is amazing. Also, every group gets free Jasmin tea.

name: Nicholas Baker
text: I have lived in North Pole for roughly 4 years now and eaten Pagoda at least once a month since then. First couple of time I ate here, both dine in and to-go, it was great! Prices were reasonable for the food, wait time was never terrible, and the staff was kind and attentive. But, recently(as in the last 4-5 months) the food has been subpar, the portion sizes have gotten smaller, and the prices have increased 3-5$ per meal. Now instead of having a tremendous Chinese restaurant right down the road I choose to drive into Fairbanks and order elsewhere.

name: Johnny Danger
text: Best Chinese food I've ever had!

name: David Claar
text:
Best Chinese food in the interior! This place is always busy, yet they find a way to quickly seat you. After ordering, the food is promptly served. The speed of the service always amazes me. Finally, the food is consistently delicious!
For me, staples such as egg rolls, bbq pork, walnut shrimp, dragon shrimp, and Mongolian beef always satisfy! Nothing like the crunchy egg roll and moist pork dipped in their hot mustard to get the meal started. The walnut shrimp has perfectly cooked shrimp covered with a sweet sauce and candied walnuts. This appetizer is a surprisingly delicious combination. The Mongolian beef is amazing! The meat is always tender with a peppery flavor. The dragon shrimp is a uniquely spiced sauce with perfectly cooked shrimp and veggies.
I absolutely love this restaurant! Great job staying consistently great for all these years!!!

name: John Pile

text: Everyone raves about the place and I would agree it is one of the best in North Pole.  Don’t go late at night.  The food is heavy but good.

name: Karla Jacobsen
text:
I really wanted to like it. Everyone else in town always raves about how great it is. The dining area was nice. The staff was great, friendly & attentive.
The problems I had came from our food. I ordered General Tso's Chicken. Its my go to for Chinese Food. I think someone in the kitchen must have been confused because there was so much vinegar it tasted like a spicy Sweet & Sour Chicken. The breading on the chicken looked so nice, golden and delicious. The first few pieces were great, airy & crisp breading and juicy chicken. Perfect. After that, the rest of the chicken pieces were that gorgeous golden fried color but inside was a different story. The chicken was barely warm and the breading was still pasty batter where it touched the chicken. Our table also requested that our food to please be made without MSG, since I can't have the MSG that they add to foods. The waitress made a note and said it wouldn't be a problem. Well, there was MSG. I started bloating before we left the restaurant. At the moment I thought maybe I had eaten too much but I ate way less than I normally do. By the time my friend & I made it back to Fairbanks I couldn't wait to get home. My stomach hurt so bad. I guess, if I ever try Pagoda again, I'll really have to stress the importance of my request and not order breaded fried food.

name: Alexia Hines
text:
My husband and I were starving and ready to tear up some delicious pizza. I discovered the Hungry Robot on yelp and we decided to give it a try.

They used to be in a food truck from my understanding, but now they have a permanent location. The little pizza shop was just big enough for their toppings bar, the cash register, a bench to sit on for those who choose to wait inside, and their 2 brick ovens which could be seen outside of the shop. This isnt a sit and dine place so call ahead to order your pizza so you can skip the wait.

The menu has lots of interesting pizzas to choose from and they have a monthly special as well - something I saw on their menu inside and not on their website.

We ordered 3 small pizzas - each for about $10. (Medium pizzas are about $20 each) Then the wait began. We did have to wait for about 20 or 30 minutes but we sat in the parking lot and colored (err.. I colored and tried to get my husband to color with me lol) while those delicious pizzas cooked.

We finally got our pizzas which barely made it back to the hotel with us because they smelled  SO GOOD.

The margherita pizza was my favorite - it lacked no flavor whatsoever with its delicious hand made sauce and fresh basil. I loved the fresh mozzarella - there was just enough but not too much that it made you feel gross from all the heavy cheese. It let the generous amount of pizza sauce shine through.
We also got the dilly dilly - I'm the pickle lover but my husband liked this one more than I did. The pickles go great on the pizza (surprisingly) but it was so heavy from all the cheese that I couldn't make it past 1 slice.
Our final pizza was the chicken bacon pizza. I didnt get to try it but my husband loved it so much, he ate the entire thing. That's a compliment considering hes very good at stopping when hes full, but this pizza had him eating and eating until he felt like he was going to pop.

Needless to say this is our new go- to pizza place here in Fairbanks. We will definitely be ordering some for our next gathering with friends.

text: Over priced, limited menu and pizza quality is inconsistent.  Prefer East Ramp, if you want authentic wood-fired flavor give it a shot.  Owner’s rebuttal to my review failed to mention their inconsistency.  East Ramp is consistent, hybrid oven or not.

resp.text:
Hello,  I am sorry you feel we are overpriced but we are actually cheaper than the place you are recommending.  I do not like picking apart other local businesses but you are comparing us directly so I feel we need to address the differences.  Here is a comparison - A Veggie pizza from us is $20, the same pizza from East Ramp would be $18 (at least we think as their menu stops at 7 toppings and that pizza has 9), our pizza is even 43 cubic inches bigger.  That means you get 1/3 more pizza for $2 more in cost, yet we are overpriced?  You mention that we have a limited menu, but we have over 30 different ingredients and East Ramp offers 21.  We make our sausage in house, purchase locally raised meats and use organic ingredients and are still comparable in price.  You also mention that if people want authentic wood-fired flavor they should go to East Ramp yet they cook in a GAS oven and we actually use WOOD since it is a wood fired pizza.  Their oven is a hybrid gas oven that can additionally burn wood, ours is purely a wood fired oven.  If people would like authentic wood fired pizza they can come to us or go to Alaska Coffee Roasting Company on Geist as we are the only two wood fired ovens in city limits.

Part 2 - you speak of consistency. We are content doing what we do, Fairbanks seems fine with us doing what we do. Is this related somehow to DPW?  Did I not do something for you at work and you feel the need to try and drag my business down?  We have been in the top three pizza places in Fairbanks for three years, we took second in state last year. We have grown from one oven to three in as many years. I won’t waste my time replying over and over to a review that most likely has no merit. Thank you for coming in, I hope you are happy with your pizza at East Ramp.

name: Vincent Sabio
text:
The ziprider is great, and the ropes course (Adventure Park) was fun. The food at the Smokehouse was overpriced and marginal at best. We were planning to take sandwiches with yes, but were told we couldn't bring food into the island lest we attract bear. Our luggage was never inspected for food, and those who were in the know brought their own food into the island with them.

The activities, while fun, are disorganized. We weren't instructed on where to go, then received conflicting instructions, we were never told what our rally time was for the ziprider so they had to reschedule us for later in the day, etc. The townspeople are nice and are great to chat with.

Despite the disorganization, we're still glad we signed up for the ziprider and the Adventure Park. It was better than staying on the ship for the day. Next time, we'll bring food. 😊

name: Mason Reilly
text:
Absolutely beautiful. The rangers are very friendly and knowledgeable, and they do a great job of guiding you through the park. If you're doing a boat tour, expect to see and learn about some very fascinating birds. You will almost definitely see sea lions, humpback whales, and sea otters. You have a chance of seeing orcas, mountain goats, and bears, but it's less likely. I've been here all summer and I've only seen one wolf for a split second.

The glaciers are awe inspiring. If you have a choice, I would recommend John Hopkins, as the approach around Jaw Point gives you a really unique perspective on glaciers, which helps to wrap your mind around the scale of the things.

Overall - highly recommend.

name: Amandeep Godara
text: Glacier Bay National Park and Preserve occupies the northernmost section of the southeastern Alaska coastline, between the Gulf of Alaska and Canada. The Canada–US border approaches to within 15 miles (24 km) of the ocean in the St. Elias Mountains at Mount Fairweather, the park's tallest peak at 15,300 feet (4,700 m), transitioning to the Fairweather Range from there southwards. The Brady Icefield caps the Fairweather Range on a peninsula extending from the ocean to Glacier Bay, which extends from Icy Strait to the Canada–US border at Grand Pacific Glacier, cutting off the western part of the park. To the east of Glacier Bay the Takhinsha Mountains and the Chilkat Range form a peninsula bounded by the Lynn Canal on the east, with the park's eastern boundary with Tongass National Forest running along the ridgeline. The park's northwestern boundary, which also abuts Tongass National Forest, runs in the valley of the Alsek River to Dry Bay. The preserve lands comprise a small area at Dry Bay — the majority of Glacier Bay lands are national park lands. The park boundary excludes Gustavus at the mouth of Glacier Bay. The lands adjoining the park to the north in Canada are included in Tatshenshini-Alsek Provincial Park.
