name: 金山劳模
text:
(Translated by Google) The Glacier Bay National Park and Reserve was named in 1980, and it covers an area of ​​10,784 square kilometers. This national park has no roads to connect with the outside world, but hundreds of thousands of tourists visit every year.
Glacier Bay (Glacier Bay) was formed in the Little Ice Age 4,000 years ago. Thousands of years later, the glaciers continued to move forward and reached their peak in 1750. However, since then, the glaciers began to melt back. Covering 3.3 million hectares, it is surrounded by steep mountains and can only be reached by boat or plane.

Best experience: Kayaking in the ice and snow

The presence of 11 glaciers entering the sea has made Glacier Bay National Park a world-famous ice and snow wasteland. These glaciers connect the mountains and the sea and bring blue ice blocks of different shapes, sizes and colors to the sea.

In order to enter the Gulf of Moore in Glacier Bay, you have to raft the ocean — kayak off the coast of Alaska and experience extreme tide changes, icy seawater, and the violent winds and waves that may be encountered. No matter where you turn, in this large park you can see the glacier in the sea recast the park like a knife. Humpback whales, black bears, seals and vultures may also be seen here.

(Original)
冰河湾国家公园及保护区是1980命名的，它占地10784平方公里。这一国家公园无公路跟外界连接，但每年都有数十万的游客来参观。
冰河湾（Glacier Bay）形成于四千年前的小冰河时期，数千年后冰河不断向前推进，并在1750年时达到鼎盛，然而自此之后冰河却开始融化后退。占地330万公顷，围绕在陡峭的群山中，只能乘船或飞机到达。

最佳体验：在冰天雪地里划一次皮划艇

11座入海冰川的存在让冰川湾国家公园成为世界著名的冰雪荒原，这些冰川连接了群山和大海，并为海面带来形状、大小和色泽各异的蓝色冰块。

为了进入冰川湾的穆尔湾，你得泛舟大洋—在阿拉斯加沿海划皮划艇，感受极端潮汐变化、冰冷彻骨的海水以及可能遭遇的狂风巨浪。无论转向何方，在这座大公园里都能看到入海冰川如刻刀般重铸公园大地。在这里还可能看到座头鲸、黑熊、海豹和秃鹫。

name: Andrew Elegante
text:
A tale of 2 pizzas (or experiences):

The first day I went was during a relatively quiet time around lunch. I ordered the northern lights pizza but asked if I could substitute portabello mushrooms for the chicken because I'm vegetarian (and had checked to see that they had portabellos on a different pizza) . The very cheerful server said she had to ask to make sure it would be okay but she thought that it would.

After a few minutes she came back and confirmed it was ok so I placed my order and ate the more beautiful of the 2 pizzas in my pictures. The spicy aoli was especially delicious. I ate half and she packed the rest up and I joyfully ate it later at the Savage River picnic area in Denali. Nobody mentioned an upcharge for the substitution and I don't recall there being one on the bill.

The pizza was so good that 2 days later I went back for another one, this time in the evening. It was pretty busy with the only open seat being at the bar. I sat down and waited a few minutes to get a menu and a water cup then tried to order the same thing. The bartender was surprisingly harsh and told me he could do that but he'd have to charge me for the mushrooms. I was confused because this wasn't what I had experienced the previous time. He said it was very busy and that wouldn't work then he pointed to a part of the menu that says no substitutions and told me that if he tried to put my order in the chef would come out and yell at him. When I reiterated, somewhat sheepishly given the level of aggression I felt, that I was just confused because that's not what happened 2 days prior he called the general manager over. When I explained to him what happened my prior visit he got a surprised look on his face and said that wasn't how they normally did it but they would do it again since that's what I'd had before. I thanked him and the bartender asked him to go explain that to the chef.

Later my pizza came out, on a very beat up pan, with a sparse amount of generic mushrooms and without the aoli and cilantro. When I mentioned it to the bartender he apologized and got it properly dressed. I don't know if this was a test to see if I'd actually had three pizza or not but it seemed strange that this pizza the GM had talked to the chef about came out wrong. The pizza came back properly dressed (photo with weird lighting as a result of some overhead obstruction that made it hard to see where I was sitting)  It was still good, but not as good as when it had the portobello mushrooms on it. I ate the whole thing this time, paid and left. After the ordering process the bartender was friendlier so I gave my customary 20%.

I've owned a restaurant so I understand that there are always reasons for things. High volume kitchens perform best when they execute a set menu without variations so preparing things becomes reflexive and having substitutions can interrupt that, slow things down, create more errors and require more training. I also know that the food cost for chicken is way higher than mushrooms (at least in my market) and that their margin on the item would probably be higher with my substitution.

I also understand that sometimes you're not having a great day or something gets you fired up so you don't treat the customers as well as you might like so I'm not too put off by the bartender's initial behavior.

I do have two suggestions for the managers (from my relatively blind customer point of view):

1) The apparent conflict between the kitchen and the servers/bartenders probably should be addressed as it seems to be spilling over to customers

2) where you have chicken as the main protein on your menu consider offering the choice of portabellos or chicken to open up more of your menu to vegetarians (potentially increasing your margins)

Also keep up the good work on these pizzas. The crust is amazing!

This place is not staffed correctly to handle the amount of business available to them in the summer. Unless you came to Denali to sit around for 2+ hours waiting for a carryout pizza order don't waste your time!

name: David Perez
text:
Great pasta selection and within walking distance from the resorts.
Moderately expensive.

name: Sara McCaffree
text: The crust was pretty thick for me but it was tasty, the kids liked it and the ambiance is really great.  Don't go if you don't like seeing live animal pelts everywhere.  😉 Warning: the tomato soup is actually a pepperoni pizza in a bowl. My parents loved it.

name: Bill M
text: They should rename this restaurant "the roller coaster" because it was a series of ups and downs, so brown bear with me *ba dum tisss*. We walked in and were seated immediately. Very tight seating. service was muy bien (very good) but it took around 30 to 45 minutes for the food to come out. Food was delicious, portions could satisfy a lumberjack, and the ambiance was all designed by Gaston from Beauty and the Beast.... antlers everywhere. Would recommend but consider other options if you aren't dead set on this place.

name: Steve Frost
text: Wow! This place definitely lives up to it's hype. Me, my wife, and our friends all loved our pizzas and the beer was great. Also, the gluten free dough/vegan pizza tasted just like regular pizza, which is not exactly easy for most pizza joints.

name: Laura Yvonne Pelletier
text: One of the few dog friendly eateries we've found in Alaska.   Dogs (in stroller) were welcomed at outdoor patio.  And the pizza was excellent...the crisp crust done to perfection!  We had originally gotten the pizza to go,  expecting the traditional card box box handed to us.  But....they also handed us a bag with paper plates, napkins, red pepper and parmesan packets, and hand wipes!  Everything one would need to enjoy the meal.  When we found out the dogs were welcome and decided to stay, our table was set with dishware and water provided.  Service was as excellent as the pizza!

resp.text: Thanks for dropping in, Laura, and for the review!  Which pizza did you get on your visit? I have been craving our North of the Border pizza, it has grilled chicken, corn and jalapeño mix, cilantro, cotija cheese, and chipotle aioli. Its to die for! Hope to see you back soon!

name: Aditi Partani
text: What a delicious pizza in that very small place. We got the recommendations from some local people from Denali and we decided to give it a try and had amazing experience. Food was delicious. Totally in awe for this place.

name: James Wells
text: The best pizza I have had in a long while.  Well worth the drive from Fairbanks or a good stop when passing through Denali Park.

resp.text: Thanks for stopping in and choosing Prospectors, James.  Did you have a favorite pizza on your visit? I could really go for our Kodiak Bear pizza right now. It's our take on a meat lovers pizza with pepperoni, elk fennel sausage and more!  Hope to see you back soon!

name: Julia Lavin
text: Quality seems to have gone down, as well as quality of wait staff. Very unfortunate, used to be the best pizza in Alaska. They were also out of 3 kinds of drinks we were interested in having - disappointing for sure.

name: Amit Kakde
text: Excellent Alaskan themed pizza place! Great selection of unique flavors. Also a good selection of beer as well. The interior decor is also great. You are immersed in a true Alaskan experience! Good place to familiarize yourself with Alaskan culture and history too with great pictures and maps etc. Displayed on the walls. Staff are friendly and helpful.

name: Alice Castillo
text: Service was good and food for 8 was great. Good spacious place for us . But they where running out of beer that we ask for.  Go figure  ale house out of popular beer.

resp.text: Thanks for dropping in, Paul! Did you have a favorite pizza on your visit? I love the Brushfire pizza, it has reindeer sausage, jalapeños, a drizzle on honey, and more, its spicy, sweet, and delicious. Hope to see you back soon!

name: The 3 B. Lockwins
text: Surprised by all the good ratings because this place did not live up to the hype. First of all it was a gorgeous day and they have a large deck area but "it was closed and we were not allowed to sit out there today because there was no server" and then inside there was no view of outside.... it really sucked. The soup was OK, salad was tiny, Grizzly cheese pizza (ordered with extra cheese - but would not have known it) was a huge disappointment. Crust was so tough that I could not even cut it with the knife for my youngest daughter. We had half a pizza left and did not get it to go it was so bad my kids were like no way am I eating any more of that. Would not recommend or come back next time we are around the area. So far the only poor review of our trip.

text: This place is filled with fun Alaska memories on the walls through memorabilia and photos and artwork. The pizza is delicious. Build your own is a better deal than the premades. The price is reasonable, especially considering it's in a tourist trap town. The beer selection is good and there is a mix of local and imported options. I haven't had the fries but they looked and smelled delicious as I was eyeing other tables.

text: It was awesome quite. And very scenic! For the area I was in it had a gorgeous panoramic view!

name: Zee Cale
text:
3rd largest park in America that covers almost half a million acres
Three day hiking at -25 degree.
There are at least 50 trekking tails in the state park, from East to hard, from easy sightseeing trails to adventurous ones.
There’s lots of wild berries when it is berry season.
Carry bear spray while doing hikes in summer and fall.
I had three-day hike in the state park.
Day one: Spent one day snowshoeing in the park, experience of lifetime
Day two: Hiking along the eagle river and in the forest,  spectacular views of the frozen waterfall
Day three : Hiking along the ridge line, breath taking views of the wild snow mountain range.
And Saw three people parachuting. Crazily cool!!
Would definitely come back to do the hikes again in the summer and fall!
Love Alaska!

name: Sierra
text: Beautiful views and lots of wildlife. Heavy bear traffic so travel with bear spray and a weapon. Chilly at night because you’re up in the Mountains. Definitely wear layers. We went in September and it was beautiful.

text: From the Glen Alps parking area to Power Line trail. This is such an amazing place to explore. We saw a bull moose off in the distance. It was pet friendly, we brought our dog and saw many others with theirs. There are several trails I'd still like to explore here (Middle Fork, Flattop).

name: Brian Booth
text: Awesome adventure, serious climb to top, not for beginners, but unspeakable breathtaking, will do again, highly recommended

name: Kyle and Jenn Todd
text:
Always a great local get-away to come and visit the Chugach state park. Flattop is one of the main local favorites and is a good fun hike with great views of the greater Anchorage area. Despite it being fairly short there are some pretty steep spots your average grandma might throw a fuss over. Alas, come go for a hike in our beautiful state park and you wont regret it.

Bring $5 for parking.

name: Steve D
text: The scenery alone is something to behold whether its summer, fall, winter, or spring. Each picture I take shows me something new each time. Alaska is the top state in my book to visit!!

name: Becky Noyes
text: They're aren't to many places in the world where you can driving down the road and pull off one of the multiple scenic turn offs to see Beluga whales right from your vehicle!  I definitely wasn't expecting to have such an opportunity!  Outside of seeing Belugas, I hear this is also a very common spot to see Mountain Goats and Dall Sheep, although we weren't lucky enough to see then as well.  The landscape is also very beautiful with mountains all around and coming right up to the road.  The only thing I warn is that it is a very well-traveled road and people can sometimes pull off or back onto the road, so just be sure to travel with caution, maybe with a buddy or two so they can tell you when they see something cool and where the safe places to check them out are.  I hope we get to go back someday!

name: Ryan Stafford
text:
If you're in the woods then you might be in the Chugach State Park.  The Chugach State Park is home to many trails, fishing, camping, and sightseeing; however the Chugach State Park doesn't include free parking.  Make sure you have a parking decal or you'll need to bring cash for the parking fee.  You can buy the Chugach State Park parking decal at REI in Anchorage.

Flying drones is prohibited in the Chugach State Park.  Read "AAC 20.020 Aircraft" for more information.

text: Great family experience. The signs and decor kept our eyes entertained and the food was good too. The term Classic comes to mind, as this was a unique experience that would satisfy most. We'll be back!

name: Brian Bowen
text: This was a nice stop for lunch.  Everyone was super friendly and the service was great even though they were super busy.  Everything we had tasted great. Definitely recommend you stop in if you are in the area.

name: Neal Schanbeck
text:
Nice place, friendly staff, food meh.
I had the chicken fried steak breakfast.  Obviously the eggs and hash browns were plated long before the steak and gravy.  They were both quite cold.  Overall meal was tasteless and the chicken fried steak was way over cooked.

name: Seaangel Siren
text: Love coming here. Never a disappointment. Amazing food, great environment, awesome staff. What's not to love

name: David Ustick
text: Great new waitress... I thought her name was Dominique (probably wrong though) happy and friendly was very aware of the menu and her patrons.

name: Alisa Cross
text: It was a full house this morning! The service was great, the food was really good, and it was pretty spendy. I had a skillet- my over medium eggs were spot on, the potatoes were a little burned, and the bacon was awesome. My boyfriend had an omelette and he said it was really good. Overall it was a good experience, I would love to come back again if my wallet can handle it.

name: Julia Satterwhite
text: The food is always good when I eat there! Yum! The service is always good as well!

name: Michael Forte
text:
So there was a lot wrong. First no breakfast for 2 adults and 2 kids should cost $48 before tip. Secondly the kitchen staff should be coached on how home fries should come out. Not extra firm, over salted, no seasoning, and no crunch. Thirdly bacon should not be brittle and tough.
Unfortunately I didn't take pics. But really an overall fail. Not sure what happened since the last time I was in.

name: Martin Marshall
text: The other reviewers really nailed this place. The food is top-notch and you cannot make a wrong choice. All of the staff we interacted with were super awesome.  They were happy and took great care of us. I'll definitely be coming back here, but not too regularly; otherwise, my waistline will pay the price. Keep up the great work!

name: AkGrown71 Alaska
text: Excellent service, awesome food. My favorite is the Chicken fried Chicken.

name: Geo
text: My wife and I have stopped in on occasion for many years now and it has always been a great experience.  Recently we visited for a needed breakfast.  Our server was so nice and attentive, wish I could remember her name... she is in a military family and studying to be a doctor?  Let me tell you, this is one of the best places in Alaska!  The Staff here is always courteous and friendly too.  The food here is outstanding every time.  This is a must visit place for a great dinning experience.

name: dee'z nugz of information nunya
text: Good service great food cool sign everywhere ambiance

name: Lucy Moose
text: This restaurant is one of my new comfort food places. Clean, friendly, and awesome good. We love reading the humorous signs while waiting. My favorite is french toast with banana and nuts. My husband loves the Country Benny. Coffee is delicious. Love it here.❤️

name: Tricia Harrington
text: Always good fast service food is yummy try the dipped French fries mmmmmm

name: Harry Rohr
text: Got the chicken fried steak breakfast this morning. portions are huge and the steak is homemade as is the gravy. the eggs cooked perfect. will definitely be back! great service!

name: kyle Kjerstad
text: Old fashioned diner with some delicious food

name: Blaze Martin
text: Super friendly staff and wonderful food!

name: Drew Raught
text:
Just good home-style country cooking!
Great breakfast. Servings are large and filling. A must breakfast stop on your way out of town.

name: Brian Lervold
text: I had chicken fried chicken with hash browns, eggs and an english muffin. They were over busy from the gun show across the street, but my service and food were great. This is the best place to eat good, home style food in Mat-Su and Anchorage, bar none.

name: Gregory Adrien
text: If you want a great home cooked meal in palmer, this is your place! Find a better place, I dare you!

name: Joesph Tackett
text: Your going to love this place. Definitely worth bringing the whole family but a great place for a lunch meeting.

name: John Lane
text: Great place with great home style food. Even when it was packed there wasn't much of a wait. Food was amazing. Their eggs Benedict was on point. Try the Northern omelet, also great.

name: Tanesha M
text: Delicious food and great service. This Birthday dessert the apple crisp was AMAZING

name: Si Philbrick
text: Amazing food! I love all the sarcastic signs around the dining area and the stuffed animals are awesome! I thought they were really quick at making the food and it was delicious!! I HIGHLY recommend this place!!!

name: Donza Short
text: Great family restaurant,  clean and comfortable!

name: Gregory Hartley
text:
Two words: Country Benny.
For those who need more words: I love restaurants with a homespun vibe and a great sense of humor. This one has both. Take the time to read all the signs on the wall to keep you grinning while you wait for your food. Heck, just read the menu all the way through for a ton of great, snarky menu humor. Servers are kind and they keep that coffee flowing! What more can you want on a cold Alaskan morning?

name: Jack
text: Delicious breakfast with topped off cup of  the whole time!!!☕

name: Nancy Winters
text: The perfect spot for brunch, it does get busy so come prepared to wait for a table.

name: Stewart Andringa
text: Great place for breakfast, good coffee, and i recommend the corn beef hash. Friendly and attentive staff won't let your coffee cup sit empty,and I even like the antler decor. I will be back if I'm ever in Palmer for breakfast again

name: Lori Kroening
text: Service and atmosphere is beyond wonderful. Highly recommended.

name: Jack Eppley
text: Great service even though very busy. Food was good

text: My absolute favorite Palmer restaurant. I love their burgers and adore their pie. Can't want to come back!

name: Rhonda Jarboe

name: Ro
text: We drove by and the parking lot was packed; you know it's good when all the locals go there. So many choices for eats but settled on an omelette with fruit on the side. Presented nicely and really tasty! What a fun place to visit; there is so much stuff to look at...funny signs on the walls, just kept us busy right until the food came. Definitely recommend!

name: Mark Sabo
text: Great group of lovely waitresses and good food!

name: Ellen Gamel
text: Friendly service and good food.

name: Eric Collier
text: Great service, great food, short wait. We showed up about 1030 AM on a Saturday. Had to wait about 15 minutes to be seated. Once seated, we were provided out drinks while we looked over the menu. Our order was taken and 10 minutes later our food arrived hot and fresh. Wait staff was very friendly and always kept our drinks full. I highly recommend for breakfast if you are in the Wasilla Palmer area.

name: melisa kelsey
text: Excellent food, community environment and authentic joyful service. Very much look forward to our next visit 😋🙌

name: Tina Tennille Hummingbird Medina
text: Amazing. I love it

name: Dorothy Rogers
text: It was recommended by a local and we are tourists. It was a wonderful find, with wonderful food, and outstanding staff.

name: Jennifer Frysz
text: Had a great meal and wonderful service! Thank you so much. Very efficient & kind and friendly when needed most!

name: Gabe Fewkes
text:
Cozy country atmosphere, friendly fast service. Food was spectacular. Perfect place for comfort food.

I'll be stopping here whenever I drive through Palmer

name: Ashley Johnson
text: Love it!!!  Great food!!!  Fieat time we have all cleaned our plates in a long time!!!

name: Randy Windsor
text: Great food and service.

name: Jeff baker
text: Country Benedict was fantastic

name: Emily Clarrey
text: Amazing! This is must stop when you are traveling outside of Anchorage! The food was wonderful and the staff was very nice and helpful!

name: Trisha Brown
text: The prices were big, the proportions were small.. Wouldn't go back. Food was alright, nothing great.

name: Andrew Hess
text: Consistently great food and service!

name: Duane Spellecacy
text: Great, super, super fast, super good, super staff!!!

name: Norman Tweet
text:
Food and service are excellent at the Noisy Goose. The atmosphere and decor add to a rustic, family style dining experience.

One small complaint is that sometimes the wait to get a table can be rather long, although then again, that just goes to show how popular this place is.

name: Angie Cottrell
text: A great place.. Will defenitleyhelp your smile

name: Barbara Hrubes
text: Really good food. Don't go if your in a hurry as they have always been packed when I have gone. If you don't mind waiting a bit then this is your place. Fun decor, love looking around at all the cool things on the walls. Helps pass the time.

name: Jordan Clay
text: Great service and friendly staff.

name: Philip Brower
text: Very busy, but worth the wait.  Standard American and comfort food.  Lots of fun things to read on the walls.

name: Ethel Reed
text: Hearty Delicious Food, Homemade Desserts, Delicious Shakes,Fresh drinks, friendly staff, Family oriented dining experience, we have been dining there for over 20 years and hope to continue to dine there the next 50 years 🏞️💖

name: LeeAnna Bohnert
text: Absolutely delicious! We'd much rather drive the 40 min to come here, than eat at any restaurant here in Anchorage. They've remembered us every time we come in, are very friendly, food is delicious and not crazy priced, and service is great! We'll be back many, many more times! 😊

name: Under the Stars Eric Larson
text: Great food and good price. A busy place with friendly staff

name: Rick Harrison
text: Love everything about this restaurant..

name: Salina Brightbill
text: I live about 45 minutes away but will most definitely go back for the great food and service. It was really busy but our food arrived hot and in a very timely manner. Staff was very helpful our drinks were always full. Will definitely be back.

name: Kevin Meaux
text: The breakfast food here is amazing!! This my second time here and everything I’ve eaten here is delicious!!

name: Tyler Turner
text: Always great food and service!

name: Katie Netherton
text: We have been here a few times for take out, but today was the first time we had sat down and ate. The wait was a lot shorter than expected. I figured we would have to wait at minimum 10 minutes because no matter what day of the week there is a line out the door. So I was pleasantly surprised when we were seated with in 5 minutes! The server was friendly, attentive and had a very upbeat attitude! The food was even more amazing sitting down and eating it than it was with the take out. You can for sure tell the food is always made fresh, made to order and made with love! I don't care how long the wait is, if you want real home cooked breakfast this is the place to go! I can't comment on anything other than their breakfast food because I haven't ordered lunch or dinner there yet, but I'm sure it will be just as amazing as the breakfast!!!!

name: tamunnlyn
text: The Noisy Goose is a nice quaint restaurant with good food. All the staff I have encounter is nice and friendly. The only reason why i didn't give 5 stars is because they don't serve grits.

name: Jacob Franklin
text:
Great service
Excellent food
Nice atmosphere

Absolutely earn a 5 star. I will be back

name: Sergey Mkhitaryan
text: Liked the hot apple cider even though it's a bit too sweet. Hot tea is just a Lipton bag.

name: Kandi Williams
text: Love stopping in to get their Corn Fritters

name: AK Honeybee 907
text: Super great food! I've been going here since I was younger. Very friendly staff and down home cooking! Everyone in the valley must feel the same because some days you will be waiting an hour for a table!! Most find it worth it though!

name: Lenard Lynch
text: Kitchen Sink skillet is awesome! French toast is very good too.  Coffee is lite-to-medium roast and is delicious. Service is excellent, well done all!

name: Damon Landreau
text: Very good food.  Nice atmosphere.  Great service.  This was out first time there, next time I'm getting the chicken fried steak - it looks really good!

name: James Doherty
text: Love the atmosphere and service. By far my favorite restaurant in the valley

name: Mike Criss
text: Lovely place, but they need to improve the oatmeal.

name: Dream Catcher
text: I love this place. It’s always good, literally everything on the menu is good. Staff is always very friendly. Best place to get chicken fried chicken for breakfast

name: Jeff Ward
text: Good food even better pie, great coffee. They decorate the place really nice for Christmas. Definitely go during the holiday season you will not be let down.

name: Dmitry Berezhnoy
text: Hash browns were slightly undercooked in the middle. Reindeer sausage shell was tough. Just kidding, everything was tasty and made with heart. Halibut was fine and soft. Blueberry pie was such a blow! Expect friendly service.

name: Trudy Brown
text: Good food, fun atmosphere.

name: Elizabeth Plumb
text: One of my favorite places to eat! Never disappointed!

name: Kimberly
text: Excellent homestyle cooking and delicious pies!

name: Mike Warriner
text: The food is great, the prices are good for the amount of food and quality. The front of the house staff are super friendly and are checking on you to keep drinks full, and extremely helpful. Ten out of ten, would advise people to go and enjoy their meal there.

name: Angela Amaya Mata
text: Good food

name: Jon C
text: The food is always good. On a rare occasion we will get an item that is not the best. The service is great. The only complaints here come from my children that "its to noisy"

name: Roger Porter
text: Excellent food and great service. The lemon meringue pie is amazing.

name: Teagan Roehl
text: Good food quick service. Can't wait to go more!

name: Michael Vanhorne
text: Great place for home cooking!!! Clam chowder and prime rib on Friday night great way to start the weekend. Help didn't make me feel welcome however service was beyond adequate.

name: Edmund Ausman
text: Very good. Great food choices. Alaskan atmosphere. Excellent service.

name: Hank Reuter
text: Awesome meat eaters gilet, with the French toast, and a rhubarb pie for dessert with ice cream. It was all excellent and the serving staff was so kind, and the ambiance was both light hearted and fun to look at. I would highly recommend you go.

name: Jason Paes
text: Full as a tick., Great service good food. Expect to wait for a table.

name: AK TAZGIRL
text: AMAZING staff, AMAZING Food, Great Alaskan atmosphere.  *NEW* ENTRANCE, NOT CLEARLY MARKED. DOT road changes, be aware.

name: Autumn Paris
text: Yummy food good prices great service.

name: M M
text: This is a welcoming diner that we love to visit when there is no line.  The servers are skilled and the kitchen is fast.  The food quality is not worth waiting for a seat--just typical diner food.  It is expensive, a specialty omelette can cost $17+.

name: Jessica DePatie
text: The food was good and the staff was friendly... I loved the humorous sayings all over the walls and the taxidermy was cool as well

name: Jolene Arendse
text:
Great food/service. Didn't take long for food, even though they're busy.
Friendly staff, love it

name: Christine Hohf
text: Amazing food, recommend the chicken fried chicken

name: Jenny Clay
text: Good food and friendly service!

name: Shannon O'Hara
text:
First time here.
When you walk in there is a sign in sheet.
The server said they were short staffed and that it might take longer than usual even though they weren't discernably busy.

We got to our seat and were given water with menus. We ordered.
My side salad came out in plenty of time to eat it before the entree.

The atmosphere is pleasant and somewhat lax. Spend time reading all the witty signs hanging all over the walls and don't forget to check out the massive encased brown bear.

The entrees were ample sized. The service was excellent. Our server told us the special.

I had the special. My friends ordered the grilled chicken and a hamburger.

Located across from the fairgrounds and a hop, skip and a jump from The Butte, it's a must stop.

name: LeeAnna Bohnert
text: Absolutely amazing staff, excellent place to grab a meal! Waitress was so nice and friendly, food was delicious. Love the atmosphere! We'll be back!

name: megan _ thomas
text: Food is great! Service was awesome! And even though the wait time can be long it's completely worth it!

name: Karl Schloer
text: Standard, tasty comfort food served in generous portions in a distinctly Alaskan setting. A gorgeous grizzly bear mount welcomes all visitors and the rest of the dining room is full of smaller mounts and  hunting-themed artwork. If it's busy, you can fill your wait time reading the humorous signs all over the place as well.

name: Jace Olsen
text: Really nice staff and amazing food.

name: Tammy Schmidt
text: Love this place.  Always good diner fare. Fun atmosphere and decor. Super nice, friendly waitresses. Feels like home.

name: Ethan Kalicin
text: I had Mexi cali burger with onion rings. They were great. Will most definitely  go back.

name: Joe Stout
text: Go for breakfast. Everything else is just ok.

name: Marnie AK
text: A piece of Alaska and so much more. Everywhere you look you will see another charming, funny picture or plaque. The food is excellent, the service is great, even on busy days. You can't go wrong eating here.

name: Alex Kreilich
text: Great breakfast and pie

name: Justin C.
text: Great place, reasonable pricing, clean, good food, and friendly wait staff. One of the best places in Palmer for down home county style comfort food. Only down side is the weekend wait Saturday and Sunday guaranteed there will be a wait.

name: Zac Keyes
text: Really happy with the quality of food. One of the better breakfast places I've ever been.

name: Leland Jones
text:
Literally amazing. Perfect ambiance for the culture they are creating! Especially as an armed and law abiding citizen, they really do make you feel welcomed!

AMAZING Food and outstanding service! I would eat hear anytime I head out north or am coming back into town through Palmer!

name: Richard Eaton
text: Always awesome. The best place in the Anchorage vicinity for breakfast.

name: sixonenorth
text: Awesome local dinner. Great breakfast lunch or dinner. Staff is always friendly, food is always hot. Never had a bad meal here and we’ve been going there for years. If your passing through swing in you won’t be disappointed.

name: Rachel Estes
text: Our favorite local diner! I’ve never had anything from them I didn’t like. The pies are FANTASTIC.

name: Terps Madison
text: Shared breakfast burrito combo and was full by the end of it. Everything is well priced and made. Definitely a cute spot I'll visit again. I loved the country diner feels.

name: Vikke Stokes
text: The food was great!   Servers were wonderful, thanks....    I have been a repeat cußtomer for many years.  Eggs Benedict is the best in the state - many thanks.

name: Jason Nesslage
text: Always so good! Service is excellent and whoever the cooks are, don't let them go!

name: Chelsey M.
text: Amazing food! Great Staff! Hilarious wall signs!

name: Travis Rogers
text: Noisy Goose is a great family oriented place to eat. Generous size helpings, fair prices and very friendly staff. Very Alaskan in the style of decor and flair, it has a sort of sportsman novelty, with its stuffed ducks geese and even a brown bear. Not everyones choice of visual stimulation, but Alaskan at its heart. I've been taking my family here for over a decade and swear they are one of the best places for burgers and fries in the valley.

name: Bruce Owens
text: Just moved here about a month ago and came here for the first time.  I will be back staff was great, good food, and got a military discount.  Most importantly they kept the coffee cup filled.

name: Nathaniel Henderson
text: It was good... Good food, good atmosphere, just a busy place, that's all. :-)

name: Dana GAYLOR
text: The food was really tasty and good.Workers were very nice and smiles for all.

name: Charles Roper
text: Great food.great service. Food.was out and hot in no time. The waitress was really great.

name: Jessica Grgurich
text: My kids love The Noisy Goose but it's EXPENSIVE so I cringe whenever we do end up going.  They have great nachos!  Wonderful attentive waitresses too

name: Tim Kenney
text: The Noisy goose is okay. I've never had bad food but it's not particularly good either. It has pretty standard breakfast, lunch and dinner options (pancakes, melts, burgers/sandwiches/wraps that sort of stuff). The food is generally a bit too salty and sweet for my taste and I feel like it's a little bit more expensive than similarly styled restaurants.

name: Amus Evans
text: Great food👍great service

name: Becky Oviatt
text: Great food. Wait staff has a wonderful sense of humor.

name: Iceealaskan
text:
Great food... great views.
Love this place!

name: Geni Decker
text: The best service we have had anywhere! Did was excellent as well.

name: Cee Jay
text: Awesome food!  Great atmosphere and friendly staff!  Best restaurant (according to me, anyway) in the valley...by far.  Thanks guyz!  d:-)

name: Kiana Hiler
text: Fast staff just a bit of hurry up and order. Im sure our waitress. Was just having a bad day.

name: Jacqueline Libby
text: Very cozy and comfy. The waitress was kind and friendly. And the food was really good comfort food.

name: Aback Images
text: Good food nice wait staff

name: Laurie Jensen
text: No matter what time of day you go, there is always a bit of a wait and for a very good reason. The food, service and atmosphere are awesome. You can pass the time waiting for your food reading all the humourous wall signs, chatting with your friendly waitperson or visiting with your table neighbors. The staff are attentive and courteous. I highly recommend the Eggs Benedict (with a touch of lemon juice added to the hollandaise)! Its the best in the Valley!

name: karl conditt
text: Great food. Great and friendly staff all the Times we have been there. And never boring. Best breakfast around.

name: Yolanda Thomas
text: Not good for wheel chairs,  when we went they placed us on a level with 2 small steps, I was expected to pull an adult up safely. NO wSmy answer waited another 20 minutes.

name: iriscaldentey
text: Great Mom and Pops restaurant of Alaska. Delish food and excellent service. Fun place to go.

name: Brandon Ochoa
text: This has been one of my favorite breakfast places for awhile. Miss it since moving to town. No wrong breakfast choices. Also it's never wrong to get bacon on anything. I like it on everything

name: Karen Nichols
text: LOVE, LOVE, LOVE!!  We've ate at so many valley restaurants and honestly not many I'd give 5 stars to, but ate at the Noisy Goose for the first time 3 weeks ago after seeing some online reviews.  Ambiance 5 stars, staff 5 stars, food 10 stars.  Have already recommended to several friends and though it's a drive for us, we will gladly make the trip here again.

name: Nathaniel McCormick
text: Waiting staff is amazing always good at seeing if you need anything and they actually maintain eye contact while doing it all, the atmosphere is always welcoming I highly recommend them over any Restraunt in the valley the prices are affordable and the food is always good.

name: Lizz Stewart
text: Locals love it here, it was good and noisy. Busy and the service was on top of it! If we are in the area, we would recommend stopping. A lot to look at too!

name: Jaye Salter
text: Always busy and always good food. Caveat being i was disappointed with the portion size on my corned beef hash breakfast this last visit. Seemed more of a half or senior meal . My mothers CFS was regular sized.

name: Joyce Perez
text: Good food and great service

name: Donald Vieira
text: Always great

name: Kevin J
text:
Very good breakfast.
Even with a waiting list for seating, we got seated very quickly. Order was taken within minutes, and food arrived a lot faster than I expected for how busy the place is.
Only complaint I would have is the booth was more "cozy" then I prefer, but with the service and food quality, there is no way not to give 5 stars.

name: Tanya Elizabeth
text: Great food! Large portions! Awesome staff! Palmer Landmark

name: Nyssa Jones
text: There's really nothing on this menu that you can go wrong with. The coffee is real good, try it black if you're that sort of person. The corn fritters are hot and delicious, breakfast skillets are so good that you're sure to clear your plate or wish you could. Portions are big! Staff is friendly and the decor is entertaining; typically themes for the season but also full of signs like "I hunt because my wife can't climb trees," and "sarcasm is a language."

name: Cheryl Watkins
text: Great food-great service

name: Daniel Wilcock
text: This is always my go to place! Always friendly staff and great food for a great price!

name: Aaron Hunter
text: Great food great service and wonderful atmosphere with all the great phrases

name: Bsauce
text: Nice place, has a funny menu

name: Clayton Baxter
text: Their food is spectacular and their service is great.

name: Al
text: Excellent service, loved the signage/decor, above average diner fare for the state.  Coming from Anchorage prices were higher than expected, but I don't have points of comparison for the area.  I'd happily eat there again.

name: Ronald Mills
text: Excellent service and great atmosphere

name: Michael
text: Meh. The food there is OK, but over-rated. Lived here for 13 years and never understood why some people rant and rave about how good it is. Customer service also isn't great. The waitresses we've had have been tightly wound and have no patience for kids.  If it was just one, I would expect they were having a bad day and let it slide, but we've gone 3 times and its always the same. Last time one of them snapped at my toddler for being in the aisle next to the table. My kids aren't exceptionally wild. She was clearly just stressed out and decided to take it out on him. There are other places in Palmer where the food is just as good, the folks are more welcoming, the floor is less crowded/claustrophobic, and with happier waitresses.

name: Cherry Robichaud
text: Always good food. My fave waitress is there. Known her since teenhood. All the girls are great. I feel like a favorite customer when I eat here.

name: D Wilson
text: Turn at the traffic light now to get into parking lot.  Great food, staff and atmosphere !

name: Vincent Rogan
text: The servers didn't wear masks.

name: Cairo
text: The best option for non-fast food in the area.

name: Fred Avessuk
text: Outstanding service and delicious food.

name: Troy Bloxom
text: Food was great and service was even better

name: Tony Lauderdale
text: Always a fun place, and the food is good. Servers are pleasant and very good at what they do!

name: Rick Feller
text:
The "Goose" is a stalwart Palmer eatery; consistent quality and service. I gave it a 4-star rating only because they are, by design, a more homey 4-star place. Maybe I should have given a 5-star rating for it being a top notch 4-star place?

You'll find typical café fare, along with the daily specials. I've enjoyed many breakfasts and burgers here through the years, but have also enjoyed very good salmon, halibut and prime rib dinners.

The servers are always friendly and eager to please, and a senior menu offers some smaller portioned meals for a smaller price.

name: Michaelann Jackson
text: Great food and service!! I had a chicken Philly sandwich with homemade onion rings! The waitress was super nice and friendly which always makes my day. I highly recommend this restaurant!

name: Joe z
text: Great breakfast

name: Terri Reynolds-Rogers
text: Fun place to take out of town guests.  Taxidermy decor and saucy signage, an extensive comfort food menu and witty pamphlets keep you entertained while selecting a meal. Fast service.  Don't forget to ask for senior size meals at reduced cost.

name: Paula
text: Great senior breakfast. Homey, good service.

name: heather stanton
text: Cute place and pretty good quality food. I love ranch an was super surprised the ranch wasn't home made, I feel that would have topped it off.

name: Brian Martin
text: Great atmosphere and the service is awesome very attentive to your wants.

name: Paula Brooks
text: Great breakfast. Pie a little disappointing tho they went out of their way to please us!

name: Melissa Jenkins
text: This is one of my favorite places! Good food. Fast service. Lots of funny stuff to read on the walls. :) Take a gander and go try em!

name: Stephen Blankenship
text: I was a first-time visitor and plan on returning! Fantastic server, delicious food from a fun, eclectic menu. I highly recommend it!

name: Gwendolynn Robinson
text: A surprising little gem.  Good food great service.

name: Rick Kelly
text: Anything you get there is going to be good. Great service too.

name: George Gillman
text: Excellent Service and Awesome Food

name: John Tyler
text: Food is good old fashioned Alaskan goodness. Service is top notch. Most definitely recommend it

name: Hosea Kaahu
text: Had the full BBQ rack of ribs very delicious

name: Renee Waters
text: I had the chicken wrap.  It was delicious with lots of chicken, bacon and lettuce.  It was very filling and hit the spot!

name: James Lane
text: Great food, great wait staff, fair pricing - will definitely go back.

name: Leeta White
text: It was okay.got the steak and cheese stuffed potato. The potato was WAAAAY over baked and the "steak" tasted like Steak Ums basically...no flavor either. I had to add a lot of tobasxo sauce to make it edible.

name: L Robinson
text: The restaurant was a very nice rustic atmosphere and the service was excellent. The food was superb.

name: Solar Studios
text: Food is great

name: Adrianell Poteet Sorrels
text: There's usually a wait, but it's worth it. Such delicious food. Everything is great. Plus, they serve breakfast all day. I love their grilled breakfast burritos. They have great pie as well.

name: Eugenia Bakunova
text: Awesome service. Loved the signs on the wall and the bear. Huge serving of breakfast for dinner tasted amazing! But the food gave me a headache; and then the leftovers I ate the next day again gave me a headache.

name: Debra McGhan
text: Busy, bustling place. Good food and service. Nice atmosphere and all their cute signs are entertaining and make this a fun place to stop.

name: Michael Stanley
text: Great food and fast service. Looking forward to going back.

name: Regina Layman
text: Decent food, friendly staff

name: E Perez
text: The Noisy Goose is my favorite breakfast place in the valley. The food is good. The staff is friendly, and I enjoy the Alaskan atmosphere inside.

name: Mahana Petersen
text: Friendly and fast service and good down home food. The menu has a ton of variety so it's great for families. Reasonable prices too.

name: Jim Kelly
text: Good greasy spoon type place.  Friendly staff and reasonably priced.

name: Ken B
text: One of the best places to eat in Palmer, AK. Try their club sandwich and beer batter fries if you are looking for a delicious meal. Friendly staff and service. Church crowd shows up in force on Sundays!

name: Mae Lewis
text: They decided they wanted to mix politics and food on an official Facebook page so gotta take back four of my stars.

name: morgan williams
text: Good home style food at reasonable Alaska prices. Generous portions and good quality. Decor is unique and is sportsman themed.

name: PEDRO Panzardi
text: Fin place to get good comfort food!

name: Pamela Tapert
text: Well it was Noisy to say the least, our waitress was excellent ,food was fresh,good...

name: Evelyn Buchert
text: Friendly attentive service, relaxing atmosphere that gives you comfortable seating and plenty to look at, the pies are delicious!

name: Michael Rosebeary
text: Lovely place to go for dinner. Great atmosphere and very friendly waiters and waitresses. Very good food and right across the street from the state fair.

name: Margie Rother
text: Really busy place and small.  Excellent homemade pie.  Peach raspberry was wonderful.

name: W F
text: Great service and delicious food.

name: Barbara Frey
text: Good food and desserts!  Good comfortable atmosphere.

name: Lisa Haney
text:
I can always recommend the Noisy Goose to any of our visitors and friends.. the service is always spot on and the food is always fantastic. They keep the small town feel good vibe flowing... great staff!
The signs on the walls make me chuckle.. the portions are big I most often share with my daughter or bring half home. I feel the prices are fair. The food is home cooked style plus the pies are delicious and there are choices for everyone in the family.

name: Joe Vanderbleek
text: Good service and food. Close to fairgrounds

name: nathan matthews
text: Good service friendly waitress food was cooked proper wait time was ok for as busy as it was

name: Ada Schmidt
text: Great food.  Better soup!!! Just like home.

name: madmusial
text: Excellent food and friendly service. A little bit cramped and right off the highway.

name: Colin Crandall
text: Always good honest food, nothing fancy.  One of the few places that truly honor military vets & active without a hassle.  Unfortunantly prices were just raised a bit.

name: Josh Bannow
text: Great place to eat. It's always packed. It's the food that brings people in.

name: Allyssa Davis
text: Foods enjoyable, service is consistent, always enjoy myself when I'm there

name: Hunter UAS
text: Great food and options. The staff is awesome

name: Tiffany Briggs
text: Cute restaurant with good food and good service. Will go back.

name: Kaitlyn P
text:
Very popular place so often longer wait times. Great friendly staff. I prob won't go back for breakfast just because what we ordered was gross. Our kids ate the pancakes, but an adult would not be pleased, very rubbery and tough. Their "eggs benedict" is a thick, watery slice of country ham on an English muffin with a very undercooked egg on top. The hollandaise was very very salty, couldn't eat it - nothing about it was authentically eggs benedict if you've ever tried a quality dish. On the other end of the spectrum the hashbrowns were tasteless, had to doctor them quite a bit to make them palatable.

The place is sweet, has a nice atmosphere, bathrooms are clean, but the food is what I'd prob expect to find in a motel restaurant or bar.

name: Ryan Zappia
text: Probably one of the best meals of my lifetime. Soooo good! The ground beef steak was incredible!!

name: LeRoy Roberts
text: Love this place!  Always good food and a cup full of coffee. The decor is both rustic and hilarious.

name: Cedric Conner
text: One of the best breakfast places in the valley. Always good food and service.

name: Karen Restad
text: Good food good service!

name: chris botner
text: Great food and location within the Palmer area

name: Hunter Philbrick
text: Great burgers! I love the atmosphere (except the music)! A great restaurant!

name: Andy Reimer
text:
Great food, great service. It's been my family's go to breakfast spot for years.

You came to wrong eating here

name: Matthew Scott
text: This place is by far one of he best breakfast places in the Anchorage area. Definitely one of the best in the valley. The biscuits and gravy are excellent as are there omelets. You really can't go wrong with any of their breakfast options. The restaurant is filled with funny, corny signs that give it a really casual feeling. The views of the mountains are awesome. Parking is OK, they take card, and the staff are all great. If you're in the area is recommend it.

name: Paul Munson
text: Every thing I've tried here has been good.

name: james wahl
text: Great food an friendly service

name: Gayla Rickey
text: Great atmosphere with great food.

name: jaime clement
text: One of my favorite breakfast joints in town. Great for groups and families. Busy on weekends.

name: Bryan Chaisone
text: Love it. Good service. Good food.

name: Peter Noreen
text: Pretty standard Mom and Pop family style restaurant. A lot of space and the kitchen processed our order quickly especially considering the numbers they were tending to on Sunday morning.

name: Miranda Panda
text: Great fun atmosphere, friendly staff, good food!

name: Kristina Scholtz
text: Average local breakfast place.  Nothing unusual.  Good service.  Basic menu.  Country decor.  Rustic theme.  Food was quick.

name: Mike Harris
text: Amazing food, busy, but for good reason.

name: Benjamin Seegraves
text: Always good food !

name: Micah Miessner
text: Great small diner restaurant. Good food, good service. Only downside is its popular and hard to get seated during peak hours

name: A K
text: Friendly staff and good food

name: William Burton
text: Love the Noisy Goose. Good food good service.

name: JoAnn Nelson
text: Adorable place. Great food. Very nice staff.

name: john diumenti
text: The food is pretty good and the service is great. They serve American comfort food. The food is better than average...but not 5 star good.

name: Natisha Johnson
text: We was seated, a party of 2 and everyone in the restaurant was served before us. It took 15 min for a waitress to come to our table to get our drink order, over an hour to get our main dish, when asked what was taking so long, we were told that it was taking a long time to make sure the stakes were cooked well and then it was not prepared to order as requested and the other partys order was cold when it was brought to the table. However we did get the salad with some adorable dipping sauce cups promptly 🤨. Took the stake home and ended up throwing it away. I usually don't give bad reviews, I just won't return to the establishment but this encounter had me feeling some kind of way down in my soul. Please do better, not sure what was going on that day but my money's green like everyone else, I even drove from Talkeetna just to eat there after having nothing all day.

name: Amandeep Godara
text: Wrangell–St. Elias National Monument was initially designated on December 1, 1978, by President Jimmy Carter using the Antiquities Act, pending final legislation to resolve the allotment of public lands in Alaska. Establishment as a national park and preserve followed the passage of the Alaska National Interest Lands Conservation Act in 1980. The park, which is bigger than the country Switzerland, has long, extremely cold winters and a short summer season. It supports a variety of large mammals in an environment defined by relative land elevation. Plate tectonics are responsible for the uplift of the mountain ranges that cross the park. The park's extreme high point is Mount St. Elias at 18,008 feet (5,489 m), the second tallest mountain in both the United States and Canada. The park has been shaped by the competing forces of volcanism and glaciation. Mount Wrangell is an active volcano, one of several volcanoes in the western Wrangell Mountains. In the St. Elias Range Mount Churchill has erupted explosively within the past 2,000 years. The park's glacial features include Malaspina Glacier, the largest piedmont glacier in North America, Hubbard Glacier, the longest tidewater glacier in Alaska, and Nabesna Glacier, the world's longest valley glacier. The Bagley Icefield covers much of the park's interior, which includes 60% of the permanently ice-covered terrain in Alaska. At the center of the park, the boomtown of Kennecott exploited one of the world's richest deposits of copper from 1903 to 1938, exposed by and in part incorporated into Kennicott Glacier. The mine buildings and mills, now abandoned, compose a National Historic Landmark district.

resp.text:
Dear Ms. Walicka,

Thank you for your recent stay at Talkeetna Alaskan Lodge and taking time to write your review.

I am sorry your expectations of the lodge were not met entirely.
At no point we would want our guests to feel as a captive audience in the lodge. There is a taxi company which operates in town and can take our guests anywhere they desire. Our complimentary courtesy shuttle is here to help guests experience the Downtown of Talkeetna, it's architecture, history, museums, salmon center, other activities in town. All those are closed after 5 p.m. and this is where we are coming from offering the shuttle hours mentioned in your review. I hope you did have a chance to enjoy your meals in our restaurants because we do offer dining services.
True, it's getting warmer and warmer in Alaska year after year. Back in a day when the lodge was built there were some warm days here and there but never so many hot ones as this summer. We definitely will be looking into the solutions in the near future.
Of course there are alternative lodging in Downtown of Talkeetna where travelers can stay, it all depends on they are planing to do on their trip to Talkeetna. We have multiple common areas, spacious lobbies, beautiful 57 feet tall fireplace with couches and armchairs, several beautiful observation decks overlooking Mount Denali and the whole Alaskan range, beautifully maintained grounds with hiking trails, and so much more. The mentioned rate might seem not corresponding to the value, but it depends on what one is looking for during his stay at the lodge. I respect and value your concerns, we will work on improvements and solutions for air conditioning. Again, thank you for your feedback and stay at Talkeetna Alaskan Lodge.

Sincerely,

Anna McCullough
Assistant Genaral Manager
Talkeetna Alaskan Lodge

name: Jonathan
text:
2-Star Hotel at 5-Star Prices -- Rooms are very basic and poorly planned.  Great view of Denali from the hillside location of the lodge.  Would not eat at restaurant again but rather go into town.  Price is WAY too high for what you get.

The Experience:
My wife and I researched the Lodge online prior to our honeymoon and per the reviews decided to get the Denali view room for a three night stay... $350/night
The staff was very friendly to greet us and checking-in was painless.  However, there was no elevator to go up to our room though it was offered to have someone carry our bags.
No valet.  No complimentary waters.  No room service.  No welcome binder/magazine for amenities.  No instructions regarding radiant heated floors.
The room was VERY BASIC (mind you we upgraded to the North facing room on the 3rd floor).  I was only impressed by the radiant heated floors. Otherwise: Bed was average... Furnishings dated and basic... small vanity...  Mini-Fridge just sitting in the corner of the room and not tucked away... Old fabric couch of questionable cleanliness... And above all, the SHOWER ROD was so low it was a constant head banging risk (see photo as I am only 6'1")!
The views were epic when you can see the mountain (only 30% of the time is there a clear view to the mountain top), but I wouldn't pay the extra fee as you can just go outside and get the same views and the bed doesn't face the mountain at all so you can't really wake up to the views (again, poor planning).
Dining is a disappointment.  Clearly frozen foods thawed which you might argue is the way to do it for Alaska... however, in town WILDFLOWER and MOUNTAIN HIGH PIZZA and ROADHOUSE were all amazing!!!  Do NOT waste your time with the restaurant.  Also... stop by Cubby's on the way in to grab a bottle of wine or stop by Denali Brewery to get your beer/mead of choice prior to settling in so you don't have to pay the "Lodge" price for beer/wine.

Overall, this Lodge appears to be servicing tour groups brought in by bus/train.  We were asked multiple times what train we were on and what group we were with when we drove ourselves.  This is not much more than a pit stop for most and would treat this as such as opposed to an extended stay (which we did).
Recommend Mat-Su Resort in Wasilla or Alyeska Resort in Alyeska for extended stays.

name: Peter McDougall
text:
Here's an edit after an amazing response from management which made me stop and rethink.

I'd complained I didn't like the lack of a lift to take baggage upstairs. The lack of air con. And the disastrous bath design.

The response was to say they'd strip out the baths. Rethink aircon and reconsider luggage. I'm impressed. A management that responds like this is one I'd support, I regret not meeting them when I was there.

Still no safe in the room.

I raise it to 3star.  Gracious of me I know. But thank hotel management for taking suggestions seriously and in good humour.

If you have issues, address them with these guys on site. A rarety is a management that listens. Cheers

resp.text:
Dear Mr. McDougall,

I want to thank you for staying at the lodge and apologize for all the discomfort. I understand you expected to find an elevator rather then an itinerant staff trying to do you a favor by lifting your bags up one floor. This is unacceptable - red flag for me - we will think more about how we are perceived and work on our ways of interaction with the guests. I am glad you walked safely out of your bath-taking experience while staying with us. Definitely, point taken - we will look into taking those bathtubs out and getting all the new ones - a good project for us in the future. I have to admit - we do not have a gym, what we have is an exercise room. The room does not fit lots of equipment. One won't find a gym anywhere in Talkeetna - historically guests coming here are those authentic wilderness seekers you mentioned about, they like to hike, kayak, camp, go out there into the wild for whatever reason. I completely understand you when you say: no air conditioner in the room is unacceptable even in Alaska. 20 years ago, when the lodge was built, it was not the case, as back then this place did not have summers like this. Noways, indeed, it is not acceptable. Comments like yours makes us believe it's time to take an action - we are definitely planning on a solution for in room air conditioning in the soon coming future.
Indeed, the shuttle hours are not the most convenient for taking guests to dinners and bars. Our complimentary courtesy shuttle is here to help guests experience the Downtown of Talkeetna, it's architecture, history, museums (there is a couple), etc. All those are closed after 5 p.m. It does not mean you are trapped or have to walk 1.7 miles - there is a taxi company which operates in Talkeetna and can take our guests to town any time they wish to to experience dining elsewhere but at the lodge.
It was very sad for me to learn we did not meet your expectations, I entirely understand all the reasons and once again bringing you my sincere apologies.

Thank you for giving us a chance in the first place and staying here. Thank you for the feedback and an interesting read.

Sincerely,

Anna McCullough.
Assistant General Manager
Talkeetna Alaskan Lodge

There are spectacular view of mount Denali from the back of the hotel, the resort is beautiful, restful and well maintained, there are great trails everywhere, and it is a short shuttle ride or walk to town. The room was quite spacious and comfortable with great beds, a refrigerator, and good coffee. The view from the room was looking out over the lawn with the lodge as a back drop and mountains beyond. It has great trails all around the hotel which are well maintained and easy to walk. There is plenty of wildlife about. The walk to town is 1.5 miles with a gentle slope and good path so easy to do, but there is a shuttle until late afternoon if you prefer. I would definitely go back to this place if in the area and was my favorite place of anywhere in Alaska. Love it!!!

text:
This is the most expensive hotel stay we have ever had ($415 per night) -- and NOT worth it. Upgraded to a mountain view room as part of a train/lodge/bus trip from Denali to Talkeetna and back. Mountain view room was 217 which overlooks a huge deck that overlooks the mountain range. Yes, we could see the mountains in the clouds, but everyone on this quite popular viewing deck could also see us, so no privacy or sipping coffee in your bath robe. Spoiled the romantic intent of this birthday present for my husband. They should make the two rooms directly over the deck into small conference rooms, not private rooms.

Shuttle service from train was confusing. Two vans there with lodge name on them-but nothing to designate that one was for a private tour where we were rudely redirected. No air conditioning was surprising for the price. Also, WiFi was pitiful. Wifi turned off every time you switched websites or cut off every 10 minutes or so and you had to log back in. In contrast, the free WiFi at most of the local pubs just worked.

The only really nice part about our stay at the Talkeetna Alaskan Lodge was eating at the Foraker Restaurant, writing a separate review for their excellence.

text: Had a blast hanging out to see if the lights were out. I always love coming here. name: Mari Rueter
text:
This local mountain is a wonderful place to see a beautiful view of Anchorage on nice days. I try to hike up here at least once a year. I consider it a beginner-level hiking trail, but it does get a little trickier toward the top and coming down from that can be hard if you're brand new to hiking.
There's also Blueberry Loop for those who may not want a hike and just a short 10-minute walk to see the views from next to the parking lot.
I absolutely love this place, always kept pretty clean and a great place for visitors.

text: Love this spot. Just far enough away from town light pollution that you can sometimes get a view of the "lights". It has a nice viewing area over Anchorage. name: Tom Reale
text: A definite must-see for visitors and residents alike.  Access to hiking trails up to Flattop mountain, and to the extensive network of hiking, biking and X-C ski trails in Chugach State Park.  And the views from the overlook just to the north of the parking lot are spectacular- on a clear day, you can see Denali and the surrounding peaks in the Alaska range, the Mt. Spurr, Mt. Redoubt, and Mt Iliamna volcanoes, and the Talkeetna, Chugach and Kenai mountain ranges as well as the peaks in the Alaska range.  You can see the entire Anchorage Bowl, Cook Inlet, and Turnagain and Knik Arms.  Like I said, an absolute must-see.

name: Nicholas Conrad
text: There are several trails accessible from this trailhead, but the most traveled is the Flattop Mountain trail. Most of the trail is well marked and generally wide (though it can be steep in places) making it not particularly difficult if one takes their time. However after the second saddle the trail becomes very steep over rocks and boulders, and it narrows and splits into several paths which twist onto each other unpredictably, and some dead-end, making it a much more tricky assent to the summit. There are several lookouts and vantage points along the way offering wonderful views of Anchorage and Cook Inlet, so it is not a wasted hike if one doesn't make it all the way to the top. The biggest drawback of this trail is how popular and crowded it is. While it's conveniently located just outside of Anchorage, there's Arctic Valley to the north, and Bird Ridge and the Turnagain trails to the south, each about 10 minutes out of town that offer equally wonderful hikes with less crowding.

name: Harold Yutuc
text: The motorcycle shop has always had stellar service. This was my first time buying a motorcycle from them but have had multiple friends and family who have bought from them and always praised their service. They are easy to work with, very friendly and not pushy at all when it comes to sales. The only reason I didn't give them 5 stars is because when I bought my motorcycle, I wasn't able to pick it up the same day and had to pick it up a few days later. They didn't mind holding the bike for me and storing it until I could pick it up, which was great but during business hours they kept my bike outside, which isn't a big deal but what concerned me is that one of the days it rained and they kept my bike outside. When I came to pick up my bike it was dirty from the rain and dirt. Luckily Andrew noticed it and got it wiped down. A bit of an oversight, but still enough to notice, especially when buying a new bike you would expect it to be kept clean and stored away from the elements. I am probably nit picking here and this won't deter me from going there again. I plan on continuing doing business there whether it be servicing my bike or when I'm ready to make another bike purchase and I still would recommend anybody whose looking to get a bike to go check the motorcycle shop!

resp.text: Thanks for your review Harold! We've changed where we keep bikes until they're picked up so this doesn't happen again. We appreciate the feedback, and hope you have a great time with your bike!

text:
Brilliant experience from start to finish. No pushy sales, lots of good advice which helped me make the right decision on a new bike.
I was mentally committed to a machine but I knew it wasn't practical deep down. Andrew listened to my requirements and then asked if I was interested seeing what other manufacturers had been doing since my last purchase.  It had been years since I had looked at a new bike to replace my 2000 Honda VFR 800 I sold 6 years before (moving from the uk and too cocost to ship).
Don't get me wrong he would have sold me the bike I went in for so it wasn't a case of being told I didn't know what I wanted.

Long story short, went in to get a bike and expected a challenge. What ended up happening was an easy sale for me, a great deal on a bike I always admired (different to the one I went in for)  a mountain of great insight and freely given knowledge and the creation of a loyal customer.

Side note: the teami inparts are awesome. They will spend time with you to discuss gear, look up items in catalogues to show you, won't push you to the most expensive item "just because", they have fair pricing and most importantly they follow up with you as your order updates through to collection at the store.
One of the guys called me to say he had a bag type I might be interested. He had asked one of the reps to leave his own bag for the weekend so I could see if it's something I MIGHT like. This was off his own back not at my request which shows he listened and he heard  what I wanted.
A+ and 10/10 for effort.

name: Dan Wilding
text:
We've been to Skagway before and we've done White Pass, and we wanted a different experience, so we opted for the Douglas Glacier paddle adventure.... WOW.... What a great day. You start with a 40 minute boat ride. We saw seal, see lions, eagles, a whale and several other interesting things. They stopped at a beautiful waterfall for us to photograph.
Upon arrival near the Glacier, we walked for less than 10 minutes where we boarded the canoes. The paddle up River took about 10 minutes then we walked the river Delta for about 10 minutes to the nearest point to the Glacier. The views were amazing.... But the best part of the trip was the staff. They were simply the best I've ever experienced, they are fun and intelligent. You could tell that they loved their job and knew what they were doing.....I highly recommend this excursion.

Everything is so green! There are so many beautiful shades of green end the Fallen trees and overgrowth makes the forest appear like it is full of Modern Art or statues! Around each turn was a new, beautiful experience. It is definitely a place I recommend people visit, not only for its natural beauty, but for its spirituality and peacefulness. If you get a chance to steal a few moments to yourself, simply stop and listen to the birds chirping or the sound of the water lapping against the shore, the wind whistling through the trees, and just breathe. name: Dr. Martha Martinez
text:
Great location, comfortable, spacious coffee shop with expanded menu including smoothies and gelato, but beware of VERY POOR SERVICE!  Sometimes they don't even wash the cups!  Many of the employees seem inexperienced, tired, and worn out and generally have this "I couldn't care less" attitude, which is very sad. This might work with tourists that spend less than 24 hours in Juneau, but hurts the business and the locals.
We love supporting local businesses and we go out of our way for Heritage Coffee, but you will be better off visiting the other downtown Heritage Coffee locations (e.g., Baranof Hotel) where the coffee AND the service are great 👍.

name: Brian Bull
text:
As the only full service coffee shop in the downtown area, Heritage takes little to no pride in serving an exceptional cup of coffee which is a shame.

The Heritage monopoly in Juneuo has 4 or 5 locations just in the downtown area. Only one of these locations can you actually get ceramic cups if you choose to stay. You also need to ask for a ceramic cups, they don't ask you for here or to go.

Heritage well not service you a pour over cup, they are unfamiliar with serving you club soda with a expresso. They have no expresso ceramics and most importantly Heritage seems to be happy with there lukewarm experience with priding themselves as the coffee mecca of Juneuo.

I gave them a one star because of the fact the have multiple locations and are more worried about hitting there audience geographical locations vs. one expeceponal location that that has the town talking!

text: Grady is the man and so is their coffee

text: Organic options are needed.

text: Beautiful coffee shop....
